topic:
My reflection will be based on the ability to take initiative and the will to make decisions in the face of uncertainty; considering the challenge of being able to communicate in an orderly manner and respecting the contribution of others.

ENG1050 was my first encounter with engineering at Macquarie University, as an exchange student I was introduced not only to new academic knowledge but also to a new education system and culture. My initial fears were based on the fact of knowing whether I was going to understand the content of the unit, if my previous education was enough to cover the requirements.
The biggest challenge for me personally was to communicate my thoughts and ideas given the language barrier. Consequently, if I wanted to have an active role in my group and contribute as I was required to do so; I needed to get out my comfort zone and express myself.
situation: Although it may seem a very broad task, our main need as a group was to break the ice and get to know each other util we felt comfortable enough to work in our unit assignments. Improve our communication was the key if we wanted to succeed in the unit’s projects (Team meetings, RGM project planning). The problem that happens to us is that nobody spoke, there was no initiative, and we weren’t sure what the next step was. This was not because we did not want to work, but because no one knew where to start. Therefore, needed a leader who could step up and guide the meetings and tasks. There was one of the members of the group who had good leadership traits and he was able to sort out were, when and how we were going to have the meetings. At first there was not much contribution from the rest, and we just nod along with the plan.
task_action: To overcome this challenge I read the requirements of each week (to understand what our short-term objective was) and started engaging more in the leadership of the tasks. I then realised that the more I contributed the I motivated others to do so. For example, as a group we struggled to find a theme for the RGM project, so I sent a couple of videos with RGM ideas, and we then discussed and inspired from them. Each of us had to come up with one theme and then we anonymously voted the one we liked the most. I had the advantage that my group was open and made big efforts to understand me despite the language barrier.
result: As a result, we created more enriched ideas because they had contributions from all of us, not only from one perspective. Each of us has different approaches and skills to face tasks, so our projects reflect a variety of personal opinions.
pfr: I realised that because I was afraid or shy to talk, I couldn’t express meaningful ideas nor oppose to the plans I didn’t consider effective; therefore, I was acting very passively inside the group. At first the idea of wanting to speak up and propose suggestions was certainly intimidating, and I also didn’t want to transmit my thoughts in an authoritarian manner because I truly believe that the most effective projects are the ones that are enriched from different minds. But throughout the weeks I felt more comfortable and become an active group member because of my initiative.
learning: Facing this challenge has helped me in my other university units and work, not only because it helped me to improve my oratory skills but because it gave me confidence and boosted me to apply my previous knowledge. Next time I hope it will take me less time to speak up.

situation: Before we started on any conceptual design for our Rube Goldberg Machine we first had to figure out the purpose of our machine. What was it going to do in the end?
task_action: We underwent a brainstorming session as a group, numbering six, all members newly acquainted. The session lasted about half an hour in an online environment. With all six members sharing similar personalities. Working with a well defined end goal and a rough understanding of what was expected of us as students.
result: we decided to use the first and only proposal that was forwarded by our members with everyone agreeing very quickly to said proposal which was to pour some juice into a glass or cup.
pfr: Perhaps as a result of our similar personalities we weren’t able to come up with many different ideas. Anything we thought and proposed was accepted very quickly by others with only minor changes here and there and we decided on everything in a very quick fashion. This might also have been a result of us being only newly acquainted thus being too shy or embarrassed to speak our thoughts and just going with the flow of the conversation instead of providing conflicting ideas that might put us in an awkward situation. At the time I was indeed feeling as such and could easily imagine my fellow group members feeling that way as well, especially since we were all introverts. The online nature of the meeting probably didn't help as well. Being unable to physically interact with each other, the “ice” was much harder to break.
learning: When we find ourselves outside of our comfort zone we tend to hide our thoughts and emotions. A thought confined within only a single brain , no matter how brilliant, will in the end, be a thought left behind. Our reluctance to voice our thoughts cost us many brilliant ideas I’m sure. Although it did make the process much quicker. Going forward in such brainstorming sessions I will aspire to be a lot more encouraging towards my team members. Creating an atmosphere where it is ok for conflicting ideas to coexist and meeting in person instead of online whenever possible.

topic: Trade-offs, judgment, and balance in resolution.
situation: We needed to come up with a sequential series of events for the conceptual design of our Rube Goldberg machine.
task_action: During zoom meetings we discussed what items we had around our house that we could possibly use and the concepts we had without being degrading to ideas presented. We weighed up the possible trade-offs of our ideas respectfully towards finding a resolution using our judgements to piece together the best ideas for the machine.
result: The result was formulating a cohesive conceptual design with an idea that we were all satisfied with to be able to refine with the preliminary design.
pfr: As we in the group were still fairly unfamiliar with each other, sharing ideas and voicing options was a little daunting at the start of the process, but the more we opened up and shared we were able to build off of our ideas towards developing a concept which we all were satisfied with. We were happy with our conceptual design as we all voiced our ideas and felt like we used our judgment to be respectful to the tradeoffs of our ideas in order to create a successful design.
learning: By utilising the skill of trade-offs, judgment and balance in resolution, we were able to come up with a conceptual design that were all happy with. Through this experience, I have learned to voice my ideas more as it is beneficial that we hear each others opinions as it enhances our perspective leading to better judgement and being able to weigh trade-offs toward the best idea.

topic: The ability to think creatively and communicate possibilities will be reflected upon.
situation: We had to decide upon an innovative yet functional RGM theme.
task_action: Assignments were set out sequentially by weeks, with certain tasks concerning the RGM theme requiring a high level of creative thinking. The RGM theme needed to be completed by the week 3 workshop, hence a pre-workshop meeting was needed to brainstorm ideas. Whilst tutors recommended completing a LinkedIn Learning course on group ideation, I didn’t complete this till after the pre-meeting. During the brainstorm session we set up a Miro board with the topics ‘theme’, ‘events’, and ‘materials’, allocating coloured sticky notes to put ideas up for each part. Approximately an hour was spent completing this process and therefore a large quantity of ideas were produced. We proceeded to present these theme ideas back in our week 3 workshop, highlighting the theme concepts we were more interested in however not a singular theme. Following the creation and presentation of our problem statements in the subsequent week 4 workshop, we had the task of refining our problem statement to be more connected with our theme as well as producing a conceptual design for the week 5 workshop. Both required a definite theme, which our group had not decided upon. Our pre-workshop meeting for week 5 was allocated to refining our week 3 theme brainstorm into one theme. This was done by each individual selecting 2 ideas they liked in order to lower the quantity. Breakfast was a favourite however it was a common theme amongst other groups. Hence to be more creative we conducted a small 10 minute brainstorm session to communicate other possible meal times (e.g lunch and dinner) and how we could do a theme around them. We continued to then refine these ideas for the remainder of the session.
result: We were able to form 3 key themes surrounding meal times such as breakfast, lunch and dinner. We performed a group vote where a unanimous decision was in favour for the theme I had presented, an RGM to set up a dinner date for a couple. Thus we were able to tailor our problem statement to the theme, and begin our conceptual design.
pfr: REFLECTION Brainstorming an RGM theme seemed very distant to me initially, where I didn’t know how to go about it and thus left the challenges of it for the future. Additionally I had misunderstood the theme as something similar to a party theme (e.g superhero or hawaiian themed) rather than an overall function. This led to my concealed confusion in our brainstorm session on the theme, as I was too concerned with coming off as ignorant to people I had only recently met. As teammates kept posting theme ideas, I was hesitant in producing theme ideas and often found that the contributions I made were heavily refined. Watching my teammates as well as other groups present, my confusion was cleared as to what a theme for the RGM was. Our next group ideation session concerning the theme again in week 5 felt much more comfortable to me. I had completed a course on group ideation and thus brought in a more open attitude when we were attempting to communicate new ideas for our definite theme. The brainstorm session we had during week 5 had a shortened period 10 minutes plus a refining process shortly after. This was more effective opposed to the hour brainstorm as we didn't waste time stuck in a plateau and instead were able to use this time refining ideas. As we were looking for a theme surrounding a meal, I was thinking of a dinner date which I also thought would come off as ridiculous and laughable to the others. However by this time I had become more comfortable with my team and was less concerned with them viewing me as ignorant, thus I suggest the idea to which they all latched onto almost instantaneously. As a team we continued to suggest humorous ideas (such as having a male team member dressing as the girl date), which showcased my new found comfort, confidence and trust in myself and my teammates.
learning: By approaching situations with an open mind, creativity can flourish. The most detrimental factor to my communication of possibilities was my enclosed mindset. I had prioritised looking intelligent over presenting unrefined ideas, leading to my lack of involvement in our initial brainstorming sessions. After completing a course on group ideation and reflecting upon my own habits, I was able to eliminate my fear of being criticised within my group. Presenting unrefined and original ideas are the goal of a brainstorming session, as merely suggesting a raw concept to your group can ignite more solutions as a collective. Thus I have developed my ability to think creatively and communicate possibilities through my experience as of late.

situation: Communication is a vital part of teamwork that we are being tested on throughout this semester. In this semester we will design, construct and test a Rube Goldberg Machine completing individual sections individually, all contributing to the team’s final product. With a project such as a RGM, that has so many small moving parts, it is vital that communication is strong and effective for our group to function correctly.
task_action: The task at hand is to effectively create a communication structure that allows individuals to have a voice and work collectively on straying on-time and on-task. Over the past 6 weeks, we have implemented technology to our advantage to create a strong and effective network of communication. Social applications such as ‘discord’, allowed us to share ideas on an online communication server, joining calls for online group meetings and having specific ‘chat’ channels to discuss certain topics. We also implemented the social media platform ‘Snapchat’, as it meant we could easily communicate ideas when we are away from our computers, notifying our group chat of urgent meetings or tasks due. This tool will also be useful for efficiently sharing images as we can easily take photos on our phone-cameras of prototypes and ideas, then instantaneously upload them to the group.
result: The result of these methods of communication were very effective as we were able to very easily communicate ideas without wasting time hosting multiple formal meetings. Discord was vital for supporting our virtual meets and allowed us to complete tasks collectively using the call feature. Snapchat was even more important especially in coordinating who would upload certain tasks and allocating roles to individuals. Organising set meeting times became very easy using the group chat function as everyone could share their availabilities so we could plan our meet times. These technologies also had their negative impacts, often leading to distractions and off-topic conversations. Using our mobile phones also allowed for distraction from the group altogether, as people were easily persuaded to use other applications during meetings.
pfr: I believe that this semester our communication overall has been quite effective, and we have managed to create a strong communication structure. Although there were personal issues and certain members at different times could’ve been more attentive, the communication was constant and efficient. I believe that personally I should’ve contributed more and in hindsight was not as involved in the communication structure as I could’ve been.
learning: Working in a group this semester I have leaned many important skills and improvements to carry though into the following semester. I have learnt many communication skills such as group management and formal speech, through writing group agendas and formal emails. I have also learnt that for a group to function properly it is about each individual’s contribution and I will work to contribute more to group conversations and general projects in the next semester.

topic: Learning the skills to effectively communicate and organise a team to complete a series of difficult tasks
situation: We all need to communicate and organise ourselves to successfully construct a functional Rube Goldberg Machine and complete a series of weekly assessments and presentations in order to pass our course
task_action: Approaching each weeks assignments and being able to function well as a team to get better marks; through weekly meetings (outside of session time), we were able to communicate and organise ourselves to approach the weekly assignments and evenly distribute the workload amongst each other in order to be prepared for each session. Additionally we were able to formulate a roster that clearly articulated to each member their role for each week.
result: This allowed us to keep us all on the same page on each others weekly duties and making sure everyone is happy with the groups decisions, giving us the opportunities to learn and figure out how to problem solve between a team in order to improve.
pfr: It can be challenging to formulate a good structure between our group members as everyone has their own personal lives and jobs. Additionally amount of weekly tasks given, not just in this unit but others, can be quite daunting. However, by having weekly meetings and finding a time that best suites everyone in the team, we have been able to not fall behind any of our assignments and maintain a sense of organisation through our communication.
learning: By maintaining communication we have been able to learn the necessary skills between us to organise multiple people to successfully attempt each assignment with all of our ability. Through this experience i have learnt how to take charge of a group and evenly distribute tasks but also knowing when to let other members take charge as their methods of operations can be more successful than my own. This has become an experience that i will be able to apply into my career as a big part of engineering is collaboration.

topic: Dealing with different personalities and communication styles within a team.
situation: We needed to develop a team communication style which allows all members to contribute maximally in accordance with their unique strengths.
task_action: Completing DISC and OCEAN personality tests and discussing the results with the team, we became aware of the personality traits of each team member. We then compiled a team charter which assessed our strengths, weaknesses and goals to allow us to collaborate effectively and assume roles consistent with our skills and personalities.
result: We were able to consider the different styles of each team member before undergoing the design process, and we were able to assign roles based on individual skillsets.
pfr: Throughout weeks 1-6 of this project, the primary course for improvement in overall project planning and management lies in the communication between team members. We have encountered some issues involving efficiency and planning. This has impacted the delivery of our design, both from a group cohesion perspective and a timing perspective. This has also impacted the ability of individual team members to set themselves tasks with which to continue on. Before embarking on this project, I underestimated the importance of assigning clear roles to each team member, as well as scheduling set tasks. The way our team has navigated this has been suboptimal, with 2-3 people tending to run each team meeting, doing all the talking and setting all of the tasks. While this team dynamic does not inherently endanger the project outcomes, we have not been able to optimise workflow and communication by assuming this role due to some of our team members being left behind with little opportunity for contribution. Each team member has characteristics which affords them an opportunity to add a unique and personal touch to the project. Until this point, we have relied on the leadership skills of 2-3 team members to propel the project, without much consideration for other team members who may not be so inclined to readily offer their ideas. The group “leaders”, myself included, could have done a much better job of intentionally including the less talkative team members when brainstorming and planning.
learning: It has become apparent during the design phase that the quieter team members have their own valuable skillsets as we have reached the point where there are detailed tasks assigned to each person. Upon seeing the results from these tasks, I am inspired to re-think the way we navigated the initial team-building tasks. If I had taken the DISC and OCEAN tests more seriously, as well as the strengths and weaknesses sections of the team charter, it could have greatly improved our team dynamic, as well as the team’s overall functionality as it would have been clearer where each person’s unique skills lie. In addition, a more in-depth analysis of these activities would have allowed us to adjust our team plan to cater for a broader range of communication styles. As someone to whom a leadership/organisational role comes easily, I should have made a greater effort to ask individual team members for their contributions, instead of leaving discussions up to only those inclined by opening up each question to the whole group. In addition to assisting with future projects at university, these strategies will help me perform at my best in my future career, as well as in my personal life. Clear communication and awareness of the strengths of different personality types are crucial aspects of all kinds of relationships, and have an outsized effect on project outcomes and personal satisfaction.

situation: After an ENGG 1050 workshop, documents have to be submitted by the end of the day. That it was my job to submit those completed documents. In addition to that, I also had a math quiz due that day which was 12% of my overall grade. To add more complexity to the day had an 8-hour shift ahead of me for that day. I would regularly finish work at 8:30-9 o’clock at night. I had known about the math quiz and work shift in advance. Completing all of my university tasks on time and meeting the requirements set seemed impossible.
task_action: Talked to my manager about my current situation. I broke down the rest of my day into 15-minute segments while on the bus to work. Putting in time for transport, dinner and work exposed how much time I really had for my tasks. Asking some of my ENGG team if they could also help though out the day on small parts of the documents. Additionally coming to an arrangement with my manager on when my breaks were and for how long also further expose the true amount of time I have.
result: Using all the time and resources at my disposal resulted in the completion and submission of the documents on time and to a high standard, completing the math quiz to the best of my ability and working for 8 hours with various breaks throughout that time.
pfr: THE INITIAL THOUGHT WAS THAT THERE WAS NO WAY THAT ALL OF THESE COULD BE COMPLETED WITHIN THE TIME FRAME WHILE WORKING 8 HOURS. FEELINGS OF ANXIETY AND STRESS OVERWHELMED MY BRAIN. BUT ONCE I TOOK A STEP BACK AND BROKE DOWN MY DAY INTO 15-MINUTE SEGMENTS, I WAS ABLE TO THINK CLEARLY AND OBJECTIVELY ABOUT WHAT COULD BE COMPLETED FIRST AND ESTIMATE HOW LONG EACH TASK WOULD TAKE. ADDITIONALLY, THE BREAKDOWN OF MY DAY ALLOWED ME TO SEE WHERE TIME WAS BEING WASTED. (I.E WAITING FOR A BUS OR SCROLLING THROUGH MY PHONE ON THE BUS). IN ADDITION, REACHING OUT TO MY TEAM MEMBERS AND MANAGER HELPED TO REDUCE THE FEELINGS OF ANXIETY AND HELP REDUCE THE PRESSURE OF THE SITUATION.
learning: Learning from the situation above, managing your resources and breaking down time-sensitive situations into smaller parts has allowed me to see how to manage my time effectively and how to use the resources at my disposal. This situation has also pushed me to be better about my time management and what I use my time on. It also exposed that we only have so much time per day and we need to use it effectively. I have also learned that when you ask for too much, relationships can be strained and in some cases, bridges can be burned. OVERALL TIME AND RESOURCE MANAGEMENT IS A SKILL THAT TAKES YEARS TO PERFECT AND BREAKING DOWN PROBLEMS INTO LITTLE SEGMENTS CAN MAKE THE LARGE PROBLEMS INTO SEVERAL SMALL PROBLEMS

situation: As a part of a team, I needed to think creatively and communicate possible ideas for the creation of a Rube Goldberg Machine.
task_action: Through completing a brainstorming session as a team using creative thinking we were able to draw up a list of possible themes and task ideas for our machine. Once we had several themes and task ideas, we conducted a group discussion to determine the overall viability of each idea and what was achievable for each team member.
result: The overall result was being able to clearly communicate and discuss possible ideas as a team to ultimately select one solution to put into action. From that solution, we were able to think creatively and develop 12 unique events to make up the machine.
pfr: Initially the task we were faced with was quite daunting and confusing as I and others were unfamiliar with the concept of an RGM. However, through communicating as a group and reading the concept this confusion soon became absent and we were able to begin discussing and communicating ideas for possible solutions. As a group, we were able to determine one idea and design a machine that best suited each individual and the overall brief.
learning: By approaching the design decision using creative thinking and discussing possibilities, we were able to devise many solutions and themes for our machine. This process made designing each task much simpler and allowed us to best fit our design within the constraints. Through completing this process I have been able to improve and develop my overall creative thinking toward design while learning to communicate these ideas to a group to ultimately get the best result.

situation: The situation was we were put into a group where we were left to design an RGM from scratch where we haven’t had much experience in mechanisms or project planning. We had easily planned what our RGM was supposed to achieve however struggled to come up with mechanisms/events to set up in our RGM. To add to this problem, we had to do majority of the planning and designing online which didn’t make explaining events easy to other team members.
task_action: I recognised that we were lacking in ideas for events so I set the task for each member to do some research and come up with 3 of their own events and once this was done, we would write these down and discuss how they would interact with each other, and which would be the best order to put them. Our team did their research by googling other RGM’s and adapting some of their events to our theme of rubbish, replacing balls for rolling events with cardboard toilet paper rolls and cut up milk cartons instead of cups for our pulley systems etc... The next problem of getting the other members to understand our 3 events through a zoom call was delt with by drawing each event on the zoom white board and if that failed sending a link and timestamp to where they got the inspiration for the event.
result: The result of these tasks led to the creation of all our events and for all our members to understand what each event involves and how it works so that we can then work on making each event interact with each other smoothly thus fine tune.
pfr: At first the task proposed to us seemed challenging and difficult due to our lack of experience in project managing and mechanisms. We knew we had to further our knowledge in what events we could come up and find a way to convey what events we came up with to our other members due to the challenge of working online. As we broke down what was involved and where our problems lied, we put a plan together and once we got working, we became much more structured and organised. Our decision for each member to come up with 3 events each organised and gave us structure to where to focus our efforts, this decision sped up the process as instead of all of us working on the 12 events we only had to work on 3 each. For our communication problem in conveying our events to each other we needed a way to draw out these events so the other members can visualise what’s going on. This led to the discovery of zooms whiteboard feature where we drew out each event and how they interacted with each other. As a result of the above actions what initially seemed like a challenging, unknown task became an organised, understandable fun way of learning.
learning: Through this experience I have learned that what sometimes seems like a challenging task can be broken down into little pieces and worked on. Through effectively communicating with my classmates we have come up with a great structure and organised system that has made this task a lot more achievable and enjoyable.

situation: During week five our group brainstormed our conceptual design for the Rube Goldberg Machine (RGM) which would involve various modularized systems culminating in pressing the space bar on a laptop.
task_action: Using the problem definition from the previous group meeting, we identified the design constraints for our RGM machine: each member creates two unique events with each lasting a minimum 3 seconds, each event flows seamlessly to the next, materials are supplied using household items and the total system lasts a maximum 5 minutes. Next, we established the sequence of system in terms of member, who has initiating system and who finishes the system. Subsequently, we brainstormed various ideas and systems we could use for different events such as dominoes, pulley systems, ramps, balls/marbles, tubes, fans and so on. From there, we collectively brainstormed variations how each item/idea could be implemented in an event. Once all the suggested ideas were thoroughly assessed, each idea was ranked against different variations in terms of feasibility given time constraint, complexity, and uniqueness.
result: The result was collectively selecting 10 conceptual ideas from the list of 20 ideas brainstormed. Further, two mechanisms were given to each member depending on their assigned position within the RGM system to maximise a seamless transition between each event. This was done collectively after the team discussed and assessed each idea in various positions along the RGM machine.
pfr: Initially, I felt we as a team would get carried away with the brainstorming activity because the design parameters are very broad. I felt we would get too creative with our ideas to stand out to the point where the feasibility and reliability of design will be questioned. Additionally, I felt we were spending too much time on coming up with ideas due to creative freedom of the project. However, this easily resolved by limiting the brainstorming ideas to 20. From here, we methodically narrowed the 20 ideas to 10 through a voting system based on creativity and feasibility given the time constraint. Subsequently, we assigned two ideas to each team member depending on their position in the sequence of the machine and materials they had home to construct that idea.
learning: Through this, it was evident that attacking any obstacle regardless of size and scope in a systematic manner is paramount. By first establishing the main objective and the relevant parameters involved it allows gives the team clarity and direction given the time constraint. Further, by involving all members of the team through brainstorming it encouraged a greater creativity within the design process and using a voting a system to decide on design plans made all the team members feel inclusive and contributory. As such, it allowed us as a team to create the best design possible in line with the requirement. Hence, my appreciation and understanding of creative thinking and importance of setting goals has heightened.

situation: During the first 3 weeks of ENGG1050, we were getting to know each other as a team while planning ahead for the upcoming weeks. As a part of this process, we needed to manage our times, in order for everyone to do equal amounts of work each week without it being unfair on anyone. Furthermore, we needed to organise a weekly meeting before each workshop.
task_action: At first, to decide on our weekly meeting time, we were just guessing and brute-forcing a time and a day that everyone was available. However, as more and more guesses were being rejected due to one or more team member not being available at the selected time and day, we soon figured out there has to be a better way of managing our times. To fix this inconvenience, we decided to create an excel spreadsheet, with the columns being the days of the week. Each of these columns were further separated to include each of our names. The rows were hours, starting from 9 AM and ending at 8 PM. As a group, we all filled out the cells with red if we were unavailable due to personal and/or educational reasons, and filled it with green if we were free. After observing this method, I also decided to make a similar spreadsheet for myself to organise times where I am free to work on my part of the project for each week.
result: As a result, we were able to quickly conclude a time and a day where everyone was free for the team meeting. Thus, this significantly helped us manage our times and make it fair on everyone. Furthermore, for my own spreadsheet, I was able to organise times each week where I was free to work on my part of the project without restricting any aspect of my lifestyle.
pfr: Initially, trying to manage our times for the weekly meeting was such a time-consuming task. I was stressed and hopeless as I thought there was no way we were going to find a time and a day which everyone agrees on. Each time a day and a time was rejected I was feeling more and more anxious. However, by using the excel spreadsheet, we were very quick to conclude a time and a day where everyone was free of personal and educational activities. That was such a relief to me and to all my team member. On top of that, the personal schedule that I constructed helped me tremendously in reducing my procrastination, as it made it feel more organised and it did not affect any aspect of my lifestyle. Overall, I was very joyful of this experience, as I got a real taste of time management which I have rarely done before.
learning: By experiencing the inconvenience of scheduling a weekly meeting, it opened my eyes to the importance of time management in a team. If we were to pick a random date and a time each week for the meeting, it would be very time consuming and a team member is more likely to not be able to attend the meeting. However, with the time management, we are all available during the chosen meeting time and date most of the time. Furthermore, this experience assisted me in appreciating organisation more than ever. The availability excel spreadsheet was such a efficient solution and a clear example of organisation that it lead to me making my own time management schedule on excel for other events and responsibilities in my life. I always thought time management was too complicated and a hassle. However, after this experience, I realised that it takes minimal effort and it is significantly beneficial in anything in life.

topic: Allocation of Team/Group Meetings - Accountability in a team operation
situation: In my example, the experience took place at the Macquarie University within the context of a team/group project that is directed towards the Rube Goldberg Machine. This project was undertaken as part of an Engineering unit (Engg1050 - Engineering Design). My team consisted of six team members, including myself. During week 3, our team as a whole contributed to propose a suitable availability for our team meetings in order to enhance our internal communication on a weekly basis.
task_action: Undergone a meeting session prior to our workshop, formed a small operational group and interacted on a cloud-based collaboration tool 'Miro', we constructed an organised schedule plan. This consisted hours and days we were available throughout a week. Essentially, our task was to resolve the communication barriers that arose as a result of dissimilar availability slots. Consequently, through the use 'Miro' and our schedule plan, we evaluated each availability slots suggested via each team member and placed them in order of majority. This was by means of a majority based upon the amount of hours and team members that were able to contribute. In conjunction to this context, we had also nominated the person with the most time slots to create and upload links to the video conference platform on a weekly basis, so that we reduce the confusion amongst our group.
result: The result of the actions mentioned above resulted in successful conflict management, better and eased communication, and allowing us to advance into completing several tasks related to the project. The existence of our group meetings not only boost our team morale, but also played a major part in contributing to the satisfactory completion of tasks. At its core, the outcomes had significantly met the purpose of a team meeting, which is to share information efficiently and to provide scope for discussion around what is being shared.
pfr: Through my eyes, I perceive that in order to kickstart our project as a team, the initial stages of forming a better communication is through sharing one another thoughts and essentially getting to know each other's capability well. In conjunction, teams of people working together for a common purpose have been a centrepiece of human social organisation ever since our ancient ancestors first banded together to hunt game, raise families, and defend their communities. The initial formation and allocation of our team meetings was ominous as a newly formed group it seems to form an overwhelming arc over our individual shoulders. However, we were able to agree on the time slots as a group by delving into the issue methodically and documenting individual responses to their suitability. Once we had established an overview of our weekly availabilities we put together efforts in allocating the perfect slots for our team meetings, which were largely focused on the majority viewpoint. My self introspection of the experience faced during the project development stages were to always remember you will have to let go and sacrifice your own opportunities to seek a total and an enhanced outcome. I strongly believe this was the case in my aforementioned recount as us team members clutched onto our one specific goal and allowed others within the group to settle themselves in and be more open. Hence, our individual accountability in the group work was set to be responsible for our own actions, behaviours, performance and decisions. Additionally, it is also linked to an increase in commitment to work and team morale, which leads to higher performance as I personally appraised through our experiences and recount of situations.
learning: Through the key contribution of team members, we could ramp up decision-making procedures for even the most complicated problems by employing a criterion-based approach and having effective team organisation. My individual experience placing an input to deciding the appropriate availability slot was all dependent upon the benefits our group received and therefore the notion of "first come first serve" does not exist within our entitled group. Due to working in a team of six team members its the contribution of placing six like-minded thoughts instead of a singular person carrying a group. topic: Reflection on “Forming effective teams” and “The design process phasing and approaches” and how these contribute to each other.
situation: Throughout the first 5 weeks of Eng1050, as part of team C15 we’ve been through the first few stages of engineering design including brainstorming, conceptual design, and preliminary designing. Becoming acquainted with my teammates, Nathan, Keith, Jake, and Rita has been a rewarding and new experience and has opened my eyes to the importance of teamwork in an engineering setting
task_action: We’ve been tasked to design and create a Rube Goldberg Machine under certain restrains and within a time limit. The machine has 10 separate events, 2 for each person, within a 13-week period (by the end of the semester) As a group we first needed to becoming familiar with each other through the use of some ice breakers and working together on our ENG1050 project. Through the use of Miro and Zoom Whiteboards, we have successfully completed our brainstorming and conceptual designs to a satisfactory standard. We have also begun the preliminary design phase, designing and finalising what we are planning to build for our RGM and the materials required.
result: The brainstorming included our problem definition, theme, and events of our RGM. Our problem definition is “Create an RGM with strict criteria (including materials and rubric) and time sensitivity (13 weeks)”. Our theme is “trash/garbage” to fit in with our material restrictions. As a team we thought that since we could only use items found around the house we would try to stick to this theme. The events have been a major accomplishment so far for our team, creating a system of flowing events in the RGM that we believe would work the best with each other. We also use a rotating system of roles, including chair, minute taker, and presenter to let everyone try different aspects of team roles and to build a more effective team, highlighting strengths and weaknesses of each team member.
pfr: Forming a team and employing engineering design processes and approaches has proven to be an exciting yet daunting challenge as a first-year engineer. In the beginning, our group struggled with awkwardness and didn’t know how to communicate. Personally I've always struggled with getting myself part of a group and preferred to work alone. However, through determination and many workshops together as I team I realise how important teamwork is. We have gotten to know each other very well and are enjoying the challenge of using engineering design processes to fulfil our final project goals, making it a fun and rewarding experience. Using the information provided on iLearn along with our creativity and dedication, my team has begun exploring the engineering design processes and are steadily tracking towards our end goal of a completed RGM. The brainstorming process has been a major struggle as we had so many ideas yet no clear direction or theme within them to progress with. As a team we worked through this challenge and landed on a single theme and events to go along with that theme. Then through the conceptual design phase we went through a range of events and how they could pair together to create a flowing machine. Some events were simply not feasible, so we decided not to go with them, and other events did not connect well so we had to rearrange the order of these events.
learning: Overall I’ve learnt that working within a team, especially with complete strangers is definitely a challenge, but having an end goal and the motivation to push each other toward that goal can lead to amazing friendships and enjoyable sessions together. When faced with an engineering challenge its important to follow each step of the engineering design process thoroughly to create the best outcome for a completed design. Although the initial problem definition and conceptual designs I thought to be initially very easy steps turned out to be quite challenging especially in a group with conflicting ideas. But, to work together as a team and decide on the best ideas to put forward is the amazing part of teamwork and through the engineering design process becomes quite trivial. Although I thought the first few steps of the design process were useless and wasted time, I’ve come to realise that they are the essential foundation to any engineering problem and are the key to a successful solution. I also need to put more faith into my teammates. I am always worried about the quality and work ethic of those around me, and when I want something done correctly I find myself taking over as I trust myself to do most things to a high quality, however through this engineering problem I found I need to let that go and to be able to put trust into others to contribute their part to the end goal. We are a team after all, and everyone in my group is capable of producing high quality engineering solutions, I need to let my ego go.

topic: _The transferable skills/employability skill I will be reflecting on is 'Conceiving, systems engineering, and management'. In week one, my team and I focused on understanding the needs of the workshop and setting goals on how we will achieve the task (Rube Goldberg project) and sent out a professional email every week. Through weeks 2-6, my team and I focused on defining a function, concept, and architecture, the design process phasing and approaches, disciplinary design, test, verification, validation, and certification, and finally, implementation management. We went through the preliminary design and conceptual design as a team. We decided that the idea behind our project would be, 'Dropping a Berocca Tablet Into Water' and i__n chronological order ,the creative process was, to start rolling a marble to hit a pendulum, which will open the Berocca cap lid and the tablet would fall out of the container, onto a track and then the Berocca rolls down an inclined plane utilising a folder, it’ll then rolls off a benchtop onto a popped open umbrella flyings up to another benchtop. The marble will then roll down a tube, hit a stack of dominoes, and hit another marble which will fall into a water bottle, a soccer ball would hit a toilet paper roll which will, in turn, hit the water bottle causing it to tilt the marble out of the water bottle. The ball then rolls off the benchtop onto the stick of the shovel and declines while swinging off the bottom end of the shovel. The Berocca will fall into a tube/Pipe and simultaneously the marble will spiral down the tube, a ball will hit the coins and roll down the slope, dropping down into the cup and moving the balance. The balance will then release the Berocca. The Berocca rolls down a tube and hits a windmill, the windmill then sends the tablet down. At this stage, the marble will roll down the track hitting a track that is on a rotating bearing to align a path for the Berroca to continue rolling down on. The ball will roll onto a pulley system that causes an object on the other side of the rope to cause dominoes to fall. The dominoes hit a lever pushing a water bottle to fill up a glass while also hitting a ball to then cause the next actions. The marble rolls down to hit a block that is blocking the path to allow the tablet to go through which will eventually fall into a crane of a Lego truck. The marble will then fall onto the remote control of the truck and rotate the crane so that the Berocca can fall into the cup of water._
situation: We needed to brainstorm a design mechanism through weeks 1-6 for the creation of the Rube Goldberg machine which involves dropping a Berocca tablet into water. The tablet falls out of its vessel and undergoes various complex situations and processes until it finally falls into water and dissolves.
task_action: We went through various brainstorming sessions throughout the weeks and came up with the Berocca tablet idea for the RGM. Our group came up with a problem statement for this idea, which was that the Berocca tablet cures headaches, releases energy, reduces tiredness, and helps support immunity, which would help a university student get through university. We went through the gallery method of brainstorming, wherein we all put forth our ideas and started building ideas on them, and finally came up with our final design for the RGM machine. We also spoke about various other ways we could have designed our machine but came up with the most creative and fun way in which we could complete our project, which included 3d printed pipes, marbles, cardboards, umbrella, folder, dominoes, track, lego truck, shovel, coins, cup, windmill, balance, Berocca track bearing, water bottle, a cup of water. After analyzing the weight, complexity, availability, manufacturability, etc we decided to go ahead with our final idea, based on all these factors.
result: The result was being able to select a design solution that included the Berocca tablet being dropped into water, and after undergoing various other solutions, we shortlisted and came up with our final design.
pfr: When we first heard about the RGM project, we were intimidated and overwhelmed with the topic, as we were unsure on how to go about the topic, but once we realised that it was fun, and wasn't as complicated as it seemed, we became more comfortable on how to go about it and started putting ideas forward more freely. Once we started developing the preliminary design and the conceptual design, systematically, and making notes on miro about everything we decided on every week, we were finally able to come up with the final design in week 6. The design did satisfy the required conditions it had to meet, like being of proper type, weight, complexity and was resourceful and therefore satisfied the ascribed problem statement.
learning: Decision-making using a merit-based approach is a very good approach which my team and I implemented. Decision-making narrows down complex situations to only the important aspects of the problem and is therefore very important. The understanding of choosing the appropriate design was all contingent upon the constraint’s requirement like whether or not we will be able to execute the idea, etc and therefore the conception of the “best design” is not valid; every design has some constraint limitation. Therefore, through this experience, I have come to appreciate the effect of vigorous and structured ordered decision-making, and learnt that thinking outside the box is always good and important, no matter how complex our thinking is, as it will only guide us down the right path.

topic: SKILL/SUBJECT REFLECTED ON: Accountability in a team operation and design brainstorming.
situation: In week three of our workshop for ENGG1050, we as a group brainstormed of ways to conceptually design a Rube Goldberg Machine that would consist of a minimum of 10 action events with each action event lasting 3 seconds minimum.
task_action: We came up with two different, but flawed solutions to the problem presented before finally deciding upon a better alternative towards the end of our brainstorming session. The first flawed solution being to make a software that simulates the actions of the machine, but due to the complexity of creating such a software and questions as to whether it violates any of the constraints presented by the problem, the idea was abandoned. The second idea was for each of us to design two action events and that we would later physically compile those action events into one machine, but this idea was also flawed as one member wouldn’t be able to participate in the physical creation of the machine and would have to burden other group members with the responsibility of physically creating the individual’s design.
result: After researching some more, we came to the conclusion that each individual member would be responsible for creating and recording a video of a working version of our Rube Goldberg machine consisting of 2 action events and that the ending of each action event would be a transition from one group member’s video to the other member’s. Through video editing, we would make it seem as one complete Rube Goldberg machine that at the time satisfies most of, if not all the constraints presented by the task.
pfr: Currently being a student geographically studying in Bangladesh and having to communicate and work with students located in Australia was definitely a frightening task for me initially to say the least. When I first heard that this unit would consist of group work, two thoughts came to mind, the first being that I’m probably going to have to do most of the work and the second being that I won’t be satisfied with the grade I receive. In the past, I’ve had terrible experiences with group work, where I’ve had to do most of the work in order to get a satisfying grade while the rest of the team shirked their responsibilities. As a result of those prior experiences, I was not excited to work in a group, but after meeting up with my team members, I am happy to say that I am satisfied with my team as each member is willing to take responsibility and work on their own actions. Furthermore, being the only member that is currently not located in the same geographical area meant that for the physical construction of the machine, I would have to heavily rely on my other team members and possibly delegate most of my responsibilities onto someone else. Since I know what it’s like to shoulder someone else’s responsibilities, that isn’t something that I wanted to do, so we continued to brainstorm of different ways to complete the project.
learning: Finally, through brainstorming as a team, we were able to find a solution that all group members were satisfied with. As long as we met the constraint requirements, we decided that the conceptual design of creating our own two events and transitioning into one another’s was the most suitable one for our current situation. I was able to learn through rational decision making approaches and effective team communication, that we as a team could come up with a solution that not only holds the team accountable for their respective operations, but also able to create an effective and efficient solution where each team member would be able to maximize on their own strengths and minimize on their own weaknesses by taking on the responsibility of creating their own action events, where we wouldn’t have to rely on anyone else’s knowledge or resources, but also be able to communicate and share our expertise if one of us needs it. I hope to use these skills in creating effective and accountable teams in the future.

topic: Trade-offs, judgment, and balance in resolution
situation: During the making of my stages in the RGM I discovered that working with dominoes was harder than I thought.
task_action: I began working on my sections; a spiral ramp on which a circular object would roll down and hit a piece of domino and start the chain reaction of falling dominoes. Initially I planned to make the domino chain loop 2 times around my spiral ramp. However very quickly I discovered while arranging the dominoes that when I made a mistake; perhaps my hand slipped or I shook the table I was working on too roughly or I didn't get the spacing right, the whole domino chain would fall and I would have to make it all from scratch again. I did this about 8 times and quickly realized the longer I made the domino chain the more fail points there were in the system and the more stuff I would have to rebuild when it failed.
result: I decided to make the domino chain only loop around my ramp 1 time which drastically reduced the amount of dominoes used and therefore the amount of failure points however it made it less impressive as well.
pfr: At the time I was feeling very frustrated because it took me 2 hours to build and fail then rebuild and fail then rebuild… and so on. I must have built the domino chain 8 or 9 times. And after all of that, when I realized I had to compromise if I wanted to get it done in any realistic time frame and therefore make it less impressive than I initially wanted it to be, I was very frustrated. But when I made the chain smaller and finally got it right I came to the conclusion that the compromise was a wise decision.
learning: When confronted with the fact that sometimes what you have in mind doesn't quite work out as well as you hoped in real life, it can be very frustrating and disappointing. And you have to make a decision on whether you want to proceed with your original plan despite the difficulties or compromise. And if you do decide to compromise, by how much? It's a careful balancing act of trying to make as much of your idea a reality as realistically as possible.

topic: Collaborate with team members remotely on the same project
situation: We needed to design a Rube Goldberg Machine (RGM) as a team of six, with each section of the machine to be completed by one person. All sections must be filmed individually and compiled into one video which demonstrates seamless transitions between all sections of the RGM. The team members met only over Zoom, with each person having access to different materials. The RGM was required to have a consistent theme and relevant end goal.
task_action: Each member of the team chose their own section of the RGM, in which we came up with our design individually, and built the section individually. We all tested our sections for reliability and worked individually on improving the reliability of our respective sections. Filming was also done individually.
result: The result was a somewhat choppy series of videos in which some sections of the RGM were vastly more reliable than others.
pfr: Our team's final videos displayed our theme accurately, however they were not very cohesive, and there were some issues with reliability and final design changes at the last minute. Some sections of the RGM were a lot more complex than others. The shortcomings of our final project were largely due to the team's inexperience in working on a common project with a group online. While each team member contributed roughly equally, and each succeeded in creating an RGM section which fit the assignment brief, the teamwork ethic was lost as each person worked on their section almost completely by themselves.
learning: To have a group of six working on a single project, it is extremely advantageous to foster a holistic and collaborative team evironment, where each member is responsible for not just their assigned task, but the outcome of the entire project. If I was to re-do this project in the same work environment, I would encourage much more conversation, where the team could brainstorm solutions for each person's RGM section, together. This would drastically improve the quality and reliability of each section as six brains are better than one when it comes to solving a problem. The overall cohesion of the final RGM would also improve as each person would have more information about the other sections of the RGM, thus allowing them to design their section to better integrate with those of other team members.

topic: Identifying the issue, problem, or paradox
situation: Improving the reliability of my RGM
task_action: I had to improve the reliability of my RGM's action from 70% to a higher amount. This was done cooperatively where as a group we brainstormed ideas for solutions to problems to our individual actions. My second action where I had an object(wood glue) swing on a string fail when it did not swing straight, i.e. in a curved fashion, or not at all. During my failure analysis, I identified the issue as the object having too many dimensions to move in as it could move forward and backwards which would cause the action to fail. To resolve this my team suggested I have the object swing against the wall to stop it from moving forwards and backwards.
result: Although this solution seems good, it resulted in lower overall reliability of 60%. This initially seems counterintuitive as the problem of swinging back was solved, however, a new problem was added and the initial true problem which was not identified still existed. The new problem was that the object now "bounced" off the wall thus causing more of the curved motion to fail more tests. After further failure analysis, I identified the problem to be the way in which I initiated the action wherein I pushed the object off a ledge to begin the swing. When pushing I would sometimes push to the side causing a curved motion and the bounce off the walls.
pfr: Although I initially felt that improving a 70% reliable action would be extremely easy, I was quickly proven wrong as the failure analysis I performed identified the wrong problem and a new problem arose when a solution was implemented a new problem arose. I feel that I had not taken the task seriously enough and was lax when identifying the problem thus wasting the time of my team members to solve a non-existent problem.
learning: By properly identifying the cause of a problem properly I can bring my team correct problems in which team time and resources can be better spent. My mistake resulted in later steps of our methodology in improving reliability to go down showcasing the statement "a chain is as strong as it's weakest link". In future the team could be more involved in the failure analysis to double-check the work of other members instead of relying on one member. This experience taught me how to identify the problem in our engineering designs and methods with an added appreciation of cooperation and team synergy.

topic: Initiative and the willingness to make decisions in the face of uncertainty
situation: During week 4 of the project, we started to work on our RGB design concept. During brains storming process of the project design, we were advised not to limit our imagination and let out creativity work at full and come up with as many ideas as possible no matter how unrealistic they could seem.
task_action: It was interesting to discuss a project with no limits in terms of design, however, the situation at this stage was uncertain. We didn’t know what kind of difficulties we can encounter in the future building RGB machine, and at that stage, it was already clear that our group has some credibility, attendance, and contribution issues. Aiming to avoid difficulties with deadlines I suggested choosing the simplest design so we could compensate if someone wasn't able to complete their task on time.
result: As a result, we came up with a simple solution that still complied with the project requirements and constraints. By now I can say that in a long run it was a very rational decision.
pfr: The decision to create the simplest design was based on my previous group project experience during ENGG1000. In a similar situation, our group overcomplicated the initial design by not thinking ahead. Short time, neglecting duties by some group members, and the amount of work due to project complexity put our project at risk of not being done on time. This time I didn’t want to be in the same situation. I was optimistic about our team’s capability and dedication at the beginning until it became clear that not everyone is willing to put effort into group work. Watching other’s group presentations, I was impressed by how complex and creative their RGB projects were. At this point, I started to doubt if we made the right decision. Inspired by others I thought maybe we should change direction and make our project more creative. But reality brought me back to the initial plan. I think there are no limits to what can be created as long as there is a strong team working together hard toward the aim. Being in a situation where half of the team is not enthusiastic about a project, I think the best choice was to keep it simple in order not to put extra work on the rest of tee team.
learning: I can’t say that I learned something new from this situation because I’ve already experienced it before, and what I’ve learned from the past contributed to the decision-making process this time. Besides personal traits that could draw a team back, there are always other commitments and unexpected situations that anyone can experience, so occasional team members’ absence or lack of participation should always be taken into account when working on a design and construction. It might be not applicable to a working place due to different conditions but in a situation where I have to work in a team with randomly chosen members for a short period of time, I would make it a rule for myself: start low and slow and add complexity if time allows, rather than start with something complicated and not be able to finish it on time because human factor has not been considered.

topic: I'm reflecting over the skill of adaptability when applying theoretical ideas in a practical setting.
situation: In this class, we had to design a physical process (Rube Goldberg Machine) over the virtual medium of Zoom, and were therefore unable to actually design it with exact physical considerations.
task_action: My team and I used Miro, Lucidchart and Zoom whiteboard to design the series of events for the RGM, however until we got together in person we were unable to accurately account for all physical factors. Once we did meet and attempted to construct the RGM, we were met with problems such as the ball bouncing too far off some events due to the solid wood tables we used for the foundation. To resolve issues such as these, we had to modify the elements on the fly, for instance, we replaced a mini basketball with a cricket ball to make it more weighted when the former wouldn't work, or when we adjusted the locations of the bumpers for the second event.
result: We managed to complete the construction and filming for the first 7 events in a single attempt, and the next 3 were done a week later, without too much adjustment to the actual plan and while achieving basically the same result. Being adaptable and using improvisational solutions allowed us to save time in the design process but meant that nothing was lost in the actual design.
pfr: Originally, the whole process of creating an RGM online without a physical design space seemed overwhelming and impossible. If we stayed fixated on the idea of 'perfection' despite being unable to work in it while planning, we would not have been able to make progress. These presentations specifically involved a member from each group to present on weekly based objectives infront of other groups and an assigned tutor. In a nutshell, the weekly presentations were not only focused on the group's visual aspects, but also examined the oral presentation.
task_action: Undergoing weekly presentations, for week's 7 presentation we were tasked with a team/group presentation consisting of 3 members from each group and restricted with the time constraint of 10 minutes per group. This presentation had to consist our group's complete detailed design and an in-depth discussion on how the individual scenes of our project led to a fulfilled Rube Goldberg Machine. As the name suggests, the task was to be completed through the use of several systematic diagrams to enable the audience to visually capture our group's RGM model. Consequently, through the use of 'Miro' and our schedule plan a week before the presentation submission, we allocated 3 members of our group to conduct the presentation for week 7. As a team we assigned and distributed the work evenly so that we could work at a fast pace and also have fair contribution towards the project itself. This was by the means of having 3 presenters to create the visual presentation and an oral script. Whilst, the rest of the team members were tasked to achieve the weekly objective which was to construct the detailed design of our RGM model.
result: The result of this situation was being able to present our group presentation and also meeting our weekly objective for week 7. In our viewpoint, we strongly believe that due to our presentations being commenced online, this gave us less room to engage and interact with the presentation overall. We are also of the opinion that a good presentation should be concise and should be focused on the topic. It should not move off-track. Essentially, this led up into the main context of the ‘effectiveness of oral presentations within remote learning’ and what makes the best use of the relationship between the presenter and the audience. We felt that it takes full consideration of the audience’s needs in order to capture their interest, develop their understanding from the early preface, inspire their confidence and achieve the presenter’s objectives. Subsequently, we learnt a lot about conducting effective presentations, such as, how to speak confidently in front of a small/large audience, control your voice projection, reflect on your body language and many more communication skills. As a group we had come to a similar ground of how face-to-face presentations can lead to a better and an effective presentation compared to online presentations. We also felt that 'Miro' was a great opportunity and addition to make working a lot more streamlined. We felt like communication was one of the largest setbacks as most of us were used to face to face communication with many thinking that less interaction with each other made the work harder. The presentations were difficult and in some cases hard to gauge facial expressions and emotions while presenting on Zoom.
pfr: My personal reflection towards the situation and the weekly objective was daunting because I perceive that in order to kickstart our project as a team, the initial stages of forming a better communication is through sharing one another thoughts and essentially getting to know each other's capability well. In conjunction, I personally think that although online work and preparation is more easily accessed within our group work environment, there are many flaws tied to the overarching topic of remote learning. With having to conduct weekly oral presentations online we are restricted to less room of engagement and interaction with the presentation, in particular the audience. I genuinely feel that the communication and addressing or delivering your messages is vital, however this was one of the largest setbacks as most of us are used to face-to-face communication with many thinking that less interaction with each other made the work harder to progress through. In reflection, conveying of oral presentations within online learning space was difficult and in some cases hard to gauge facial expressions and emotions while presenting on Zoom.
learning: My self introspection of the experience faced during the project development stages were to always remember you will have to let go and sacrifice your own opportunities to seek a total and an enhanced outcome. This experience of having a lack of interaction working remotely and in an online virtual space allows us to realise that conducting oral presentations online can be a difficult case for several people amongst us. This also enables us to recall possible downsides of online presentations, which are the disconnection between the presenter and audience, delays from technical issues, distraction from overwhelming presentations and last but not least lack of purpose. However, in order to break down possible barriers and to achieve an effective presentation we practiced and rehearsed speech from a transcript we as a team would develop prior to the presentation. Similarly, sitting within the audience's shoes when designing and creating visual/vocal aspects of the presentation also contributed to us gaining confidence and resilience. The main learning for us is that imagining how others might feel in any overwhelming situation is a great way to find the similarities that we ground and essentially overcome any difficulties we might have while presenting. Also, this allows an individual to account their previous experiences of the lockdown that we had faced a few years ago where we studied and worked remotely. This involved several instances of undergoing meetings and presentations online, which in many cases were negative due to the lack of communication and interactivity. environment. Furthermore, we also learn a lot about what the future may hold with many industries shifting towards remote working. Usually some sort of pulley system would be able to move from a low to high elevation but that's too common in my opinion. As effective and appealing that a pulley system may be I wanted a wow-factor to my actions in the RGM.
task_action: The easiest, unique thing I could think of to get the level change I needed was flying a drone. My brother has a drone which made it available to me and he would be able to fly it for one of my actions. But after reliability testing, although it actually was reliable enough to proceed with, it didn't look seamless and it would break up the flow of the RGM. This realisation made me have to come up with a new action and seamlessness and high tempo is a must in a RGM that retains the audience's attention and remains interesting.
result: Reliability testing occurs in week 9-10 which is towards the end of the semester. So one I decided to change the action even though I knew I would have less time to make a replacement action work. This is a clear example where being flexible and resourceful, as well as willing to persevere and have urgency comes into play, when almost 10 out of 12 weeks have gone by and pretty major changes need to be made for the benefit of the team. The replacement action has been decided – a long broom stick handle which will be held up straight, a toy car will roll and hit the broom stick which will then activate the next action on the wall. I'm using the height of the broom stick to gain the elevation onto the wall.
pfr: As the weeks went by and other university assignments began to pile on, being able to manage your time became so important. Times may get stressful but the main thing ENGG1050 has promoted and especially helped me is to be flexible and resourceful in the face of adversity, to persevere and have a sense of urgency and will to deliver.
learning: Perseverance, urgency and will to deliver, resourcefulness and flexibility – an important array of skills necessary to be a successful engineer. ENGG1050’s teachings allowed for me to learn these skills and begin to build upon them throughout the semester. Learning to persevere comes through failures and setbacks which I experienced in the construction of the RGM and I needed to have an urgency to deliver by being resourceful and flexible.

result: The result was a a seamless presentation that showed the journey to improved reliability in our RGM that was effectively orally presented such that positive feedback was given in response.

However, as I worked on the oral element of the presentation with help of group members, I found there was an effective balance to be had between images to show qualitative data and explanatory oral presentation which makes sense of the visual data provided on our presentation.
learning: By firstly collection the information from group members on what I wanted to present, brainstorming how I wanted the information to be processed by the audience and finally showing that through the visual presentation and creating a basis on which the oral presentation should cover, I found I was able to effectively communicate the information I wanted the convey to the audience.
