topic: I will be reflecting over the importance of accountability in a team operation.
situation: As ENGG1050 students, we were tasked with the creation of a Rube Goldberg Machine in which we had to develop a project plan, create a design, assess the risks, build, test and present. This task had us assigned into teams of 6 in which we had to individually display accountability in a team operation in order for the task to be completed sufficiently.
task_action: For the latter half of the unit in which we had to build, test and film the components, we have been having regular team meetings (every week) in which we discuss amongst ourselves the tasks that need to be completed that week and codify them into a shared platform (MIRO). In order to do this sufficiently it requires all team members to be present, participating and "pull their weight" when it comes to individual aspects of the project. As the components are built, filmed and tested individually in each team members own space, accountability within the team is of the utmost importance as each team member relies on one another to produce the work required in order to make the entire project flow. Personally, understanding the importance of this in a professional engineering group environment, I have made sure that I am 'pulling my weight' within the group whether that is showing up on time to the group meetings, taking down the minutes each week as I have been assigned to do and also building, testing and filming my component of the machine on time and with sufficient quality. I have seen this mindset and similar value in most group members within C6 however I have also experienced having a team member who does not possess this skill and constantly lets the team down by failing to produce what is needed from him each week, not contributing to group discussion and ultimately causing detriment to the quality of our work as a group.
result: As a result of holding accountability for myself in team scenario's I have ultimately fulfilled an intrinsic desire to be useful and helpful to my team, as well as made my team feel more confident knowing they can rely on me to complete a task to the best of my ability and within a designated time frame. In consequence to a group member not being accountable in team operation, the group has been disadvantaged in the latter half of the unit.
pfr: Working with new people as a team in ENGG1050 initially felt quite unnerving as I had no idea who my teammates were, and whether we would work well together in an engineering environment. These initial fears and doubts were ultimately put away as the project progressed, as I found that the team communicated well in our scheduled zoom meetings and tasks were completed with a great deal of confidence. Any doubts we had as a team in terms of the assembly of our individual components were quickly resolved with a formal discussion, making me feel self-assured in our ability as a group to complete the ultimate task assigned to us, and feel self-assured in my team mates in completing their individual sections and their accountability towards the group.
learning: From this experience in ENGG1050, I have learnt about the great significance of accountability in a team operation in relation to completing a project. I have learnt that if you 'pull your weight', which includes showing up to team meetings, contributing to discussion, adding value to relevant tasks and holding yourself accountable for any mishaps, it does the group a great deal of justice in completing the project with confidence and eliminates any unwanted doubts that a task won't get done or something won't be completed with the required quality. I have also learnt through a group member that doing the opposite, not holding yourself accountable in a team operation, places a great deal of stress on the other team members in relation to tasks getting completed and ultimately creates detriment on the efficiency of the team.

topic: This reflection will be on 'Accountability in a team's operation'. Specifically, this requires the team to follow through on its commitments, to finish projects. on time, and to meet goals/deadlines.
situation: We needed to establish a system that provoked team members who were unreliable/unprincipled, ensuring all team members maintained an equal workload and maintained high standards throughout the assignment of building an RGM machine.
task_action: The greater task at hand is to build an RGM machine within the 12-week deadline. However, in this matter, the task at hand is to ensure all team members put in an equal amount of effort and maintain a steady/equal workload without individual members slacking on their part. This needed to be done to ensure individual team members were not forced upon a heavy workload and to ensure marks were not dropped through attendance and unsatisfactory completion from some members. Subsequently, the action C12 took in order to tackle this potentially detrimental situation was to set up a multi-stage disciplinary system. This system included strikes in which a team member may have three strikes, each possessing a larger punishment. For example, if a team member were to miss one weekly meeting or scheduled class they would be issued with a warning. This warning remains between the group and is informal. However, if the offence is repeated, they may be issued with work required to be completed outside of the scheduled times or may have to do extra work in the following weeks. Lastly, if the offender has not taken any action on their mistakes they may be reported to the tutors, or handled with other punishment deemed suitable.
result: The results of this disciplinary program were deemed beneficial to the entire team. The program was successful at ensuring all team members participated in their duties equally and ensured all team members attended the meetings necessary. Through this program, C12 was able to complete all tasks and assignments to an above-satisfactory level and didn't need to rely on any unreliable group members. Each task was broken down equally and completed to a high level and was completed easily as it was distributed fairly.
pfr: Initially, the task at hand was daunting because as a group it seemed unfeasible and overwhelming to possibly become punished if meetings or tasks were missed. However, as we discussed the solution and practised it over the weeks, the thought of punishment became less of a scare and more of a motivation as it was a way to ensure ease of ability, practicality, and maintain a strong grade. The program motivated me to go to all group meetings and to complete my section of the tasks on time and to a high level as I didn't want to let the team down and I didn't want to become punished. Reflecting upon my experience with punishment, some group members missed one or two weekly meetings due to other commitments. The program ensured these members completed their side of the task in their own time, ensuring the rest of the team was not left in the dark. Overall, the program was very successful in my eyes and I will definitely be using it for group tasks in the foreseeable future.
learning: Approaching group tasks, specifically decision-making using the disciplinary program, group organisation was ensured and group decision-making processes were made less complex as each member was keen to contribute in their individual sections. This allowed work to be split up and done more quickly and in a simpler manner. As all members were in attendance at meetings due to being motivated by the program, the possible limitation of making group decisions was minimised. All members appreciated each other's contribution more and communication and organisation were maintained at a high level as everyone's attitude was kept high as the tasks were successfully completed to a high level.

During all workshops, even when I am not assigned as chairperson, I observe to see if any members are not participating in group discussions, and then I will ask them a question to encourage them to speak. result: After the very first workshop, I knew I was in a group with respectful members, as I felt included instantly, and I was treated equally. As a group we discovered that we all come from diverse backgrounds, and by learning about them, we had appreciation and respect for them. I have definitely noticed that by discussing rules and values, we have become closer as a group, and hence worked more efficiently. I also believe that by being in a multicultural group, we get the chance to learn about different cultures, which is very interesting and important, especially in the workforce. learning: During the workshops I have learned many things about myself and my group, specifically in terms of the way we all behave and act towards making our group inclusive and a good environment to learn. I have also learned about new cultures, beliefs and backgrounds, and how to respect them. I understand how treating others with fairness and respect can impact the efficiency and effectiveness of the team. I have found that no matter how different we all are from each other, in the end, my team members and I all have the same goal, which is to complete the Rube Goldberg Machine Project to the best of our abilities.

topic: Transferable skills/employability skill: Understanding needs and setting goals
situation: I needed to make my RGM action which included planning of materials, measuring and recording.
task_action: I took action in this situation by creating a timetable with specific goals. This meant that I'd do a portion of my RGM action today and finish the rest later if I didn't have time. This ensured that, rather than doing all of the material planning and attempting to execute the final video all at once, I was able to do each part slowly, which I was confident would make the process easier and more manageable.
result: As a result, choosing precise measurements of materials such as cardboard length and height allowed me to complete my action quickly. Other factors influencing this process included adjusting the weight of the ball aswell. As a result of all of these precise measurements and timing, I was able to complete my RGM action with ease.
pfr: The first task was difficult because I had not been able to properly set goals due to bad habits that caused me to procrastinate. For example, when I planned to complete my RGM action for tomorrow. I was stuck in the routine of not doing it the next day. However, because I had a clear goal of what actions I would take, the process became less complicated because I knew when I would do them.
learning: By approaching the skill of understanding needs and setting goals, I discovered that it is important not only in my situation, but in all other situations. Understanding needs and setting goals taught me that things should not be done at the last minute, which means they must have a clear goal of what is going to happen through extensive planning if they want to succeed.

topic: The Transferable skills/employability skills I will will be reflecting over are, roles and responsibilities of engineers and creating new solution concepts.
situation: During week 8 me and my team C12 are tasked to conduct a RGM reliability assessment, in which to determine the potential errors in the whole system and ensure improvements are made to certain events within the RGM.
task_action: Throughout our weekly meetings, each team member have listed the 2 events in which they will be constructing for the entirety of the RGM and performed experiments to the 2 events to determine the overall reliability of the events. The amount of trials conducted is directly proportional to the level of difficulty of the events so we can determine if an alternative option is needed to increase the reliability percentage.
result: The results after the individual experiments are then finalized and shown in our weekly team meetings, as we discuss if an alternative option is needed for a specific event in our RGM in order to increase the reliability percentage. As a team we have determined all events that have a percentage below 70% should have an alternative option to increase the reliability percentage.
pfr: Throughout week 8's task I have learnt many skills such as the roles and responsibility of engineers and creating new solution concepts. The roles and responsibilitiy of engineers has taught me management skills as I had to ensure that all members in the team are completing their required tasks such as conducting experiments for their RGM events. I have also gained knowledge in the roles of engineers through continuous problem solving and discussion with my fellow team members. Another skill I have also learnt is creating new solution concepts, I have acquired this skill through the continuous brainstorming with my fellow team members about the specific RGM events that have a reliability percentage below 70% and how we can find the best and most efficient solution to ensure our RGM operates in a smooth and efficient manner.
learning: This task have allowed me to understand the roles and responsibility of engineers is to listen to every form of idea from each team member and as a team communicate together which is the best solution. These skills have also taught me to be welcoming of creating new solution concepts and allow different individuals in the team to come up with creative solutions to meet the required need of our RGM system. Through this experience, I have learnt two different skills that I will carry further in my career and learning.

situation: During the second half of the semester of ENGG1050, we have been tasked with developing and refining our individual components for the groups Rube Goldberg Machine. We utilised previous work to ensure timelines for our deliverables and used communication skills to compromise and find the best solutions to all our skills. There was the additional impacts on this portion of testing and validating our own work as workloads and requirements continually changed to chase reliability targets.
task_action: The Task was to create, by designing initial events, then refining, 2 events for a Rube Goldberg Machine which had to last at least 3 seconds in length. We created our first drafts independently and aligned with our Gantt chart to ensure we had enough time to draft and then present them for the next weeks presentation. We presented our drafts within the team and looked critically at our own and others to find possible flaws or errors in assumptions that led us to our draft designs. With these conversations we developed a better understanding of what we were targeting for designs and the metrics we’d use to measure how successful we were in them. This led us to complete our final design which in some cases were significantly closer to reality than others, this allowed us to take insight into how others constructed and pieced together their respective systems to trigger key events within the Rube Goldberg Machine.
result: We were mostly successful in achieving our overall goals. A majority of us were able to create and draft events similar to the final product that was delivered.
pfr: Throughout our work in designing and refining it was more of an eye-opening journey by way of cutting out work you feel may be incredibly cool or well thought out but just simply doesn’t provide reliable tests or work well within the grander scheme of the RGM. This is a bit of a harsh reality but it helps me to look at the picture a bit more clinically, detaching my own personal view of my part and looking at the greater design project; if a component doesn’t work, or isn’t needed, we must simplify or remove it to ensure the overall project achieves a successful outcome. This is something I feel will come up a lot in the workplace, so dealing with the emotions at a low level in University will set me up to manage them as an employee later on.
learning: It’s been a major bit of learning my limits to be attached to my work, but to also work through and develop a refined problem solving mindset. While this will surely grow and develop more as I enter the workforce and encounter more varied issues that require even more varied skillsets, I am of the view that this exercise has also worked these mental muscles. Being an engineer means admitting when a solution simply doesn’t meet the requirements, or doesn’t pass the tests, and its a harsh reality but one we must all confront, by doing so now I can feel more confident in being able to manage my emotional response to it in future.

topic: The topic I have chosen to reflect on is 'The design process phasing and approaches'. My group B15 has to design an RGM project. topic: I will be reflecting on transferable skills such as taking accountability in a team operation and communications structure as our team learned to face challenges and develop these skills.
situation: We needed to create our prototypes and conduct reliability tests for each component we were responsible for, in the Rube Goldberg machine project.
task_action: Initially, the week we had to conduct our reliability tests, 4 out of 6 members of our group was absent. We had to develop proper communication skills to discuss matters outside of designated class time. I coordinated methods for the group to upload pictures of the components, and encouraged everyone to upload videos of their components to our discord channel for videos and updates so the group can be up to date with each event. As a result of this, by our second reliability test we had a couple of pictures of prototypes from a few members. Furthermore, I had developed the skill of taking accountability in a team setting and informed and updated my group in the group chat on the development of my RGM events. Unfortunately, I neglected to take initiative and ask each member for their own contribution, pictures or updates to the event. Many others seemed to be hesitant to ask questions or suggestions to improve events or even asking updates from other members, which slowed the progress of our team down.
result: Members that could not attend or did not have components ready by the weekly meeting, were advised by myself and Shirsho to upload videos and photos in their own time onto the discord group chat. We didn’t have many updates from each member for the RGM events, besides their discussion of what they had tested. We encouraged photos but only half of our team provided photos, the other half hadn’t.
pfr: The task felt discouraging at first without all our members to contribute and update, especially after the break. After creating the group chat channel to update videos and pictures for components, I felt more hopeful for others to contribute their part. I believe our group finds it difficult to hold one another accountable and call them out when they are behind on group work, as I personally found it hard to hold other people accountable out of fear that I may hurt their feelings. After reflecting on this, I concluded that I shouldn’t worry about hurting their emotions because that is not my intention and this RGM project is here to help us work better as a team. I realised holding people accountable allows the group to progress forward, it would benefit all of us since we are all working towards the same goal.
learning: I had to learned to recognise where communication is lacking within our group. As a result, in the future I will take accountability for my own tasks and hold other team members accountable for their own part. I would also offer help and recommendations in case they are having difficulty executing certain RGB events. Nevertheless, we still found success after we identified the lack of communication and response from other group members and created a group chat so that we are regularly updated on these components during the week. I learnt the importance of communication as each members event relied on the next person’s event. In the future I will ensure there are group-chats for a team to update all members. I will contribute more often than once weekly to update all my team members for progress and ask for guidance.

topic: Being a first year student, I believe an appropriate transferable skill to reflect on is 'Time and Resource management'.
situation: During this semester I have had difficulty with appropriately managing my time. Specifically, in regards to balancing my part-time work with studying. At the beginning of the semester I was disorganised and working 35-40 hours a week. This caused me quite a bit of stress, which is reflected in my grades.
task_action: I re-evaluated my priorities and reflected on how I could realistically manage my time and resources (e.g. money). To do this I drew up a study plan which included a weekly checklist of the most important tasks for each of my five subjects. I also used a calendar board to visually display all due dates as well as when I should begin tasks, such as, assignments. To help me manage my resources I created a budget accounting for my major spending points, how I could reduce them and thereby how many hours I really need to work each week. Finally, I spoke to my manager to request less hours so I could focus on university.
result: The result has been effective to varying degrees of success. The visual calendar has successfully helped me submit assignments and prepare for tests. Additionally, the calendar helps me manage my time in all areas of my life, not just university related. However, less successfully is the amount of hours I work. My current place of work is very short on staff and as a result employees are pressured to work more hours. This is still an aspect of my time management that I am still attempting to improve.
pfr: During this semester I have felt very stressed, feeling as though I don't have enough time to keep pace with my university workload, part-time work, nor to do other activities that I enjoy and value. However, as I began to identify my most important time requirements and financial necessities, it became easier to manage and spend my time and money on the most important and urgent tasks. I feel that my weekly checklist effectively helped me keep track of and complete smaller tasks. Similarly, I feel that my calendar was vital in monitoring my overall progress and performance in regards to university.
learning: When reflecting on what I have learnt about time and resource management I now better understand the importance of being organised from the beginning of the semester and not falling behind. I have recently spoken to my manager and told them my hours needed to be reduced or I would have to find another place to work. Following this my hours have been reduced. This experience has taught me the importance of valuing my time and standing my ground when it comes to other people wanting too much of my time, such is the case with my part-time work.

learning: through reflecting on my personal growth in this unit from the multiple transferable skills I have developed and enhanced I have significantly boosted my confidence in all aspects of my professional behaviour and mindset. topic: TRANSFERABLE SKILL: How to manage deadlines in a group setting.
situation: Throughout this unit, we have faced numerous team deadlines, but one of the key ones was when we set our own deadline for individual component videos so that there was adequate time to edit and make adjustments if necessary.
task_action: With the overall unit task of building an RGM project approaching its own deadline, we decided, in a democratic manner, to complete our two individual components within five days of our last workshop. This was due to needing to edit as well as multiple other assessments for other units taking place the week after, and, thus, would relieve some of the pressure by getting it over and done with. To maintain the timeframe we had allocated I had to follow up directly with two members who showed no progress two days before it was required to be finished. This involved providing quick check-ins as there was still time. However, this evolved into more direct requests when one team member still had not uploaded anything. I had to use logical reasoning such as "the group depends on this as it will all affect our marks", to which they eventually uploaded their part before the deadline.
result: By taking this course of action we were able to meet the deadline and the editing process is underway with time for further improvements now that the video stage is out of the way.
pfr: While at first, the deadline appeared manageable for everyone - as it was voted for by the group - it quickly became evident some members had other personal commitments or were unable to video for other reasons. situation: I WAS LOOKING OVER THE EVENTS THAT WERE ASSIGNED TO ME FOR MY GROUP’S RGM AND I WAS TRYING TO BRAINSTORM DIFFERENT WAYS I COULD INCREASE THE RELIABILITY OF MY COMPONENTS.
task_action: To give some context about my events, I will describe them. In the last inclined plane from the previous event, a ping pong ball goes down the ramp from event 5 and it knocks over some coffee beans, into an empty cup connecting to another pulley system. Once the empty cup is filled with coffee beans, it weighs down a string and lifts a glass bottle on the other end of the pulley system. The end of the popsicle bomb has a few sticks that, if released, blow up the entire bomb. These sticks were stabilised by the glass bottle that was lifted off by the pulley system. At first, the only change that came to mind was that the cup was too unstable and did not have a wide enough surface area to catch the coffee beans so, the cup was replaced with an open drawstring bag, which had a wider opening, and would potentially the coffee beans better. However, when I tried to actually implement my events, I realised there were many flaws in the design. It was extremely difficult to get all the loose beans into the drawstring bag, and the glass bottle was not heavy/sturdy enough to keep the popsicle stick bomb in place without prematurely exploding. The ping pong ball was also too light to hit the coffee bag. Fortunately, by using my creativity and problem-solving skills, I was able to make use of other materials that were available around me to solve each and every problem I was facing and end the day with my final video.
result: I broke down the problems I was facing and tried to solve them one at a time. The first issue was the drawstring bag being too light, causing it to move about a lot from the position that would be ideal to catch the coffee beans. I looked around the Ada Lovelace room at 4RPD, and found a MQ goodie bag in the cupboard, which was way more stable and stayed in place. The coffee beans would spill everywhere, so to improve the repeatability and a higher chance of success, I decided to drop a bag of coffee rather than individual coffee beans. At times, the coffee bag would slide sideways down the cardboard ramp. To stabilise that, I taped a long wooden stick under the ramp, making it a lot more sturdy. I grabbed a big box from the cupboard and put it under the ramp, stabilising it further. The other issue was the glass bottle not being heavy enough, so I decided to fill it up with water. Those adjustments solved all the issues I was having with the design.
pfr: INITIALLY, I FELT FRUSTRATED AND WORRIED THAT I WOULD NOT BE ABLE TO FINISH MY FILMING ON TIME. THAT WAS MY ONLY DAY OFF, AND I HAD MANY OTHER ASSIGNMENTS DUE DURING THAT TIME. I ALSO HAD WORK THE NEXT 2 DAYS. HOWEVER, AFTER SOLVING THE ISSUES, I FELT RELIEVED, AND ALSO MORE CONFIDENT IN MY CREATIVITY AND PROBLEM-SOLVING SKILLS.
learning: I always thought I was not good at designing things physically and was better at maths/coding. I did not think I would have been able to come up with solutions on the spot, using the things available around me. I was able to make a pulley system by using everyday materials. The pulley system is made of carabiners hooked onto 2 long wooden sticks, & a rope is sliding through the carabiners. The 2 big sticks are on moving whiteboards found at 4RPD. The process of making our Rube Goldberg Machine helped me realise that I also do have the ability to problem solve and be creative, even in scenarios I am not familiar with.

topic:
SKILL/SUBJECT REFLECTED ON: 

Resource management, understanding needs and setting goals.
situation: Throughout the duration of our mid-semester break, we were tasked with building and testing the Rube Goldberg Machine components that each of us were responsible for designing.
task_action: The task is for each individual member of our group to build the Rube Goldberg machine components consisting of 2 action events, with each action event lasting a minimum of 3 seconds and that our components must be modularized, where the ending of each action event would be a transition from one group member’s video to the other member’s. It’s important that each member supply their own material and keep sustainability in mind, where the resources that are used are recyclable or items that we already have in our possession.
result: After finding out ways to use the resources that were readily available to me more efficiently and effectively, I was able to not only create my RGM components but I was also able to make sure that the action events for each RGM component lasted for at least 3 seconds and that the beginning of the action event I was responsible for would transition from one of my group member’s video and that the ending of my action event would transition to another member’s RGM component. The first action event created was for a marble to go down a pipe and the second action event would be triggered by that same marble, where the marble initiated a domino effect where multiple CD boxes would topple over each other and the last CD box would trigger another marble to fall down which would transition to another rube Goldberg machine component created by another team member.
pfr: Personally, I’ve never created a mechanical device so the idea of creating something called a Rube Goldberg machine seemed very daunting to me. Even in high school, I’ve had very limited experience with experiments, where I haven’t even done something as basic as a carbonated soda volcano. So, from the start I felt like I had a weakness in terms of my inexperience with practical work. It was also initially a detriment to me where I kept trying to think of very sophisticated ideas in order to make sure that the action events lasted the bare minimum of 3 seconds, which probably would’ve required resources that wouldn’t have been available to me and skills that I hadn’t really developed. Upon further reflection, I realized that as long as I met the requirements of the project, using simple methods and adjusting the way that I use my resources for this specific case would be the best idea.
learning: When building and testing my Rube Goldberg Machine components I learnt that for someone who’s inexperienced with practical work as I am the simple ideas are the best and that there is no need to overly complicate matters. For instance, when I was trying to make the length of first action event longer, I was thinking of using different contraptions and machinations such as a pulley system along with my initial idea of a marble going down a pipe to make the action event longer. Upon reflection I realized that I just need to make it within the requirement of lasting 3 seconds, there was no benefit to intentionally making the event even longer than that, so I decided to simply increase the length of the pipe that I used to make sure the action event lasted the minimum of 3 minutes. I also had an initial reliability issue of where the CD boxes would fall on their own and were not stable enough to stand by themselves. Instead of replacing the boxes, I simply opened them slightly, which gave them a larger base, which in turn gave them more stability to stand up by themselves. By simply adjusting the way that I am using my resource, I conserved materials and increased the overall resource efficiency of the project. These actions have allowed me to understand the needs and requirements of my project and by simply adjusting the way I use my resources I can meet the goals that I have set for myself using effective resource management.

situation: We were given instructions on how to build a simple toolbox out of metal supplied by the workshop. We will be given 7 lessons each are 3 hours long with the help of instructors and demonstrators if necessary. Extra time can be booked via email sent to our inboxes.
task_action: We began the toolbox by measuring out the parts shown on the instructions (depicted in mm). After measuring out each part using a ruler we proceeded to cut out the metal parts we measured so we would end up with 2 side panels, 2 front panels and a bottom panel. We would then file the cut metal to make it so that the edges aren't sharp and dangerous. I then bent the metal according to the instructions by measuring a line of where it needs to be bent and bending it by 90 degrees using the clamp. After all the metal pieces are bent properly I then weld them together into the shape of a toolbox. I then measure and cut out the handle with a hollow metal pole. I had to cut out 2 short pieces of solid metal poles to drill and 4mm hole into and cut out the inside so a screw can fit inside. the 2 solid pieces are fit into each end of the hollow pole and then the handle was screwed onto the side panels of the completed toolbox. The final process was to sand blast the toolbox to remove any rust that has built up over the past few weeks and paint the toolbox black which was optional.
result: The final result which was our completed tool box was then evaluated by the instructor along with how we abided to the rules of the workshop, ensuring both our safety and other, and our overall efficiency during the whole process. We were each given individual marks out of 90 based on our performance.
pfr: It was exciting to learn new skills in the workshop, being able to use the different machinery and working with metal for the first time. pfr: I realised that my approach in solving my problems depended heavily on my attitude towards what I wanted from myself. I have always been a perfectionist, and while this attitude has summoned some of my greatest works, it undeniably caused myself a lot of frustration and anger because I often struggle to start a piece of work until the last moment out of a fear of creating something lackluster. This time, I actively reminded myself that it was human not to be perfect, and since I am a human, its okay to not be great. I can just show up. That's what I did, I showed up to do something and that something was something okay.
learning: How I think about my idea of 'success' shape my efforts in attaining said success. When I allow myself to just be enough, not great, just enough, I often perform quite well. This attitude to thinking and learning is new, so I must give myself reminders when dealing with the future. While I may not create a great piece of work now, I am happier without the added stress, anxiety, and frustration of trying to be perfect. And this is healthier and more sustainable for a student that has to keep learning after university and during my lifetime.

situation: In my software engineering class we had to form groups for a competition in which we had to use our interpersonal skills of teamwork and communication to successfully brainstorm how we would create two programs that users could interact with.
task_action: Through the use of brainstorming and clear communication between group members, we were able to form two group pairs spreading out skill equally to keep quality of the software high and consistent. We were randomly assigned the topic of skateboard, spiralling and boxer with the goal of creating two programs that would involve a skateboard spiralling and the other involving the boxer. To create the programs effectively and efficiently, consistent and clear verbal and written communication and teamwork was used in the development stages of the programs to eventually deliver the end product.
result: The end result was two well-built programs that did what was intended. This was due to the use of interpersonal skills such as teamwork and communication which made the development process and flow of ideas for the program successful.
pfr: Initially, working as a team and communicating effectively was a difficult task as team members were all unfamiliar with each other and slightly nervous to begin with. As time went on, we got to know each other more and became comfortable with our group. This allowed for us to take on the challenge of creating two programs as a team through the use of our interpersonal skills, most notably our teamwork and communication skills.
learning: Through this learning experience of working on a team project, we were able to develop our communication and teamwork skills. As a result of this experience, I have learnt to appreciate the importance of using effective communication and teamwork skills within a group to achieve a common end goal. This is because without solid teamwork and communication skills, the team is doomed to fail and that is why I now realise its importance for future projects.

situation: I had to finish a game variant of rock paper scissors with two extra signs as well as a detailed project report full with an implementation plan and testing plan for each of the modules as well as according to a very specific set of criteria within a limited time span.
task_action: This project was a very large in size and had a lot of distinct stages;each with emphasis on different kinds of work; and needed to be done in a particular order in order to ensure that each stage got the most efficient amount of time as possible for it so that no stage had too much or too little emphasis on it. Due to this being a large amount of work that had complex stages and steps - In order to most efficiently manage my time I had to break the task up into smaller milestones; each with deadlines that lead up to each other and have the deadlines setup in stages. In order to effectively adhere to these stages - I learned how to utilize tools like the gantt chart and the kanban board to have mindfulness and direction towards the specific tasks that needed to be done in order to effectively ration my focus to make sure that one thing at a time was accomplished properly instead of falling into the multi tasking trap. I created the stages of "Create implementation plan","Create Testing Plan", "Execute implementation plan", "Execute testing plan" and had a kanban board full of tasks for each of the stages i.e define system functionality, create system flowchart, define function functionality etc. Through adhering to these tools; I was able to enter a flow state whenever I worked where I had one big task that I focused on entirely - a task that was recorded on my kanban board for a specific phase - a phase that was recorded on my gantt chart for a specific time.
result: The outcome of me breaking up my long term goal into phases and rationing my focus using planning tools was that I ended up finishing my project well on time and to a very high degree of quality in my personal opinion.
pfr: The initial task seemed quite danting and tedious - as there were alot of unknowns regading how things would end up being done that significantly interfered wiht my ability to plan for them. However; through spending time specifically on brainstorming ways to deal with the most obvious unknowns; I was able to get very concise on how much time I should spend on any particular stage.
learning: I feel that while elements of this task may have been tedious; the principles that I used in order to achieve this task on time could definitely be used again in the future to achieve tasks. The simple act of taking a long term goal; identifying stages and monastically focusing on tasks while aiming to fulfill a stage - after which the goal is to fulfill the next stage until the task is complete - is very universal amongst long term goals of all types. In the future - I believe that focusing further on fully breaking down all of the stages and tasks and calibrating could have a very high return in time investment.

situation: Being presented with the large load of content to learn in the Technical Drawing workshop.
task_action: Breaking down the fundamentals of each drawing style and their requirements prior to any attempt to ensure I understood their purpose and distinctive qualities allowed me to form my own understanding of the content with every session, before having ample opportunity to practise the process itself.
result: The result was incrementally furthering my skillset with every piece completed, and feeling more capable and confident with my abilities.
pfr: Initially the workload seemed overwhelming, having completed an engineering class throughout my senior years of high school, I chose the workshop as I knew Technical Drawing wasn't one of my strengths, having had a very shallow understanding of dimensioning and AS1100 standards beforehand, once we really got into the depths of the content, my prior experience made my time significantly easier, I was able to reconsider and reconstruct my experiences as not a shortcoming but as practise.
learning: I came to appreciate my prior learning experiences regardless of how lacklustre they may have seemed in the moment; hopefully moving forward I can continue to embrace and build upon my past endeavours, regardless of how insignificant they may seem.

situation: Our software development class in year 12 was split up into groups and given a task, we needed to create a game for our HSC assignment.
task_action: Firstly, we began a brainstorming session to decide what we were going to make. We took many factors into account such as difficulty to program, time to program, and adherence to criteria. Eventually we decided to make a solo Blackjack game, which seemed like our best option and reasonable to make within the time constraint. Once we chose the game we were going to make, we devised a plan for the program which had four components. The four people in our group was assigned one of the four components to make, each of which were relatively equal in difficulty and time to program. We chose the component that each of us were responsible to program by declaring our weaknesses and strength’s and choosing based on these abilities and lack thereof.
result: The result of this group plan was being able to make a sufficient Blackjack game within the given time constraint. Our group assignment was given a 91%.
pfr: The assignment was overwhelming due to the freedom we were given. We had little to no restrictions, but were expected to create a complex program that felt playable to all users. Furthermore, the time constraints we had was around 2 months long, but with it came an expectation that our game would be of the highest quality. The decision process was lengthy and many in our group had strong opinions about what we should make although the majority of us decided it would not be wise. Eventually we all came to an agreement about the game we should make, as Blackjack most closely met our criteria. Once we agreed on blackjack, we declared that no programming will be done until we establish a plan and expected due dates for the components of the program to be completed. The planning of the program required all of us to state our programming abilities, and to be completely honest with ourselves and each-other. Once the plan was established, we individually went to work, whilst keeping each other updated and holding meetings for all of us to state what we are currently doing. Eventually we all finished the components we were assigned and were happy to put the complete program together.
learning: This was the biggest group project that anyone of us had ever been apart of, therefore we all treated it seriously and with great respect. The whole process was planned out prior to any attempts, and during the programming we were all kept updated by each other as to where we were all currently working. This extremely organised and planned method was a unique experience to me at the time. It is extremely effective for complex and large assignments, as it keeps all members of the group accountable to what they should be doing and when it should be completed, and it reduces errors as the planning prior to programming makes the objective clearer for each of us. Through this experience, I have built an appreciation for formal planning whenever executing a group task.

situation: Multiple Arduino Tasks due for marking in week 7
task_action: After an individual brainstorming session I worked out the parameters of the problem being the marks allocated to a task and completability of Arduino tasks due for final review in week 7. I set out to find which Arduino tasks were most easily completable by my understanding of code and the requirements of the tasks. Then considered that end of week tasks reward the most marks and the final task rewards the highest amount as its the hardest task. Evaluating each remaining task based on (difficulty and mark allocation).
result: I had an actionable prioritization of tasks and knew which to focus on to properly score high grades in my class.
pfr: Initially figuring out how to effectively prioritise and focus on my required tasks was overwhelming as I didn't know how to tackle the problem or a method of sorting tasks. Once I brainstormed and worked out which parameters I could use to justify the prioritisation of tasks. It was allot clearer on which tasks should require prioritisation and focus to in order to efficiently achieve the highest mark within parameters for my course and time.
learning: The approach of utilising important parameters as a method of prioritisation and taking time to brainstorm my issue allowed me to gain a clear understanding of the issue. Allowing me to effectively prioritise and focus on the Arduino tasks due. Due to my experience on this problem, I've learnt that structure when problem solving through finding parameters, limitations and criteria can heavily aid in decision making and problem solving. This allows for a seemingly overwhelmingly problem to be tackled and faced with simple and understandable criteria.

situation: To brainstorm and design a tool box out of sheet metal that can hold tools without collapsing.
task_action: Brainstorming and design within small group; the key is excellent communication so using mind maps and visual communication is essential. This allows us as engineers to visualise our ideas and further have a greater understanding in the design. We each contributed our own ideas in order to choose the most fitting and functional design for the tool box.
result: The result was selecting a design that included the best of our ideas. These ideas were blended together to make a tool box that is most beneficial to the user. Then the design was further developed using prototypes and then the team was able to construct the tool box.
pfr: Coming into this task it was shaky as I was not fond of the people I was surrounded with. Once getting to know the others and where they were from we were able to move on and I felt much more comfortable knowing that everyone was in the same position with the same goal. I found that when we communicated properly using visual and interpersonal communication we were able to come up with the best product possible.
learning: I have learnt that through communication and teamwork we are almost always able to produce something greater than an individual. This is due to multiple ideas from different people coming into play to benefit the situation/design brief. The experience of working as a team will benefit me greatly as I move on to become an experienced engineer as it will allow me to communicate and use teamwork to create great innovations that positively impact many different people around the work.

situation: Needed to create and deliver a presentation on an emerging technology.
task_action: Brainstormed and researched different emerging technologies until deciding to make a presentation on sonic fire extinguishers. Then two weeks were spent researching the emerging technology of sonic fire extinguishers the information was compiled into concise dot points in a PowerPoint presentation.
result: The result was being able to deliver an oral presentation on sonic fire extinguishers with an in-depth understanding of how it functions as well as the pros and cons of the technology.
pfr: As the task was open ended and students were able to present on any emerging technology they wanted it was difficult to pick one technology alone as well as find substantial information on the topic as it was not well researched and documented. However, after making a list of possible technologies to present the sonic fire extinguisher was chosen as there was enough information for an in-depth explanation of its functionality and the advantages and disadvantages of using it. Although the presentation was well researched, presenting orally was very difficult due to nervousness leading to forgetting the words I had previously memorised.
learning: Despite how well researched the presentation was, it was not reflected in my oral presentation as I forgot it all in the moment I was at the front of the class. From this experience I have learnt not to purely memorise information from a script but to instead learn and understand it so that I could freely speak on the topic without having to refer to a script. It has also pushed me to be more confident in my presenting and changed the way I approach oral presentations where instead of being nervous because I could not remember the words, I would have a scaffold I would follow with an introduction and some dot points I would like to talk about where I can further elaborate on my own terms. This more flexible method of presenting has made me feel more comfortable as I can speak freely from the information I learnt rather than follow what I previously wrote down which is a lot harder to memorise.

situation: We needed to identify and make slight changes to the cut angle of the folds present on the side pieces. This was in order to aid in the overall cohesion and fit of the tool box components.
task_action: By forming a small group, we worked together to identify and interoperate provided diagrams, whilst brainstorming easy and time efficient solutions. Through brainstorming and discussions, we were able to collectively agree on a viable solution for the side pieces.
result: The result was increasing the angle of the cut, which in turn kept it out of the way of other pieces which ultimately aided in a better fit between all toolbox components.
pfr: The initial task was quite intimidating as the problem was identified mid way through our allocated time which in turn added an element of time pressure when devising a solution to the problem. Once we, as a group actually sat down and really discussed and look at different ways of interoperating the provided drawings and diagrams, we were able to come up with an easy and time efficient way of overcoming the issue.
learning: By approaching issues as a group, we were able to speed up the decision making process whilst also having multiple different perspectives. This allowed us to account for all solutions and ideas without bias. The process of choosing the suitable design was entirely based on the limitations requirements, We were tasked with creating the best toolbox possible within the time constraints and as a group we made a relevant decision to better our toolbox under all limitations.

situation: I needed to draw objects and shapes provided with several different methods such as single-point perspective, oblique view, isometric view, multi-view and sectioning on a drawing board table.
task_action: The approach to some drawing methods was difficult to grasp, especially when the object of focus is composed of a variety of shapes and sizes. For example, drawing a circle in an isometric view. I thought that it would be best to get used to the methods through the countless failures and to take it slowly regardless of being able to finish the allocated task in class(which could be otherwise done at home).
result: The result was that I gained valuable experience with the different methods of technical drawing which boosted my understanding of more complex shapes.
pfr: At first I thought that the technical drawing classes would be simple and easy-going with the three hours of in-class time. This was definitely a miscalculation as I find myself not being able to achieve replicate a nicely scaled, clear, and accurate drawing on the object. I couldn't wrap my head around some of the methods of drawing in complicated shapes which led to many failed drafts and not enough time to complete the allocated tasks of the lesson. So I prioritised my time and effort at understanding and getting used to the complicated shapes in different views (e.g. isometric view) and being at to reflect it on paper.
learning: Prioritising my time on understanding and getting used to the complicated shapes in different views was definitely my best choice. It would have been a waste of an experience to half-ass the tasks and I really enjoyed the process. I learned that the mindset of 'just' getting things done is not the way to approach tasks, and openly reflecting and refining your failed attempts and the skills required for the task is much better

situation: We had a group project in high school in which we had to make a presentation and use the limited resources given to us to create a pop up project of the solar system. We had one week to complete it and were in a group of 2. However, I had been very sick/ill that week and my partner wasn’t that enthusiastic or motivated to complete or do the project, however he did say that he will design the pop-up art of the solar system. Long story short even though I was sick and didn’t attend school for that whole week I had done some of the work at home on the information of each planet and the solar system that was going to be included on the pop-up art. However, on the day of the presentation the partner I had been with had done nothing. Luckily for us we were the last to present and the teacher had given us some paper, colours and other equipment to quickly formulate our project, although we had little to 50 minutes to get it done and present it.
task_action: We had to be quick and intelligent with our decisions as we had short amount of time on our hands. We had split the task into two sections, my partner worked on the design of the pop up art and myself worked on finishing up on the information of the pop-up art. However, we realised we needed to work on the project (pop-up art) itself as without it we wouldn’t be able to present a project at all. I made a vital decision to help to make the pop-up art as it took longer than expected. The materials the teacher had given us weren’t the best but we had to make do with it. Once we finished the design of the project my partner and I quickly copied down the information I had gathered online on the pop-up art, we had around five minutes to do this, and there was a lot of information to copy down. Somehow, we had completed the entire project just under 50 minutes due to strategic planning and working hard.
result: The result was being able to complete the project under time restriction and limited resources having to strategically resource management. Even more surprisingly was how well we worked together due to this adversity, it gave us even more of a reason to complete the project and to do better and that showed in the results/feedback that were given to us a few weeks later in which our project had the second highest mark in the class.
pfr: The task was very daunting as my partner and I had practically done very little work on the project, due to perhaps lack of motivation and lack of communication. However, due to the time pressure and lack of materials something within our brains switched and we were both in full focus mode to complete the project and not fail. Due to strategic thinking and fully focusing on the task at hand we managed to complete the project just in time for presentation. This somehow felt more fulfilling and rewarding to me as I felt like due to the adversity given to us at hand, the completion of the task gave me a dopamine boost or something of that sought.
learning: By approaching this task differently than the other groups due to the limited time and having to resource management it gave me a more profound and clear understanding of the saying, ‘Don’t leave things to the last minute’ or ‘Do the hard work especially when you don’t feel like it’. This is because by delaying instant gratification and getting the work done earlier my partner and I wouldn’t have even been in the situation that we were in. So perhaps even though I was sick and my partner was lacking motivation, if we had just pushed through and looked at the bigger picture we could have saved a lot of time and done other productive things with that time instead of indulging in instant gratification. Through this experience I have come to appreciation of how valuable time is and even concluded that in my opinion ‘time’ is the most valuable thing a person can have and with the right resources and managing resources, a person can achieve anything on this earth.

situation: We were given the task to construct a tool box made from either steel or aluminium whilst having limited knowledge on the machinery we needed to use.
task_action: Thus, we had to research the functionality of each machine needed to give us insight on how we were going to construct our toolbox. Through the research we communicated with each other to gain a better understanding on how we were going to start the construction. During our collaboration we evaluated the most appropriate machinery to use and helped each other use the machines.
result: The result was that we were able to construct a tool box using teamwork and communication with each other. It also resulted in time efficiency and accuracy as our tool box were constructed faster and more accurate due to us providing help to each other.
pfr: The initial task was intimidating because some of us had limited knowledge on the machinery needed to construct the toolbox. However, once the construction began it became less intimidating as we were able to communicate and work with each other to achieve our result. The people with more knowledge of machinery were able to provide assistance to the people with less knowledge. Thus, the outcome became less intimidating as we all had similar outcomes due to the help we gave each other during the construction process.
learning: Through our research and experience with machinery we were able to provide each other with assistance in our construction. This allowed us to gain new knowledge on the different machinery we had to use. The experience of the machinery also allowed us to determine that multiple machines will help us achieve the same result, thus using different machines will not have a drastic impact on our outcome and everyone should have a similar design that will fulfil the same purpose. Through this, experience, I have come to the conclusion that teamwork and communication is essential in engineering in order to achieve an outcome.

situation: A group of people, numbering 7, were tasked with the design and production of a civil model of student housing building.
task_action: * Planning: We began by determining the scope and size of the model and plan in the site analysis. * Gathering materials: Once we have a plan in place, gather all the necessary materials. You'll need cardboard, a cutting mat, a craft knife, a ruler, glue, and any other decorative materials you plan to use (such as paint, markers, or stickers). * Cutting the cardboard: basic shapes of our model from the cardboard were cut. * Assembling the pieces: Bothe glue and tape were used to assemble the model * Adding details: A group member used a 3D printer to print our own extra details, e.g., furniture.
result: OUR GROUP COMPLETED OUR BUILDING WITH ACCURATE DIMENSIONS AND TO SCALE.
pfr: The beginning was slow as our group were unsure of where to begin. But once we began our process of building everyone fit well into different roles to efficiently complete our task.
learning: Attention to detail: Building a model demands a high level of attention to detail. Each cut and glue must be precise to create an accurate representation of the structure. This can help develop your ability to focus and pay close attention to small details. Engineering concepts: Civil models often involve principles of engineering, such as load-bearing structures, framing, and stability. By building a model, you can gain a deeper understanding of these concepts and how they apply to real-world structures.

situation: Writing a report on a recently completed project.
task_action: Making a to-do list outlining the tasks with higher priority and how long it should realistically take to complete. A Gantt chart is the most effective way to format the time to complete a task, visually showing how long it took and when it took place. Colour coding a Gantt chart helps to signify priority and which tasks should take place first and take priority.
result: An easy way to organise tasks and which to focus on first, making the process of writing the report easier and more efficient to complete on time with key components out of the way first.
pfr: The initial task was daunting because seeing a 7 page sample report is quite intimidating, especially with a lack of prioritisation and focus resulting in completion being left to the last day/hours. The gantt chart resulted in a way to break down the task and make focusing on it easier as the overall task seems less daunting as you can see what tasks are to be completed instead of one big daunting report.
learning: By approaching the task with a broken down structure, it allows bigger tasks or jobs to be completed first and the other jobs to be completed after, making it seem more rewarding as you complete tasks, making it more engaging to complete. This keeps the focus on the tasks rather than other distractions.

topic: Initiative and the willingness to make decisions in the face of uncertainty
situation: In a crucial must-win game for my football team, our star striker went down with a rather nasty cramp in the early minutes of the second half.
task_action: Given we had already made all of our allotted substitutions, it seemed like a no brainer to most of the players on our team that our striker should continue playing with the cramp as we would be better off having eleven players on the field with one injured over having just 10 players to take on our opposition, who were beginning to build momentum and were threatening to take the match away from us. However, we were still quite indecisive in the heat of the moment. Given no one else appeared ready to make would could be such a crucial decision for our season, I took on the initiative and got the team in a huddle to explain to them that it wasn’t worth the risk to aggravate the injury and that I believed in every player that we could still fight back harder and stronger without our striker.
result: Subsequently, my initiative and address to the team worked brilliantly and we went on to win the match and progress to the finals, in which I would captain the team.
pfr: Making the initial decision was very daunting and intimidating as if it had gone wrong and the match result had gone the other way it would've been extremely difficult for the whole team to shake off and a loss of confidence for myself in that I lacked that killer instinct. However, as it turned out, I learnt to trust and back myself in whatever situations I would end up in In the future as I know believe in my strong initiative to get me through anything.
learning: Further adding onto the last point, I am of the opinion that one's willingness to make decisions and trust their own gut feeling in the face of uncertainty and adversity is a key and important attribute that one should have as it is may come extremely useful in many aspects of life. This has been especially relevant in my studies of Engineering, as trusting my initiative in making tough decisions has been very necessary in completing my coursework up to this point, whilst boosting and developing the skill all the while.

situation: At my current job, I was being rostered for long shifts across all of my weekdays during a busy period of Uni. I was struggling with managing my time effectively and found myself feeling overwhelmed with the amount of work i had due during a time period with little time to accomplish it effectively. Upon a specific situation upon being asked to stay back a further 4 hours of my shift I approved well knowing I had work due the following day that I hadn't started.
task_action: My personal task was to improve upon my time management skills and find ways to effectively balance my work schedule adequately with the amount of Uni work due. To address this challenge, I first assessed how I was currently using my time when I wasn't busy. I began by being self aware of my daily activities and whether it was an effective use of my time. I then prioritized my Uni tasks within those periods reliving me of the buildup of stress. Furthermore i adjusted my work availability to cater towards my heavy Uni workload to provide myself more free time outside of work to complete my tasks.
result: As a result of my actions, I saw a significant improvement in my time management skills. I was able to complete my Uni project deadlines consistently across the period and deliver work of a quality that approved of. Additionally, I found that I had more time and energy for things outside of Uni and work without feeling like i was wasting my time or that i had things to get back to.
pfr: The initial feeling of dread to complete my Uni work always daunted me during my shifts whereby afterwards i was too exhausted to build up the energy to complete my tasks. While the problem itself has a simple solution being that of improving my time management to fix the issue, leaving things to the last minute has always been an issue for me, therefore i had to make small changes and obvious ones to eventually change how i structure my time management to something more suitable.
learning: I found that i can acknowledge my bad behavior and that it is something that i can most definitely easily fix only if i put in the necessary effort to change it. This is something that can impact further aspects of my life in other areas other than time and resource management.

situation: We needed to design a wooden aircraft.
task_action: A group of myself and one 3 other team members decided to split the workload into two separate bits. Myself and one other team member would work on the CAD and physical design of the aircraft, and the two other team members would work on the written report section. Breaking up into small groups allows for better results, as not everyone will have the same take upon the task given. Communication in this step is important to allow the team to collect each persons thoughts and intercede their options. Through this method, several designs of the aircraft were suggested each with their pros and cons stated.
result: The result led to a whole group discussion to figure out which design would be best suited and be most successful. In the end, we were able to come out with a final design which the whole team had agreed on.
pfr: Splitting the workload at first as most of us wanted to work on the physical design. As we accounted for each others experience in certain areas, we were able to devise a final workload structure. Subsequently, working on a part that another person in your team wanted to work on led to a sense of pressure to not make any mistakes. In the end, the design was a team decision and chosen upon what we believed had the least flaws.
learning: By splitting the workload by method of discussion, we were able to come to a steady and logical agreement on how we would structure it. A display of interpersonal skills and communication were required to make sure everyone carries their weight throughout the project. Furthermore, selecting a final design as a team let everyone use their personal knowledge to partake in the final decision as if done by just a singular person, may lead to the design being flawed in areas that the decision maker was simply unaware of.

situation: During the HSC I needed to plan out my timetable of study, schoolwork, social life and work outside of school. I needed to effectively prioritise and plan my life so it was balanced, healthy and able to reach my goals.
task_action: I was able to achieve this by allocating my time and resources using a schedule. I prioritized my study periods, this included studying for my tests, any schoolwork I had to do and tutoring for subjects that I wasn’t confident in. These study periods would be straight after school and in my free periods for as long as I was capable of. I then prioritized my social life. I allocated my time and resources for this to be on the weekend. During the HSC I would try to stay around my local area when I went out to ensure I didn’t spend too much money as I had least prioritised working. I least prioritized work and making money as I believe it was not as important as focusing on my studies and would’ve reduced the amount of time, I had to do these studies.
result: The result of my time and resource management reflected my plan and I was happy with my results.
pfr: The idea of making a schedule for my studying was a task i had put off for many years and throughout highschool i had been doing things as i go and not sticking to a plan. This caused me to have a lack of time and resources management. But deciding to finally make one and manage my time and resources effectively caused me to enjoy my time more during the HSC as i wasnt stressing as much. If I had differentiated my schedule and plan to prioritise my studies even more then my social life I may have scored better but I wasn’t willing to make my life all about the HSC in the moment.
learning: By deciding to manage my time and resources during the HSC has enlightened me to the benefits of managing time and resources in other aspects of life to ensure a fun and stress free lifestyle. I am now able to plan out my days according to what i have on and what needs to be done effectively and also am able to budget my money per week to ensure i am saving money.

situation: As a group in year 10 my team had to design a box that was not only stylish but also ergonomic towards our users. Which inevitably failed as a result of poor communication and teamwork.
task_action: At first we all thought that we fitted into a position and planned our roles according to out strengths and weaknesses. For me I was responsible for the design of the watch. Over the next few weeks, problems arose with conflicting ideas as to what our project should do, look like and operate. We had all each come up with elaborate ideas, plans and models that did not take into consideration the plans of others. With little time remaining, we came together as a team, threw away our conceited ideas for the project and really focused on how we could draw ideas from our projects and put them all together.
result: As a result we surprisingly finished ahead of all the other teams, who instead of dealing with their teamwork problem just left the project to one person who couldn't handle the work and submitted a less desirable product. By breaking up the tasks once again but this time all under one universal plan we successfully created a watch case that was designed for modern day businessmen and won first place in the class.
pfr: Personally the final pull through came to me as a shock, due to the arrogant and prideful nature of ourselves we more times than not will not surrender to the idea of others. Looking back it could have been very easy for anyone of us to say, "your design sucks, here's why you should all conform to my design and if you don't agree I'm not participating anymore". However, thankfully we all wanted this project to succeed and the only objective way to do that was to surrender our pride and work together as a team towards a product that maybe not many of us would would have liked but it was all for a greater purpose. I still remember being responsible for designing the indent which would hold the watch, a small and insignificant part of the design. Yet it required the most teamwork and communication with my team members because without the correct measurements, how wide or high is the watch or will it fit diagonally or horizontally, the whole project falls apart. By having effective teamwork and communication can be the difference if something is finished or not.
learning: It should have never taken weeks to come together, put aside our different ideas and come to work as a team. Strong teamwork and communication should be at the forefront of every group activity. Without them it becomes a collection of messy ideas. I learned there is no team with out teamwork and without strong communication it makes working with other people much more difficult and straight up impossible. I take this as an important lesson, although there will certainly be more projects that test my teamwork abilities I hope to start building upon this crucial skill now, rather than later.

situation: We have come up with a plan for three different groups to do a specific task each in order to construct a new road.
task_action: Once the plan has been finalised and the details have been ironed out it now must be shared with the workers who are going to carry out the plan. The WAY that the plan is shared is vital as by being CLEAR and ASSERTIVE to make sure no group mistakes any details so that when the time comes their part of the plan is carried out without issue. This will be done by making sure the three groups are in their correct group and when their aspect of the plan is delivered it is done with clear pronunciation, along with visual aids to aid incase of a misstep by the presenter. By addressing each group individually no one can get the details mixed up with the other groups.
result: The result was a successful presentation were all parties know the exact details o the job they will be undertaking in the coming days.
pfr: The most nerve racking part is making sure that during the presentation a consistent clear tone of voice is kept so there is no detail is missed by anyone in the presentation. Then making sure when speaking to each group individually I am only speaking to them and not wondering off and look as though I am speaking speaking to other groups and confusing the information spread to them.
learning: By going over the information and REHEARSING it before to a mock 'audience' prior to the actual presentation in order to minimise any mistakes that can occur and practice the tone of voice that will be used throughout the the presentation.

task_action: your task is to manage the time and resources of the project to ensure that you meet the deadline and the report by setting 1. clear and achievable goals. 2. allocate required resources such as personnel, materials and equipment. 3. track time. 4. review the progress.
result: As a result of your effective time and resource management, you will be able to deliver the project report to the client on time and within budget. The client will be satisfied with the quality of the product and gives positive feedback, leading to future business opportunities.

learning: I learnt that effective time and resource management is essential for achieving my goal and delivering the right result on time. by setting clear goals, allocating resource tracking time, I can optimise my productivity and reduce stress.

situation: Projects within the ENG1000 software design and logic workshop are especially daunting as it is my first-time coding, and I know that to succeed I need to manage my time and resources more efficiently.
task_action: As it is my first year of university, the way I approached assignments and homework in high school will not work out the same with the university, as I know the workload as a student am provided is more challenging and requires more time to understand. I realized that to try to succeed in this workshop, I needed to break my bad habits of poor time management and create new good habits that would serve my purpose. My attempt at breaking my bad habits involved creating an assignment spreadsheet that listed all the assignments and homework within the workshop and its due dates. It acted as a constant reminder for me that I needed to work on them and helped me plan out which assignments to focus on first. Sleeping earlier and going to the gym early in the morning instead of later in the day, also helped with allowing me more time to do things later in the day, such as reviewing extra material provided such as C programming lecture videos on YouTube.
result: Implementing good habits and managing my time and resource resulted in extremely positive outcomes. Compared to the start of the workshop, I noticed I have a better work ethic than I usually would, and I feel better mentally and physically.

However, I realized that in order to do good in the engineering workshop, and university in general, I had to allocate more time to studying the resources and at the same time not get burnt out and give myself a break occasionally.
learning: By forcing myself to schedule and plan out my days accordingly, I saw an improvement from the beginning of this workshop compared to now. Through this experience, I have noticed the importance of managing time and resources within this workshop, and have learned that good habits in general create discipline and responsibility, which in the future will be very important for a student like me.

In future group projects, I will make sure to communicate regularly with my team members and establish clear guidelines and expectations from the beginning that will keep the group and track on where we are at in the project progression. I will also make an effort to actively engage in discussions, listen to others' ideas, and provide constructive feedback to produce the best possible outcome.

I had difficulty keeping pace with the assignment demands due to the fast-paced nature of the class, and my lack of precision yielded in cutting the wrong sections of my metal pieces. result: As a result of my efforts, I was able to efficiently manage my time and resources, allowing me to complete the metalworking project within the timeframe specified. The approach to marking and organising the metal pieces reduced uncertainty, saved time, and facilitated terms of growth.
