pfr: During the metalworking course, I felt overwhelmed with the pace and demands of the assignments. I became frustrated with my lack of precision and the setbacks caused by my mistakes. However, as I reflected on my situation, I realized the importance of managing my time and resources effectively, and the need for precision in metalworking.
learning: This experience taught me the value of commitment and diligence in excelling. To ensure a productive workflow, I realised I needed to improve my time management and optimise my tasks. I also realised that precision and accuracy are vital for achieving the desired results while minimising errors and setbacks. To achieve my aims, I must fully commit to the task at hand, expend my time and effort, and work productive In the future, I intend to take a more structured approach to managing my time and resources, employing tools such as schedules and prioritisation techniques to ensure that I am making the most of my time. I also intend to work on honing my attention to detail.

situation: I needed to build multiple circuits with an Arduino using AnalogWrite, PWM, Libraries and Servos within the workshop under a time restraint.
task_action: Build the circuits on Tinkercad before the workshop, allowing the code and working circuit to be completed online using Tinkercad. result: The result was being able to complete the Arduino circuits using AnalogWrite, PWM, Libraries and Servos under the time constrain, while using the Arduino hardware. I used an online resource Tinkercad to create the circuits online before the workshop began.

learning: By using time management and recourse management skills when completing the task, I efficiently completed building the Arduino circuits within the workshop. The experience of using an online resource to complete the circuit before the workshop which allowed me to replicate the online circuit to the hardware in the workshop, demonstrated to me the importance to use resources effectively to allow the tasks to be completed efficiently. I have learnt through this experience the importance of time and resource management to complete tasks to a satisfactory level under a time restraint.

topic: Perseverance, urgency and will to deliver, resourcefulness and flexibility
situation: When constructing my toolbox handle, I encountered the issue of the thread inserts spinning inside the handle, and thus had to develop a solution.
task_action: At first I assessed the reason why the inserts kept on spinning. Soon I found out it was due to the fact I did not press them in straight in line with the handle, causing the handle to expand. At first, I evaluated the shape of the handle, which had been deformed. Soon after I tried clamping certain areas of the handle to return it to its original shape, however this failed. As a result, I had to deliver perseverance by reconstructing the handle, the inserts and tapping the threads. Furthermore, I had to deliver urgency as this meant I was taking a step backwards, and may fall behind.
result: As a result of my actions, I was able to complete my toolbox on-time to a satisfactory level, due to my perseverance, urgency and flexibility
pfr: Initialing, this task was quite stressful as I was uncertain if I would finish in time due to the limited amount of machines and everyone else also working on the handle at the time. However, in the meantime I was able to work on other parts of my toolbox such as welding in order to maintain progress in the mean time and stay on track for completion. In the end I was able to finish successfully and was proud of my efforts.
learning: By overcoming this difficulty through perseverance, flexibility and urgency I have learned successful organisation, decision making and task-managing skills. In particular, the experience of ordering different processes regarding urgency and importance allowed me to improve my time management and organisation skills. Through this experience, I have been able to effectively learn and improve these skills, thus greater preparing me for future situations and challenges.

situation: While presenting my project, I discovered that there was an error in my code.
task_action: Fix the error, either by fixing the code or by writing alternative code that completes the same task. I opted for the second option, as the error was in the find_round_winner() function, and the issue came from my attempt to complete Extension 2, that being to find a winner mathematically. I knew I wouldn't be able to figure out what was wrong with it in the time I had, so I ended up having to accept a lost mark and instead write out a bunch of if/if else statements to get the job done so that I had working code to present.
result: The result was having code that worked as intended and met all requirements from the user's end, at the cost of the mark for the inclusion of Extension 2.
pfr: It was annoying to discover that there was an error in the code while presenting as I had spent a lot of time testing the code and it all seemed to work fine. It didn't help that I had so little time to fix the issue due to when it was discovered.
learning: In the future, I need to make sure I dedicate more time to testing my projects, and not just rely on manual tests, but write unit tests as well. If I had written unit tests I would likely have been able to spot the issue sooner and fix it.

result: The result was being able to finish the project more efficiently. With the use of teamwork, people in the group were able to do different tasks and stay communicated with the group.
pfr: Reflection My personal feelings for the use of teamwork and communication are that it’s very useful to have especially after graduation. This is because having a team will help to share ideas and responsibilities instead of keeping them to ourselves. This would benefit from avoiding mistakes. Without the use of teamwork, the project wouldn’t be able to be completed on time. With teamwork and mainly communication, this would allow us to set a time frame for the project. So, I would say having a team and communicating constantly is very crucial.
learning: With the use of teamwork, others from the team will be able to learn new things and improve their decision-making when it comes to their ideas and thoughts. This would allow people from the team to gain more experience and be more successful when it comes to making projects as a team in the future. So, I personally think that learning new stuff will help others to gain so much experience and help them with their future jobs.

situation: We were doing a group assignment that consisted of 3 individuals and the task was to create a design and prototype of a portable speaker that could be used at places like the beach without it being affected by sand and dust particles.
task_action: We all then researched and came up with ideas in regards to the design. We ended up with numerous ideas and designs, however we then had to come to an agreement and decide the design. Further we managed out our time frame by using an action plan that consisted of all the necessary requirements in order to build an appropriate speaker meeting all the needs as stated. We split the workload equally as this then allows us to work in a more efficient manner and also allows us to complete the required works before the deadline. We also manage our resources so that we know what will be used and that nothing will be going to waste.
result: The result was the completion of designing and creating a prototype of a portable speaker that could be used at places like the beach without it being affected by sand and dust particles.
pfr: The assignment at first seemed as if it was impossible to complete due to the complexity of the task and the time constraints issued upon us. However, as a group we successfully managed to create an action plan that allowed us to complete the tasks on time. The action plan helped us to split the workload and the tasks that were required to complete, based on the certain time frame that we as a group had issued for each task. By doing this we managed to finish well on time and had also managed to save many resources due to the planning and managing of our resources and time.
learning: Through the use of time and resource management, we as a group were successful in completing our desired target. The use of time and resource management helped us to counter this difficult situation by allowing us to work in an appropriate manner that would allow us to finish before the deadline, also assisting us in saving resources and eliminating costs through the adequate planning management. By using the method of managing we managed to gain experience as this further helps us being organized and focused. By the completion of this assignment, I've understood the value of having appropriate time and resource management.

situation: Woodwork was one of my electives for my HSC preliminary course and had to submit a project before a certain due date.
task_action: In doing this I had to manage my time as well as the resources used. In order to ensure I was up to date, I needed to create a schedule to monitor my progress and keep up with all of the steps. Furthermore, I also had to manage my resources in terms of efficiently using the materials to not waste resources and money.
result: For my schedule, I used a gantt chart which allowed me to know what my next steps were whilst displaying the tasks I have done as well as how quickly I should have these tasks done. Managing resources was done by keeping scraps and off cuts and are used in areas where it may not be seen so it doesn’t affect the aesthetics of the project, or the off cuts can also be used in areas where it only requires a bit of material.
pfr: Initially, I was very stuck as to how to plan the timeline of my Gantt chart. This is because of the nature of the task, where it is hard to predict how long a specific task is going to take as you have to take into account how many students have to complete this task and how many machines are available. There are times where I don’t get much done in a lesson because there aren’t enough machines available. This commonly happens at the start where everyone is on the same stage. However, it evidently became easier to predict the time it would take after guidance from peers and teachers. The teachers also made sure that we kept up to date this would be done by setting a machine up with specific settings, the machine settings will remain the same for a certain period of time, and if we didn’t complete the task, we would not get any help. This forced us to keep up and manage our times. Managing resources was not easy, natural human nature will want the best things for themselves. While we were making our project, it was very common for students to throw their offcuts into the scrap box as they do not think ahead. It wasn’t until I was around past half way where I realised, I could have used parts I threw out for a different part. For example, I had to thin down a plank of wood and was done by cutting on a table saw. This left me with a long, thin plank of wood which can be used as a frame for a door. Although it was a bit too late after I realised, it was a mistake to learn from.
learning: Through this experience of time management, I learnt a new format of scheduling i.e., the Gantt chart. The Gantt chart is suitable for projects that require a to do list and has to be done in specific steps, a recommended period the tasks need to be completed by and keeping track of what you have completed. Additionally, I have learnt that collaboration gives the ability to produce more solid work and there is no shame in asking for help. Furthermore, I have also learnt that to work efficiently and effectively, incentives are a good way to motivate people to get the job done. Through managing resources, I learnt that it is important to think ahead of time, about what materials I am going to need, which can potentially save money and resources. These experiences have allowed me to be a more diligent worker and be more proactive.

situation: I was given the task of coding a program to count to 20 in even numbers only.
task_action: I thought of multiple solutions including hard-coding and utilising a for-loop or a while-loop. I trialed each method and found that the use of a for-loop would be the best way to complete the task since I understood it the most and it took up the least amount of lines.
result: Lastly, I was able to complete the task by using the best method.
pfr: The task seemed fairly easy and I immediately knew what the three main solutions would be. From prior experience I was able to make an example solution concept for each of the methods and I found that one method was superior based on the amount of lines it used and how straight-forward it was since I believe that simplicity and readability make good code.
learning: I learnt that there are always different methods for coding even though there may only be one obvious path for me.

situation: Time and resource management has become more of an essential element to achieving life goals and meeting deadlines especially in relation to university studies and assessments.
task_action: Overtime, having a strong management plan for your timing and resources has become a vital aspect of everyone's life especially in university. Assessments and tasks are quite congested for some and therefore force people to have solid plans in which quality productive time is spent. Due to these impacting changes, one must adapt to a heavy workload and productively manage their time. Utilising time scheduling software's and other alike programs can effectively alter ones bad habits of time and resources managements. Some may also improve their time management skills by setting priorities, reducing procrastination, and the like.
result: Effectively managing ones time and resources is very effective as it streamlines their workflows and increases productivity. These also improve ones lifestyle and reduce their workload which allows for a more productive day to day.
pfr: Since working for a long period of time on studies has become quite overwhelming, I have learnt to effectively reduce stress and benefit myself through the use of time and resource management skills. This has allowed for a more productive time during my studies in university and allowed me to have more free time during my day to day life.
learning: University and have many workloads has introduced me to the real world and the pressure that one is put through. Through this experience, I have been able to learn the value of time and resource management. This has extremely assisted in matters out of work and have eased me into the real world work.

situation: During year 12 as the head of staging in the school entertainment crew/course I was in charge of a team of my peers, delegating specific roles pre-performance and during. I communicated issues live to other departments around the building. During a production wherein there was a trivia segment, one of the contestants was missing.
task_action: We had to find the contestant or find a replacement, and since it was a live show we had at most 2 minutes to figure the situation out. As the decision maker for the team I asked my crew if anyone had ideas on how we could solve it efficiently, we discussed for a short time then based on their suggestions, I gave each of them a job to do that would have us ready to send the set on at the right cue. Backstage roles were shuffled around with some people doing two smaller jobs so I could send a small handful out, one to ask around the performers for other sets if they knew where the contestant was, another to find out if a replacement could be organised among the pool of students we had backstage waiting for their time.
result: The situation and response showed that as a team, even the leader must seek ideas and collaborate with others, because the crew knew what they were each capable of and came up with ways to solve the issue. The contestant was not found, but a volunteer was found by the crew member tasked with finding a replacement, meaning the show could continue as planned. The backstage crew all worked together seamlessly to cover the missing manpower and execute all the moves on time and satisfactorily. The show was a success.
pfr: In such a time sensitive situation, clear communication was the most important aspect of identifying and solving the issue, a stage crew can be quite large, not to mention as a head of department issues must be communicated to other departments far away from the stage such as lighting and audio. As a leader and team member, it is imperative that the crew feels heard and respected, listening to their ideas to help allowed a solution to be devised with multiple plans happening simultaneously. Being heard by the person in charge meant the crew were in the loop about the issue and what was being done to solve it, it meant that those who knew they were capable of handling more responsibility had the chance to voice themselves meaning others could be sent away from set.
learning: Understanding that each individual with their own set of experiences, skills, and ideas, means those qualities can be utilised in high pressure situations, without the crew coming together, a solution would not have been devised, let alone in the extremely short amount of time available. It also took trust between the crew and leader that they were being acknowledged and their skills were being considered, as well as trust in each others ability to handle the added tasks/responsibility. The response time showed that this crew did have the necessary trust, innovation, and problem-solving attitude to ensure the situation was handled effectively. From this, I came to fully realise how imperative open lines of communication are, as a team and in specific situations. Knowing each of their strengths and weaknesses, I could hand the most suitable jobs to each of the crew and make sure they all knew where we stood in the situation throughout the whole thing.

situation: I need to be able to complete all of my technical drawings in the allocated time frame
task_action: every week, we are given 3 hours to finish each lesson. These 3 hours are very important, because we are given special tools that allow us to draw with consistent angles and lengths. Without these tools, it is almost impossible to draw up to standard, meaning I can't finish these drawings outside of class time. I prioritised which drawings would be harder to do without the special tools provided. for example, Isometric and Oblique drawings had a very high priority, since the need to be drawn at very specific angles, which I can't do with the tools I have at home. Next is the technical drawings, since everything has to be drawn perfectly vertical or horizontal. These have a lower priority because I can do touch-ups and small lines by lining up a small triangle ruler with my page at home. Finally, the lowest priority drawings are perspective drawings. Vertical and horizontal lines can be done as mentioned before, and are much rarer. All of the other lines require no tools except for a basic ruler making them less risky to do at home. After I prioritise my drawings for the day, I allocate no more than 1.5 hours per drawing. If any take longer than that, I'll skip them and try finishing them at home.
result: A total of 19 technical drawings completed and submitted before the due date.
pfr: I was able to finish every drawing in the allocated time. However, it still took me 4+ hours to compile and upload my work, as the time limit I put on myself decreased the quality of my drawings. I had to spend my time darkening the lines by drawing over lighter lines. Fortunately, all of the drawings came out legible in the scans. Also due to my time restrictions, I had to do all of my measurements at home for the technical drawings. I also had to skip using compasses to draw some circles and free handed them. This is because the compasses in class barely work, and I just so happen to have the exact same non-functioning compass at home, down to the blue and black colour scheme. Unlucky.
learning: due to (an attempt at) proper time and resource management, I was able to complete and submit all of the tasks on time, unlike some of my previous experiences with similar classes in high-school. This experience has taught me that I shouldn't expect to be able to finish everything in the minimum allocated time frame, and I should expect to and plan around working on projects in environments where I don't have access to standard tools, because I can never know what situation I might be put in, especially in engineering.

situation: We need to formulate a design fix(s) for the harbour bridge under a 14 day time pressure, with 1 major design problem and 7 minor design problems.
task_action: After brainstorming ideas under the leadership of our lead engineer; we formulated into multiple minor groups based on speciality and were re-explained clearly and in depth what the 8 issues were; thus our job became to further brainstorm design fix's using the gallery method of brainstorming in smaller groups then come back together after. After getting back together and deciding on the 8 solutions for each we assigned one person per task to further develop on it.
result: The result was being able to design 8 working solutions, and worked on individually by one person for each solution to then apply it.
pfr: Initially the major solution seemed quite daunting to the group and we were quick to focus on fixing the easier tasks at hand first, as we knew we could handle it quickly. Yet, despite finishing it all in a systematic method of approach we did not finish on time. Our decision making and prioritisation was incorrect, and what we thought was easy ended up becoming hard. We were overwhelmed by the 8 solutions to attempted to complete the minor 7 to then just have one to think about, but instead we ended up taking longer on the 7 and not giving ourselves time for the larger and more prioritised solution problem. Our designs worked and we fixed the problems. Despite coming up with a list of 8 design solutions around the harbour bridge with the brainstorming session, we did not focus and prioritise enough on our main objective, meaning we submitted the designs at 15 days rather then 14, despite each member further working on a specific task as we did not expect the major project to be so large or difficult. We prioritised the smaller things that needed restored or fixed, which went against our objective, thus we ended up being late for the project.
learning: With better leadership we could have approached the task with better decision-making to ensure we not only effectively solve the solutions but complete them/the major task on time. This instead of rushing into the easy tasks, I have appreciated the importance of planning to prioritise and focus better, as being an engineer requires more then being able to fix an issue but to prioritise issues to make sure you make deadlines and complete the right tasks first. Instead of placing one person on each task, we should have created a priority list and had multiple people working on the major task first, and then we could move to the smaller ones.

situation: The situation relating to time and resource management that I experienced was the 2 weeks leading up to my HSC (High School Certificate) final Year 12 exams in 2022 (these exams would determine my final mark and what degree I would qualify for accordingly). During this 2 week period I had my 18th birthday and I had my Year 12 formal party, so it became very difficult to balance studying and celebrating. The stress of the final exams was finally settling in and I was unable to enjoy these 2 major events that a person only gets to experience once. So whilst I wanted to fully enjoy my 18th birthday party and my Year 12 formal, the thought of the final exams was constantly lingering in the back of my mind. Hence, I had to find a way to manage my time such that I didn’t regret not enjoying these events but also not regretting that I didn’t study enough for the exams.
task_action: To ensure that I enjoyed my time during these 2 once in a lifetime events and also did my best in the HSC, I had to implement certain time and resource management strategies. It was through these strategies that I was able to achieve my task of maximising my efficiency whilst studying so that I would be able to spare time to enjoy my 18th birthday party and my formal. The very first step I took was to plan ahead, as time itself is also a vital resource. I utilised Google Calendar to break each day up into study sections. Each study section was 2 hours and I would focus upon a single subject. During these study sections I would either go through my flashcards using an app called Anki (which utilises the study technique called spaced repetition) or I would attempt practice exams and reattempt questions I got wrong. By reattempting questions I got wrong I was able to gain maximum benefits out of the practice papers which were limited. The next action I took was setting clear priorities. As the dates of each exam was spread out, I would spend more time on the subject that had its test the earliest. Next, I would prioritise topics within each subject whereby I knew I had gaps in my knowledge. This enabled me to not only reinforce what I knew but also ensure that I wasn’t going into my exams without knowing everything that I needed to. Another step that I took was to focus on one task at a time. Rather than thinking about each subject as a whole, I made a To Do list on Google Keep which enabled me to break the subject down into parts. This reduced the stress greatly as larger topics were broken down into more mentally digestible smaller topics. The final step that I took was setting shorter deadlines. For example I would aim to get at least 5 practice exams for a subject, 1 week prior to its exam date. This would ensure I was completing my work earlier than I should have. By doing so I was constantly ahead and on top of what I needed to study.
result: The objectives of my actions were to maximise the use of the little time I had to study for my exams so that I would be able to enjoy my 18th birthday party and my Year 12 formal party. The result of my actions was that I was able to fully enjoy the two events with only minimal effects on my exams. I had attempted each test to the best of my ability and I was confident that I was going to receive the mark that I wanted. I hadn’t regretted enjoying the parties or wishing that I spent more time studying for my exams. Moreover I had very little stress during my exam period. When I got my ATAR (final mark) back, I had achieved the goal that I had set. However I was certain that I could’ve done better by not attending the parties, but this didn’t bother me as I knew it would’ve had no extra benefit as I achieved the goal I wanted to. In the end, I had no regrets and I achieved the initial task that I had set out to complete.
pfr: Before I set out to efficiently study by utilising time and resource management techniques, I was quite overwhelmed with the workload and very stressed. This affected other areas of my life such as not exercising or eating properly. I was thinking that I was going to fail my exams, I would not get into the degree I wanted, that my future would be ruined and that I would not be able to enjoy my parties. However after implementing the strategies I was more confident than I had ever been about any exam I ever took. During the exams, I didn’t pay much attention to whether or not I had enjoyed my parties and my only focus was doing the best I could in the exam. However, after the exams I was content and joyful with what I had done, as I had not only done well but also enjoyed my parties.
learning: By utilising such time and resource management strategies I was able to achieve all the goals I had set out before the exams. I learnt that it was futile for me to be stressed before the exams because I should have been confident when I implemented the strategies. Moreover, I learnt how to fully maximise my time and organise tasks efficiently. I have been able to carry forward these skills into university and I have constantly been on top of my work with minimal stress. Through this experience I have learnt not only these vital time and resource management skills but also how to reduce stress and have a more positive mindset when faced with larger workloads.

situation: Product cost fluctuation makes it harder to arrange the balance between worker (supplier), middle man (transport), and final buyer (seller). We are the middle man, and we want to find a solution to guarantee our money because the price may change instantly after we buy from the supplier and the buyer may not offer the price that we want. We need to make a profit to pay for the labor, transportation costs, and future investments. What is the solution?
task_action: Making a brainstorm session; forming a discussion group involving everyone in the organization; writing down every suggestion on the whiteboard; encouraging everyone to be creative and contribute. After we make a mind map and identify any related ideas, we select the most feasible ones to turn a profit. The main success came from the fact that there was no hierarchy postulating solutions; everyone was included, so we gathered many ideas.
result: Solution 1: Suppliers prices are defined by the demand of the market. The possible solution to controlling the supplier price is to dominate the supplier market by producing a unique product. Solution 2: Let's say we pay certain money to the labor and to the trunk for one day; however, our job finished in 2 hours. We paid for 9 hours, but since we do not have a second supplier, our 7 hours money is basically wasted. The solution is to negotiate with other suppliers and convince them to sell their products at a reasonable price. Solution 3: Finally, we brought the product to the buyer, but the buyer changed the price to a lower price. The buyer was greedy; they wanted to make more profit. Solution is: Instead of begging them to purchase our product, we parked the trunk in front of the potential buyers and held an auction, and the highest bidder earned the right to buy the product. By doing this, we get into a more advantageous position. Solution 4: Another reason for the disagreement with buyers is that they do not know us because we are new in this market. They are right in that they are not sure about the quality of our product. The solution is to make ourselves known to them by preserving our high quality all the time. In addition to that, we always have those products, so when the demand increases, they will know that they can reach us and we can supply the demand. This trust will get stronger with time. Solution 5: In the long term, becoming the seller itself by building a platform Solution 6: Building a logistic center to encourage the small supplier to deliver their products Small suppliers will be compensated with a good price, so they will trust us that we are not taking advantage of them. Trust is the best advertisement, which spreads from ear to ear. It will make us more recognized in the industry. Solution 7: Exporting the product

situation: In my Rock Paper Scissors code, I found an occurrence where the player choice value and computer value would be within the 'valid' range for a round, but still wouldn't be identified as a valid round even though it was supposed to be valid.
task_action: Identify the origin of the coding error and adjust the code to make sure the values can be identified as valid inputs for a valid round. I thought that if the incorrect 'if' statement was running, that means that the values must have been true for the if statement, therefore if I evaluate the code backwards from the origin of the incorrect lines of code that it ran, i might find a possibility for an error. It turns out that the computer's value was at fault, originally, the program would recognise the 'round' as a tie, I had written this a while loop to fix the value while it was still an invalid input. However, the criteria for the if statement would first identify if the value was invalid, randomise the computer's value, and then categorise it into either a tie or an outside-of-range value (with the outside-of-range value being 'else'). In the weird occurrence I mentioned earlier, the outcome would have been a tie, meaning the program would run the invalid if statement, randomise the computer's value to change the outcome into a "non-tie" round and state it fulfilled the 'else' criteria meaning it was an "out of range" value, despite both values being valid I changed the code to randomise the computer's value AFTER recognising the round is a tie or out of range, that way the values would be identified accurately.
result: The new piece of code would never input an incorrect process for a correct value after the changes made to it.
pfr: Reflection After being completely confused about how the computer had inputted the incorrect output, fixing the problem had become a big problem with the current form of evaluation I was using to identify previous problems in the code. I then decided to change my way of critical thinking by looking at the problem from a different perspective.
learning: By evaluating the code backwards from the origin of the problem, I was able to run step-by-step the possibilities of the code and identify the problem clearly by first identifying the facts of the situation. I should use this for future situations where the code shows incorrect outputs, where I should evaluate facts such as which lines of code were run and work backwards from there.

situation: One must teach a university student how to create loops in the programming language C.
task_action: Teach student how to do infinite and finite for, while and do loops. Get student to create their own loops without support from a teacher. First we must establish a positive learning environment, encouraging the student to ask questions, engage in constructive dialogue amongst peers and create groups amongst themselves. Next should brainstorm ideas about what students think a loop structure might resemble and go through their logical thought processing. Afterwards one must demonstrate the general structure of a loop and show the three different types; for , while and do. One must explore the difference between finite and infinite loops. Next one must provide an example of each in a specific situation(ie for a while loop teacher might show the following loop --> int Counter = 0; while (Counter <= 10) {printf("Hi"); Counter = Counter + 1; } ). Subsequently one must ask the university student to create their own for, while and do loops giving them certain criteria to follow. If the students are struggling guide them by showing them a solution to a different similar problem.
result: The results was students were able to create their own finite and infinite, while, for and do loops in C independently of external support. Students could also apply these loops in coding situations allowing them to tackle problems like this in their other units or courses at uni.
pfr: REFLECTION Teaching an undergraduate university student loops is challenging as it may seem difficult to convey the core principles to them as they have little coding experience and literacy in C. However, as I delved into the example problems using a methodical approach my students uncovered that there are certain structures and patterns that they can use. My coding student and myself came to an agreement that coding loops must follow a unique structure and can be implemented into different situations. The coding task that I assigned was chosen based on difficulty and topic that the student found was the hardest to understand.
learning: By approaching teaching through a trial and error based approach, experimenting with what the student can and cannot accomplish on their own I was able to make significant progress teaching the student how to tackle loop problems on their own, eventually, due to my guidance, my student was able to expedite any loop challenge irregardless of the difficulty. The example the for, while and do loops that I selected where picked to be easy to understand such that the student could recognise patterns and be able to understand the correct structure format. The questions picked for the student do complete had challenging requirements that were designed to make them think about complex loop structures which ultimately worked to improve their ability to competently write loops in C. However, something that could have been improved on in my teaching method would have been to get my student to collaborate in a group with peers to discuss ideas. Due to this experience, I have discovered a new appreciation of the impact of attitudes, thought and learning based approach in teaching a student.

situation: In my COMP1000 class, we were given an assignment to work on which was a basic game made in Processing. task_action: With a few of the students in my class, we decided to help each other on the assignment, while following the guidelines for the task. Some of the kids were more experienced with programming and had more to give than others, but sharing information with the group in a way that is non-intrusive of the assignment guidelines is a teaching experience in its own way Using the information and concepts we learnt from class, we began to work on our Assignments, and we discussed ways in which we could implement the code we worked on in class into our own assignments. result: The outcome of our efforts was a more cohesive and effective code for our programs. pfr: The task of helping each other on an individual assignment by giving ideas and tips but not explicitly telling each other where and what to type in their code was an interesting learning experience. At the end of the task, all of our games looked at least visually different, and there were some functions and mechanics that I did not implement because of my lack of knowledge in programming, which others were able to implement.
learning: Working in a social environment and sharing knowledge and valuable information will always trump learning from a textbook or video. Making sure we were following assignment and university guidelines was a hard task, but it worked in our favour because it meant we could learn more, both about the task and the ways information can be communicated to others.

situation: I needed to create multiple variants of the game "Rock, Paper, Scissors" using the C programming language. These variants had to: * exponentially incorporate additional hand gestures; * utilise a unifying algorithm that could mathematically calculate the winner of a round in any given variant.
task_action: Engaging in the 'pattern identification' stage of computational thinking; brainstorming and discovering the relationships between the gestures. This involved identifying several key parameters: * The total number of gestures must be odd; * Each gesture must win against half of the other gestures, and lose to the remaining gestures.
result: The result was being able to order the gestures based on these parameters, so that a winner could be calculated using modular arithmetic. For example: Order: * Rock = 0 * Paper = 1 * Scissors = 2 * Spock = 3 * Lizard = 4 Assuming that: * N = number of gestures * A = player 1 choice * B = player 2 choice The following algorithm was born: (A - B + N) % N: * A result of 0 would determine the outcome as a tie; * An odd number would determine the victory of Player 1; * An even number would determine the victory of Player 2.
pfr: The task seemed impossible at first, because I didn’t think it was possible to use the same algorithm for any variant. Adding additional gestures created chaos in my mind, preventing me from thinking clearly about possible solutions. Once I broke the problem down into smaller pieces, I found that it was much easier to approach the task objectively and define a solution that satisfied the prescribed criteria.
learning: By breaking down the problem into smaller, manageable parts, I learned that it’s easier to define the solution through abstraction. I found a way to generalise an answer to a specific problem, by finding an answer to a more general problem. In doing so, I defined an efficient solution that could be applied to multiple variants of the game, avoiding needless repetition. Through this experience, I’ve come to appreciate optimal solutions that can be applied to multiple problems.

situation: While building my toolbox, I encountered a problem with the side panels being incorrectly measured and cut, which made it impossible to fold them correctly.
task_action: My task was to find a solution to the problem to ensure that the side panels fit correctly and securely into the toolbox. I used critical thinking to identify possible solutions to the problem. My first idea was to fold the side panels with a small fold of about three millimetres on each side. However, this solution presented the problem of the side panels appearing thinner than they should be. Then, I evaluated a second idea of using scrap metal to recut the side panels, but this solution would take more time. Finally, I realized that I could measure and cut one side piece perfectly and use it as a stencil for the second piece, saving me time and ensuring that both side pieces fit correctly into the toolbox.
result: My actions resulted in two perfectly cut side pieces that fit correctly and securely into my toolbox without requiring any further alterations. This experience required me to use critical thinking skills to identify and evaluate different solutions to the problem, weighing the pros and cons of each option. It also required me to think creatively about how to make the most of the resources I had available to find the best solution. Overall, this experience helped me develop my critical thinking skills and problem-solving abilities, which I can apply in future engineering situations.
pfr: When I realized the side panels of my toolbox had been incorrectly measured and cut, I felt frustrated and a little overwhelmed. With a lack of sleep, breakfast and coffee, I was not at my cognitive best. I had put a lot of effort into building the toolbox, and this mistake made me feel like all of that effort was going to waste. However, as I started to think critically about how to solve the problem, I began to feel more confident in my ability to find a solution.
learning: Through this experience, I learned the importance of using critical thinking skills to tackle problems. I discovered that being creative and resourceful is essential when faced with challenges and that sometimes the best solution is not the most obvious one. Additionally, I learned the value of paying close attention to details like measuring and cutting accurately, which can prevent mistakes from happening in the first place. Overall, this experience taught me a lot about problem-solving, and I plan to apply what I've learned to future challenges.

situation: After a lot of group work many tasks had been completed, many members of the group became rationally ignorant but did not ask for help. Workflow was being organised on a Trello Kanban board using cards.
task_action: The final stage of the civil modelling project involved documenting all work and assembling the concept model. Tasks were assigned by members to other members. I noticed that there was duplication in tasks with some tasks having already been completed. I acted to refocus the group activities and recommended members review the completed section on Trello.
result: Group members who were not highly engaged found it difficult to locate information on the Trello even though it was clearly labelled. I have concluded that for projects with Asymmetric member engagement of sufficient scale completed work must be migrated off the workflow space and into a documentation space such as confluence.
pfr: This sudden unexpected group disconnect at the late stage of the project was incredibly distressing. The fact that members felt they could no longer rely on the shared group interface caused the group cohesion to collapse and members to break off into individual work. The person assembling the concept model stopped communicating for days, the person tasked with annotating images thought the task was complete, the person laying out the presentation didn’t know what content was too be presented, the person laying out the document couldn’t get anyone to provide information he needed, and although I was busy assistance was never requested.
learning: Reliable stores of project documentation must be maintained to ensure all members share in the progress of all other members. Its obvious now, but I assumed all members were staying abreast of task progress when they were not. Usage of the project management tool “confluence” will be added to my group formation strategy (when the project is of sufficient scale or complexity that rational ignorance becomes a feasible outcome). For example, members should have been easily able to find the size of the building by searching project documentation without asking another member. The confluence will effectively act as a traceable project wiki of all generated information and files.

situation: Throughout my university experience I have had to learn how to take accountability for myself. During the Engg1050 RGM project, I have had to put my skills to the test and continuously refine them to ensure the success of both myself and my team members, with whom I have been actively collaborating.
task_action: I first started my academic career at UTS, where I studied for 2 years before I took a semester off due to an ADHD diagnosis. During my time at UTS, I had the opportunity to partake in four group projects, each with its unique set of group dynamics. It was during these projects that I initially began to develop my sense of accountability. As a student with ADHD, I face ongoing challenges in holding myself accountable, particularly with respect to tasks that require time management. This is the first group project I have been in since beginning my ADHD treatment and I have resolved to maintain my organisation and continue to enhance my sense of accountability. Since the initial workshop I have aimed to be a valuable member for my team. I took proactive steps, making a note of my team members names and reviewing their LinkedIn profiles to familiarise myself with their faces prior to meeting them. I took up position of team leader temporarily, ensuring that each member introduced themselves and that we had a platform to communicate outside of the scheduled workshop meetings. In preparation for our group sessions, I had established our Miro board and familiarised myself with the software in the event that none of my team members had done so. As it turned out, this was the case, and I took it upon myself to guide the team through the features of the platform and how to access our group board. Assuming the role of team leader, I was not only responsible for my own accountability, but also for the successful presentation of our team. I recognised the criticality of leadership and organisation for effective teamwork, and I committed to ensuring a seamless semester for our group. As the project progressed, I continued to fulfill the duties of team manager, even though I did not actively seek this role. However, due to the needs of the team, I remained in this position to ensure our collective success. Taking on the responsibility of organising a team in a group project requires the utmost accountability. Any oversights or failures on my part can potentially harm the team's progress and success. Additionally, it also means that I must hold others accountable for their responsibilities within the project, which can be challenging as a student, since I do not hold any formal authority. If I fail in this task, the completion of the work often falls to me. Throughout the project, I have consistently assumed responsibility not only for my own tasks but also for encouraging effective teamwork and communication. While I acknowledge that there is always room for improvement, I am committed to further developing my professional skills and enhancing my ability to take accountability for myself and future teams.
result: By taking accountability for my work and responsibilities I have successfully coordinated with my team, and we have managed to produce a high quality RGM design.
pfr: Taking accountability for ourselves is a hard task. It can be daunting to own up to our mistakes and you can be tempted to conceal them. Taking accountability requires self-awareness and honesty, shame or hurt pride in a failure is natural. However, by acknowledging those emotions and taking corrective action you can learn from your mistakes. By taking accountability you increase your self-awareness allowing you to see your role in the team and feel a sense of pride when your contributions aid in the team's success. Throughout this term, I have gained insight into the value of accountability, and its ability to enhance one's contribution to a team. This has empowered me to recognise the weight of my input and increased my self-esteem. Prior to this, I have encountered situations in which I felt unheard during group projects. However, through demonstrating a strong work ethic and reliability, I have earned the respect of my peers, which has allowed me to view myself in a more positive light.
learning: Through this course, I have gained insight into effectively managing my responsibilities, enabling me to consistently meet deadlines. Taking accountability has taught me valuable lessons that I can apply in both my personal and professional life. It has allowed me to become more self-aware and recognise my strengths and weaknesses. I have been able to identify areas in need of improvement and actively work towards refining my skills. It has also helped me to become more organised, manage my time effectively, and communicate better with my team members. Overall, taking accountability has allowed me to become a better team player and has improved my confidence in my abilities.

situation: As a first-year undergraduate student at Macquarie University, it’s been 6 weeks since I started grasping skills for unit ENGG1050 Engineering Design. So far, the class has been put into groups to implement a Rube Goldberg Machine for a project concerning 12 key events of 30 seconds duration. My experience with Team A12 has been nothing but exemplary since the weekly presentation and professional documentation of the meeting's agenda and minutes require a constant rotation of roles in the Team Charter. Looking back, I have had to take up the role of Minute-Taker twice and I’m not complaining since it’s a given that tasks are assigned based on the group member’s availability. However, when accepting a role, it is very important to get things done on time. The tutor-in-charge for our team has advised that it is recommended to turn in assessments before Tuesday night. Although records till week 2 show due dates having gone past Friday, it is a student’s responsibility to be aware of the content details provided in the unit guideline. I observed that procrastination is a problem that I am faced with and it took a hit on team morale. The matter at hand became worse when the Minute Taker for week 5 didn’t come through on their end. Absences were noted and hence there was nothing much to report for said person. For ENGG1050 Workshop, I had to take the initiative to do a presentation for the same week since the team member responsible for it had personal matters to attend to. Although a failed attempt, it also gave me a chance to learn that prepared speeches go a long way. The technical difficulties I faced during that time made me a bad candidate for the Presenter role.
task_action: Procrastination is a very bad habit for group assessments as one member's contribution could help to complete the given role of others. Back in year 10 high school, there was a task based on the recent Biology zoo excursion the class had to submit in writing. A group of three consisted of a Note-taker, Report-writer and Key-note Presenter. At the time, I was assigned to write the report but both of my friends were busy cramming for the upcoming Business Studies Exam. In the end, I had to stay up all night to prepare a PowerPoint Presentation as well. I want to avoid putting one of my team members in that kind of tough spot. Having to stay up all night is not a nice experience. So, it was decided that the Chairman role for Team A12 will also have the burden of supervising the shared Google Docs and Slides. To be targeted with deadline notifications in the group chat is rather motivational in its embarrassing way. The issue of absence led to the idea of choosing a Sub-Presenter for the Workshop Zoom Meetings. An alternate option of one person doing the slides while the sub-in prepares a speech has concurred. In case of an emergency, minutes-taking will be divided among all five members. Although not disclosed in Team Charter, a position for Group Leader is elected every week on a rotational basis. The person is then asked to update the Agenda Status while directing topics for future meetings. If a situation were to arise, even if inconvenient, they should be willing to take up the challenge.
result: For week 6, I noticed that Team A12 has had over three meetings outside of the Workshop hours. All meetings were initiated by the Group Leader while she conveyed that Preliminary Design Diagrams for the RGM events be posted up on the Google Slides created. The seriousness of task completion was highlighted when she warned that negligence will mean that the person in question will have his/her event ideas modified in the later stages. I was surprised to see that in response, even the least active member had started to reply in group chat discussions after 6 pm. This could be a result of our Group Leader’s decision or could be due to the marks weighed on the Week 7 Presentation. Although I’m not selected to be one of three Presenters for the upcoming week, a request has been made to share everyone’s speech on Google Docs. I’ve learnt my lesson from experience, it’s better to have something to blabber on than to space out in front of the whole class. I will be ready to fill in for a member if things don’t go as planned.
pfr: The idea of a Punishment and Reward Approach is not relatively new. The Group Leader has announced the punishment incurred when team members are not diligent in their assigned roles. But though unnecessary, a reward would attribute to a positive change in attitude. I.e, the power to choose any roles for next time. It is advised that the idea of penalising fellow group members for irresponsibility will garner hatred in the long run. In my opinion, the first impression is always and will ever be the last impression. A personal fear in essence, but one that stops me from lazing around when I’m being relied upon.
learning: There’s a lot of politics involved in group assignments. From past encounters, I have found that it is beneficial to argue over inconsequential things. No one wants to be dubbed as the ‘pushover’ in a team dynamic. Just enough to show that your opinion should also have value when it comes to any decisions that are made.

situation: We needed to think of a final action for our Rube-Goldberg Machine, and think of an overarching theme for the whole thing that was somehow connected to the final action.
task_action: We individually brainstormed many different ideas, then laid them out in a list on Miro. Once we had as many ideas as possible, we began whittling down our options, eliminating based on feasability and overall design quality. We initially had some conflicting ideas, but through proper and professional communication, we were able to decide as a team more effectively, willingly compromising if needed. Everyone’s ideas were seriously considered because it was very important to us that everyone in the team had a voice and felt that they were being heard.
result: We were able to come to an agreement on our machine’s design. We decided that the final action for the machine was to water a small house plant, and that to fit into the theme of watering a plant, at least every other action of the machine should involve the movement of water. Following this, we could think of the actual actions and find ways to piece them together.
pfr: During the brainstorming session, I was quite overwhelmed by the sheer amount of ideas presented. Everyone had their own idea of the direction they wanted to take with the machine, and it seemed like we would never come to an agreement. I initially thought that having a lot of people in the group would result in many conflicts and time inefficiencies. However, even with four other people in the team there to offer their own advice and criticism, I found it easy to take each idea and evaluate them one by one. We eliminated options based on whether we could actually construct them within our given time frame, whether the proposed design appropriately fit into our “water” design, and if the end product would look presentable.
learning: After coming to a final agreement, I found that we were able to work so smoothly because we were able to clearly articulate the reasoning behind our proposed designs, and when agreeing or disagreeing with somebody else’s proposal, we objectively laid out reasons on why it would or would not work without being dismissive or rude. This experience reinforced the idea of good communciation being the foundation of all professional environments. I found myself overthinking a situation that was, in retrospect, quite simple. Through simple communication, my team was able to overcome our conflicts and meet our goal smoothly. Moving forward, I will be sure to communicate my ideas and opinions clearly while also taking into account my teammates’ ideas and situations, as it is important to be aware that I am not working alone.

situation: My team was tasked with creating a Rube Goldberg Machine (RGM) of our choice. The goal was to complete a simple task using multiple complicated tasks in a chain reaction. Each member would have 3 sections in the RGM and needed to have at least one unique element that was not present in another team members’ section.
task_action: We began with some basic research and taking inspiration from other RGMs that we saw on YouTube. This helped our understanding of our task and helped start the conversation around our brainstorm of our own unique ideas. We came up with a variety of tasks that are usually simple, such as making breakfast and getting ready in the morning. These simple tasks can be made more complicated to fulfil the requirements of a RGM. The other aspect of our task was to ensure we had a unique idea, so after seeing similar ideas from other groups, we had a further team brainstorm. Our new task was to complicate the simple task of making breakfast, but with a unique twist of using one of our team member’s pets. We approached the development of our RGM by breaking down the process into little steps, constantly thinking outside the box to make our RGM unique and stand out from the other groups. We all contributed to each other’s sections coming up with a range of creative ideas such as using our own pets in the RGM as well. For example, one member would use their birds by giving them food to eat off a plate which will lighten it and release a hot wheels car. I could use my cat by pointing a laser onto a button causing my cat to press it, activating an Arduino. The end result would be for the dog to receive treats, water and its favourite toy. I constantly encouraged and motivated my team to express their ideas no matter how big or small and I elaborated on their ideas in a respectful way, and encouraged them to be creative. I actively listened and provided positive feedback and suggestions to build on their ideas.
result: Ultimately, through the use of creative thinking skills and effectively communicating our individual ideas to the team, we were able to create a successful RGM that achieved our goal of feeding our dog. The project was well-received by our instructor and fellow classmates, which was a positive influence on the dynamics of the team. Our result was highly successful, even though we undertook this project as strangers. There was mutual respect and collaboration, and I believe my encouragement and support helped everyone feel included and empowered to contribute and be proud of our final product.
pfr: Throughout the project, I experienced a wide range of emotions such as excitement, frustration, and satisfaction. In the beginning, I was extremely excited and filled with anticipation about the possibility of meeting new people and I looked forward to the building a RGM together. However, as we began to brainstorm ideas, I started to feel frustrated due to the lack of progress and seeing that other teams were coming up with similar ideas to us. It was challenging to settle on one idea that was unique compared to other groups and interesting. I realized the importance of creativity when solving this problem. After a lot of brainstorming, we finally settled on the idea of feeding our dog using an RGM. But as we continued to think outside the box and came up with new ideas we slowly began to work better as a group as we understood our communication styles. For example, I realised my role in being a confident and encouraging peer who empowers more shy people to speak up and be heard in team discussion. In the end, I felt satisfied because I realised that even though at some points during our project timeline, there may be parts where we are discouraged, but by persevering and experimenting with different ideas, there will be innovative solution that I am proud of contributing to.
learning: Throughout the development of our RGM, I learnt several valuable lessons. Firstly, I learned the importance of patience and persistence when working on a team project, as it takes time and effort to come up with an innovative idea, and it is crucial to remain patient and not give up easily. Secondly, I realized the significance of effective communication skills in a team setting. Without clear communication, it can be challenging to coordinate efforts and make progress on the project. Going forward, I will prioritize improving my communication skills to be more effective in team projects. This means establishing deadlines for each person’s task earlier in the term and communicating with my tutor about any members who are not responding to the team’s messages. Finally, I realized that being encouraging is crucial in a team environment, and this determines the success of a project. We had to work together to design and build the RGM and our team avoided major disagreements and setbacks because we spoke to each other with kindness and respect and listened carefully to what we each had to say to ensure there was no confusion during communications. This streamlined the progression of our project. Without encouragement and kindness, there would not have been a collaborative environment. This is something I will take into future group projects. In conclusion, the experience of working on the group assignment taught me valuable lessons about creativity, communication, and teamwork. Going forward, I will work on improving my creativity, communication skills, and prioritizing teamwork to be more effective in group projects.

task_action: To approach rectifying our problem, a team discussion was held with each team member contributing possible solutions and rearrangements they had brainstormed. Then each arrangement of the machine was critically analysed and we worked on achieving an unanimous decision in which everyone was pleased with. This took perseverance as a team as many of us at the beginning of the discussion were sure our idea was the strongest, however, by staying open-minded and being flexible to change we were able to work out the best possible layout for our functions.
result: My team was able to unanimously decide upon the most effective layout of our individual events to achieve our main function and a smooth running machine. This result was a direct result of our shared determination to deliver the most suitable machine achievable in this course. We then could begin to conclude our detailed design concept and begin the construction of our machine.
pfr: The process of making critical decisions as a group with a goal of achieving an unanimous decision is always challenging as every individual has their own ideas and opinions on how the final project should work. I was thankful that my team was able to effectively communicate our individual ideas to each other in a professional capacity and practice patience, perseverance and flexibility. By remaining unbiased, we were able to listen to, critique and critically analyse each idea and discuss the effectiveness, room for error and creativeness of each one. This process demonstrated our growth in teamwork throughout this unit, as if this discussion had been held in the first few weeks, we would not have been able to communicate as well, reply with honest feedback and constructive criticism, or have the same level of trust and respect in one another which was undeniably transferred to a respect of each others ideas. I feel that by using all my engineering skills to date on teamwork and communication I was able to pitch my idea to the team in a more fluent and understandable method which highlights my personal growth in this unit.
learning: By approaching decision making in a methodical approach my team and I were able to reach a decision unanimously. This is attributed to staying unbiased and openminded in the process, persevering until a decision wad been made in the same session so each idea was fresh in our minds and sharing a common goal of creating the most effective machine we were able to deliver in a timely manner. This experience of making tough decisions around our overall event and function layout of our machine has demonstrated my teams positive and supportive group dynamic and reflects on our strong ability to work collaboratively. situation: For unit ENGG1050, the focus on the group project regarding the Rube Goldberg Model is a step-by-step process in which where the team’s progress is summarised in the weekly workshop through a 10-minute slideshow presentation. As a high-school graduate, I have been provided prior opportunities in preparing PowerPoint presentations and have adequate experience in making announcements in Year 12 class. However, the professional aspects involved in oral presentations are hugely different at Macquarie University. Expectations are high as the convenor for the workshop meeting has pointed out that speech as well as slide orientation needs to be concise and have a content structure. The concern regarding time constraints is strict as it is understood that real-life company meetings are not designed to suit the employee’s comfort. Students are trained to be flexible regardless of any interruption faced during a slideshow. For Week 11, it was my turn to present for Team A12. From certain feedback, I understood that the importance of visual representation is just as important as the content in each slide. For example, in one slide, a table format was displayed to show the before and after improvements that were made on RGM event reliability. Two different colours were assigned to separate the content before and after. Although the content was well-organised, the colour coordination was chosen poorly as the green-orange mix caused reading difficulty. Colour coordination comes naturally to a creative person. I find that I am lacking in this aspect as over the semester, my teammates have suggested other alternative methods to modify my RGM events to pass the reliability test threshold. As an aspiring engineering student, the quality to come up with original ideas is just as important as following your superior’s order. It defines capability to a certain extent.
task_action: There are dreamers, and then there are the realists. Both need each other to accomplish greater things in life. Back in Yr9, a poster needed to be designed for the WWII Holocaust. In a two-person group, one person is asked to type up the relevant content while the other had arrange the theme and images for the poster. The problem arose when almost all of the poster was composed of information. From this, I have understood the need for balance when compiling the 10 RGM events for Team A12. One member had his event ending with a water balloon being popped and the spilt water being collected in a bucket. To transition to the next event, a similar bucket element is required to zoom out of, but the member responsible for the said event has decided to change his focus from a pulley system to a projectile instead. Overall, the event order had to be re-arranged and this simple solution was suggested by a team member who got annoyed by a 20-minute quarrel that was wasted in zoom-meeting. The moral of this whole dilemma is that too much creative thinking can get on a realistic person’s last nerve.
result: For week 12, a group member who has avoided the role of the presenter was pointed out in Team A12’s group chat. Said person has eventually volunteered to make a slideshow but has clarified that it is not wise for him/her to speak as his words are not very fluent. The team has voted in favour that any marks denied from such an issue are not relevant to the tutors, but the speech needs to be shortened to meet the time limit of 10 minutes. The minute-taker assigned for week 12 was held responsible for timing the presenter’s speech duration. Through trial and error, 1600 words of content were shortened to 1180 to meet the requirement. In terms of the visual design of slides, a second opinion is advised by the Chairperson for Week 13 RGM Project Presentation.
pfr: Creativity is essential to bring out the originality centred around any tasks at hand. But it does not mean that others should prioritise the whims of one person to deny progression that is well established. Improvement is good, but it is a suggestion and not the only alternative sought after. Quick and efficient methods are just as valuable as a creative approach. If the end goal is to stand out and wow the audience, then might as well search out for RGM events in movie scenes. An oral presentation is most reliant on content, slides, and time constraint. Fluency is a hurdle that only makes it hard for the audience to understand what is being said. For that, practice is the only medicine. Accents can be mimicked with proper dedication.
learning: It is hard to accept rejection when a great idea is put aside for project completion. But if it irks that person so much, then bear the burden of taking on more responsibilities. Show that you are serious and are willing to go the extra mile for your selfishness in a group assignment. To quote Taylor Swift; “Haters gonna hate, shake it off!”

situation: When constructing our RGM events, we had some difficulty with creative designs, and communicating possible solutions for our individual events.
task_action: To overcome this problem, we first consulted with the rest of the team. In a team this should be the first step when you are presented with any problem.
