Each team member is constructing and conducting tests individually in their own workspaces, and it can be very hard to offer solutions when each team member can't physically see the construction and determine the cause of the problem. After consolidating with the team, if the issue persists, it is also helpful to search resources online for similar problems or alternative methods for solutions.
result: The result from communicating solutions with team members is a stronger team. Sharing ideas with other people is a useful way to expand creative thinking skills, and develop more creative solutions to problems. The longer a team works together, they tend to develop similar ways of thinking and generating solutions, which helps in understanding the problem a team member is proposing. It then becomes easier to conceive a solution in a way that the team member will be able to understand and succeed upon. Online resources can help the team member find inspiration to potentially solve their problem or other collective issues the team may have. Online resources (e.g. videos) provide the ability to visualise a similar solution to your given problem. This will make it easier for the team member to solve their problem, developing their problem solving skills further.
pfr: When doing something for the first time, it can be difficult to make up solutions to new problems you haven't encountered before. It can be even harder to make any of these solutions work, which was a problem my team encountered. Through the duration of the assembly and testing process of the RGM development, we encountered problems with reliability and finding creative solutions to the project brief. When we communicated these issues to the rest of the team, ideas were proposed and tested accordingly. It was found through this testing that some solutions were unattainable with the material and environmental limitations of each team member. When this happened, we also made sure to check online resources for potential solutions as well. Due to the popularity of RGM's, we were successfully able to find some potential solutions that we could adapt to our own circumstances, however some solutions could not be found and had to be eliminated from the final project.
learning: If the solution could not be found after this effort, we deemed it acceptable to try a different method for the RGM so valuable time wasn't spent on an unattainable action for the final project. While it is always good to strive for excellence, sometimes approaching a difficult problem with unsuitable solutions is not the ideal way to complete a project brief with a given deadline. Even if this means sacrificing the very creative and elaborate actions planned in the brainstorming phase of project development, for more simple creative solutions to reach a finished product. In this way, our final project would be successfully completed by each team member, however the scale of creativity of our actions had to be lessened slightly in order to produce this successful product.

situation: Our group needed to manage our time and resources to complete milestones for the final RGM.
task_action: Employing appropriate project management strategies to increase efficiency of both time and resources invested in the project. Clearly defined the goals and project scope early, and made sure everyone comprehended the project scope through using effective communication. Furthermore, we evaluated project risks such as scope creep and employed mitigation plans to lessen risks posed to the project. To ensure the completion of milestones by the deadline with maximum time and resource efficiency we employed time management strategies such as using the Priority Matrix software (based on the Eisenhower Method). In addition to Priority Matrix we used a Gantt chart to have a more comprehensive guide to key milestones in this project.
result: The result was efficient teamwork where time and resources were managed appropriately, which helped us greatly to avoid project risks and complete project milestones on time.
pfr: Without the aforementioned time and resource management strategies in place, project milestones were difficult to complete on time and to the desired standard. I feel that the time and resource management tools that our group collectively decided to utilize helped immensely with the success of our group. Priority Matrix software was chosen because of the well documented benefits to using the Eisenhower method. The Gantt chart was chosen due to it's popularity as a project management tool, and as a tool to further simplify the Gantt chart, especially when there were multiple overlapping tasks. Ultimately, we found that clearly defining the project scope and mitigating risks, in addition to using good project managment tools improved our overall success as a group.
learning: Through our groups experience using the aforementioned time and resource management tools, we learned the importance of simplifying complex problems. The experience of making the Gantt chart allowed us to appreciate the time and resource saving capabilities of simply having a comprehensive guide to key project milestones. During our time using Priority Matrix software, we found that clearly defining task priority, especially in the face of multiple overlapping tasks on the Gantt chart made tasks less overwhelming. Through this experience, I have come to value the importance of project management and the impact of good time/resource management tools.

situation: When approaching any engineering task, using data driven decision making is absolutely crucial. Collecting data in engineered structures allows engineers to have a clearer and scientifically supported understanding of their mechanism. By incorporating derived data into your decisions surrounding your product you will be able to produce a higher quality result. Through learning this during the ENGG1050 unit, the quality of our RGM machine was thus called into question when collecting data on the reliability of the machine to complete each individual function. We had many events in the function that originally had a low reliability score when tested 10 times. It was decided that we would need to have a discussion on how to improve these events and use our current data to assist our decisions.
task_action: Therefore, by utilising this method we held a team discussion on what areas of the questioned events was causing the weakness by analysing and assessing our current data. We next changed necessary variables in each event until the accuracy met the satisfaction of the entire team. This step was repeated a number of times to ensure the highest result was obtained, such as assessing whether a change in the weight of the ball, reinforcement of elements of the events or a multitude of things being incorporated simultaneously would produce the highest reliability score. When incorporating this tactic into our RGM machine my team and I were able to significantly improve our machine's accuracy and reliability, therefore increasing the overall quality of our product.
result: Through my team's shared desire to produce a high quality machine that could be reproducible due to high reliability scores we used our collection of data to effect our decisions of each individual event. This proved to be an incredibly efficient and effective tactic for our RGM. We are all very pleased with the new reliability results of our RGM with each event achieving at least 90% reliability.
pfr: The process of making critical data driven decisions as a group with a goal of achieving high reliability was trying and difficult at times, however, through working hard my team and I performed very well. I was thankful that my team and I were able to effectively communicate our ideas around what the data was reflecting, and what we could do to utilise this information in our decisions to each other in a professional capacity and practice patience, perseverance and flexibility. By remaining unbiased, we were able to listen to, critique and critically analyse data and discuss the effectiveness, weaknesses and ideas for improvement in reliability for each section. Our success in using data driven decision making is reflected through the smoothness of our filming stage which we were able to complete together in one group session.
learning: By approaching decision making in a methodical dat-driven approach my team and I were able to reach highly satisfying reliability and accuracy scores which filled us with confidence when entering our filming stage of the RGM. This is attributed to staying unbiased and openminded in the process, persevering until a decision wad been made in the same session so each idea was fresh in our minds and sharing a common goal of creating the most effective machine we were able to deliver in a timely manner. This experience of analysing data and thus making tough decisions around our overall event and function layout of our machine has demonstrated my teams positive and supportive group dynamic and reflects on our strong ability to work collaboratively. I feel that by using all of my engineering skills taught in this unit I was able to effectively analyse the data recorded to make beneficial decisions surrounding the future design of our RGM components with additional strength and understanding of how to effectively use data to aid design, thus developing a strong appreciation for the SPINE units that influenced my ability to achieve a strong final result in my group, particularly the 'Analysis' and 'Engineering Design' units.

topic: Trade-offs, judgment, and balance in resolution
situation: Throughout the second half of the semester, I have been unable to attend workshops as I had suddenly found employment during the break that required full-time attendance while training.
task_action: As my training for work now clashed with the time of the ENGG1050 workshop and my other classes, I had to make the right judgement on how to handle the situation and make trade-offs to achieve balance in my commitment to work and uni. As soon as I was aware of the fact that I had to attend my training full-time during when my classes would run, I had to make sure whether I could really commit to starting that job, as uni is my first priority. Initially, as was communicated to me, attending training meant I'd only have to miss the first two workshops and so I just let my team know of the situation and completed any work that needed to be done. I also stayed in contact with the team and talked to them regularly, especially before and after workshops to get caught up with everything. This way I could attend my work training while also not sabotaging my uni performance. As training finished, I learned that I'd have to do full-time consolidation for a few weeks as well. With the ENGG1050 workshop and my practicals that are hurdles, there was no way I could skip them all. So, after speaking with my manager I was able to obtain a few days off for my other mandatory practicals, and for the ENGG1050 workshop, as it wasn't a hurdle, I decided to continue with ensuring all the required work was being done, especially for the final RGM presentation.
result: By communicating effectively with my team and making the appropriate trade offs, I achieved a balance between work and uni. I can confidently say that our final RGM presentation is something our whole team can be proud of.
pfr: When I first got the new job offer, I was really proud of myself and excited to start, as the role was really good, had good pay and had room for growth in my career. However, I was feeling really anxious after learning that I'd need to attend full-time during training as I wanted to accept the role but uni was my first priority and if it jeopardised my studies, I'd have to reject the job offer. I was relieved, to find that training was only 4 weeks, so after the 2 weeks break, I'd only miss two workshops, which wasn't that bad. I was again stressing when I found out that consolidation was full-time too. My manager understood my situation and since I was meant to be a casual employee anyways, he gave me some leniency, but I thought it'd be best not to abuse it and only take days off for my mandatory uni classes, as I felt like not attending the workshops had zero impact on the final project as I was communicating with everyone regularly and I was watching all the lectures and doing the work, so I wasn't missing out on much from there either.
learning: I learned that good communication goes a long way. Even though I wasn't attending the workshops, simply being able to communicate my situation and working around that with the team, we overcame this little obstacle. I also learned how to make the right judgement in stressful situations to achieve balance. I obviously prioritised uni over work at this stage of my life, but being able to balance both out without too much strain on my studies is really great.

situation: During our team project, I was assigned the task of constructing a Rube Goldberg machine for our RGM project for ENG1050. Our goal was to create an elaborate, functional machine that would demonstrate various scientific principles in an entertaining way.
task_action: My task was to ensure effective collaboration among team members, manage the project timeline, and oversee the design and construction process. It was crucial to maintain a professional and respectful environment where everyone felt valued and motivated to contribute their best. I facilitated regular progress meetings to track our advancements, address any challenges, and provide support where needed. I actively listened to team members' suggestions and incorporated their feedback into the design process. I encouraged brainstorming sessions and promoted a culture of collaboration, where every team member felt comfortable expressing their opinions. I also encouraged the team to maintain a clean and organised workspace, promoting professionalism and efficiency which helped our team to work effectively and coherently.
result: As a result of my professional behaviour and effective teamwork, we successfully created a Rube Goldberg machine that met all the project requirements. The project not only demonstrated scientific principles but also showcased our team's ability to collaborate and work together in a professional manner.
pfr: Reflecting on the importance of professional behavior, it is crucial to maintain a high standard of conduct in various situations, whether in the workplace or in professional interactions. Professional behavior encompasses traits such as respect, integrity, accountability, and effective communication. Which I personally used in the development and progress of the RGM with the my fellow peers which helped create a strong bond with my peers. A personal reflection of my mine which I would like to add is the lack of professional behaviour I had when working which usually led to incomplete projects which would have affected me majorly in this project but as I begin to start being more professional I was able to create a developed RGM design.
learning: I have learned that maintaining professionalism during challenging situations is crucial. It is essential to remain calm and composed, even in stressful or conflict-ridden scenarios. Responding to adversity with professionalism and resilience can help in finding constructive solutions and resolving conflicts more effectively. In the future, I will continue to emphasise the importance of professional behaviour and encourage individuals to be mindful of their actions and their impact on others. I will strive to provide guidance and support in promoting professionalism, effective communication, empathy, and ethical conduct in professional environments.

situation: Our team encountered a situation where my friend forgot to submit a weekly assessment, which could have resulted in a significant loss of marks. However, when questioned about it, he took responsibility and honestly admitted that he had accidentally messed up the times.
task_action: In response to the situation, we decided to address the issue as a team. We approached my friend with understanding and discussed the importance of accountability and timely submissions. Recognizing the potential impact on our overall grades, we collectively decided to take immediate action.
result: By acknowledging his mistake and taking accountability, my friend displayed a commendable level of honesty and integrity. This incident served as a valuable learning experience for the entire team, highlighting the significance of punctuality and responsibility in meeting deadlines. As a team, we quickly emailed our teacher to explain the situation and requested an opportunity to complete the weekly assessment with minimal penalty. This incident not only strengthened our sense of unity but also emphasized the importance of effective communication and support within the team.
pfr: The situation we faced when my friend forgot to submit the weekly assessment initially seemed overwhelming and without clear solutions. As a group, we felt daunted by the task at hand. However, we approached the problem systematically, documenting our decisions at each stage, which allowed us to navigate through the complexity and reach a consensus on the design.
learning: The incident with the weekly assessment highlighted the importance of taking accountability when it comes to our work in general. By acknowledging mistakes and taking responsibility, we can learn from them and improve ourselves as individuals and as a team. Accountability plays a vital role in our personal and professional growth. When we take accountability for our actions, we demonstrate integrity, ownership, and a commitment to learning from our mistakes. In the context of our team, holding ourselves accountable for our individual responsibilities ensures that we can trust and rely on one another. It fosters a sense of mutual respect and collaboration, as we understand the impact our actions have on the overall team's success. Looking to the future, this experience has reinforced the significance of robust and structured decision-making. It has shown us that approaching problems with a systematic and organized mindset can lead to more efficient and effective solutions. We now understand the impact that well-informed decisions can have on our collective success, and we will strive to apply this approach to future challenges we encounter. Embracing accountability will not only contribute to our individual success but also strengthen our team's ability to achieve our collective goals and excel in future endeavors.

situation: The team was struggling with communication revolving around team meetings and assignment of the minute taking and writing the reflection. Due to unforeseen circumstances, the rotation of the roles had been thrown off and uncertainty remained about who was responsible for what role
task_action: Undergoing a brainstorming session; forming a small working group with the problem statement clearly articulated and using the gallery method of brainstorming we devised several viable options. Subsequently, we evaluated each of the suggested options and rank them in order of importance, based on the parameters (such as weight, complexity, and manufacturability). After intervention from our tutor and a unified team understanding of the improvements needed to be made, the team organised for two people to be given their respective roles of writing minutes and the reflection with additional time given immediately after the Monday class to address the specific topic of reflection and the quality of the minutes.
result: The result was we were granted the leniency to resubmit our previous weeks reflection and improved upon some of our previous marks. We also had a more structured understanding of who was responsible for what role leading into this week.
pfr: The initial problem was quite frustrating. I'd had to take on the role of minute taker and writing the reflection for both of the previous weeks when it hadn't been submitted by other team members. However, after the intervention from our tutor and a proper team discussion, we were able to share the burden as a team and work together towards improving the quality of the work.
learning: Because I'd been resistant to this discussion and instead resolved to trying to figure it out on my own I'd actual made the problem harder for myself and very well could have worked with my team instead of being frustrated by them. An approach of the team vs the problem would have worked much better initially than just myself vs the problem and the team.

topic: Trade-offs, judgment, and balance in resolution
situation: One requirement of ENGG1050 is to hold weekly meetings to work on our RGM machine. This poses a challenge due to the varying schedules of our team members, where only a few members can consistently make it to the zoom meeting. The question arises of how we are going to make this work.
task_action: Keeping every team member up to date and on track with tasks ensures the ongoing development of our project. Consistency and communication is important not only to execute this project, but to do it to a high standard. With this in mind, we knew that we had to work with our unaligned schedules. Some questions that arise include how we would work with our unpredictable schedules. How would we make up for the missing members? Our solution includes using zoom, where a delegated chairperson would assign each person’s weekly work to be completed. Whatsapp would be used to relay this information, so that the remaining members are informed of their responsibilities for the week.
result: This is a trade-off of not having a set time for a live discussion, for our busy schedules. This is made up with the whatsapp group chat where no information is lost, only delayed. This ensures the balance of the work, and creates the expectation for everyone to complete the work despite meetings not being attended by everyone. The scheduling issue for each meting has been resolved and now everyone will be up to date thanks to utilising online resources.
pfr: One disadvantage of this system may be that clarification available in the zoom may not be available in the whatsapp, leading to an inaccuracy in the conveying of information and the feeling of being left out in the group. Also and not being able to have a live discussion as a team as a whole may hinder or delay the development of ideas and solutions thus being less efficient. This can lead to worries of aspects of our project not being acheived on time. However this trade off of efficiency for tending to other aspects of our lives works for our specific team where we are all satisfied with the distribution and communication of work. Us all being busy uni students has allowed this system to work as we can have empathy and respect for the fact that we all have our own lives, and one individuals schedule is bound to differ from the next’s.
learning: This situation can reflect other situations of our lives, where we have to balance work and life for our well being, in fact this may be seen across all other future units in our academic careers where putting energy into other aspects of our lives eg. health, social lives, may help us achieve higher grades in a way doing more work can't. There are always different combinations of trade offs that will work for each specific scenario and achieve the best outcomes for everyone and it is up to the individual to make that judgement.

situation: The past twelve weeks have consisted primarily of elaborate and fluid teamwork to complete our Rube Goldberg Machine. Having had the ability to work amongst a group of five, it is without doubt that we all come from different backgrounds and life experiences. Different personalities and different ways of thinking can complicate the fluidity of a team. I was faced with the requirement to develop my communication and teamworking skills to enhance my performance within the group; and to produce work that is consistent with my team.
task_action: Understanding my strengths and weaknesses was the first step in developing my teamwork and communication skills. I completed a LinkedIn learning course on interpersonal communication to broaden my understanding of forms of communication, and their importance in professional environments. Acknowledging that our group project required collaborative effort to produce an effective and fluid machine, I suggested the use of an external platform such as WhatsApp to maintain communication amongst each other. Through further discussion, we set group rules which would ensure equality and maintain open communication within the group. Additionally, I completed the DISC and OCEAN analysis tests and compared the results amongst my group within the initial weeks of our project. Adopting the skills demonstrated through the LinkedIn course, I suggested we utilise our discovered strengths, whilst also working on our weaknesses, to be able to perform to our best capabilities. Rotating everyone through each role weekly allowed the opportunity to enhance our individual weaknesses.
result: By using WhatsApp to communicate throughout the week, we ensured that all our designated tasks were completed in a timely manner. This ensured that project checkpoints adhered to our timeline and reduced the risk of failure to deliver. It allowed us to seek guidance and/or provide support where required. We were kept informed and were able to keep on top of any missed tasks and or need for change. Furthermore, by rotating through a new role each week, I was able to foster an environment of growth in which supported both myself and my team members to utilize our strengths, whilst also working on our weaknesses. Developing and utilising my communication strategies within my team allowed us to collaboratively produce a functioning and fluid Rube Goldberg Machine.
pfr: As a current Registered Nurse working in Oncology, I have developed an understanding as to the importance of communication within the workplace, however this is limited to patient interactions. Although I may interact with my colleagues, teamwork is not broadly used within the workplace due to the nature of the occupation. Accustomed to working independently, I found difficulty in learning the dynamics of working in a team and understanding my role as an individual amongst five in a group. Through my experience in the ENGG1050 course, I have developed an appreciation for the immense significance of communication in teamworking environments. I feel that I am better equipped to communicate openly within a team, whilst also being able to foster collaboration to transform a group of differing individuals into a team.
learning: The transformative effect communication and teamwork has on group projects is immeasurable; challenges can be made opportunities, driving innovation, efficiency, and success. I have learnt that active listening, adaptability, and consideration of backgrounds fosters an environment of collaboration, trust, and growth. I recognise that by embracing diverse perspectives and open communication, I can cultivate success and meaningful growth within myself as an aspiring engineer. I acknowledge that I have yet to refine my expressive skills, in learning how to better express my thoughts and ideas within a group. I feel that in the future, I will be able to adopt my interpersonal communication skills and my teamworking skills to work harmoniously amongst others to produce optimal results in future group projects.

situation: In the week 7 STGA I had the opportunity to present along side two team mates to half the ENGG1050 tutor group.
task_action: Each team in ENG1050 were required to present their RGM to half the tutor group. We structured the presentation to match the marking rubric and spit up the sections evenly, aiming for three minutes each team member with 1 minute remaining for Q&A. Finally, we came together and practiced a few times before presentation. We managed to keep to our 10 minute limit.
result: The team did deliver in week 7, although there was constructive feedback directed at my presentation section. I'll pay closer attention to timing in our next presentation.
pfr: Any form of speaking in front of a crowds is a challenge - even in a casual setting. I didn't know what to expect going in to the week 7 STGA, and that unknown can add to the angst. How many people will I be presenting to?, how will they react?, Will I deliver for the team?
learning: I've always had a fear of public speaking and it's clear to me now that this fear was misplaced. It's not the fear of public speaking, it's the fear of embarrassing myself in front of a crowd. This semester I've had practise recovering from mistakes in my presentations and received invaluable feedback from my tutors. Now that I've practiced presenting I know that when the time comes to do the same in a professional setting, it'll be okay.

situation: I was part of a team project during my final semester in high school. Our task was to develop a comprehensive marketing plan for a fictitious product and present it to a panel of industry professionals. This project represented a significant portion of our final grade and required us to work closely together over several weeks.
task_action: Our team had to divide the project into various aspects, including market research, product development, pricing strategy, and promotional activities. Each team member was responsible for leading one aspect of the plan while contributing to others. I was assigned the role of coordinating our promotional strategy.
result: Our teamwork and effective communication paid off. Our group delivered a well-coordinated and comprehensive marketing plan during the presentation. We received positive feedback from both our professor and the industry professionals. Our project received the highest grade in the class, and we were commended for our teamwork, adaptability, and professionalism.
pfr: Team members often feel a sense of satisfaction when they successfully collaborate and achieve their goals. Accomplishing tasks together and receiving positive feedback can be rewarding.Achieving a high grade or receiving recognition for a job well done can instill a sense of pride in one's work and contributions.
learning: This experience taught me the importance of interpersonal skills in achieving successful outcomes in team projects. It highlighted the significance of clear communication, collaboration, and problem-solving in achieving our common goals.

situation: I was in one of several groups in a Maths competition in which we had to solve questions of varying difficulty for a prize consisting of a basket of sweets.
task_action: We as a group selected several questions of varying type and difficulty, and then attempted to solve them separately within two minutes. After the two minutes were up, we put together our answers and determined who was more suited to specific types and difficulties, and split up the work accordingly.
result: The result was that we were able to work with increased efficiency, with multiple questions being solved at a time by the person most capable of solving them quickly and correctly.
pfr: The task at hand was proving to be difficult as we were expected to coordinate with one another and solve questions of varying difficulty despite not knowing what level each person was that. By attempting to solve the same questions and showing one another our answers, we as a group were each able to determine what level the others were at. With this information, we were able to best allocate questions to the person most capable of solving them.
learning: By choosing to spend time determining what the mathematical ability of each member was at the very beginning, we were able to split the work between us with each member getting questions they were capable of doing. Through this experience, I have learnt the importance of selecting the right individuals for the right job. In the future, if I am ever in a situation where I must delegate tasks to a group of people, I will make sure to determine what their capabilities are and split up the work accordingly.

situation: During the tense environment of my 12th-grade final exam, I was positioned next to a copycat girl. Initially, her subtle glances at my paper didn't bother me much, as I valued concentrating on my own task. After hours, her pestering grew annoying. She kept requesting me to repeat my answers quietly. To protect my academic integrity, I cautioned her to fear the examiner's keen eye because expulsion was guaranteed if he saw us. Though severe, my words didn't discourage her. Then suddenly she boldly slid my paper across the desk into the dangerous no-man's land between us. My heart raced between right and obsessive craving for an easy way out as I watched my hard-earned work teeter towards deceit. My nerve-wracking choice determined my fate and character.
task_action: My tolerance for the girl's flagrant plagiarism on my paper was becoming thin. I asked her calmly but firmly to stop because her behaviour was unfair to me and violated the standards of honesty and academic integrity that should be upheld during tests. With every word, I made an effort to emphasise the importance of honesty, and our academic career should be a reflection of our genuine abilities, not a mere facade based on dishonesty. I spoke about the moral obligation we had to uphold to both the responsibilities we carried as students and the moral duty we owed to ourselves and our education. She kept trying to ignore me, but I was adamant that I would uphold these principles. I came to the realisation that our behaviour in the test room would define who we are as people more so than the grade we obtained. This was more than just an intellectual test; it was also a moral character test. And I was determined to do it while upholding my moral principles.
result: My pulse raced as the teacher's attention focused on our desk. Surprisingly audaciously, the girl seated next to me charged that I had taken her paper and placed it in the center. I was called out in front of the entire class as being a dishonest student. The most painful part of my friends' shock was watching them try to share this bogus story with the friend they knew. The humiliation pierced faith with a profound, knife-like wound. However, I refused to back down and said the truth. The trick was eventually exposed by the teacher, and justice was done. Although the humiliation hurt, it strengthened my resolve to be honest and ethical, and my friends gradually came to realise the reality. And that girl had been expelled for the final exam.
pfr: The shock of being falsely accused by the girl who had been copying my paper left me feeling utterly humiliated and embarrassed in front of both my teacher and classmates. In those tense moments, I watched as the cloud of suspicion hung over me, casting doubt on my integrity. After proving myself innocent, and as the real story unfolded, the weight of embarrassment lifted, and understanding washed over the faces of my classmates. They realized that I had been a victim of deceit, not a perpetrator of dishonesty. This experience left an indelible mark on me. It reinforced my belief in the importance of ethics and honesty in every aspect of life. It served as a reminder that social responsibility is not just a concept but a vital practice. In that classroom, I learned that we should all be steadfast in our commitment to honesty, integrity, and responsibility, for they are the pillars that uphold a just and honorable society. This is obvious that our integrity is part of our social responsibility because many people will suffer as a result of our actions.
learning: This exam coping event in my life taught me a valuable lesson, instilling in me the indisputable value of ethics, honesty, and societal duty. It was a turning point in my life that inspired a lifelong dedication to these ideals and a strong desire to inspire others to embrace them as well. I determined that day that I would never, ever compromise my own honesty, even in the face of tragedy. Being genuine to oneself, I realised, is a beacon of light that can guide us through life's harshest storms.But the lesson went beyond my actions. I realised it was my responsibility to champion these ideas in the world around me. I became an advocate for integrity, attempting to set a good example and inspire everyone around me to follow suit. This incident became a pillar of my values, a story I would tell others to emphasise the pervasiveness of ethics, honesty, and social duty. I realised that these values were not simply abstract ideas, but the actual foundation of a just and healthy society. I remained firm in my commitment to these ideals over the years, believing that by cultivating a culture of ethics and accountability, we can all contribute to a brighter, more honourable world, one person and one decision at a time.

situation: A project involved constructing a new house, but we faced challenges in coordinating different tasks and managing the construction timeline.
task_action: Tasked with overseeing the project, we organized a project planning session with the construction team. We outlined specific tasks such as foundation work, framing, electrical, plumbing, and interior finishing. We assigned responsibilities to team members based on their expertise and availability.
result: By breaking down the project into distinct tasks and assigning roles, we streamlined the construction process. Each team member knew their responsibilities, leading to efficient task execution. As a result, the construction stayed on schedule, and the house was completed within the expected time period. This experience highlighted the importance of clear task distribution and effective project management in achieving successful outcomes in construction projects.
pfr: When I set out to choose make sushi as my part time job, I felt a mix of excitement and uncertainty. Sushi has always been a favorite cuisine of mine, and the idea of making it myself was both interesting and daunting. The process appeared complicated, involving precise steps from rice preparation to rolling techniques and slicing fish even more. Before I started to make sushi, I had done a position for 3 months that required me to prepare steamed rice and other materials such as chicken patty and tuna salad as well as chopping veggies like cucumber and lettuce. I realised the importance of practice and attention to detail that making sushi requires a bunch of basic skills that I have never grasped in my life. As I delved into sushi-making about the inari which is a sushi made with bean curd, my Initial attempts were a bit clumsy, but I persevered, learning from each try. Breaking down the process into manageable steps, like choosing different ingredients and perfecting rice seasoning, helped me improve over time.
learning: This experience highlighted the value of patience and step-by-step learning, similar to the merit-based approach in decision-making. Just as sushi ingredients harmonize to create a balanced flavour, I understood the significance of balance in facing challenges. I'll carry these lessons forward, embracing gradual improvement and seeking harmony in various aspects of life. In the future, I'll approach new skills with the understanding that progress takes time. Just as sushi-making requires practice to achieve perfection, I'll apply patience and balance to achieve success in my future career.

situation: one of the final exercises of one of the worksheet for the arduino module was that we needed to program a game using a 7 segment display. there would be a top cycle and a bottom cycle and when the two collided and a button was pressed at the same time a led needed to light up. The problem was that the starting segments for the cycles needed to be random, but if you would let the segments just be random you would have a 50 percent change of having a situation where you cannot win the game.
task_action: Programming requires you to go through ideas step by step (especially during debugging). As such, i took the approach of beginning with programming a fully deterministic version of the game (same beginning segments always) and slowly adding more randomness while making sure that i didn't introduce the unwinnable situations untill i couldn't add any more randomness.
result: The result was that the game was not fully random, since that would result into unwinnable situations. However, I did add as much randomness as I could so that the game was still not deterministic. This resulted into me getting the points for the exercise.
pfr: At first when i encountered the problem i felt frustrated. This was becuase i had the idea my program was working perfectly as intented and i suddenly could not win the game i was playing. I reset the arduino many times and every time i would encounter a game i constantly wouldn't be able to press the button to win. At this point i had no idea that there could be unwinnable cycles and the thought of my program not working as it should was confusing to me. However, after calming down and patiently writing down the cycles i was encountering I slowly figured out that my program was actually working fine, it was just that some cycles are unwinnable. When i actually knew the problem and could now actually fix what was going on that made me feel better. As programmers it is easy to quickly get frustrated with your program and ragequit, but by slowly and methodically writing down your observations and analyzing them we can better figure out where we went wrong.
learning: I have been programming for more than 5 years by now and this situation has again proved to me that I should slow down a bit when trying to make a program. If i slowly entered the randomness into the program i would have known immediately where the unwinnable cycles came from and it would have saved me an hour of debugging and observation. Instead i made my program fully random from the start and then had to backtrack to find my mistake. This way of doing things step by step can at times be annoying and feel unnecessary, but we only appreciate doing it like that when the opposite it actively causing us problems.

learning: This experience taught me the power of effective prioritization and focus. It was a reminder that with the right approach, even seemingly overwhelming tasks can be successfully completed. situation: We needed to create a game from start to finish in the span of a weekend.

We settled on a short, single-player platformer in which the player could control the direction of gravity to manipulate their environment.
result: By dividing the workload of the project between the two people according to their respective skills, we were able to produce a finished game that played to the strengths of each person involved in its development. My team member, who was tasked with creating the art and assets for the game, was also happy with this decision as it necessitated simple and modular graphics that could be used to build a 2D game.
learning: This task required quick and reasoned decision-making and time management in order to plan and complete the project in such a short period of time. ACTION: I looked for answers on why I may have been so unable to concentrate and do well in high school, this lead me to a psychiatrist that I could speak to about my troubles and get help with how to manage the things I found difficult about school.
result: I was diagnosed with ADHD and shifted my thinking from “I’m not smart” to “I just have a different way of thinking”. I sought out strategies that worked for ADHD learning and implemented them in my learning journey. I believed that I could do it, and so I did. I graduated from the college with an average of 88, was asked to do a speech at the graduation and was presented with a Letter of Commendation from the director of the college.
pfr: I was very scared to attend university, I was almost sure I would fail and comments from family members only seemed to back up that state of mind. Simultaneously, I felt determined, almost defiant. I wanted to do well, so I was going to shift my attitude, learn new skills and succeed. I came into the experience with an open mind, knowing that I would try anything to make sure that this was a positive experience for me.
learning: I know now that I am not incapable, I just need to have a positive attitude, a willingness to think in ways I haven’t tried before, and a desire to succeed. Every little thing I learn, makes learning the next thing just a little bit easier. Wanting to learn, rather than just wanting to pass, is the most important thing that someone going to university can keep in mind. I’ve heard too many people say “P’s get degrees”, but I know that for me to succeed, I need to care about what I’m learning, I need to prioritize it and I need to put the things I learn into practice over and over until they make sense.

topic: The impact of engineering on society and the environment
situation: Engineering has had a profound and far-reaching impact on both society and the environment. It has played a vital role in shaping the modern world, contributing to both progress and challenges. Here, we will explore the various impacts that engineering has had on society and the environment.
task_action: The actions taken by engineers or overall, the impact of engineering on society and the environment, has been clearly shown, as engineers themselves design, construct and maintain the systems, buildings and technologies that enhance societies quality of life. Infrastructure development, healthcare advancements, energy generation and efficiency, are among a few of the impacts engineering has had on society. Engineering’s influence on the environment exhibits a diverse range of impacts, covering both favorable and the adverse aspects. Detrimental outcomes of engineering on the environment include pollution, deforestation, and the generation of waste, among other adverse effects. As well as, engineering also yields beneficial impacts, such as the promotion of renewable energy, the development of sustainable infrastructure, and improvements in energy efficiency, are among many positive contributions. In order to improve connection and facilitate the efficient movement of people and products, infrastructure development engineers have constructed essential infrastructures including roads, bridges, and transportation systems. Medical device, diagnostic, treatment, and outcome improvements have all improved thanks to engineering innovations in healthcare. Engineers have created and improved energy sources like solar, wind, and hydraulic power sources, which have led to the clean and more effective production of energy. THE NEGATIVE IMPACTS ENGINEERING HAS HAD ON THE ENVIRONMENT: Industrial operations, transportation, and energy production have had a significant negative impact on the environment, contaminating the air and water supplies, endangering human health, and degrading ecosystems. Some engineering projects call for the development of industrial and urban areas, which has resulted in habitat degradation and deforestation, endangering biodiversity. The majority of engineering projects have all led to the production of solid and hazardous waste, both of which are harmful to human health and ecosystems. THE POSITIVE IMPACTS ENGINEERING HAS HAD ON THE ENVIRONMENT: Having developed and promoted alternative energy sources like solar, wind, and hydropower, we as a society are using fewer fossil fuels and emitting fewer greenhouse gas emissions. Engineering has also resulted in significant advancements in the energy efficiency of industries, transportation, and infrastructure, lowering energy consumption and having a less negative impact on the environment. Engineers are always coming up with new and better ways to build a building with sustainability in mind, including green building techniques, efficient transportation methods, and eco-friendly building materials.
result: The effects of engineering on society and the environment are quite varies. Through technical advancements, economic expansion, and healthcare innovations, it has improved society’s quality of life. Although, it has also brought forth problems for the environment, such as pollution, climate change, and resource depletion. Engineers are putting more emphasis on sustainable solutions to lessen these negative impacts and creating a more balanced future for society as well as the environment.
pfr: When I first learned about how engineering has impacted society and the environment, I had a lot of thoughts about both positive and negative, about how engineering has impacted the world. On one hand, I feel a sense of pride in the remarkable achievements of engineers in improving the quality of life for countless of people. Engineering had brought us, conveniences (roads, transport, and many more), increased access to information, and improved healthcare, which has positively impacted the way of living for society. Although, I also experience a sense of guilt, there is a growing awareness of the negative consequences of engineering on the environment. The production and disposal or electronic waste, depletion of natural resources, and the contribution to climate change are some of the environmental consequences that engineering has inadvertently worsened.
learning: To address these challenges, engineers must adopt a comprehensive and ethical mindset to handle these challenges. Sustainable techniques are crucial, including developing eco-friendly products and infrastructure, cutting waste, and utilizing renewable energy sources. Finding creative ways to reduce the harmful effects of engineering also requires encouraging collaboration between engineers, legislators, and environmental experts. Engineers should also constantly educate themselves on the latest developments in environmentally friendly technologies and promote ethical practices withing businesses and industries. By integrating sustainability principles into engineering education and professional development, we can ensure that future engineers prioritize environmental consciousness in their work.

situation: Prioritising an assessment task that needs to be done very quickly and worth more than other assignments when I have many assessments due at once.
task_action: Writing down all current assignments due in order of what was due first, then writing a seperate list of what was worth more, comparing what same assessment appeared first on each list. After this I was able to begin on the assignments that needed most attention first.
result: The result was being able to finish the assignment in a timely manner to be able to have enough time work on other assignments using prioritisation to see what needed more attention, furthermore increasing overall marks.
pfr: At first looking at the large amount of assignments at one time was very overwhelming and put me into a state of procrastination, which made me lose time on each assessment task, but by ranking each assignment in terms of what needed more attention based on when due and the weighting of the assignment, I was able to prioritise the most important ones first and made it less intimidating to get started on the work.
learning: I was able to use this ranking method to improve time I had for each assignment and it made me less intimidated to begin, making hard assessments that much easier. Through this experience, prioritisation of certain assessments quickened the time taken, taking off stress especially when there are multiple assignments needing to be done in a strict timeframe, in contrast, without this method procrastination was more frequent, leaving less time for assessments and jeopardising marks.

situation: 2 people from our group withdrew from the unit, leaving the group with only 3 members.
task_action: We needed to decide which elements of the project were the most important to complete, knowing that some aspects would need to be sacrificed as we did not have enough people to complete the entire project. We organised a group meeting outside of class time to delegate the most important tasks amongst ourselves. We also discussed which aspects of the project were the least important, and hence which tasks would only be worked on if the most important parts were completed with time to spare.
result: We each made a commitment to dedicate time to complete our sections in order not to let the rest of the group down, and get the best mark possible. We decided that finer details in the model such as stairs, rooftop spaces and landscaping would not be prioritised until the majority of the model and report were completed to a high standard.
pfr: It was quite daunting knowing that our group had 2 less members than every other group and I was not sure that we would be able to complete everything to a high standard. This made me feel very overwhelmed as I am a high achieving student and am not comfortable with submitting work that does not meet requirements and expectations. As a result of this, I overloaded myself with work to try and make up for the absence of other people in the group and this made me feel quite stressed.
learning: Through this process I have learned how important delegation is, as well as knowing your own limits. After allocating various parts of the project to the two other members in the group, the task felt much more achievable as it no longer felt like the entire assignment was resting on my shoulders. It also taught me that sometimes you can't do everything, and that it's important to prioritise your own wellbeing, rather than attempting to complete something that is designed for 5 people (not for 3).

situation: In a group of 5 people in the civil engineering class, 2 dropped out at the last minute and one teammate unable to come in for 2 weeks whilst during the building and designing of project stage.
task_action: The remaining 2 group members had to work outside of class hours and messaged after hours about dividing the workload into two. It was decided after building most of the house in class for one to take the model home and complete that. We found that was more practical for one team member to finish the remaining work as they lived much closer and was getting picked up. The other team member would not have been able to do it effectively as they caught the train and live further away, so they agreed for the other to work on the presentation only and do the pictures for the model. Another action that was done is speak to unit convenor to make sure they were aware of the situation and this resulted in them granting amnesty that reassured the remaining team.
result: The result was that the work was effectively divided after consideration of facts and the strong time constraints. A happy medium was found between the 2 teammates once the 3rd was able to do some work.
pfr: the situation seemed pretty bad in the moment but however when the team member and i went over the actual work left to be done, it seemed all we had to do was divide the workload carefully based on some factors to make it as easy and fair as possible. The solution was helped by the unit convenors who reassured us if we didn't finish due to 3 less people working on it we would be marked fairly considering the situation.
learning: We found that, if you break stuff down into units and ask for opinions and help of the experts, things will seem a lot less daunting and able to be done. Through that experience, even with less team members than expected, work can be made to be not overwhelming when devised milestones are done and work is divided up the best as possible.

topic: Perseverance, urgency and will to deliver, resourcefulness and flexibility
situation: During the transition from high school to university, I found myself at a pivotal moment in my personal life/journey. Uncertainty surrounded me as I was unsure as to what career path I would choose or what I was destined to do. This period of induction had a significant impact on my mental wellbeing, as the idea of potentially wasting valuable years weighed heavily on me. The shift from high school to university life proved to be an arduous challenge that demanded introspection and determination. In order to embark on a path of self-discovery and personal growth, I made the decisive choice to pursue engineering by enrolling in four engineering subjects. This step marked a crucial millstone in my career journey of self-discovery, personal growth and success. Using the STAR framework
task_action: In order to navigate this uncertain period in my life, I realized the need for a well-organized pan. Seeking guidance from academic counsellors, mentors, and career advisors became a priority for me. Additionally, I actively engaged in exploring various academic fields and extracurricular activities by attending workshops, seminars and engaging with media resources like television shows such as ‘Drive to Survive’ to gain insight into potential career paths. Understanding that personal growth often requires venturing beyond one’s comfort zones, I made the decision to enroll in four engineering unit's this semester as an opportunity to potentially transfer degrees despite it not being a requirement for my current field of study in Speech and hearing Sciences. This choice was driven by my determination to explore different aspects of engineering while challenging myself academically. Recognizing the urgency of the situation at hand, I embraced taking immediate action as crucial for making informed decisions about my future endeavors. Furthermore, I displayed adaptability and resourcefulness by utilizing various online resources, books and seeking guidance from knowledgeable individuals to enhance my understanding of engineering subjects. I also remained openminded to new opportunities and ideas while exploring additional hobbies such as playing the violin that would contribute to my personal growth. Notably, watching the Formula 1 has solidified my passion for this career path and further empowered me to adjust and thrive in ever-changing circumstances when required.
result: Through my journey of self-discovery and personal growth I embarked on a transformative path by transferring to an engineering program. This decision allowed me to delve into the diverse world of an engineering, collaborate with peers from various engineering backgrounds, and gain a deeper understanding of this field. I actively sought clarity regarding my passions and career aspirations which has a positive impact not only on my mental well-being but also affirmed that choosing this career was the right choice for me. It became evident that my purpose in life extended beyond any specific career path; rather it centered around my dedication to continuous learning and personal development as an individual- a realization that becomes clearer with each passing year.
pfr: The transition from high school to university was a time of immense uncertainty and self-doubt. I often felt overwhelmed by the pressure to make life-altering decisions, causing anxiety and decisiveness about whether my choices were truly the right ones. However, choosing to pursue engineering courses became a pivotal moment in my journey. It served as a reminder that sometimes-taking bold risks and embracing urgency can result in significant personal development, leading to the achievement of lifelong aspirations and dreams.
learning: From this experience, I have come to understand that life’s purpose is not always a fixed destination but rather an ongoing journey of self-discovery and personal growth. It requires qualities such as perseverance, urgency and adaptability in order to navigate the uncertainties that arise. By being resourceful and flexible during this transitional period, I was able to gain valuable insights about myself. Moving forward, I aim to apply the lessons learned from embracing uncertainty, taking decisive action, and remaining open to new opportunities as I continue to explore and define my path in life.

situation: In my digital media course, the task was to create a multimedia project that would effectively convey a social issue using a combination of images, videos, audio, and text.
task_action: Here's how I approached the task using the STAR framework: * SITUATION: The project was multifaceted, demanding the application of critical thinking to navigate its complexity. * TASK: My task was to select a relevant social issue, strategize how to present it using multimedia elements, and ensure that the narrative flowed logically and engagingly. * ACTION: Engaging critical thinking, I meticulously researched and identified a suitable social issue. Forming a team, we outlined a comprehensive approach. Throughout the project, I critically evaluated each media element's alignment with the narrative and purpose. I structured a storyboard that logically connected images, audio, and text to captivate and sustain viewers' attention. Critical thinking played a crucial role in each decision – from sequencing visuals to harmonizing audio narration. Every choice was underpinned by thoughtful analysis.
result: The outcome was a multimedia project that effectively communicated the chosen social issue. The narrative was cohesive, guiding the audience through the issue's intricacies. The selection of visuals, paired with an appropriate mix of audio and text, contributed to the project's impact. The project not only fulfilled the assignment's requirements but also encouraged viewers to engage their critical thinking, stimulating reflection on the social issue's implications. Furthermore, the process of applying critical thinking strengthened our team's collaboration. Carefully evaluating each media element's relevance sparked insightful discussions, resulting in a unified final product that transcended individual contributions. Through this experience, I recognized the pivotal role of critical thinking in multimedia creation. As I move forward, the skills I've acquired will empower me to approach future projects with a strategic mindset. The insights gained have equipped me to meticulously plan, thoughtfully curate content, and align each element to deliver a compelling narrative.
pfr: Engaging critical thinking in my digital media course was both a thrilling and demanding journey. At the outset, I felt a mixture of excitement and uncertainty. The task of creating a multimedia project that effectively highlighted a social issue using various digital media elements seemed like an immense challenge. The complexity of the project and the myriad of choices to be made triggered moments of doubt and apprehension.
learning: Through this experience, I've gained a deep appreciation for the significance of critical thinking in the realm of multimedia creation. Just as in the engineering context shared earlier, the Atkins and Murphy model of reflection played a pivotal role in guiding our process. By breaking down the critical thinking process into Situation, Task, Action, and Result, I was able to navigate complexities effectively. As we brainstormed, formed our approach, and curated multimedia elements, critical thinking emerged as a compass guiding us toward decisions that resonated with the project's objectives. Evaluating available resources, considering the impact of various media elements, and ensuring coherence throughout required a methodical approach. The reflection model mirrored our critical thinking journey. Situating ourselves in the project's context, clarifying our tasks, taking deliberate actions, and assessing results provided a framework for continuous improvement. This experience underscored the dynamic nature of critical thinking – a skill that adapts and evolves with each challenge encountered. FUTURE ACTION: Looking ahead, I will carry the invaluable insight gained from this experience into future endeavors. I'll continue to harness critical thinking as a cornerstone of my decision-making process. Just as in the engineering example, I've learned that every element in multimedia creation serves a purpose, and critical thinking ensures each choice aligns with the project's objectives. Ultimately, this journey has solidified the notion that critical thinking transcends disciplines, providing a structured approach to problem-solving. Whether engineering or multimedia creation, the Atkins and Murphy model of reflection and critical thinking remain steadfast companions on the path to meaningful and impactful outcomes.

Witnessing our collective progress each day, training every member, and being an integral part of this transformative journey filled me with pride. Our triumphant win underscored the effectiveness of teamwork and communication strategies.
learning: This profound experience taught me that seemingly insurmountable challenges can be conquered through effective teamwork and communication. Our victory hinged on the contributions of every team member, emphasising the significance of active participation. It underscored that a team can only function cohesively when communication is at its core, revealing the miraculous power of effective communication within a team structure.

situation: During my first year of college at Macquarie, the last few weeks of the semester, I had to turn in multiple assignments for different courses. One of the assignments was to write a report on one of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Simultaneously, I had other course and programming assignments as well.
task_action: My primary task was to manage my time and resources efficiently to research, draft, and finalize the report without compromising its quality. Additionally, I needed to ensure that my other academic commitments weren't neglected. ACTION: I began by breaking down the research paper into smaller tasks: topic selection, literature review, drafting, revision, and finalization. I allocated specific blocks of time for each task, ensuring buffer periods for unforeseen challenges. For resources, I prioritize recent articles in Google Scholar that are most relevant to my topic. To keep track of my progress, I write the progress of my report on a calendar, which allows me to set milestones and monitor my progress. For the other courses, I allocated specific hours during the day to make me focus on other courses.
result: By effectively allocating my time and using resources judiciously, I submitted the report well before the deadline, receiving a high score of 80%. My structured approach also ensured that my other coursework was completed on time, and I was well-prepared for the end-of-semester assessments.
pfr: Handling a major assignment would be stressful at first. The task seems big, and the pressure to get it right can be intense. But by breaking it down step by step, the pressure eases, and things start to make sense.
learning: The vital lesson is the power of decomposition. When confronted with something vast and intricate, breaking it down can transform how it's perceived. Big tasks become manageable when split into smaller parts. The insight I've gathered is that tackling tasks systematically can diffuse the inherent stress and provide clearer direction. In a hypothetical future scenario, instead of being intimidated by the scale of the challenge, I instinctively break it down. This way, I can focus on each part and ensure a holistic and effective approach.

situation: We are given the challenge of creating a water filtration system for a remote town with limited access to clean water sources as part of a group assignment for an engineering course.
task_action: We used strong critical thinking to address the project's difficulties. This included vital design elements including the choice of filtration material, the installation of system components, and the maintenance strategy. Our strategy was launched with a design thinking session. We started by identifying the main issue that was providing an underserved population with reliable access to clean water. We investigated a huge range of filtering processes and materials. We used brainstorming techniques throughout the workshop in order to encourage an atmosphere of unrestricted idea exchange. To support original ideas, we aggressively supported unusual thinking. After the brainstorming process, we honed in analytical idea classification and evaluation, placing a priority on viability, efficacy along with connection with project objectives.
result: We evaluated alternative based on their technological viability, financial efficiency as well as social impact. Together, we decided on a plan that made use of inexpensive, readily available, along with locally sourced components. This choice was supported by a careful analysis that took socioeconomic and environmental factors into account in addition to meeting technical standards. The teachers were pleased with our final water filtration design, which improved our problem-solving abilities and emphasised the value of carefully examining engineering solutions for applicability in the real world.
pfr: Firstly, The project's scale and the complexity of engineering design left me feeling unprepared. Due to varying viewpoints, working with a diverse group that presented tasks. Nevertheless, I felt more in control as the design thinking session went. My initial concerns were put to rest by the methodical approach and encouraging environment.
learning: This experience brought home the need of methodical problem-solving and disciplined teamwork. The design thinking workshop taught me how different viewpoints may improve decision-making, even when they disagree. Innovative solutions result from openly embracing unorthodox viewpoints. Furthermore, I also realised that it's rare to make the correct selection. Requirements as well as resources are all balanced in decisions. My attitude to problem-solving has evolved as a result of pragmatism, and I value collaboration and sacrifices in limitations. Secondly, I will put organised thinking and diversified collaboration first in the future. I realise that using critical thinking requires making decisions using organised procedures. By accepting several points of view and weighing your options, you can approach problems with more confidence and come up with well-rounded answers. My desire for closely and honestly approaching challenging engineering problems and finding possibilities for progress was stoked by this experience.

topic: Perseverance, urgency and will to deliver, resourcefulness and flexibility
