After I had finished making my presentation, I PRACTICED speaking. I recorded myself and made notes to improve, and also performed in front of my family and friends. Importantly, I started to work on my presentation task as soon as I had received it, in case I needed further practice or to make improvements.
result: I was able to present confidently and received positive feedback. I also got tips and advices from classmates about different presentation formatting techniques that I could implement in my future presentations.
pfr: I definitely felt anxious at first, and felt a sense of pressure since this task was an important part of my unit. Once I began to speak, I had picked up confidence from previous practice and research. It had became more from my interest than just simply remembering a script.
learning: I learnt that planning helps a long way into any task or project. Since unique ideas started to appear and made me more engaged with the task. From my previous tasks that I had done, I often didn't perform as well as I do now. Because of a lack of planning and structuring, the tasks became over complicated and felt as if it would take a long time to complete. Stepping outside my comfort zone and practicing different ways to improve also helped me a lot with embracing challenges. These types of approaches have driven great interest for oral presentations.

situation: Present a speech for a toastmasters course clearly, and confidently.
task_action: Created a lengthy speech describing various things about myself, my interests, and the topic i was talking about. The focus was to control my nerves and present something that was clear, and engaging, whilst using techniques taught to me in the toastmasters course.
result: Increased oral communication skills, better engagement from public speaking.
pfr: The writing of the task was easy, but the presentation in front of the group was a very nerve-wracking thing to do. My heart rate shot up and I felt weak in my legs, my mind was overwhelmed with anxious thoughts. It was confusing to find myself losing control like that but it provided good insight into how I could go about improving the issue.
learning: By being in that situation, I was able to break down why those feelings arose and develop techniques to counteract them. One example of this was that once I utilized a technique of directing my attention to just one person in the crowd and treating it like a one-on-one conversation. My oral communication became much more clear and more effective. Instead of feeling like I was in a very high-pressure situation, I could adapt it to a situation I was comfortable in. I have also learned that because my heart rate increased when I talked in front of a crowd, I could counteract that with proven techniques to lower my heart rate, such as breathing slower and deeper. This would produce a better result in communication through increased confidence.

situation: Need to create a plan to efficiently manage my time and resources while studying at university.
task_action: Create a list of all tasks that need completing, using the handbook and calendar write due dates and how long i should work on each assessment. Then create a weekly study plan for general revision to stay up to date for exams.
result: Had a detailed calendar covering all assessments and a weekly plan to use throughout the session for study.
pfr: The time investment was hard at the beginning to create a detailed plan for university, however throughout the session was able to know what assessments were due and when, making me feel more comfortable. The study plan was also helpful as it let me stay on top of my subjects.
learning: Throughout the session I used the study plan to stay up to date on my subjects, however could have adapted to then focus on subjects that I needed to practice more.

situation: The use of critical thinking as a university student during assessment tasks
task_action: As a university student, the critical thinking used whilst undertaking coursework, the analysis of information, and making informed decisions can help me excel in my studies and achieve the most of my time at university.
result: As the skill of critical thinking is being constantly used, this develops over time and in future will be a key part of who I will become in my career as an engineer.
pfr: Basing of the Atkins and Murphy model of reflection, my journey as a uni student has had its obstacles that could not have been conquered without the skill of critical thinking, empowering me to ask theoretical questions and analyse all aspects of the situation overall enriching my learning experience. Critical thinking does not just shape me on an academic level, but on a lifelong level ultimately portraying me as a future engineer.
learning: When applying the skill of critical thinking, you understand and reflect on one's own thinking processes and previous assumptions to ultimately enabling you to evaluate the strengths and weaknesses, helping you reevaluate your previous work and build on the assignment. Throughout my experience as a university student, I find that critical thinking has played a key role in all my classes and I find myself continuing to grow each week, learning from past feedback and implementing it into all aspects at university and in my own life.

situation: I was working at a company while also pursuing my university degree when a situation arose where I was asked to take on a temporary job position. One of our colleagues had to take an emergency leave, and my manager approached me to cover for her during her absence.
task_action: The task at hand was to step into this temporary role and ensure the smooth continuation of the department's operations. However, this request presented a significant challenge as my university schedule was already quite hectic. I needed to prioritise my responsibilities effectively and find a way to balance my work and academic commitments. ACTION: Assessing My Current Commitments: To start, I took a step back and carefully reviewed my existing commitments, both at work and at university. This involved assessing my course workload, assignment deadlines, and class schedules. Creating a Planner: To address the challenge of managing my time efficiently, I created a detailed planner. This planner incorporated all my university classes, assignment deadlines, and work hours. It allowed me to visualise and focus on my commitments and identify potential time slots for focused work. Prioritising Tasks: With the planner in place, I prioritised tasks based on their importance and urgency. I allocated dedicated time slots for studying, attending classes, and fulfilling my work responsibilities. I made sure to accommodate the temporary role without compromising my academic progress.
result: The actions I took to prioritise and focus on my commitments yielded several positive outcomes: - I was able to effectively cover the temporary position during my colleague's leave without any major disruptions in our department's operations. - Despite the added workload, I was able to maintain my academic performance and meet my university commitments, including attending classes and submitting assignments on time. - This experience also improved my time management and focus skills and ability to balance multiple responsibilities efficiently. - Both my manager and colleagues appreciated my dedication and ability to step up during a challenging time. This experience also strengthened my professional relationships within the company. In conclusion, by carefully prioritising my tasks, creating a detailed planner, and maintaining open communication, I successfully managed the temporary job position while continuing my university studies, demonstrating my ability to effectively prioritise and focus on critical tasks in a demanding situation.
pfr: When I was faced with the opportunity to take on a temporary job position alongside my university studies, I initially felt a mix of excitement and anxiety. I was thrilled at the prospect of stepping up and proving my capabilities at work, but I was also worried about the potential impact on my academic performance. The task seemed overwhelming at first, and I questioned whether I could effectively manage both responsibilities without burning out. It was a situation where I needed to strike a delicate balance, and I wasn't sure if I had the skills to do so.
learning: -Reflecting on this experience, I've gained valuable insights into time management, communication, and prioritisation. Firstly, I learned that open and honest communication with my manager is essential. By expressing my concerns and limitations upfront, I was able to create a supportive environment where my manager understood my situation and was willing to accommodate my needs. This taught me the importance of proactive communication in any professional setting. -Secondly, I realised the power of effective planning and time management. Creating a detailed planner helped me visualise and focus on my commitments, identify potential conflicts, and allocate my time efficiently. I now understand that even in challenging situations, a well-structured plan can make a significant difference in achieving a balance between work and personal life. -Furthermore, I gained a deep appreciation for flexibility and adaptability. Life is unpredictable, and unexpected demands can arise at any time. I learned that it's crucial to stay flexible and be willing to adjust my schedule when necessary. This adaptability allowed me to handle unforeseen challenges effectively and avoid unnecessary stress. -Lastly, I recognised the importance of seeking support from colleagues and classmates. It's okay to ask for help when needed and building a network of support can be valuable in managing a heavy workload. I will remember this lesson in the future and be more proactive in reaching out for assistance when faced with challenging situations. In the future, I will continue to apply these lessons to my personal and professional life. I will prioritise effective communication, structured planning, flexibility, and seeking support when necessary. This experience has taught me that with the right approach, I can successfully navigate complex situations and maintain a healthy work-life balance.

topic: Initiative and the willingness to make decisions in the face of uncertainty
situation: We needed to design and then build a 1:50 design of a student accommodation based on a set amount of floor space
task_action: Throughout the first couple of weeks, we made sure that we were all on the same page with the design of the building and how we were allocating the floor space. The short time frame of this project meant that we needed to be brave enough to use our conceptual designs and trust in our own abilities even if our ideas were not fully complete. Once we had designed the building, we were able to start making the parts for it and allocate roles which best suited the members of our team.
result: The result was that we were able to design a building and build it in a limited time frame, using the design process to show that your initial ideas can be good but there is always room for improvement.
pfr: Upon receiving the task, everyone was worried about the timeframe of the project and how we would be able to get it done within the 4-5 given weeks. It was interesting us to see what designs we liked as a group and how they best fit with the topography of the area as well as the given floor space. We were able to choose our design through the combined effort of our group members and the culmination of our best ideas.
learning: Due to our timeframe, it was essential that we worked together as a team and used all of our ideas to progress our project. We adapted a framework which allowed us to load manage and incorporate our ideas into the one project. We decided to keep all good ideas and then once we had compiled a large list of them, we were able to make decisions that we were all comfortable with and even have more ideas in backup just in case one of those ideas didn't pan out. Overall, I have learnt that having more, better quality ideas that reflect the direction and goal of the group is a beneficial way to take on a project to minimise group conflict whilst progressing quickly through a stressful project.

situation: We need to design a student accommodation building. The building must follow a set of guidelines containing the total floor space of the site, the required room sections of the building and the areas within these rooms. A vast area of land has been presented to our group, and it is our job to analyse the land and climate condition, to choose the best spot for our building to be situated. We are then required to build a 3D model of our design.
task_action: Throughout the early weeks and group meet-up sessions, we delegated floors to one another and rooms to go on these floors. We then individually had to design them and come together to mesh them into a building and change anything necessary to create a complete design. We evaluated the final design and cross-referenced it to our site analysis and the guidelines of the building. From this successful evaluation, we began putting together the building within class time, meeting outside of class if extra time was required.
result: After all these weeks, we were left with a completed floor plan that was evaluated against the guidelines and site analysis. This then allowed us to create a 1:50 scale building reflecting our floor plan. Thus, completing our required task.
pfr: From the first day of engineering, knowing no one had done anything related to engineering or civil modelling, it was very daunting to think that in 6 weeks we would have a 1:50 scale model building that we created and designed from a set of guidelines we have never seen before. However, from forming our team, collaborating durations class and brainstorming in our own time, we were able to design and develop a well-thought-out and complete student accommodation building, following these guidelines and a group site analysis of the land. The final design started off as individual designs, then collated together to create the complete building. As the weeks went on, the workload increase as two group members left the course, leaving more work for the three remaining members. Although, we were able to delegate the work fairly and evenly across the remainder and work faster to achieve the final design and presentation alongside it.
learning: By watching the podcasts, learning from peers and demonstrators, the innovation process was able to be achieved. There was much doubt in my mind on how people with no experience would be able to design such a building, but by learning the process it was possible. Breaking down the brainstorming steps, collaboration and design processes, the innovation progress of building the students' accommodation was able to be followed. I have been able to appreciate the importance of teamwork, patience and following processes set out to us throughout this experience.

situation: our group was looking for a unique way to seperate our own building from other groups and solve our problems with the number of rooms we have been tasked to make.
task_action: group meeting and having a brainstorming session using mind mapping and figure storming methods. Aanaylising our site analysis, sketching out designs and diagrams for multipole buildings, bridges and floorplans and laying out features that are non negotiable when coming up with our buildings designs.
result: the result was deciding on a two building and bridge setup seperating the single self contained rooms from the shared rooms, a building for each type and a bridge conecting the two.
pfr: in the beginning the task of making a physical building was unnerving as none of us had any experience in the civil modelling and architecture that this project had asked for. A few members of our group also hadn't been participating or showing up to meetings to discuss and provide their input and insight into it, and provide 0 effort and participation to the group. this worried me as we could easily fall behind other groups with more members and whio could easily manage and deligate workload t oeach other.
learning: we had overcome this obstacle by having excellent team organisation and management and by making set deadlines to have certain goals done by. We also held regular meetings outdies of our organised class time to discuss and work on the project together. this made up for our smaller team as we had to be more organised and prepared when meeting our various deadline goal targets. Through this experience I have learned that with circumstances that seem very stressful, setting specific and acieveable deadlines to keep the timeline of the project fixed and appreciate more the importance of time management and discipline towards my work.

situation: As part of the ENG1000 course, we were given Arduino circuit building exercises that were due to be completed during the workshop classes each week.
task_action: Initially, I was struggling to complete the assigned work during the allocated workshop time so I began working on the Arduino exercises before class, attempting to complete as many of the tasks as possible without the assistance of the tutors.
result: In attempting to complete the exercises ahead of time, I was able to prioritize class time to ask questions and complete the more difficult tasks.
pfr: Having no prior experience in Arduino circuit building or coding, the concepts were initially difficult to comprehend, and I struggled to complete the work on time. However, with better time management, and prioritizing class time for asking questions, I saw an improvement in my work and ability to complete the exercises on time.
learning: By adopting a better time management approach, I was able to complete the allocated work on time and to a greater standard than otherwise possible. From this experience, I can apply this approach to future tasks to improve my learning.

topic: Perseverance, urgency and will to deliver, resourcefulness and flexibility
situation: Our internship group was tasked with designing an e-commerce website with limited resources.
task_action: In our task, we were tasked to create a fully functional e-commerce website by using React. Features such as dynamic design, user experience, and product showcasing were to be implemented along with a fully functional backend host, used to process payments and such. This was done however, by using no external resources or libraries (One major library such as ReactBootstrap) and could only be done only within the language itself. We did this by researching these pre-designed functions commonly used within external libraries, assessing their purpose as well as their efficiency in design.
result: Our result was being able to break down the purposes of each pre-designed function and use parts of those pieces to produce a successful website with all the qualities of one which relied on external libraries, therefore satisfying our mentor.
pfr: At first, my group and I were extremely stuck and frustrated as those libraries were the foundation of our learning; we rummaged ideas on how navigation bars and modals were structured. However, our breakthrough was made when we skimmed across large companies and their websites. We made sure to study each pre-designed function most commonly used in popular websites; examples including big companies such as Amazon and Shopify, then taking notes from local stores and their respective websites. By grasping features from both sides; piece by piece, we constructed our own design from scratch and as result made us feel accomplished after turmoil.
learning: As a result, we learnt the importance of the fundamentals in web development by creating websites from the ground-up, therefore deepening our experiences as both a coder and a team player. It greatly strengthened our overall abilities as software engineers by integrating teamwork, overcoming difficult challenges and improving our individual skills as coders.

situation: The team comes across issues when their work spaces accidentally overlap, and accidentally create problems for one another.
task_action: Gather together, clearly inform the rest of the team of your work, what other areas it could affect (say the graphics team affecting the modelling team), together, the team can decide on a structure that would let everyone do their work, and communicate clearly with the other workers whenever bigger changes are being made.
result: The result was a smoother workflow for the entire team, and better communication throughout, letting one's coworkers know of potential problems ahead of time, so it can be worked out ahead of time.
pfr: Initially working through the problems was rather rough, as grievances had built up. However, as the team understood that everyone has been part of the problem to some extent, everyone calmed down and we could start figuring out what we could do about the root of the problem, instead of dealing with the effects. Communications between coworkers has also been given a higher priority, so that problems can be handled before problems and grievances bottle up too much.
learning: Having gone through this issue one time makes it easier to spot in the future, and it also underlines the importance of communication, making it a bigger priority in the first place. It also helps me know the importance of reaching out and talking to people in my life, whether it is in a work capacity or a personal capacity.

situation: We had to collaborate as a team to create a design for student housing that would align with both the site's conditions and environmental considerations.
task_action: Our goal was straightforward: design student housing that’s both practical and comfortable for its residents. We divvied up the tasks, and I took charge of the floor plans and material selection. However, this was overall a team effort. I focused on creating floor plans that maximised available space while ensuring plenty of natural light. To keep everyone aligned and encourage fresh perspectives, we held regular team meetings. In these sessions, we shared our progress and threw around some constructive feedback. This collaborative approach helped us fine-tune our individual parts and make sure they fit well within the overall project.
result: In the end, we produced a design that met our expectations and also resonated well with the client. While we did overlook some elements like heating, the strength of our project lay in the selection of sustainable materials and the efficiency of the floor plans. Notably, we exceeded the client's environmental efficiency goals by 15%. Encouraged by this, we each took sections of the project to further refine as we prepared for the final presentation.
pfr: At first, the task at hand was exciting to take on. As a team, we had a lot of confidence that we were able to tackle this project head-on. As time passed, we came to a realisation that six out of seven weeks was not enough time to conduct a site analysis, create a student housing model, build a report and then present its overall result. This is where things became a little overwhelming as the time pressure took a little bit of the fun out of it. However, we stuck it out as a group and collaborated with each other to ensure we all held our end of the bargain to get the job done.
learning: This experience taught me quite a bit about how quickly time can pass when you're up against a deadline. Initially, we all thought seven weeks was more than enough time. Turns out, it wasn't, and that added some stress to the whole process. I learned the hard way that it's crucial to break things down into smaller tasks from the beginning and keep a close eye on the calendar. But I also saw how a team can come together under pressure, each of us doing our part to make sure the project got finished. For any future projects, I plan to start with a clear timeline and keep the lines of communication open with my team. That way, maybe we can keep the stress levels down and the work quality up.

situation: We needed to cohesively design and construct student accommodation located at Macquarie University within a limited three week time period.
task_action: Due to the time constraints of only attending one workshop class per week we had to arrange to meet up outside of class periods. We communicated regularly via WhatsApp to organise several days throughout the week to work on the project. Despite the extracurricular activities of team members, there was a strong desire to set aside time to work collaboratively to complete this project.
result: The result was effective communication between the group members and contributing equally to the group project.
pfr: The time limitations on the project caused stress and conflict within the group, however the desire for a good mark brought the team together to collaboratively work in a group. At the beginning of our project there was uneven workload contribution towards the design and shape of the building. This was due to students prioritising other commitments outside of the project, resulting with conflict and tension within the group members. As a result of the uneven contributions, tasks were delegated between group members to help maintain organisation and a constant work flow throughout the project journey. This was an effective method to resolve conflict and time restraints which was a key challenge our group encompassed at the beginning of the project.
learning: Through the use of delegation of tasks and the contribution of every team member we effectively managed to meet the assigned deadline of the project. In the future I will assign tasks prior to starting the workload to ensure each team member is contributing to the project while meeting the goals and objectives of the overall task. Throughout this experience I have learnt the importance of teamwork, time management and delegation of tasks.

situation: Using an arduino kit and breadboard, we were instructed to code and wire up a circuit to control the spin of a servo using a potentiometer.
task_action: When attempting to complete the task, I utilized critical thinking and problem solving skills to approach the problem step by step. To begin I first gathered knowledge and understanding on the various components of the circuit in order to avoid repeatedly stopping what I was doing to go and research, which would not only take up more time in the long run but also break concentration and train of thought. To accomplish this I first read the provided worksheet explaining what a 'library' was in order to understand why we needed servo.h in order for our code, and subsequently our circuit, to function. Afterwards, I examined the example code that was given and further researched what each new/unfamiliar command did. After I understood what the purpose of each command was, I decided to wire up my circuit first so that I would know exactly how many components I would be working with/had to code for before I began to write my code. If I attempted to write up the code first before I put together the circuit, I knew that if there was an unexpected component that came up, I would potentially have to go back and change other parts of the code I had already written, thus wasting time. Furthermore, when I was creating my circuit, I put focus into using the minimum amount of components necessary in order to avoid cluttering up/over complicating the design and hindering functionality. Once I had finished the circuit, I created my code using the new commands I had learnt as well as the commands for potentiometers that I had been taught in a prior workshop. Whilst I was creating the code, I ran into some problems where my code had errors and would not work as expected. When this happened, I looked for help from my classmates as well as tutors, adopting an open mind and taking on their constructive feedback and considering alternatives that would better improve the functionality of my code.
result: the result was a functioning circuit in which by changing the potentiometer position I could rotate the servo in a direction of my choosing.
pfr: EXPERIENCE: At the beginning I felt very overwhelmed and stressed as I was very unfamiliar with arduino and coding in general. As these eng1000 workshops were the first time I had properly worked on coding and circuit building I felt quickly overwhelmed by the sheer amount of new information I was taking in. I sometimes also gave up quickly or relied on simple/easy code without bothering to think deeper, which resulted in poor quality, or in some cases non-functioning, circuits. I also lost confidence very easily when I was met with failure and often gave up due to a lack of self-esteem/belief in myself.
learning: During this situation I was able to hone and further develop my critical thinking skills by working on my ability to approach problems in a logical manner. I learnt the importance of having to plan ahead and gather all the resources you need before attempting a problem in order to avoid feeling lost and losing sense of direction while working on a project. I also had to understand that before I attempted a complicated problem I would first have to acknowledge that overthinking and stressing over a problem hinders effective thinking and that I had to break down problems into simpler and more manageable sections (i.e. learning commands first, then learning how they interact, then the circuits, etc.). Additionally, I worked on bettering my resilience when approaching complex questions that were still difficult even after multiple attempts, and avoiding re-attempting inefficient methods or giving up prematurely. I also focused on developing the ability to communicate my questions and motives in a direct and clear manner when seeking help so that I do not waste my time or the time of the person I am receiving help from. Consequently, I made great improvements in my problem solving ability and a positive change in my approach to complex questions that I would have given up on or have performed poorly on if I had not learnt critical thinking.

situation: Firstly, I'd like to note that I currently work as a steelfixer in the construction industry to make a living, even though my actual field of study is software engineering. On one particular occasion, my co-workers and I were tasked with setting up steel protection for a clean water supply pipe in a major suburb in Sydney.
task_action: We began by reviewing engineer plan. This entailed ensuring all measurements, such as the concrete's height and width, all fundamental aspects of steelfixing were clarified and comprehended. With all the necessary information in hand, my co-workers and I distributed roles: deciding who would cut the steel, who would handle measurements, and who would be responsible for lifting and transporting the bars.
result: Despite the initial plan not being entirely fit to real world conditions, our team proficiently and independently addressed the problem, successfully repairing the clean water supply pipe. After our intervention, we confidently handed over the restored system to the lead engineer for final evaluation.
pfr: Initially, we found our task quite challenging. While our team mostly had and experience in general construction, but facing with a project as extensive as a suburb-wide pipe was unfamiliar for us. Nevertheless, we approached each arising issue methodically, tackling each challenge systematically, and successfully overcome the complications.
learning: Looking back, I've learned to value all types of education. Sometimes, lessons we think are unrelated show their importance later on. For example, I have taken ENGG 1000, currently focuses on civil engineering, but my real world steelfixing experience provided a deeper and more realistic perspective for me. Additionally, strong teamwork and good organization demonstrate that we can overcome tough challenges. It's not just about trying, it's also about having a genuine desire to understand and pushing through. Never stop learning, it's benefits might surprise you in the future.

situation: During week 6 Arduino workshops, I was tasked with brainstorming and writing code for a 4-bit binary adder. The project was challenging due to the complex wiring and coding requirements, involving both hardware and software components.
task_action: To prepare, I did preliminary research on binary addition and related operators to build a foundational understanding. I listed down unanswered questions to ensure that I arrived in class ready to seek clarification from the tutor team. Once in class, I began the brainstorming process for wiring and coding, constantly seeking input from classmates and tutors to develop the hardware setup. I followed a logical sequence of tasks, progressing from foundational research to detailed questions, and from smaller tasks to bigger ones: -Preliminary Research -Question List -Classroom Brainstorm -Task Prioritization -Hardware Development -Coding
result: By systematically employing critical thinking throughout the process, I successfully designed the hardware in class and developed the code for the 4-bit binary adder. While I did encounter challenges, particularly in coding and physical interface, these obstacles offered valuable lessons. They taught me how to think logically and problem-solve effectively by leveraging available resources and collaboration. As a result, I was able to optimize my performance, gaining both practical skills and insights into the use of a structured approach to complex problems.
pfr: Initially, the thinking of building a 4-bit binary adder felt a little bit overwhelm but I was excited about applying my research and insights. I was particularly concerned about the coding part, knowing that even a minor mistake could cause a lot of time for debugging. However, the structured approach I employed provided me with a roadmap, easing some of my initial apprehensions. As I moved through the project, I have more sense of confidence and accomplishment, especially when the hardware and code began to align properly.
learning: The project taught me several valuable lessons. One of the most significant insights was the importance of a logical and structured approach to problem-solving. By breaking down complex problems into smaller tasks and systematically addressing each, I could better manage what initially seemed overwhelming. Collaboration also emerged as a key element; seeking inputs from classmates and tutors enriched my perspective and allowed for a more informed approach to both hardware and software challenges. I've also come to appreciate that there's rarely a "perfect solution" in engineering; instead, solutions are often context-dependent and shaped by various constraints such as time, resources, and knowledge. This aligns with the general principle that critical thinking isn't about finding the 'right' answer but about making the 'best possible' decision based on available information. In future projects, I plan to apply these learnings by incorporating structured critical thinking right from the inception phase. I also intend to be more proactive in seeking collaborative insights, realizing that different perspectives can add substantial value to problem-solving processes.

situation: poor time management during unavoidable familial/personal issues.
task_action: develop strategies for efficiently managing time and resources. Action: * Assessment: evaluation of daily and weekly schedule, identifying where the conflicts were occurring. * Prioritization: ranking academic tasks, work commitments, and personal time based on their significance and urgency. * Asking for Help: recognizing the importance of clear communication; approaching university help avenues for aid in mental health. * Technology Utilization: leveraging digital tools such as calendar apps and task management software to organize schedules and set reminders for important deadlines, meetings, and study sessions. * Multitasking: better integration of certain activities. For instance, using commute time to review class notes or listen to recorded lectures, making the most of otherwise unproductive moments.
result: The implementation of these proactive time management strategies yielded several results: By effectively planning and allocating time for studies, it lowered stress levels to a more manageable degree. With more time available, it provided a better understanding of unit content after reviewing missed material.
pfr: upon reflection, I am still unsatisfied with my work and progress in my studies of this unit. I hope to remedy this in the near future as I continue to work on my time and resource management. I have no excuse for not properly managing my studies during my circumstances, and I seek to fix this.
learning: by forcing myself to use the mentioned strategies I was able to organize my time and attain a neater overview of my studies and academic commitments. I learned not to overestimate my learning ability and rely on help from others. Even talking to the university help services aided in managing my stress, even though they were busy and are yet unable to provide help.

situation: In technical drawing class, I found myself in an unfamiliar environment. As someone from a software development background, I was well-versed in coding but had always struggled with artistic skills, especially drawing. The challenge was to learn technical drawing as part of the ENGG1000 criteria.
task_action: Faced with the difficulties of not being great at drawing, I recongised the importance of teamwork and communication to overcome my drawing deficiencies. I proactively search for classmates who might excel in technical drawing based on talking to them and proposed forming a small working group with a mixture of skills to tackle weekly tasks. My intention for doing this was to enhance the group technical drawing skills and support one another in grasping fundamental.
result: During each session, we would sat near one another, discussing the drawing topics, way to improve and shared constructive feedback. Over time I can see progression with my technical drawing skills as well as those around me.
pfr: At first I was anxious about my drawing skills but working as a team and communicating with my class mate reassured me. It allowed an open learning and fun experience for everyone involved
learning: I learned that even with tasks traditionally seen as individual, like drawing, there are benenefits to teamwork and communication. It is not always necessary to go it alone and sharing your journey with others can be fun and beneficial.

situation: In my previous job as a retail sales associate at Myer, I was assigned to lead a cross-functional team for a critical client project during Christmas.
task_action: The task involved coordinating the efforts of staff members from different retail departments, ensuring clear communication and meeting my manager's expectations while adhering to a tight deadline. ACTION: During the project, a situation arose where one team member consistently showing no friendly service and was not contributing effectively to joint tasks. This was impacting the team's progress and jeopardising the project's success. Instead of criticising the team member immediately, I decided to approach the situation professionally. By scheduling a meeting with the team member and my manager to discuss and understand their challenges, I actively listened to their concerns and acknowledged their perspective. Through providing constructive feedback on the importance of being a reliable team member, we created a plan to provide additional support and clarified expectations. I also offered assistance in prioritising tasks and ensuring a better alignment between their workload and skills. topic: Perseverance, urgency and will to deliver, resourcefulness and flexibility
situation: The situation for the chosen topic is the two weeks before my HSC (High School Certificate) final Year 12 exams in 2022, which would determine my final grade and the degree I would be eligible for. I had my 18th birthday and my Year 12 formal party during this two-week period, making it incredibly challenging to manage studying and having fun. I was unable to enjoy these 2 major events that one only gets to experience once because of the stress of the final exams, which had now begun to set in. As a result, even though I wanted to completely enjoy my 18th birthday party and my Year 12 formal, I couldn't help but feel a constant sense of urgency as I thought about the final exams, which were constantly lingering at the back of my mind. Hence, I had to find a way to manage my time, have the will to deliver and become flexible such that I didn’t regret not enjoying these events but also not regretting that I didn’t study enough for the exams.
task_action: To ensure that I enjoyed my time during these 2 once in a lifetime events and also did my best in the HSC, I had to implement certain time and resource management strategies. These tactics made sure I always had the perseverance and drive to succeed. I was able to maximise my productivity while studying using these techniques, which allowed me to have a greater amount of time to enjoy my 18th birthday party and my formal. The very first step I took was to plan ahead, as time itself is also a very important resource. I utilised Google Calendar to break each day up into study sections. Each section was 1-2 hours, depending on how much work needed to be done. Each section would only focus on one subject at a time. During these study sections I would either go through my flashcards using an app called Anki (which utilises the study method called spaced repetition) or I would attempt practice exams and reattempt the ones that I got wrong. By reattempting questions I got wrong I was able to gain maximum benefits out of the practice papers which were limited. Moreover, Anki would give me daily notifications to remind me that I had a certain amount of flashcards to finish before the end of the day. This ensured that I was able to deliver and not become too overwhelmed by the sense of urgency. The next action I took was setting clear priorities. As the dates of each exam was spread out, I would spend more time on the subject that had its test the earliest. Next, I would prioritise topics within each subject whereby I knew I had gaps in my knowledge. This enabled me to not only reinforce what I knew but also ensure that I wasn’t going into my exams without knowing everything that I needed to. By doing so, I was able to use the limited time resources I had and ensure I was doing the best I could. As I knew I was doing the best I could, I had moments where I felt calm and the lingering stress was decreased. This motivated me to persevere through the following weeks without drowning in an ocean of anxiety and self-doubt. Another step that I took was to focus on one task at a time. Rather than thinking about each subject as a whole, I made a To Do list on Google Keep which enabled me to break the subject down into parts. This reduced the stress greatly as larger topics were broken down into more mentally digestible smaller topics. This also increased how flexible I could be when creating my study timetable.
result: The aim of my actions were to maximise the use of the little time I had to study for my exams so that I would be able to enjoy my 18th birthday party and my Year 12 formal party. The result of my actions was that I was able to fully enjoy the two events with only almost no negative effects on my exams. I had attempted each test to the best of my ability and I was confident that I was going to receive the mark that I wanted. I had not regretted enjoying the parties or wishing that I spent more time studying for my exams. Moreover I had very little stress during the exams. When I got my ATAR (final mark) back, I had accomplished the initial goal that I had set. However I was certain that I could’ve done better by not attending the parties, but this didn’t bother me as I knew it would’ve had no extra benefit as I achieved the goal I wanted to. In the end, I had no regrets and I achieved the initial task that I had set out to complete.
pfr: Before I set out to efficiently study by utilising the aforementioned techniques, I was quite overwhelmed with the workload and very stressed. This affected other areas of my life such as not getting enough exercise or eating properly. I held the thought that I was going to fail my exams and I would not get into the degree I wanted. I thought that my future would be ruined and on top of all of that I would not be able to enjoy my 18th birthday party or my formal party. However after implementing the strategies I was more confident than I had ever been about any exam I ever took. As these strategies enabled me to become more resourceful and flexible, while studying I had developed a sense of perseverance that didn’t falter once. This ensured that the lingering sense of stress and urgency I had, would be kept at bay and wouldn’t overwhelm me. During the exams, I didn’t pay much attention to whether or not I had enjoyed my parties and my only focus was doing the best I could in the exam. situation: Since beginning this unit, I have needed to work alongside a team in order to build a Rube Goldberg Machine.

situation: While the group was forming we recognized that manpower was the main resource we had as a group and wanted to utilize it fairly on tasks without accidentally placing to much work at one persons feet. However at this early stage how large a task would end up being was unknown.
task_action: Establishing group workflow, and roles. ACTION: Concept of ENGG1050 project management was broken down into 6 responsibilities. Project Manager, Head Engineer, Assessment Tasker, Unit Infobroker, Fabricator, and Project Wikipedian. A vote was taken to decide what roles people wanted most to least and everyone received a responsibility corresponding to a role.
result: The roles worked in allocating responsibility to make people accountable for their domain, however the agreed operation of the role for team workflow was not followed. The initial concept was that Roles created task cards on trello, which all members would take and complete asking for help as needed, or Roles could request members work on cards during meetings, however everyone was reluctant to ask for manpower to be spent on tasks without an incentive. As of this moment all assessment tasker cards are in progress or complete, but many engineering cards have not been actioned despite being on the critical path.
pfr: The initial success of the roles approach led to massive productivity many cards were generated documenting when everything was due, who was responsible for the minutes each week, a card to find the easter egg was created and assigned leading to discovery of the easter egg, research cards were generated to summarize lecture content, and a team wiki was started using google docs. However this initial success was misleading, I was disappointed to discover that people were reluctant to ask others to help working on cards that were more complex, and cards with overlapping responsibilities led to confusion over responsibility. Overall, this approach failed to properly utilize our manpower.
learning: Although a method can appear at first to working, assessment of the actual jobs being performed can reveal the problem of overlapping responsibilities. When there are overlapping responsibilities, it needs to be decided who is actually responsible to ensure that all team operations have an accountable team member assigned. Otherwise each responsible person assumes the other person is responsible and there is no one accountable for inaction. An implementation of this learning would be going over all current trello cards during a team meeting and asking who is responsible, and ensuring all tasks have a single person responsible for their completion. (under our framework roles can assign cards they are responsible to members (this was conceived to prevent work overload of roles by making them management roles))

situation: We needed to find an alternative solution for one of our events within a group task. We were creating a Rube Goldberg Machine (RGM) in which we incorporated the transportation of water from one point to another.
task_action: Upon creation of our RGM we figured that the wooden channel that we had used for this task was not effective and that it was absorbing water and was not allowing it to reach its desired point. After having multiple discussions on different alternatives, we gathered together numerous materials that could be used for this task. We had further analysed each material and had determined whether this was suitable or not. We had also thought of different ways we could make the transportation of water work.
result: Instead of only changing the materials we had also changed how the structure of the RGM would work. Instead of using water in the middle phase of the RGM, we had decided that the water part would only come at the end. So as each sequence had progressed within the task, the final outcome of the RGM was that there was a bottle that had water in it, and that was tipped over, which had created an efficient flow of water. This had successfully achieved its set purpose as the RGM was to water a plant.
pfr: At first we were all a bit worried as we didn't know how we could achieve our final outcome efficiently. However, by discussing and brainstorming, we as a group were able to creatively think of different ideas and methods. After we had all given our ideas, we had then collectively analysed which idea works best and in this situation it was incorporating the use of the bottle and having it trigger at the end phase of the RGM.
learning: The use of creative thinking had helped us as a group as this allowed us to explore numerous ideas and methods that could have been possibly incorporated within the RGM. By creatively thinking we had managed to change the structure of the RGM, which had allowed for better waterflow and had successfully achieved its target of watering a plant efficiently.

situation: Over the past 6 years I have worked professionally as a Diagnostic Radiographer across many public and private healthcare facilities. To this day I can still recollect my very first nightshift, and the experiences that I had learnt from it. Working in the Townsville University Hospital this night, I was the sole radiographer providing all the Medical Imagining services across both Xray and CT for the entire hospital. It was a busy night and at some point, I received two phone calls within seconds of each other, one was theatre stating they had an anesthetised patient on the table and needed x-rays, and the other was a MET (Medical emergency team) Call attending a patient with acute shortness of breath that needed me also. As I was leaving the workstation to change into my theatre attire, there was an announcement made through the emergency PA system “Paediatric Rapid Response to RESUS”.
task_action: I immediately called the second on-call Radiographer, explained what was happening and asked them come in. I got changed into scrubs, informed ED and the MET call team that I had to attend theatre urgently and that another radiographer would be there shortly. Once I had finished screening (taking x-rays) for the theatre case, I returned to the medical imaging department, sent the on-call radiographer home and continued the rest of the shift. Although I applied good critical thinking to able to overcome this sudden spike in the workload, I wanted to make a change, so that something like this would not happen again, to myself or my colleagues. So, I approached my team leader with my concerns about the increased workload and the pressure it has on the sole nightshift radiographer, especially the less experienced graduates (as I was). I also addressed the issue, with statistics I had gathered, in staff meetings and with the deputy director at the time advocating for increased support for the nightshift radiographer and especially for graduates undertaking nightshift for the first time.
result: At the Townsville University Hospital, I have since been the last radiographer to ever (since 2019) work their first nightshift alone. As part of my advocating for a change and the support of my colleagues, the first initial nightshift for any new staff member is rostered with a ‘buddy’, another experienced radiographer to help guide them through the afterhours procedures and processes. Although I did also advocate for a second radiographer to be rostered to nightshift indefinitely due to the increased workload, I cannot claim that I was reason that they decided to do so. COVID-19 and the increased workload that came with it was, but I supported this and undertook additional nightshifts to help the nightshift radiographer.
pfr: The nightshift in which this whole sequence of events happened was one of the worst, if not the worst shift, I have worked in my entire professional career. I was a graduate radiographer, extremely stressed due to the unusually busy night and with added emergency calls, I just couldn’t keep on top of everything and called for help, twice. Before the theatre call even took place, I had called the first on-call, the CT radiographer and asked if they could come in to help, but I was told, “Stop stressing, I’m not coming in, it’s your first night. You’ll be fine”. This did not make me stop stressing, but made me feel even worse, like I had no support at all. I was extremely thankful for the support that the second on-call radiographer provided when I called them, they calmly advised me on what I should do and handled the whole situation professionally. However, I was angered by initial lack of support and how we as graduate radiographers are put into situations like this in the first place, I wanted it to change. With a newfound determination I retrospectively produced stats showcasing the increasing workload endured by the nightshift radiographer from the past few years and created surveys which I distributed to my fellow colleagues in order to prove to management that something needed to change.
learning: Through this experience, I gained several valuable insights that have shaped my approach towards work and advocacy. The lack of support I initially encountered underscored the vital role of teamwork and mentorship, especially for less experienced staff. It taught me the significance of fostering a supportive work environment where colleagues can rely on each other during high-pressure situations. Confronted with the overwhelming workload and inadequate support systems in place, I realized the necessity of proactive advocacy for institutional change. By gathering data and engaging with management, I proved the need for additional resources and support for nightshift radiographers. This experience taught me the power of advocacy in effecting positive change within the workplace.

situation: During our technical drawing lessons, we needed to draw a Lego piece with a scale factor of two to demonstrate its isometric view. This required critical thinking skills due to its design and structure.
task_action: As we noticed the difficulty of this task, we decided to work in a pair to combine our critical thinking capabilities and attempt to determine how to approach this drawing. To overcome this situation, we analysed the necessary measurements and calculations which were dependent upon the isometric thirty-degree perspective. We then determined how each angle must correspond to each other in a parallel manner, excluding the ninety-degree angles. Through this critical thinking, we determine the measurements, angles, and how to draw up in an isometric view.
result: Our dedication to this project resulted in the succession of creating an accurate drawing of the Lego piece in an isometric perspective, with a scale of 1:2 on the sheet of paper. This was a result of our collaborative effort through critical thinking, allowing us to produce this drawing.
pfr: Initially, the task of drawing the Lego piece with a 1:2 scale seemed a bit challenging and quite intimidating personally, as my mindset was that working individually restricts my capability of progressing when all my options are catered to, causing me to feel a sense of uncertainty upon approaching this situation. As we were developing ideas, I felt more engaged within the task, and we managed to develop the technical drawing of the Lego piece at a more consistent pace in comparison to individually.
learning: Through this experience, I gained an insight on how crucial critical thinking is in engineering, combined with collaborative efforts and working as a team to overcome a problem. By working in a pair, we were able to approach this task from another perspective and develop more accurate solutions effectively. This also allowed me to learn the importance of an analysing and utilising time effectively to manage drawings. In the future, through this experience,I would know that working collaboratively will enhance critical thinking, making it an effective option.

situation: In order to complete this task and all of its extensions, I had to use critical thinking and problem-solving skills in order to construct a dynamic algorithm that could facilitate a seemingly infinite amount of gestures. In short, how could I use maths to find the relationship between numbered gestures, no matter the amount of gestures?
task_action: To complete this part of the task, I took my problem-solving skills to pen and paper. First, I drew out the relationships between each gesture in a game of RPS-11 _(Rock, Paper, Scissors with a total of 11 different hand gestures) _and then I numbered them from 0 to 10, moving clockwise around the circle. From observing the lines drawn to indicate which gestures would win and lose against others, I noticed that each gesture loses to half of the gestures that are immediately clockwise from itself and wins against the remaining half of the gestures that are counter-clockwise from itself. With that in mind, I began trying to express this relationship using maths. After a few attempts at nailing the formula, I began implementing the algorithm in code.
result: Although I made a few errors initially with the mathematical algorithm, I could test it using my code to work out what was going wrong. Eventually, I had built a dynamic algorithm for determining the winner and thus the result was a resounding success.
pfr: Going into this project I felt very confident. I've got a number of years under my belt as a software engineer, and I have made a Rock, Paper, Scissors program in the past. The majority of the code was quite easy to write, and I felt as though the extension for building a dynamic algorithm was the main challenge of this task, and I enjoyed solving it.
learning: In order to build the algorithm properly, I had to think about the modulus operator in a way I hadn't really done before. Thanks to an article written by a mathematician online about modular theory and graph theory, I wasted less time thinking about how it _could_ be used-, and was able to tighten my scope and consider how it _should_ be used. Overall, I would say I primarily learned maths for this assignment- which is always a welcome surprise.

situation: In a project to simulate a smart home automation system using Tinkercad circuits, I encountered a challenge where the simulated sensors were not providing accurate readings, hindering the functionality of the system. This discrepancy jeopardized the project's success as it relied heavily on precise sensor data for triggering automation actions within the simulation.
task_action: My task was to identify the underlying cause of the sensor inaccuracies within the Tinkercad simulation environment and devise a solution to ensure consistent and reliable sensor readings for the smart home automation system. ACTION: SIMULATION ANALYSIS: I began by thoroughly analyzing the Tinkercad simulation setup, examining the connections, configurations, and simulated environment parameters related to the sensors. I checked for any discrepancies or misconfigurations that could potentially impact the accuracy of the sensor readings. CODE REVIEW AND DEBUGGING: I meticulously reviewed the Arduino code responsible for interfacing with the simulated sensors within the Tinkercad environment. I debugged the code to identify any logical errors, syntax issues, or inaccuracies in the data processing algorithms. VIRTUAL TESTING SCENARIOS: To diagnose the sensor inaccuracies, I created a series of virtual testing scenarios within the Tinkercad simulation environment. These scenarios simulated various real-world conditions and sensor inputs to evaluate the system's response and identify potential sources of error. DATA VISUALIZATION: Utilizing Tinkercad's data visualization tools, I monitored and analyzed the sensor readings in real-time during the virtual testing scenarios. This allowed me to visualize the data trends, anomalies, and inconsistencies, facilitating the identification of underlying issues. PARAMETER ADJUSTMENT: Based on the analysis of simulated sensor data, I adjusted the simulation parameters such as sensor calibration values, noise levels, and environmental factors to better reflect real-world conditions and improve the accuracy of the sensor readings. SIMULATION REFINEMENT: Through an iterative process of testing, analysis, and refinement, I fine-tuned the Tinkercad simulation settings and code implementations to mitigate sensor inaccuracies and enhance the reliability of the smart home automation system simulation.
result: * ENHANCED SIMULATION ACCURACY: By identifying and addressing the underlying causes of sensor inaccuracies within the Tinkercad simulation environment, I successfully improved the accuracy of the simulated sensor readings. * INCREASED RELIABILITY: The implemented solutions ensured consistent and reliable sensor data within the Tinkercad simulation, enabling the smart home automation system to function reliably and accurately in virtual scenarios. * PROJECT ADVANCEMENT: With the sensor accuracy issue resolved, the project progressed smoothly, meeting its objectives of simulating a functional smart home automation system within the Tinkercad environment.
pfr: Initially, I felt frustrated and somewhat disheartened by the recurring problem. situation: The task was to design an Arduino circuit in Tinkercad to display a binary counter counting from 0000 to 1111 using 4 LEDs.
task_action: To achieve this I first searched for representations of all binary numbers from 0000 to 1111 and then thought about how to display them on an LED using an Arduino. I started to connect the LED and Arduino in tindercad, but it was not very smooth at first. My LED showed too much current, which caused the LED to burn out. After trying it a few times, I found that it was fine after installing a resistor. I also asked the tutor and found out that the resistor can effectively control the current and make the LED light up safely. The required connections for the LEDs and resistors were determined and each LED was connected to the correct pin on the Arduino board. I typed out the rest of the code to display the binary number with order with setting 1 to turn on the LED; 0 to turn off.
result: After simulating the Arduino circuit in Tinkercad, the LED successfully displayed the binary count from 0000 to 1111 in sequence. But I realized that further experiments and attempts were needed to learn more about the design and principles of the circuit.
pfr: It was scary and exciting at the beginning, because most of my classmates and I had no basic knowledge of circuit boards, and the teacher would not teach you step by step at the beginning. You could only follow the basics teaching process and make more complex circuits, and only ask the teacher questions when you encounter difficulties. However, when I tried many times, sometimes I was lucky enough to get the answer, but sometimes I was missing a little hint from the teacher to understand. I think this is to give us a better way to acquire memory and knowledge by letting ourselves try it first, instead of the teacher teaching you step by step, but you don't understand the principles and will forget it soon.
learning: By using effective experimental inquiry, we can understand various knowledge and principles, and even strengthen your brain to improve your thinking ability. It allows us to acquire knowledge better and more memorably through various attempts, and we will fully and well understand it after the teacher's teaching. Through this experience, I began to realize the impact of experimental inquiry and it brought us many advantages.

situation: The task was to design a mechanism that could effectively unload cans from a robot onto a shelving unit. This was a complex problem requiring a solution that was not only functional but also efficient and reliable.
task_action: In response, a dedicated brainstorming session was organized. We used the gallery method of brainstorming, which allows individual team members to develop ideas independently and then share them on paper around the room for collective discussion and refinement. This method was chosen to encourage diverse contributions and prevent any single perspective from dominating the discussion. After generating several potential solutions, we systematically evaluated each one based on specific parameters such as weight, complexity, and manufacturability. These were ranked, and the most suitable design was selected for implementation. Following this decision, the tasks required to develop the selected design were clearly assigned to different team members, according to their expertise and roles within the project. This clear allocation of responsibilities was essential for efficient project execution and management. This example illustrates the pivotal roles and responsibilities of engineers, involving not just technical expertise but also strategic planning, collaborative problem-solving, and effective project management. These components are vital for transforming theoretical ideas into practical, implementable engineering solutions.
pfr: I felt a strong sense of responsibility during the process. Knowing that the effectiveness of the solution would directly impact the operational efficiency of the system we were developing added a layer of urgency and significance to my role. However, the task of evaluating and selecting the most appropriate solution brought a sense of apprehension, as the decision had significant implications. Critical Analysis: Analyzing the situation, I realize the importance of clear communication and structured methodology in collaborative engineering tasks. The gallery method ensured that every team member could contribute without bias, which maximized our creative potential and leveraged diverse expertise effectively. However, I noticed that the criteria for evaluating the solutions could have been better defined. At times, discussions around manufacturability and complexity became subjective, which could potentially lead to inconsistencies in our evaluations.
learning: From this reflection, I've learned the crucial role that structured critique plays in the brainstorming process. Ensuring that evaluation criteria are as objective and quantifiable as possible will streamline decision-making and enhance the fairness and effectiveness of the selection process. I've also gained a deeper appreciation for the psychological aspects of teamwork in engineering. Maintaining an environment where team members feel valued and heard is essential for fostering innovation. Future Actions: In future projects, I will advocate for and implement more precise evaluation criteria from the outset. I will also focus on enhancing my leadership skills to better support team dynamics and ensure that each member feels empowered to contribute their best work. Additionally, I will continue to refine my ability to balance the technical and managerial aspects of engineering projects to promote both innovative solutions and effective project execution. Reflecting on this experience has reinforced my understanding of the multidimensional roles and responsibilities of engineers, which extend beyond technical tasks to include leadership, teamwork, and strategic decision-making. This reflection will guide my future actions and interactions within engineering teams, aiming to enhance both the process and the products of our collective efforts.

topic: Perseverance, urgency and will to deliver, resourcefulness and flexibility
situation: While developing a software project using C programming for "Rock, Paper, Scissors" with different gestures, I faced the challenge of determining the winner for varying numbers of gestures (5, 7, 9, and 11) while ensuring adherence to the game's rules. In this game, three possible outcomes exist: a tie occurs when both players have the same outcome, and the game continues until one player wins at least two times. Victory or defeat is based on a player's gesture chosen against another player.
task_action: My task involved creating a program to play "Rock, Paper, Scissors" against a computer with varying numbers of gestures (5, 7, 9, and 11), demonstrating how the game determines the winner and functions until one player wins at least two times. To achieve this, I developed a program that handled player input, generated computer gestures, and compared gestures to determine the winner and manage the game flow. My perseverance was evident in my refusal to give up when my initial algorithm failed to handle games with 7, 9, or 11 gestures. By analysing the rules of the Rock Paper Scissors Lizard Spock game, I implemented a simple logic using even and odd to determine the winner for 5 gestures only and another using another mathematical algorithm for 7,9 and 11 based on the chosen gestures. This experience taught me the importance of being resourceful and flexible in problem-solving.
result: Overall, my program meets all the requirements for various numbers of gestures following the game's rules and can easily accommodate additional gestures if necessary. It runs efficiently, utilising only a small amount of the codebase, demonstrating my ability to flexibly understand and resolve complex problems.
pfr: I applied my programming skills to create a fun and interactive game throughout the project's development. However, I encountered challenges that tested my problem-solving abilities. My main challenge is to resolve the mathematical algorithm based on even and odd numbers to determine the winner that works for 5 gestures. After testing the same algorithm applied on 7,9, and 11, I soon realised this approach was unsuitable for all numbers of gestures, particularly when determining the winner in games with 7, 9, or 11 gestures, which led to game logic errors.
learning: This experience taught me a lesson to reflect on, outlining the importance of planning and testing in program development. I realised that I should have spent more time analysing the game's rules and designing a more robust solution that could handle all possible numbers of gestures. When I encountered errors in my initial approach, I chose not to give up but instead sought alternative solutions and eventually found a more effective way to handle the different numbers of gestures (including 5,7,9 and 11). This experience has not only strengthened my problem-solving skills but has also instilled in me a greater sense of urgency and commitment to delivering high-quality work. This also taught me setbacks are growth opportunities and that with perseverance and a flexible mindset, even the most challenging problems can be overcome.

situation: I was required to draw 3 different diagrams of a 3D-printed object, in order to communicate the size and properties of the object on paper.
task_action: First the object was drawn in 2 point perspective, utilising two vanishing points two effectively convey the 3 dimensional nature of the object and a separate, detachable piece in two separate drawings. This 3D nature was further expanded on in my isometric drawing, where the x and z axes of the object were each drawn 30 degrees from the horizontal. Finally, I drew a multi-view drawing of the 3D-printed object, using 2D perspectives from it's top, front and side views to portray it's shape from different angles in a detailed manner. In order to ensure the readers understanding of the object, a detachable piece of the object was drawn separately, using appropriate labelling to communicate it's cylindrical nature. The drawing was made in a 3:1 scale and included appropriately labelled dimensioning to accurately convey the size of the object.
result: 5 drawings were made, each with their appropriate features in order to communicate the shape, size and nature of the provided object.
pfr: The multi-view drawing was approached methodically and accurately. With the correct use of a compass and the provided tools I was able to provide two neat, accurate and informative portrayals of the 3D-printed object and the detached piece from all 3 perspectives. The isometric drawing was informative, well scaled, using accurately measured 30 degree angles and sizing to convey the 3 dimensional features of the object. This drawing, however was not as neat as it could have been and only consisted of the main piece of the object, primarily because of the circular holes, which were drawn in freehand in the interest of time. The 2 point perspective, on the other hand, included both drawings, with the sketch of the main piece, providing accurate placement of vanishing points and their respective lines. This main piece, however, was too small to utilise the space on the A3 paper well, due to the 1:1 scale, while the detached piece was done in correct scale. The detached piece was not as neat and did not effectively utilise the vanishing points as there was not enough time to consider the neatness and orientation of the piece.
learning: Overall time management could have been utilised better, as too much time was spent perfecting the multi-view drawing, leaving little time to consider neatness and plan for the isometric and 2 point perspective drawings. Additionally, I learned the compass should have been better utilised in these two drawings, as I did not employ the correct method of drawing circles at angles, often leaving them messy and inaccurate.

Furthermore, I had to use more time throughout the week working on the incomplete exercises so that I could show it to the tutors again to get my full mark. This put more overwhelming pressure as the project deadline was getting closer. This involved 30-60 minutes of learning basic C programming and 1 hour of doing my project. Only after two days, I had gained sufficient knowledge for C programming, so I ended up working on my project for 2 hours every day, until the deadline. I remembered that I had a similar program of my project, and utilised parts of code from there in my program. After believing that I had made 70% of my project completion, it relieved some stress. I also wished I could have read the notification more thoroughly, despite having 4 weeks to work on the project. However, I had very little knowledge in C language, as I did not put sufficient time into learning it at home, and I struggled a lot during the workshop exercises. This led to having to do the work at home and showing it to the tutor the week after for better marks. I was disorganised with my time, so if I completed my workshop exercises, I didn’t spend time on the project. All my decisions led to having a week available before the project deadline. At this point I remembered there being a provided code of a regular rock paper scissors game from workshop 3, as the exercises required me to do code modifications. It included parts that I needed for my project, and I thought that I could use it. I also used ChatGPT to assist me with what syntax would be most suitable for the task I was doing. In my case, I needed to make winning combinations for a total of 11 hand gestures, and ChatGPT suggested I use 2D Arrays. My choices affected my time management tremendously as I had to put 4 weeks' worth of work into 1 week. On the first two days, I was pressured from the close deadline, therefore hindering my ability to learn C programming. Furthermore, my poor time management skills led to being inconsistent with the way I worked on my project such as doing it late at night, but sometimes I would work on it in the morning. I assumed that if I ever had less progress and had a week left before the project deadline, I could avoid it by following a routine, where I learn C programming and use what I learnt to do the workshop exercises and then I could work on my project’s program throughout the weeks, rather than cramming my time into learning C before the project deadline. Although the situation ended up as I predicted, I was never able to use my prevention plan, so I had to create a new routine, where I had to cram knowledge of C programming and only use necessary parts of C relevant to my project completion. In my case, as part of my learning, I had to use ChatGPT to help me with how I could create winning combinations for 11 gestures, and the AI's suggestion was to use 2D Arrays. At this point, I had not learned arrays yet, so I needed to understand it so I could explain it to the tutor for the Project Q&A.
learning: From this analysis, I realise that discipline is my highest priority, in terms of carrying out set tasks. During my analysis I was able to recognise that the situation could occur, but I could not avoid it since I did not follow the initial plan. As a result, I ended up putting a great unnecessary amount of effort only to forget what I learnt after submitting the project. For the next workshop and its project, I will ensure a plan is made with simple instructions, and over time, the number of tasks increases, to ensure that I can complete my project. As a result, it eases my ability to learn a concept and use it practically with a flexible amount of time to work on the project, rather than cramming the knowledge and forgetting it in a week's time. From this experience, I have learned that I should use my time more effectively by being more disciplined in making and following effective routines that can lead to the completion of my project. Furthermore, I will follow a routine, where I can complete pre-requisites for my workshops, so I can complete my exercises, and hopefully use what I learned from there for my next project. I also learned not to rely on ChatGPT even if it was to make suggestions and even if the situation is dire, as that would violate the purpose of being creative and using critical thinking skills for creating something. However, I will effectively use ChatGPT to help elaborate on a concept that I don’t understand. I will ensure that I read the project notification to see what tasks need to be completed, and also reach out to teachers or fellow students for clarification on the task. Furthermore, I will also try to be more disciplined in creating effective routines and following them, to ensure the project is 100% completed.
