To do this, I first sorted each of my tasks for all of my units upon receiving them, by both importance and urgency. I then completed the tasks at the top of the list and worked my way downwards. At the end of each week's work, I would evaluate: - How much work was left to complete - How much work I had completed / How much effort I had put into my studies - How well I had adhered to the planner - Whether any part/s of the planner were inefficient/ineffective - My mental health/stress regarding it
result: This method was very effective, however was also very time consuming and thus stressful. Although I kept ahead of most of my work, whenever I fell behind, my motivation to work would lower as the amount of work I needed to complete stacked up. To improve this method, I would create a physical checklist where you can tick off each individual task (my checklist was a simple dot-point list). This would help with the stresses of work piling up, as it shows that work is still being completed. More significantly, I would separate the sorting list into individual units, so that I can see how much work is left for each individual class. This would allow me to complete work based on a third factor, being the workload for the class, as when using my planner, I noticed that I was very far ahead on certain subject as I had ranked them as more important/urgent, and this left my other subjects with a large amount of uncompleted work.
pfr: Upon first beginning my planner/evaluation method and the 'Technical Drawing' class itself, I was very anxious and stressed as I was unsure of what would be expected of me. Upon receiving the first load of work from the class, I had a mostly positive response to it, as although there was a large amount of work to be completed, I was allocated a large portion of time to complete it during the class, which meant I had little to complete at home. Overall I was initially and when the work piled up I was very stressed and anxious, however I was able to prioritize my work and focus on learning.
learning: By organizing, prioritizing and focusing, I was able to complete all of my allocated work with time to spare before the due date. I was mentally very positive, from using the plan I had created. All of my work was completed to a standard that I was happy with and the extra time the planner provided, gave me a mostly stress-free experience. This method is very effective, however can be time consuming. The only issues I experienced with it was that creating/editing the planner itself took a large amount of time. As I have a large amount of free time, this problem was not one of great importance to me, however if someone else or myself were more busy, it could have greatly impacted my work

situation: My task was to construct a toolbox out of aluminum that adhered to the provided instructions using the given equipment within the allocated time frame for my ENG1000 unit.

My first bend was unsuccessful as I aligned the crease with the hinge in the machine rather than the clamp. Despite this, I continued to bend the other pieces correctly after learning my mistake. After ensuring my pieces correctly fit together I riveted them in place and installed the polished handle. Once all of this was complete, some of the corner edges didn’t line up correctly so I decided to use the belt sander to remove these parts and hammered in any parts that protruded.
result: My efforts ultimately culminated in a functional, durable toolbox that received kudos from those around me. situation: In Year 12 our engineering studies class had an assignment to create a rocket and reach high altitudes by modifying and innovating the design of the rocket.
task_action: The rocket design started with a 2-litre bottle without any modifications, resulting in a height of 15 meters. After receiving a baseline height, we attached a nose cone to the top of the rocket. We used a styrofoam dome, which reduced the height to 13.1 meters. So, we innovated the design to the conical top half of a Coke bottle, which enhanced the height to 17.7 meters. Following this, we constructed our first set of rocket fins, consisting of four elliptical wooden fins, which achieved a height of 9.7 meters but proved excessively heavy. We then redesigned the fins innovating it by using corflute material and changing the amount of fins to three elliptical fins, resulting in an improved trajectory of 16.4 meters. Further innovation led to a redesign of the fin shape into a trapezoidal fin, which allowed for rocket to reach a height of 20.3 meters, showing successful innovation. Our final innovation involved the addition of an epoxy resin cone to the top which replaced the Coke bottle conical top, this enhanced the tip and provided a counterweight, causing the best result of 27.5 meters.
result: The results showed how the innovation process is used to improve the rocket altitude. this was proven successful with the final rocket launch being 27.5m
pfr: This task was fun as it allowed for a fun way to show the innovation process as we brainstormed different ideas and see what worked the best. It allowed for the development of different factors that went into a rocket like shape, material, amount of fins etc. the design was good as it reflected the aspects of innovation.
learning: The process of innovation through water rockets helped with brainstorming different ideas with my group, it also allowed us to do critical thinking to make decisions on the next design and made us figure out why this happened. The most interesting thing learnt from using the innovation process was finding out why some things worked better than others e.g. the Coke conical top and the epoxy top, the epoxy top provided a counterweight that allowed for a straighter rocket trajectory. From my experience, the importance of the innovation process is clear as it shows how to think critically and always improve the rocket.

topic: Perseverance, urgency and will to deliver, resourcefulness and flexibility
situation: While developing the Rock Paper Scissors Lizard Spock game expansion, I encountered a significant challenge in scaling the traditional decision-making algorithm from the classic three gestures to include additional gestures like Lizard, Spock, and more, up to a total of 11 gestures. The complexity of the decision tree was growing exponentially, making the game logic unwieldy and error-prone.
task_action: My task was to redesign the decision-making algorithm to handle the increased complexity efficiently without sacrificing the game's performance and scalability. The goal was to ensure the algorithm could reliably determine the winner in a game with up to 11 different gestures. ACTION: I initiated the redesign by researching various algorithmic strategies that could handle larger datasets and complex decision trees effectively. After consulting with my project advisor and reviewing academic papers, I decided to implement a modular arithmetic approach, which promised to simplify the winner determination process. I developed a mathematical model where each gesture was assigned a unique value, and the winner could be determined through simple arithmetic operations based on these values. I then coded the new algorithm, integrated it into the existing game framework, and conducted multiple rounds of testing to ensure its accuracy and efficiency.
result: The implementation of the modular arithmetic-based algorithm was a success. It not only reduced the complexity of the game logic significantly but also improved the execution speed. The new algorithm could effortlessly determine the winner among the 11 gestures, maintaining game fairness and enhancing user experience. The testing phase confirmed its reliability, as it accurately determined the winner in all scenarios without any errors. This approach also enhanced the game's maintainability, making it easier to add more gestures in the future if needed.
pfr: At the outset of redeveloping the game algorithm for Rock Paper Scissors Lizard Spock, I felt overwhelmed by the complexity that the addition of new gestures introduced. The initial algorithm, while adequate for fewer gestures, became cumbersome and less efficient as more gestures were added. This challenge put my problem-solving skills to the test, and admittedly, I was unsure whether I could devise a solution that maintained both the integrity and performance of the game. However, as I delved deeper into potential solutions, my anxiety transformed into excitement. The process of researching, designing, and testing the new algorithm became a journey of discovery, revealing new ways to apply mathematical concepts to real-world applications.
learning: The experience taught me several invaluable lessons about critical thinking and algorithm design. First, it underscored the importance of adopting a flexible and open-minded approach when tackling complex problems. The modular arithmetic solution emerged only after I considered several potential strategies, which highlighted the necessity of thorough exploration before settling on a solution. Second, I learned that simplicity often trumps complexity in design. The elegance of the modular arithmetic approach not only solved the problem but did so in a way that was more maintainable and scalable than the original method. This insight has led me to appreciate the power of mathematical simplicity and its application in software development. Finally, the experience has profoundly impacted how I will approach future engineering challenges. I've learned the value of stepping back to assess the bigger picture—especially in situations where initial solutions don't adequately solve the problem. Moving forward, I will incorporate a phase of broad research and conceptual experimentation before honing in on a specific solution. This broader initial approach will help ensure that I am not only solving problems more effectively but also innovating in ways that could lead to better overall outcomes. This project has instilled a greater confidence in me to handle uncertainty and complexity in my future engineering career. It has also highlighted the importance of critical thinking and the role it plays in the innovation process, reinforcing that every problem, no matter how daunting initially, can be approached systematically and effectively solved with the right strategies and mindset.

topic: Initiative and the willingness to make decisions in the face of uncertainty
situation: Working as a plumber I received an urgent call on my non working day from a client regarding a burst water pipe.
task_action: Immediately I notified the client to turn the residents' water off at the meter. Upon my arrival at the site I saw water leaking from the bathroom wall through the tiles. I was required to determine the location of the leak within the bathroom wall to begin repairs. First I examined the wall to pinpoint exactly where the water was leaking from. Once located I used a specialised thermal imagery camera to inspect the area for further water damage. This allowed me to see hot water leaking from the pipe in a rough area within the tiled wall. Next I made the decision to carefully remove the tiles in the surrounding area. Using a jack hammer and chisel I removed the render to reveal two copper pipes. Once properly exposed, I assessed the damage to the copper pipe within the wall. The 15mm copper hot water pipe had split causing the leak. I proceeded to fix the damage pipe by cutting and removing the section of split copper. Once removed I cleaned and prepped the copper within the wall to replace the split section. With my specialised crimping tool I reconnected the piping with copper crimp sockets making the joins water tight and secure. Subsequently the water supply was turned back on to check for leaks ensuring the problem was resolved.
result: Through this display of initiative and willingness to make decisions during uncertainty I was able to successfully locate the cause of the issue and provide a carefully considered solution. In doing so there was no further damage to the property. In conjunction providing an efficient response with minimal disruption to the client guaranteed a positive experience for all parties involved.
pfr: The emergency call out from the client was concerning, specifically the feeling of not knowing the damage caused to the scene prior to my arrival. By reacting quickly to the situation and notifying the client to turn the water off to the whole residents whilst on the phone I knew I was reducing the risk of further water damage to the property which provided a sense of calm. Once I arrived it felt important to make sure the client was aware of the necessary process to find the leak as this involved removing tiles and using power tools in their bathroom. In addition I was worried about how much damage I would cause when locating the leak. However using the thermal imagery camera made me feel confident on where to start removing tiles and render. Similarly the use of drop sheets increased my feelings of confidence by protecting the floor tiles and surrounding bathroom fixtures preventing further damage. Overall I felt happy with the outcome.
learning: This experience taught me the importance of being ready in any circumstances to receive an emergency call out even on my non-working days. Responding promptly saved the client money and demonstrated our company values to provide a professional service, even outside of standard business hours. In conjunction I learnt the importance of explaining the process to the client to ensure they understood why I was required to cause damage to their bathroom. Providing the client with comfort and confidence in my abilities. The positive result of this experience has given me confidence in my ability to show initiative when making decisions.

topic: The impact of engineering on society and the environment
situation: We were required to design a 4-bit binary adder for Aurdino on TinkerCad. Each LED light represented a bit, and the motherboard would add the bits entered upon the press of a button and show the results in decimal and hexadecimal values—the project aimed to demonstrate the practical application of digital logic and programming concepts in hardware design.
task_action: This project was an individual assessment. To achieve this objective, we extensively studied the fundamental principles of binary addition. We then specified the 4-bit binary adder prerequisites, encompassing the input/output setups and operating criteria. Using the powerful tools of Tinkercad and Arduino IDE, we constructed the circuit architecture by strategically selecting and arranging the essential components within the virtual environment. This included input switches, output display LEDs, and Arduino microcontroller boards. We rigorously simulated the circuit before proceeding with the coding process to ensure its correct operation. With the Arduino IDE, we meticulously programmed and debugged the code to gain complete control over the binary addition process. We implemented functions to execute binary addition, which included mechanisms to manage carry-over bits and identify issues such as overflow or underflow. The code was optimised for efficiency and accuracy, considering the limited resources of the Arduino microcontroller.
result: We achieved the effective execution of a 4-bit binary adder by utilizing Arduino microcontrollers and software-based algorithms. We were able to check the accuracy of the addition process and see the output using virtual LEDs in the Tinkercad simulation, which did a good job of showing how the binary adder worked. We thoroughly tested the binary adder using a range of input combinations to verify its durability and dependability. The utilization of software-based methods obviated the necessity for tangible logic gates, hence streamlining the circuit design and diminishing the hardware's intricacy. In addition, we recorded the coding methodologies and algorithms employed in the project to disseminate expertise and perspectives to those interested in digital circuitry design and programming for embedded systems. The Tinkercad simulation functioned as an instructional instrument, offering a practical learning opportunity for students and amateurs investigating Arduino-based projects. In summary, the project showcased the flexibility and capabilities of Arduino microcontrollers to carry out intricate computational tasks without relying on additional hardware components. The demonstration exhibited the effectiveness of software-based solutions in designing digital circuits and emphasised the possibilities of simulation tools such as Tinkercad in creating and evaluating electronic systems.
pfr: At first, the challenge of constructing a 4-bit binary adder using Arduino without employing logic gates seemed intimidating. As an individual with expertise in conventional circuit design, I find the prospect of depending exclusively on software algorithms for binary addition alien and daunting. As I immersed myself more in the project and began investigating coding methodologies and algorithms, I experienced a surge of enthusiasm and curiosity. The idea of performing binary addition only through software manipulation piqued my curiosity and motivated me to investigate novel approaches to engineering challenges. While working on the project, I experienced irritation and anxiety, especially during the debugging process when I found problems and unpredictable behaviour in the code. Nevertheless, these hurdles proved to be excellent learning experiences, compelling me to enhance my coding abilities and cultivate a more profound comprehension of the complexities of binary arithmetic and microcontroller programming.
learning: This project gave me a profound respect for the beneficial effects engineering can have on the environment and society, particularly when combined with such adaptable instruments as Arduino microcontrollers. It highlighted the value of imagination and adaptability in engineering and demonstrated how novel ideas might result from nonconformist thinking. The project also highlighted the significance of software-driven solutions in contemporary engineering. situation: We were required to design a 4-bit binary adder for Aurdino on TinkerCad. With the Arduino IDE, we meticulously programmed and debugged the code to gain complete control over the binary addition process. We implemented functions to execute binary addition, which included mechanisms to manage carry-over bits and identify issues such as overflow or underflow. result: We achieved the effective execution of a 4-bit binary adder by utilizing Arduino microcontrollers and software-based algorithms. We thoroughly tested the binary adder using a range of input combinations to verify its durability and dependability. In addition, we recorded the coding methodologies and algorithms employed in the project to disseminate expertise and perspectives to those interested in digital circuitry design and programming for embedded systems. The Tinkercad simulation functioned as an instructional instrument, offering a practical learning opportunity for students and amateurs investigating Arduino-based projects. The demonstration exhibited effectiveness of software-based solutions in designing digital circuits and emphasised the possibilities of simulation tools such as Tinkercad in creating and evaluating electronic systems.

topic: Initiative and the willingness to make decisions in the face of uncertainty
situation: - Background information: I currently work as a casual FOH member focused mainly on bartending at the Macquarie Strike Bowling bar. my responsibilities are as follow, watching and monitoring RSA, and helping other staff with their duties such as cleaning and things like escape rooms, laser tag, and karaoke. One day were fairly low on business and a small group of lads come in looking for a game or two of bowling, seeing as its not busy we offer them a discount for their first game. As they're playing they purchase one or two standards worth of drinks between two people. As their game continues, our manager for the night stepped into the office to eat and complete end of night tasks so I (bartender at the time) sit at the front monitoring the games as per usual. Shortly after my manager is not seen by the group they start goofing around with how they bowl. Two times they throw a ball down the lane and it hits the pin sweep (this shuts their lane down to prevent more damage) and are told not to do it again. As I walk down again, they do it again.
task_action: - My coworker (casual manager but not the one currently managing this shift) and I talk for a moment, and agree that they're doing it on purpose as they are not intoxicated nor handicapped; and shouldn't be allowed to continue as they can cause damage to the machines. Subsequently, I tell them their game is suspended and were more than happy to talk about compensation for the missing turns. As I walk to the front desk another ball is thrown down in anger; likely due to their "wasted" money. As such, in a tone that everyone in their group can here I say "If that's how you're going to act, get out, and get out now." as they walk out and i check their table for the drinks i served earlier, i realize they took them outside the venue (a licensing issue), as such a short pursuit ensues as i find them finishing their drinks not five feet from the door. I request them back in a civil manner (they're already chugging them) they become hostile, slinging threats and vile language. I take their cups and request that they never come back as, "guests like y'all ruin everyone's night, not just your own."
result: - Company kept their machines in better condition, venue was kept in order/ fun was still able to be had by other guests, drink glasses were recovered that would not have been. - A small scolding in addition to praise for adhering to a venue rule: No Un-chill behavior.
pfr: - The folks described, without using the word id like to; were off putting since the beginning. I have been working in the service/hospitality industry for just under a decade, and its almost a gut feeling of whether or not an individual or group will be trouble. It was semi close to closing, and we were fairly quiet so it makes sense to have certain groups push their luck because someone in the group simply want to see what we (the workers) would do. I know the sentiment as i used to do the same when i was younger, causing trouble at a local mattress store. Talking to folks, especially reprimanding them as adults almost never goes as well as id like. Though they would receive it, they wouldn't recognize the authority behind it. As such i was especially nervous dealing with the last ball thrown as they had already been admonished thrice prior. Although I prefer to be polite, it simply was not the time for it. Yelling those words, as my co-worker can attest can bring a situation from bad to worse depending on the type of people we handle. I don't care about insults, but threats of violence i take very seriously as they had slung them i pushed them out of the building. The confrontation outside the venue was the most tense as i did not have anyone else other than passerby's looking on while i attempted to get the glasses back. Even then, I had a feeling if this was not as public they would have done something a bit more extreme.
learning: - While actively attempting to verbally rationalize with folks, sometimes communication can break down. Even in those cases its better to keep a cool and professional head to avoid unforeseen consequences, such as them leaving the venue with drinks in hand out of defiance or a physical altercation. In future situations, instead of confrontation we simply stop the game and wait for them to either leave or act until we make any more decisions.

The eventual goal is to have the game, such that there would be an indefinite amount of signs. In addition, it is important to consider that C is a statically typed language, with potential memory unsafety.
result: I haven't started yet, but I imagine the lizard-spock (5 gesture) game can be simply managed with a nested set of if conditions to achieve the correct results. This is not possible for an indefinite amount, without generalising the solution mathematically. Firstly, I'll define a function that asks for the amount of gestures in the game. Then it's a simple, alternating handshake (e.g. u choose 5 gestures, then each gesture has a relationship with the other gestures, alternating in win/loss. int x=n.o. gestures; => Create a struct of x length => choose 1 gesture => if the gesture is odd, get the first even, => if the f=gesture is even, get the first odd => This way the computer will always win, so if it is randomly picked - check both gestures if even/odd or same and return the winner
pfr: I was able to come up with my solution, by examining the figure provided in the assignment sheet. Essentially, I could clearly visualise that each gesture is related to one another in either 2 ways. Critical thinking can be sparked using visual aids which clearly define the scope of a particular problem - including the relationship between all the variables. The solution I posed would require iterating through the array of gestures (unnamed, just numbers), twice so the time complexity of O(2n) = O(n). The space complexity of O(1) as it only requires the single array, N values. Of course, this is not the only solution, and as I have not tested anything yet, this could all be negated.
learning: This exercise was simply to reinforce that I am a visual learner. It's a fun exercise but I don't personally see life-long learning as a result.

situation: In my role as a communications assistant at a small startup company, we needed to launch a new product on a limited budget. The CEO emphasized the importance of a strong communications strategy to generate buzz and attract customers.

Given our limited resources, creativity and strategic planning were essential. Action: I began by researching our target market and competitors to identify potential communication channels. We decided to focus on social media platforms like Instagram and Twitter, as well as email newsletters to engage existing customers and attract new ones. I created a content calendar outlining our messaging and promotional activities leading up to the launch date. We developed eye-catching visuals and crafted compelling copy to highlight the unique features of the product and its benefits to customers. To maximize our reach, I reached out to influencers in our industry and secured partnerships for sponsored posts and product reviews. Additionally, I coordinated with our customer service team to ensure prompt responses to inquiries and feedback from customers.
result: Thanks to our strategic communications efforts, the product launch was a success. We received positive feedback from customers and saw a significant increase in website traffic and sales. The buzz generated on social media helped raise awareness of our brand and establish credibility in the market.
pfr: Throughout the process of developing the communications strategy, I felt a sense of responsibility and excitement. It was rewarding to see our efforts pay off and contribute to the company's success. Despite the challenges of working with limited resources, I remained optimistic and focused on finding creative solutions to achieve our goals.
learning: This experience taught me the importance of adaptability and resourcefulness in developing effective communications strategies, especially in a small business environment. I gained practical skills in market research, content creation, and influencer outreach that I can apply in future roles. Moving forward, I will continue to refine my communications skills and stay updated on industry trends to remain competitive. I also recognize the value of collaboration and teamwork in achieving shared objectives, leveraging the strengths of each team member to drive results. situation: I was involved in the coordination and implementation of an international motorsport drift school as well as the maintenance and modification of approximately 40 individual customers vehicles for a quarterly event.
task_action: As part of the management involved in the coordinating of both school and customer vehicles, our role was to ensure that both school vehicles and customers vehicles adhered to strict safety regulations, as well as any other requested maintenance or modifications were carried out in the time frame required and in accordance with the rules and regulations of the venue holding the event. Action: Due to the number of vehicles that required attention, we implemented strict deadlines for both requests for maintenance and requests for modification. Our initial focus was on school vehicles for both modification and maintenance, as they had priority, followed by customer vehicle maintenance including modifications that were required for said vehicles to meet the standard to compete in the event. Everything else then followed. This allowed for a structured list of vehicles to be completed with given deadlines and timeframes for each vehicle including the required work to be carried out.
result: The result was that everyone involved in the preparation for the event was well informed of the required work to be carried out, which vehicles took priority over others and the type of work that required more focus than others.
pfr: Due to the number of vehicles that required our attention, standard required for the work carried out on the vehicles, and the inherent safety requirements to any motorsport event, the organization and prioritization proved to be rather challenging. Breaking down the requirements of each vehicle into separate sub categories we were able to prioritize each vehicle in relation to another and build a list of priority for work to be completed. This however proved challenging as each vehicle required different levels of work to be completed, as well as basic levels of safety modifications to be done. This often lead to vehicles being not completed in entirety, but instead to a level that allowed the vehicle to compete in the event even in its incomplete state.
learning: While effort was put into best prioritizing each vehicle, it was often difficult to differentiate between two vehicles and deciding on what work should be carried out first. I discovered that often we had to prioritize safety aspects relating to vehicles ahead of all other work as the timeframe given for each vehicle was often not adequate to carry out to completion. This experience showed me that although best efforts were put into the organization, often we are met with challenges that simply cannot allow us to achieve 100%, and that we are often required to sacrifice in one aspect or another. While I believe that there are a number of ways to help alleviate and combat this, our best short term solution for near future events is to reduce the workload per member by either reducing the number of vehicles being taken care of, or increasing the number of workers involved.

situation: In November 2023, whilst trying to avoid wildlife on my motorcycle on the bend of a road near the Royal National Park, I lost control of the motorcycle and crashed leading to a 40 metre slide on the pavement . The aftermath left me with negligible injuries due to my PPE, however my motorcycle was stuck in a high gear as the gear linkage was severed and thus was unable to start.
task_action: I used my understanding of combustion engines to concur that I needed to perform a running start. To do so I pushed the motorcycle up a nearby hill, used a rock to bend the handlebars back into their original position and adjusted the clutch cable. Once the bike was ready, I proceeded to ride it down the hill whilst holding the ignition button.
result: As I had hit a set speed the bike came to life and I was able to ride the grueling two hours home in third gear, with torn leathers and a concussion.
pfr: After the slide I was left with an unclear mind, probably due to a mixture of a concussion, adrenaline and confusion. With emotions running high I found it difficult to focus on what had just happened and how to resolve the issue at hand. Once I had cleared the road of my motorcycle and its debris, I sat down to focus what had just happened I used this time to control my breathing. During this period I experienced a flush of emotions, anger at the kangaroo, myself and the bike, pain to my pride, future finances and my body. However through this I was able to push through and use critical thinking to assess the situation, what had happened and what I need to do which allowed me to overcome the situation.
learning: By allowing myself time to process the situation I had at hand I allowed myself to not act on my emotions and thus I had controlled my emotions and not vice-versa. Causing my triumph through the situation, and teaching me a valuable lesson on the impedance emotion has on critical thinking and the need for processing emotions on the problem at hand.

situation: During my engineering project, I worked solo on developing a 4-bit binary adder using Arduino. The project involved using buttons as binary inputs and LEDs to display the results. Later, I integrated an LCD to show the addition results in Decimal and Hexadecimal formats. I encountered a significant issue with the inconsistent toggling of LEDs and inaccurate display outputs on the LCD.
task_action: To address this problem, I applied critical thinking and a structured problem-solving approach. First, I carefully analyzed the circuit and code to identify potential causes of the inconsistencies. I tested each component individually to ensure they functioned correctly and reviewed my code for logical errors. I brainstormed several potential solutions, such as debouncing the buttons, checking faulty connections, and optimizing the code for better performance. After evaluating these solutions based on feasibility and expected effectiveness, I implemented software debouncing for the buttons and rewired the circuit to ensure better connections. I also refined the code to accurately store and display the binary addition results on the LEDs and the LCD.
result: Implementing software debouncing and circuit rewiring significantly improved the reliability of the LED toggling and the accuracy of the LCD display. The 4-bit binary adder functioned as expected, with the LEDs correctly displaying the binary addition results and the LCD accurately showing the results in both Decimal and Hexadecimal formats. This successful outcome was demonstrated during my final project presentation, receiving positive feedback from professors. The project was also featured in the department's annual showcase, highlighting my effective use of critical thinking to resolve engineering challenges independently.
pfr: Initially, I experienced a sense of frustration and apprehension when confronted with the issues in my 4-bit binary adder project. Undertaking a complex task independently was intimidating, and the irregularities with the LED and LCD outputs were particularly challenging. I was genuinely concerned about my ability to resolve these issues without external assistance. However, a sense of control and clarity emerged as I systematically analyzed the circuit and reviewed the code. Decomposing the problem into smaller, manageable components and rigorously testing each part enabled me to regain confidence. The process of brainstorming and evaluating potential solutions underscored the significance of critical thinking and methodical problem-solving.
learning: This experience underscored the importance of a structured approach to problem-solving. Decomposing complex issues into smaller tasks proved instrumental in making them more manageable. Additionally, the experience highlighted the necessity of patience and perseverance when addressing technical challenges. It became evident that meticulous attention to detail and thorough testing are crucial, mainly when working independently. In future endeavors, I will approach similar challenges with a more organized and systematic methodology, meticulously examining each component. Moreover, I recognize the importance of contingency planning and flexibility in developing solutions. This experience has significantly enhanced my critical thinking abilities and taught me to maintain composure and systematic thinking under pressure. I intend to apply these insights to refine my problem-solving strategies and improve the overall quality of my work in subsequent projects.

situation: Throughout my career as a Diagnostic Radiographer, I have actively engaged in maintaining my Continuing Professional Development (CPD) requirements. One notable experience was when I presented my first in-service, an oral presentation on the radiographic appearance of paediatric bone development.
task_action: I approached this in-service by conducting research on the general bone development cycle, and the ossification centres of the most common areas that we image in paediatric patients. I also explored the radiographic appearance of the ossification centres and their appearance/formation in relation to age, focusing mainly on the elbow, hand/wrist, ankle and foot. I used academic journals, reviewed case studies, and consulted the radiographer ‘bible’, Radiopedia.org, to collect accurate information that I needed for my presentation. I created a fabulously put together PowerPoint presentation, with images and radiographs (x-ray images) sourced from radiopedia.org or our departments picture archiving and communication system (PACS). I created a speech and practiced my spiel for about a week prior to the actual presentation.
result: The in-service was well-received by my colleagues. The inclusion of images and radiographs reinforced the information, aiding in their understanding of the topic. Interactive components like the brief Q&A session and case studies enhanced their and my own learning experience. It also reinforced my commitment to lifelong learning and sharing knowledge with peers to enhance our collective professional development. Feedback from the in-service session indicated that apart from being great, I need increased confidence my own presentation skills, and some colleagues suggested I should perform regular in-services on varying topics or case studies to improve said skills.
pfr: I felt that the preparation of my first in-service presentation was fine. I had no difficulty in researching and putting together the PowerPoint and speech, the actual presentation was another story. Even though, I thoroughly practiced my spiel prior I found it extremely nerve-wracking at the time. I jumbled my words, mispronounced a few medical terms and spoke faster then I had practiced. So, my initially timed speech of 25 mins, was finished in just 18 minutes instead. I didn’t pause or interact with the case studies as long as I had practiced prior. The responsibility of educating my peers, many of whom had more experience, was daunting. Practicing my speech multiple times helped alleviate some of my anxiety, although I still felt nervous on the day of the presentation. However, during the Q&A session I held after the presentation seeing my colleagues engage with the material was incredibly rewarding. I even went through the more interesting case studies in more detail during the Q&A session and in a more informal setting and I felt more relaxed and confident. Their positive feedback was a great validation of my efforts, but it also highlighted areas for improvement.
learning: This experience taught me several valuable lessons about lifelong learning and educating. Firstly, while thorough preparation and practice are crucial for delivering great content, unexpected nerves can impact delivery. Moving forward, I will focus not only on practicing but also on techniques to manage my anxiety and to maintain a steady pace. The feedback I received emphasized the need for ongoing practice and confidence-building in public speaking. Regularly conducting in-services on various topics will not only help me improve my presentation skills but also contribute to the continuous professional development of my colleagues. This experience has reinforced my commitment to lifelong learning and the importance of sharing knowledge to foster collective professional growth. The constructive criticism regarding my confidence and suggestions for more frequent in-services made me realize that continuous improvement (CPD) is a key aspect of professional growth.

situation: The whole class was assigned to create a toolbox out of either steel or aluminium.
task_action: I and the person that was at the same table as me decided to work together. We chose to do aluminium because it sounded faster to do, as it required using rivets to hold everything together, as opposed to steel requiring welding, which not a lot of people could do at once. We chose to do all the markings on the aluminium before any cutting or folding, so we could get it done quickly while other people were already using the equipment. The order that we chose to make the toolbox in helped us to make it faster than others, as we didn't have to wait for people to finish using equipment.
result: As a result of us building the toolbox in a different order to everyone else, we were able to finish first and not have to worry about waiting for equipment and potentially running out of time.
pfr: Initially the task of creating the toolbox seemed easy and quick to do, but upon actually beginning the process of making it, I realised it was going to take longer than anticipated, as I didn't yet know how to use some of the equipment, and sometimes had to wait for other people to finish using it before I could.
learning: By discussing with my partner, we figured out what order of making the toolbox would be quickest and easiest to ensure that we would finish it on time. This made me realise the importance of communicating with teammates.

topic: The impact of engineering on society and the environment
situation: In the previous workshop we were tasked with building student housing that along with many other attributes was sustainable.
task_action: We brainstormed ideas that were easy to add to our design that would greatly increase the efficiency of the building. Through some thought of the location and the climate we were able to ascertain some ideas on how to make the building more eco-friendly and sustainable. These solutions included facing the building towards the east so that it caught natural wind for the summer so that the air conditioning systems won't have to be utilised as much. Facing this direction would also allow the winter sun to penetrate the building as its rising in the morning allowing the building to warm naturally. The way it was built was also taken into consideration as the materials can leave quite the carbon footprint such as concrete and steel so where it can be used sustainably sourced wood was used.
result: The building was not only built with materials that reduced its footprint in the short term but also incorporated features that reduced it in the long term as well.
pfr: Finding solutions that would fit in the building that wouldn't be too costly or invasive was a bit difficult. But as this technology is used more it will become more cost efficient and widely used such as solar panels. Our building implemented many smart saving techniques which ultimately in the future will save money and the environment around it.
learning: As we progress into the future our processes to make and do things as a society are going to cost more energy and more emissions to accomplish. As engineers we share the forefront of this innovation so I believe that we should include sustainable features on all buildings to offset this ever growing revolution. In this project I was pushing myself to find solutions to make this housing as efficient as possible because one day I might be working on an actual project that would greatly benefit from these which may contribute to the bigger global issues providing a better Earth for future generations.

situation: In our software engineering course, we needed to brainstorm a design mechanism for unloading cans from a robot onto a shelving unit.
task_action: We organized a brainstorming session, forming a small working group with a clearly articulated problem statement. Using the gallery method of brainstorming, we generated several viable options. We then evaluated each suggested option and ranked them in order of importance based on parameters such as weight, complexity, and manufacturability.
result: We successfully selected a design solution from the six options generated during the brainstorming session. We divided the required tasks among team members for further development. REFLECTION: This experience significantly enhanced my communication skills in a software programming context. By articulating the problem clearly and using structured brainstorming techniques, we fostered an inclusive environment that encouraged diverse ideas. Evaluating and ranking the options required clear, concise communication and collaborative decision-making. This process not only improved my ability to convey technical information effectively but also underscored the importance of teamwork and structured communication in achieving successful project outcomes.
pfr: Initially, the task of brainstorming a design mechanism for unloading cans from a robot onto a shelving unit felt overwhelming. The problem seemed complex, and finding an optimal solution appeared daunting. However, as we systematically approached the problem using the gallery method, my apprehension lessened. Documenting each stage of our group decisions allowed us to clearly see our progress. Working collaboratively, we evaluated the merits of each proposed solution and came to a consensus on the best design. This structured approach turned an intimidating task into a manageable and even enjoyable process.
learning: This experience taught me the value of systematic decision-making and the importance of structured communication in a team setting. By using a merit-based approach and maintaining good team organization, we were able to navigate even the most complex problems efficiently. I realized that the concept of the "best design" is subjective and highly dependent on the specific constraints and requirements of the problem at hand. Moving forward, I will apply this structured, merit-based approach to future projects, recognizing that robust decision-making processes can significantly enhance team collaboration and project outcomes. Through this experience, I have gained a deeper appreciation for the power of organized, clear communication and systematic problem-solving in achieving successful results.

situation: Myself and my group members were tasked with an oral presentation during my second skill of ENGG1000 course. We were expected to be able to present in front of a diverse audience with a variety of ideas, individuals in different courses, and their own special set of expertise. The presentation topic was to create a residence management plan for Macquarie University's students, which recognized the need for a significant upgrade in the living environment for the students themselves. With outdated facilities and a lack of aesthetic appeal, there was a growing concern about student satisfaction and well-being in the residency.
task_action: As this was a collaborative effort, I was assigned the task of creating possible designs for the building as well as creating a plan for our group to complete set activities each week in order to make fluid progress. To tackle this task effectively, I first conducted extensive research into modern architectural trends, interior design principles, and student preferences. I also went above and beyond, as I questioned not only my peers but also the other students in my class about what they preferred. In the end, I finally came up with a few ideas myself, but I stuck with a few. This was the step-by-step process. * Our team consisted of bright students who brainstormed ideas and developed a cohesive vision for the project. * We conducted site visits to assess the current conditions of the student residences and identify areas for improvement. * Based on our research and insights gathered, we developed a detailed plan that included architectural modifications, interior design enhancements, and the integration of sustainable features. * We prioritized elements such as communal spaces for social interaction, natural lighting, greenery, and ergonomic furniture to enhance the overall living experience. * We also proposed implementing technology-enabled solutions to improve safety, convenience, and connectivity within the residence.
result: The presentation received enthusiastic feedback from the students in my class, including the teachers. The proposed redesign plan was well-received for its innovative approach and focus on student well-being. As a result, we were able to mostly complete the project; however, due to having fewer individuals on my team, we were not able to complete all physical aspects of the model. However, the basic idea was conveyed.
pfr: Throughout the project, I felt very excited to complete this. Even though there was no actual building construction involved in the project, creating a strong design concept felt like a big burden, as we only had 3 group members, and I was worried that the completion itself was at stake. I had moments of doubt during the planning phase, questioning whether our concepts would be well received by the audience and whether we had taken into account all relevant aspects. However, all our designs were actually quite appealing to the eye, so that wasn't too much of an issue. Luckily, we all got along well and had agreed on a final design for the building, not just because it was good, but also due to the time constraint.
learning: I've learned from this experience how important it is to conduct in-depth research and use creativity while solving problems, especially in speculative situations. Working with a varied group enabled us to take into account different viewpoints and investigate creative design concepts. I now see how important it is to make decisions in an organised manner and to communicate well in order to effectively offer ideas. In the future, I will do my best to tackle these projects head on and with confidence, in order to not have any worries or concerns, and to take initiative. Moreover, this experience has taught me to appreciate the value of my problem solving skills, as they come quite in handy in group projects.

situation: The task was to create a computer game on replit.com in Software Design Logic Workshop that pitted human players against a computer in the game “Rock Paper Scissors Lizard Spock” by adding two additional gestures to increase the complexity and variety of game "Rock Paper Scissors".
task_action: To tackle the task of implementing the "Rock, Paper, Scissors, Lizard Spock" rules, I first searched for the rules of the game and created a comprehensive table outlining which combinations would result in victory, defeat, or a draw. I then started coding in Replit, initially using basic conditional statements (IF and ELSE) to define the outcome of each possible combination. However, this approach makes the code somewhat complex due to the large number of combinations.
result: After I finished, I shared my coding logic with my friend, only to find that he had taken a different, more efficient approach. He used arrays and matrices, techniques I'm not very good at using. Through discussions, we exchanged design logic and realized that there are many ways to achieve the same goal and that there is no single “right” solution as long as the results are consistent.
pfr: Through this experience, I've realized that there are multiple ways to arrive at the same solution using different processes. Furthermore, sharing these processes with others can lead to the discovery of various ideas and solutions. Not only does this foster inclusivity and collaboration, but it also enables us to learn more practical and straightforward methods from different perspectives on the problem. Furthermore, by employing diverse problem-solving approaches, we open ourselves to a wealth of knowledge and creativity. Each person brings their unique insights and expertise, enriching the collective understanding and enhancing the overall learning experience.
learning: After creating and successfully playing a game of "Rock Paper Scissors Lizard Spock" in Replit, it dawned on me that there isn't just one way to showcase the outcomes, as long as the end result remains consistent. Having your own logical design ability and being able to express it yourself is what we difine the right solution.

situation: I was doing a team project for COMP1050 (Introduction to the Study of Software Engineering) that involved writing a final report to submit. We wrote Acceptance Criteria for the software that we were writing, which we included in an interim report.
task_action: As we wrote the final report, we did not coordinate who was responsible for writing what. All three of our team members worked in an ad hoc manner or whatever looked like it needed doing. We wrote the entire report in this manner. We managed tasks well for the software development part of the project, but not the report writing part of the project.
result: We didn't include the Acceptance Criteria (that we had written) in the final report. This happened despite all three of us stating that we were happy with the report and that it could be submitted.
pfr: I mostly feel stupid and annoyed, because this silly mistake is costing us marks for work that we did. I wish I could go back and compare the report to the marking rubric before submitting it. It was a failure in our group's process for writing the report, checking and submitting it. The lack of coordination allowed for a gap in what was done, and the fact that none of us were responsible for thoroughly checking the report and comparing it to the marking guide allowed us to make this mistake. This is probably the first time I have participated in a group activity that is this involved, and written a report like this, so it isn't so surprising that something went wrong.
learning: I have learned a lot about how not to write a report as a group. In the future, I will be communicating with my team better, earlier on, to break the writing down and distribute responsibility amongst all team members. The team member who submits would also be responsible for checking the whole final report, to ensure that nothing has been left out. This planning happened for the software part of the project, but no one in the team considered applying such a process to the report too. I have learned from that, and will be considering the entire project when planning with future teams.

topic: The impact of engineering on society and the environment
situation: As part of a sustainability initiative at our engineering firm, we were tasked with developing a new product that would significantly reduce environmental impact compared to existing alternatives. The goal was to design a water filtration system that could be used in both urban and rural settings, particularly in areas with limited access to clean water.
task_action: My role was to lead the research and development team in creating a sustainable and efficient water filtration system. This involved not only designing the product but also ensuring that the materials and manufacturing processes were environmentally friendly. Additionally, we needed to consider the social implications, making the system affordable and easy to use in developing communities. ACTION: * RESEARCH: Conducted extensive research on existing water filtration technologies to understand their environmental impact and efficiency. * BRAINSTORMING: Organized brainstorming sessions with my team to generate multiple design ideas, focusing on sustainability, cost-effectiveness, and ease of use. * EVALUATION: Evaluated each proposed design based on criteria such as environmental impact, cost, and usability, and selected the top three for further development. * PROTOTYPING: Created prototypes of the top three designs and conducted tests to assess their performance and environmental impact. * REFINEMENT: Refined the best-performing prototype based on feedback from field tests and stakeholder consultations.
result: * ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT: We successfully developed a water filtration system that reduced environmental impact by 40% compared to existing products, due to its use of sustainable materials and efficient manufacturing processes. * SOCIAL IMPACT: The system was affordable and easy to use, significantly improving access to clean water in underprivileged communities. It was deployed in multiple regions, benefiting over 10,000 households within the first year. * COMPANY RECOGNITION: Our project received positive recognition from industry peers and environmental organizations, enhancing our firm’s reputation for sustainable innovation. * ONGOING DEVELOPMENT: The project established a framework for future sustainable product development, with lessons learned being applied to other engineering challenges. By simplifying our approach and focusing on key actions, we achieved our project goals and made a meaningful impact on society and the environment through engineering innovation.
pfr: Initially, I felt overwhelmed by the complexity and significance of the task at hand. Developing a water filtration system that was not only effective but also sustainable and socially impact seemed like a monumental challenge. However, as we progressed through the systematic research, brainstorming, and prototyping phases, my initial anxiety transformed into a sense of purpose and collaboration. Working with my team, we navigated each stage methodically, and the collective effort and diverse perspectives made the task manageable and even inspiring. Seeing the positive impact our work had on communities reinforced the importance of our mission and the potential of engineering to drive meaningful change.
learning: This experience taught me the power of structured, merit-based decision-making and the value of collaboration in tackling complex problems. By systematically evaluating each design against clear criteria, we ensured that our final product was both effective and sustainable. I also learned that the "best" solution is always relative to the specific constraints and needs it addresses. This realization has deepened my appreciation for the nuanced nature of engineering design and the importance of adaptability and responsiveness to feedback. Moving forward, I will prioritize structured decision-making and open collaboration in my projects, always considering the broader social and environmental impacts of our work. This approach will not only enhance the quality and relevance of our solutions but also ensure that we remain aligned with our commitment to sustainability and social responsibility.

situation: During our Software Design Logic workshops, we faced a series of coding challenges that required not only implementing software but also understanding the underlying logic. The pinnacle of these workshops was a final project where we had to create various versions of the game Rock-Paper-Scissors, including extended versions like Rock-Paper-Lizard-Spock and even more complex ones with 7, 9, and 11 gestures.
task_action: Our task was to develop algorithms and implement code for these game variants. We started by creating flowcharts to visualise the algorithms before diving into the coding phase. This involved critical thinking to determine the optimal structure and logic for each game variant. We had to thoroughly analyse the rules and interactions between gestures, ensuring our logic was robust and adaptable for more complex variants. Additionally, we performed unit tests to validate the correctness of our implementations.
result: Through precise planning and critical analysis, we successfully developed and implemented the code for all required game variants. Our flowcharts proved to be invaluable in organising our thoughts and providing a clear path for coding. The unit tests confirmed the reliability of our algorithms, ensuring that each game variant operated correctly. This process not only helped us complete the project successfully but also honed our critical thinking and problem-solving skills.
pfr: Reflecting on my experience in the Software Design Logic workshops, I initially felt confident about the tasks. However, I encountered significant challenges during the final project. The requirement to extend a simple game into multiple, more complex variants required deep critical thinking. As I delved into the process of creating flowcharts and analysing the logic, I found that breaking down the problem into smaller, manageable parts made it much more approachable. Collaborating with peers and receiving guidance from tutors further reinforced my confidence in tackling complex problems. This experience underscored the importance of critical thinking in software design and problem-solving.
learning: From this experience, I learned that critical thinking is essential for effective software design. Developing clear, logical algorithms and visualising them through flowcharts can significantly simplify the coding process. This structured approach not only ensures that the code is robust and error-free but also makes the problem-solving process more efficient. Moving forward, I will continue to prioritise critical thinking and the use of flowcharts in my software design projects, recognising their value in breaking down complex problems and ensuring successful outcomes.

situation: At Actrol, our team was asked to optimise the stockroom arrangement to make it easier to find parts fast. This was a tiny but significant activity that required team members to collaborate and communicate well.
task_action: To address this issue, I formed a small group of coworkers who frequently accessed the stockroom. We had a clear goal: "How can we rearrange the stockroom to improve efficiency in locating parts?" We began with a brainstorming session in which everyone may openly express their ideas. After gathering a variety of solutions, we reviewed and evaluated them based on the ease of completion, cost, and potential effect on efficiency. We then sorted the proposals to find the most promising ones. During this collaborative process, we settled on a new approach in which each part would be assigned a specific bin placement and the data would be recorded into our stock management system.
result: The solution entailed assigning each part to a specific bin location, carefully marking them, and updating the stock management system accordingly. We assigned tasks: some team members moved the parts to their new locations and labelled the bins, while others updated the stock management system with the new bin information. This rearrangement makes it much easier to find parts, resulting in a considerable reduction in time spent searching for goods.
pfr: Redesigning the stockroom setup was overwhelming at first. It seems difficult to discover the best option among different ideas. However, as we handled the problem methodically and documented each choice along the way, our group progressively acquired confidence. We were able to work successfully together and reach an agreement on the design that best addressed the problem.
learning: This experience taught me the value of effective teamwork. We were able to speed up the decision-making process by carefully reviewing ideas and considering their benefits. It became clear that there is no one-size-fits-all solution; rather, the optimal design is determined by the restrictions and requirements of the task at hand. This experience demonstrated the need of solid and organised decision-making processes to achieve positive results.

situation: During a group experiment, we were tasked with testing the tensile strength of various materials using a universal testing machine. task_action: I initiated a meeting with my group members to discuss the discrepancies in our results and to outline a plan to address the underlying problem. We reviewed the experimental procedures, including sample preparation techniques, equipment calibration, and testing protocols to identify potential sources of error. After thorough analysis, we decided to recalibrate the testing machine, standardise our sample preparation methods, and implement a more rigorous data collection process to ensure accuracy and reliability.
result: Following the adjustments to our experimental approach, we repeated the tests on the materials, meticulously recording data and maintaining consistency in our procedures. The results of the repeated experiments showed a significant reduction in variability and produced more reliable tensile strength values for each material tested. Our revised methodology not only improved the quality of our experimental data but also deepened our understanding of the importance of meticulous planning and attention to detail in experimental inquiry.
pfr: Initially, facing inconsistent results in our experiment was frustrating and made me question our team's competence in conducting the test accurately. The process of identifying potential errors and reevaluating our methodology felt overwhelming, but as we worked together to address the issues systematically, a sense of determination and collaboration emerged within the group. The recalibration of equipment and strict adherence to standardised procedures highlighted the importance of precision and attention to detail in scientific inquiry.
learning: Through this experience, I have realised the value of thorough analysis and structured problem-solving in experimental work. The need for clear communication, teamwork, and a methodical approach became evident as we strived to enhance the reliability of our experimental data. I learned that challenges in projects can often be opportunities for growth and improvement. In the future, I will prioritise regular equipment checks, detailed record-keeping, and a proactive attitude towards troubleshooting to ensure the validity of experimental results.

situation: As part of the civil modelling course, my group was assigned a project to design a new student accommodation building. We needed to create a detailed report, presentation, and a physical model. During the initial phase, we faced conflicting ideas and priorities regarding the building's design and features, which led to a lack of cohesion in our approach.
task_action: My task was to facilitate the team’s efforts to reach a consensus on the design, ensure that the report and presentation reflected our unified vision, and produce a high-quality model that accurately represented our concept. ACTION: I organised a brainstorming session to gather ideas and concerns, using a whiteboard to list features and priorities. Facilitating discussions, we used a decision matrix to prioritise design elements, balancing aesthetics, functionality, and sustainability. I coordinated task division based on team members’ strengths and ensured regular check-ins for progress tracking. Once all components were complete, I led a review session to integrate the report, presentation, and model, rehearsing multiple times to ensure a cohesive and smooth delivery.
result: Our project culminated in a comprehensive report detailing our design process and rationale, which received high marks for clarity and thoroughness. The accompanying presentation effectively highlighted key aspects of our design, impressing both professors and peers with its visuals and coherent narrative. Additionally, our physical model was lauded for its attention to detail and accuracy, serving as a tangible representation of our design prowess and ability to translate ideas into a physical form.
pfr: Initially, organising the group project felt overwhelming. Each team member had different ideas and priorities, and it seemed challenging to find a cohesive direction. However, as we progressed through the Atkins and Murphy model of reflection, I felt a sense of clarity emerge. Facilitating discussions and employing structured tools like the SWOT analysis helped us navigate conflicting ideas and prioritise effectively. It was rewarding to see the group reach a consensus and produce tangible outcomes like the report, presentation, and model.
learning: This experience reinforced the importance of structured decision-making processes and effective teamwork. Additionally, I gained insight into the significance of task division based on individual strengths and regular check-ins to ensure progress. Going forward, I intend to apply these learnings by proactively employing structured decision-making tools and fostering open communication within team settings. I now recognise that robust decision-making processes and cohesive teamwork are essential elements for achieving successful project outcomes.

situation: As a student juggling multiple courses, extracurricular activities, and personal commitments, I found myself frequently overwhelmed by the demands on my time and resources. Balancing academic assignments, project deadlines, and social engagements became increasingly challenging, leading to feelings of stress and inefficiency.
task_action: Recognizing the need for better time and resource management, I decided to implement the STAR framework to address the situation. Firstly, I assessed my current commitments and obligations, including academic deadlines, extracurricular activities, and personal responsibilities. Then, I identified specific areas where I could improve efficiency and allocate resources more effectively. Next, I took proactive steps to prioritize tasks, setting realistic goals and deadlines for each. I utilized time management tools such as calendars, to-do lists, and productivity apps to organize my schedule and track progress. Additionally, I sought support and guidance from mentors and peers, seeking advice on effective time management strategies and seeking assistance when needed.
result: Implementing the STAR framework significantly improved my ability to manage time and resources effectively. By clearly defining tasks and setting priorities, I became more focused and productive, completing assignments and projects in a timely manner. I experienced reduced stress levels and a greater sense of control over my workload. Furthermore, I noticed improvements in my academic performance, as I was able to dedicate more time to studying and understanding course material. Overall, the result of applying the STAR framework was a more balanced and fulfilling student experience, with enhanced productivity and better utilization of resources.
pfr: Initially, grappling with time and resource management felt overwhelming. I often found myself juggling multiple tasks, feeling stressed and anxious about meeting deadlines and commitments. It seemed like there were never enough hours in the day to accomplish everything I needed to do. However, as I began to reflect on my approach to managing my time and resources, I realized that I lacked a systematic method for prioritizing tasks and allocating resources efficiently. This realization initially made me feel frustrated with myself for not being more organized and disciplined.
learning: Through using the Atkins and Murphy model of reflection, I've gained insight into the importance of taking a step back to evaluate my time and resource management practices. I've learned that effective time management is not just about working harder or cramming more tasks into my schedule, but about working smarter and prioritizing tasks based on their importance and urgency. I've come to appreciate the value of setting clear goals and deadlines, breaking down tasks into manageable steps, and using tools such as calendars and to-do lists to keep track of my progress. Moving forward, I plan to implement a more structured approach to managing my time and resources. This includes setting aside dedicated time for planning and organizing my schedule, breaking tasks into smaller, actionable steps, and regularly reviewing and adjusting my priorities as needed. Additionally, I will practice saying no to non-essential commitments and learn to delegate tasks when appropriate, recognizing that I can't do everything on my own. By incorporating these insights into my approach to time and resource management, I believe I will be better equipped to handle the demands of my academic and personal life more effectively and efficiently.

topic: Perseverance, urgency and will to deliver, resourcefulness and flexibility
situation: Myself and a team of classmates was challenged to create the tallest structure with limited resources, those being a stack of paddle pop sticks, and 1 meter of string with a time limit of 35 mins
task_action: We began by brainstorming methods to effectively join the sticks together while being as efficient as possible with use of sticks and string but also being as strong as possible. we each came up with small examples and compared with one another, we gave each other feedback and found made our designs more effective and even combined designs to create a better join. once we had found our strongest joining methods we began construction
result: As a team we slowly built our structure up, using a combination of our joining techniques, due to the time restriction, the design was not perfect, but it was a compromise needed in order to meet the requirements of the task.
pfr: In the beginning the task seemed difficult given the short time limit, as well as the lack of a clear joining method that something like tape or glue would offer. however i feel that the use of only string to join the sticks together made the challenge harder and demanded a more creative aspect to the construction of the structure, which ultimately lead to each of us coming up with our own methods which was quite diverse.
learning: Seeing all the different designs which each team member came up with showed me how not only one design is the 'correct' one or best, as each was suitable in different areas, in the end we utilized a combination of the designs. This challenge showed me how creativity can thrive even while resources are limited, and is an example of how creativity improves our flexibility.

situation: Our team of five was tasked with designing a student accommodation modular housing model. Two team members consistently failed to respond to messages or participate in meetings, hindering progress.

learning: This experience was a harsh lesson in the realities of teamwork and project management. topic: Initiative and the willingness to make decisions in the face of uncertainty
situation: We need to collaborate as a group to: - Design & Construct a model - Write a detailed report - Create & Present a group presentation of our model We need to be able to communicate clearly, to allocate roles & tasks. We must also have good teamwork, to develop an positive working environment for all team members. As a group, we struggled to achieve this and were delaying simple tasks as nobody stepped up to instruct or guide the other members
task_action: I first began by trying to create friendly relations between all group members, starting conversations and discussions relating to the tasks we were given. By the next lesson, we still had not allocated any tasks or roles, as such I chose to take a 'leadership' type role. To achieve this, I first asked each member their opinions and comfortability with each part of the assessment we were given, after which I helped them to develop plans for what to do and how to do it before guiding each member towards the tasks that needed completing
result: Generally, a few of our team members remained noninteractive and refused to communicate with the group, however this method succeeded in guiding two of the four group members (not including myself), into a qualitative and productive work ethic. Though a couple members barely contributed and/or communicated, it did help to guide the others.
pfr: As the task was first given to me, I was stressed and nervous as I would be forced to work with unfamiliar people on a large task I had little prior experience with. Before starting the plan, every member of the group was anxious and we barely spoke in-person, let alone from distance (e.g. messages or emails). Upon beginning the plan, it was nerve-racking to put myself outside of my comfort zone into a leadership role. In the past I have always been uncomfortable speaking with people I am not familiar with, and the eerie atmosphere of the group did not help. After finally stepping up and beginning to guide the other members: - I became a lot more confident about myself - Was less stressed about the project, as we had actual plans for its completion - The group began acting together, with the exclusion of the two non-participating members Though I am still largely upset and angry with the members who did not participate, I am much more comfortable with the projects outcome and am overall satisfied. The members which supported me and completed their sections of the assessment (and more), are now also my friends, which will likely persist after the class.
learning: - Due to the lack of initiative in the beginning of the project, we were majorly delayed in our work and had to compensate for the lost time by working harder - While people / team members can seem one way (distant or lazy), they may simply lack the guidance to achieve their potential (I noticed this with the two members who contributed after I assigned roles) - Organization of time, tasks, plans, goals, due dates and work distribution should be the first step in any assessment (particularly group work), and have a large impact to it's outcome - Not everything is equal and I should not expect everything to go as I want. I should always be open-minded, supportive and willing to contribute even if I should not need to - While I managed to guide two group members, two of them remained distant. I need to: Be willing to take whatever role needed of me from the beginning Be considerate of every member's strengths and weaknesses Improve upon my leadership and communication skills

situation: During a critical rugby match, our team was trailing at halftime. As the captain, I recognized the need to implement an effective communication strategy to boost morale, gather valuable input, and collaboratively develop a plan to improve our performance.
