situation: While I was enrolled in the Introduction to Engineering course, I had to go to weekly workshops that were aimed to provide us with practical experience regarding various engineering perspectives. I actively participated in a project making aimed at Civil Modelling. The project was all about utilising paper and hard boards to create a model building. Five groups, each with five individuals, were formed out of our class. Our team was excited to embark on creating an incredible model. Our ability to apply academic information in a real-world situation and develop our problem-solving and teamwork abilities was enhanced by the workshops, which served as both an instructional and practical platform.
task_action: Considering each person's strengths, our group divided everyone into distinct positions. However, Nay, one of the members, was tasked with cutting the materials and making sure that every component was prepared for assembly. He appeared uninterested right away and frequently showed up late for our scheduled meetings. Notwithstanding our endeavours to engage him, he displayed no enthusiasm in making a contribution to the project. The pressure escalated as the deadline drew near. He showed up for one of our last workshops clearly agitated and disoriented. He ignored our attempts to communicate and spent the most of the time on his phone rather than concentrating on the assignment that was assigned to him. He reacted dismissively when we reminded him of his duties, stating, "It is merely a workshop, thus it is not really important." When he hurriedly cut numerous pieces of hardboard without accurately measuring them out of aggravation, everything went south. This thoughtless move produced components that were not suitable for our model and were uneven. "Utilise what you have; it suffices,” he shrugged when we challenged him about it.
result: Nay's incompetent actions had serious and fast repercussions. We had a little window of time before the presentation, so we had to quickly get new supplies and accurately recut the parts. For the remainder of the group, this resulted in needless stress and additional work hours. Though we did our best, the finished model was not as well-polished or solid structurally as we had hoped. The tutors identified our model's shortcomings throughout the presentation, pointing out its uneven cuts and lack of coherence. In comparison to other groups, we got lesser grades, and this had a noticeable negative impact on our group's morale. The event made clear how important it is for each team member to contribute and how unprofessional behaviour can derail the efforts of the entire group. Our initial joy quickly gave way to annoyance upon realising that weeks' worth of labour could be lost due to the carelessness of one person. Our team's trust and collaboration were damaged, which emphasises how important it is for everyone involved in a joint endeavour to take responsibility and work hard.
pfr: Reflecting on the situation, I recognised how crucial it is for team members to communicate clearly and take responsibility for one another. I discovered that project success and the preservation of a positive group dynamic both depend on professional behaviour. Nay's actions provided as a sobering reminder of the effect that one person's lack of professionalism may have on the overall result, which left me feeling incredibly dissatisfied and upset. I couldn't help but think that if everyone had contributed the same amount of effort to the project, we could have accomplished so much more. In addition, I sensed betrayal. We all knew what our roles and obligations were, and we had faith in one another to carry them out. It felt like a betrayal of that confidence when he didn't keep his end of the agreement. This incident brought to light the emotional toll that unprofessional behaviour takes on the cohesiveness and morale of the team as well as the project's final result. As we worked to lessen the harm that Nay's carelessness had caused, our aggravation was increased by a feeling of helplessness. There was a noticeable strain in the group, and the event emphasised how crucial dependability and respect for one another are to teamwork. I am now more conscious of the importance of having good people skills and the influence that each individual's actions have on a team's overall performance as a result of this experience.
learning: This incident taught me many important things about professionalism and teamwork. Unambiguous communication was found to be essential, emphasising the necessity of proactive conversations regarding roles and duties to avoid misunderstandings. To make sure that everyone is in agreement, open communication regarding goals and advancement is necessary on a regular basis. The significance of accountability was also demonstrated, highlighting the need of keeping team members accountable for their work through frequent check-ins and progress reports. This encourages accountability and guarantees that each member contributes equally. In a collaborative workplace, professionalism is essential. This includes commitment, timeliness, and respect for the work of others. Nay's disrespectful actions showed how a single person's lack of dedication can affect the dynamic and results of the entire squad. The incident also emphasised the significance of problem-solving abilities. Having the ability to adjust to unforeseen obstacles and solve problems under pressure are essential skills. situation: We had a project in engineering class where we had to design and construct a Rube Goldberg machine. The idea was to build a multi-step, intricate machine that could execute a simple task in a sophisticated manner. My group decided to construct a machine that waters the plant.
task_action: The assignment involved coming up with ideas, designing, building, and demonstrating a working Rube Goldberg machine that complied with project specifications. We had to make sure that the machine was creative, dependable, and interconnected at every stage. We also had to explain the physics behind each step in our design process and document the entire process. ACTION: To achieve this, my team and I took the following actions: * BRAINSTORMING AND PLANNING: To generate ideas for the machine, we began with a brainstorming session. We discussed the viability of various concepts that we drew using the gallery method. We came up with a ten-step plan that included pulleys, rolling balls, levers, and domino effects. * DESIGN AND PROTOTYPING: Each team member was given a specific part to design and prototype after I divided the machine into sections. First models of each step were made with cardboard, string, marbles, and other materials. To ensure seamless transitions between steps, we regularly convened to test how each component would interface with the next. * CONSTRUCTION AND TESTING: Once our prototypes were improved, we put the entire machine together. Precise alignment and adjustments were necessary to guarantee dependability. To find and address areas of failure, we conducted a number of tests and made adjustments to increase consistency. * DOCUMENTATION: We kept records of our designs, difficulties, and solutions all along the way. For every stage, we drew intricate diagrams and wrote explanations that emphasized the pertinent physics concepts, like momentum, energy transfer, and gravity. * PRESENTATION: Finally, we prepared a presentation to demonstrate our machine to the class. We explained each step, the design choices we made, and the physics concepts illustrated by the machine.
result: The intricate and entertaining task of pouring a cup of tea was successfully completed by our Rube Goldberg machine. The project was well accepted, and our professor and peers were impressed by the ingenuity and complexity of our machine. We received great marks for our comprehensive documentation and lucid presentation. Our ability to work as a team, solve problems, and apply engineering concepts practically all improved as a result of this project.

situation: During our group tasks and weekly tutorials, I faced challenges related to teamwork and communication specifically regarding professional behavior. Over the past 13 weeks, one of our team members, Nibir Sandipan, consistently failed to engage and contribute effectively to our group tasks. This lack of involvement is evident in multiple instances, such as during our Week 7 presentation preparation and presentation itself, and the final presentation. Nibir's lack of professional behavior, such as keeping his camera off during video calls, not assisting with assigned tasks, not taking initiative to make suggestions on how to complete tasks, significantly impacted the team's dynamics and workflow.
task_action: As a group (behrouz 6), our task was to collaborate week to week on various components of our group project 'The Rube Goldberg Machine', ensuring that each member contributed equally to meet our deadlines and maintain the quality of our work. This included preparing presentations, participating in video calls, and ensuring that each part of the project was coherent and well-coordinated. It was essential for all of us to demonstrate professional behavior, especially active participation, responsibility, and effective communication. ACTION: To address Nibir's lack of engagement and professional behavior we: - Encouraged participation to be present during our weekly video calls, even when Nibir kept his camera off and did not speak a word. - Provided specific feedback to individuals as a group and assigned clear responsibilities to ensure everyone knew their tasks. - Conveyed the importance of each member's contribution to the overall success of the project. - Unfortunately took on additional work ourselves to cover for the tasks that Nibir did not complete or give a decent attempt, ensuring that the project would still be completed to the best of our abilities. Despite these efforts, Nibir's participation and professional behavior did not improve. For the Week 7 presentation, Nibir did not assist in creating the slides, leaving Ibrahim and myself to cover his share of the work. In the final presentation, Nibir contributed to only one slide, which was differing with the rest of the presentation both in content authenticity and design. This then required additional effort from Ibrahim and myself to edit and try to integrate the slide effectively. Ultimately this affected the overall quality and flow of our presentation. Throughout this process, I maintained a professional demeanor by consistently communicating, taking responsibility, and ensuring the project's success despite the challenges we all faced.
result: The final result of all of this was a mixed outcome. Whilst we managed to complete the project on time and maintain a certain level of quality in both our video and presentation, the lack of contribution from Nibir affected the team's morale and overall productivity. It also highlighted the challenges of having to relying on team members who do not fully engage with the group's efforts or pull their weight. Finally, we have raised this issue with our tutor and unit convenor, seeking a resolution to ensure a fair assessment of each team member's contribution. This experience highlighted the importance of professional behavior in teamwork out of respect for peers. It can be a tricky situation to be in, both sides could be struggling, the team has to pick up extra work due to the inability of a team member and the individual could be going through a traumatic experience that impedes them from completing their responsibilities.
pfr: The entire situation has been quite frustrating and challenging. As an individual within this team who was committed to the project, seeing another team member not pull their weight was discouraging. It created additional stress and a larger workload for the rest of us, The thought that he was just being carried through the unit for free whilst we truly engaged in the content was truly demoralising ("why cant i do that", "Why should i put in this extra effort, if he's going to get the same mark as me for doing absolutely nothing"). The consistent lack of engagement from Nibir also negatively impacted our team's communication and cohesion, making it difficult to function effectively as a team as i am sure his lack of involvement and yet his ability to achieve our group marks rubbed off on other team members rupturing efficient team work..
learning: I have learnt through this semester the importance of effective communication and its interdependence with success. In doing so ensuring that all members are on the same page and understand their responsibilities can help reduce issues and clashes. Holding one another accountable for their contributions is also very important. Setting clear expectations as a group and following through with these can help ensure that everyone contributes equally. When challenges arise, being adaptable and willing to take on additional tasks is important. However, there must also be mechanisms to address and resolve ongoing issues of no participation. When internal efforts to resolve issues like this fail, seeking external assistance (contacting our tutor and unit convenor) is necessary to ensure fairness and address persistent problems. This Unit has taught me the importance of teamwork and communication to achieve collective goals and it has provided me with the new found knowledge on how to handle similar situations more effectively in the future.

situation: As a biomolecular science student, I've spent the last two and a half years working in small groups of 2-3 people. I decided to join an engineering unit and challenge myself by working remotely and with a team of more than three people. Starting in week two of the semester, I realised it was difficult to work in groups of six. First, because the class was offline, it was extremely difficult to understand or interact well with one another.
task_action: I enrolled one week after the semester began, and another student joined two weeks after that. It was becoming alittle difficult to collaborate online in large number of group. However, gradually through great teamwork and communication, we were able to improve and progress in our teamwork. Our primary objective was to create an RGM machine with 12 events while working online. As a team, we began to employ our team management skills; initially, we shared contact information in order to create a chat platform similar to Whatsapp, where we could easily contact one another.Then we all agreed on an online platform, such as Miro, that would allow us to collaborate and see who was executing which tasks. Then we started assigning jobs among the six of us, rotating them every week. For example, if I was allocated to do the minutes and agenda, others would be assigned to complete the weekly presentation, and two more would be assigned to present in class. We discovered that this was a crucial strategy for effectively managing the team; yet, there were instances when two or three members were missing.This caused some members to work more than others. However, as a team, we all came together and addressed the problem, and we came up with a method in which even if they are absent, they can make time during the week, even half an hour, to go over the miro and be updated, as well as provide comments or editing. Alternatively, each week, a team member would participate in updating via WhatsApp, which proved to be highly efficient. We made sure that everyone had the opportunity to accomplish something different each week; yet, by the conclusion of week 6, because everyone had to do a variety of activities, we identified our group members' strengths and weaknesses. We assessed it as a group and assigned a task beginning in week 9: if a person is particularly creative, they will work on creating the presentation, and if a member is really strong at presenting verbally with confidence, they will present in class. Using all of the methods we've learnt and perfected to work well in such a huge team. Everyone was ensured equal participation and involvement throughout the process of developing the RGM, which required everyone to include at least two activities of their choice. This allowed each team member to express their ingenuity and new ideas. By the end of each class, we ensured that everyone was satisfied with what we had planned/designed for our final RGM. However, if there was a disagreement among members, we ensured that it was resolved by a thorough assessment of the circumstances and negotiation that satisfied all members.
result: With effective team management skills, our team ensured that the RGM's design and planning processes ran successfully. Each week, we took a step by step approach to designing the 12 events with the cooperation of each member. We all agreed to conduct two activities per member, each lasting 4-5 seconds.Throughout the implementation process, our team chose to evaluate the reliability of our RGM in real life. After everyone got an opportunity to test their events, we spoke about their reliability and success/failure.If an issue/failure arose during this process, we as a team devised robust setups, explored how to choose better materials for each event, and fine-tuned component alignment to improve reliability and consistency. Overall, working on this project as a group helped everyone to learn, grow, and progress in all facets of becoming a great engineer. Working as a team allowed us to learn about each other's shortcomings and talents, particularly mine. However, there was a challenge at first working in a team of six people, but along the process, we not only learned about ourselves, but also about our team members' effective skills.
pfr: Initially, working in such a large team tested my confidence and dedication. I was never in a position to work in a group of six, particularly online. However, as I honed my collaborative and team leadership abilities, setbacks became opportunities for growth and learning. Because the entire planning and implementation was done remotely on micro, it was a little tough; nonetheless, I took advantage of the chance to learn how to use presentation platforms such as Miro and Prezi.This acted as a catalyst for the team to create a culture of open communication, mutual support, and constructive feedback, helping us to effectively overcome hurdles while maintaining confidence in our cooperative and collaborative collaboration.
learning: Throughout the development of the RGM, I discovered that working in a large team is not necessary. It is about effective team management, collaboration, and honesty in a team. These are the primary factors that contribute to a team's success. This lesson has taught me not just how to construct an RGM, but also how to be an effective team leader, and I enjoy working in large groups. I learned how to effectively manage a team, ensure that my team members are on the same page, and help one another. I learned how to effectively manage a team, ensure that my team members are on the same page, and help one another. I've realised that my group taught me to think outside the box and like an engineer, and I genuinely value the abilities. Overall, I believe I can effectively use these abilities to a future endeavour, which may not be in engineering but in healthcare.

situation: Throughout the first few weeks of the ENGG3050 unit, we have been presented with a wide range of leadership, management, and entrepreneurial skills and outlooks. In Engineering I’ve learnt the importance of how a team works together and how to produce a quality and efficient team for any task. The role and importance of leadership can involve anyone within a team and allows for problem solving and idea generation. Both the Week 1 SGTA and Case Study 1 allowed me to reflect on my own and others leadership styles and how different styles can benefit teams in specific ways, which allowed me to understand how to effectively lead engineering endeavours.
task_action: There have been many tasks across my engineering degree where I’ve had to consider the implications of teamwork and how to lead a team, whether I was merely part of that team or was attempting to lead it. The ability to lead a team is a difficult and relentless task, attempting to organise who in the team needs to achieve specific tasks in order to produce the final product. In week 1 of this semester we looked at the specific types of leadership styles and each of their advantages and disadvantages which allowed me to reflect on what I should be aiming for as a leader. I believe that a democratic and transformational style of leadership works the best in ensuring a team works well together. It allows everyone to input their ideas and thoughts whilst pushing for improved team efforts and performance. To further this I was tasked with looking at the different leadership styles in General Electric (GE) to investigate the different ways the CEO’s pushed their companies and pushed the endeavours of their engineers and how each of their leading styles impacting the company as a whole showing a general idea of what is crucial for a business to perform well. Action: Over the course of my degree I have found myself in positions where I am part of a team trying to produce a result. This includes ENGG1050, ENGG2000 and a few others to name a few, where working with a group of fellow engineers we are to design and produce some result. Although I wasn’t necessarily appointed the leader in these cases I felt the need to often step in and attempt to solve conflict, improve team morale and ensure everyone in the team gets a fair say during the creative processes and of course the actual building of whatever we had planned such as the Rube Goldberg Machine or the Marble Machine. Others also stepped in at times to lead and ensure everyone was on the right path to getting the project done. I found it was beneficial and very important to involve a wide variety of leadership styles at each stage of the process to enable different ideas flows, ensuring work was done and submitted on time and that everyone was enjoying themselves to boost the overall productivity and mental health as such across the projects. It has been very interesting now going into depth on these leadership styles in ENGG3050, looking at real life cases of where they have been used and the overall results of each. I’m excited to push forward to ENGG3000 to again be part of an awesome team and produce an amazing result whilst trialling different leadership options and how to push the engineering endeavours to even greater heights.
result: Pushing myself to be a leader in a range of engineering endeavours has really helped open my eyes as to how a team functions and how to really push for the best quality outcome in any given case. Being able to put the team back on track when getting side tracked during class time and pushing brainstorming sessions to narrow down what is a viable idea like in the marble machine. Without this leadership no one was willing to push the team forward and to come up with a conclusive idea. Specifically during the ENGG2000 project, at some point as a team we didn’t know how to proceed with our design. I sat down with the team and asked them what parts of the box they wanted to contribute and suggested what each person could do. We discussed as a team which allowed us to proceed with our engineering endeavour. I decided to lead by example and proceed with my part. I would like to see how others perceive this leadership role and how they would implement their own ideas to help achieve that leadership and pushing those engineering endeavours. I will look forward to taking the ideas learnt in the ENGG3050 class and using those leadership skills that we have been learning and applying them during the ENGG3000 workshop, next years thesis writing and my future career in engineering.
pfr: Without leadership in a team, I have experienced uncertainty and confusion in many aspects throughout my engineering degree. I find it daunting to tell others what to do and be in a leadership role, especially due to the lack of experience I have and not wanting to be wrong. But this is the most important part of learning, is being wrong and putting yourself out there. I have really enjoyed pushing myself in leadership roles as well, although I don’t consider myself a leader I have learnt that it is essential in any engineering endeavour to push myself and my team forward to the completion of the project. Over time with more experience I believe I will be able to work well in a team and be able to uplift them, and hopefully push others as well to be a leader. As a whole team I believe everyone should be a leader to an extent as this allows for many ideas and thoughts to proceed with the project and finish the endeavour.
learning: To ensure the successful completion of any engineering endeavour there are many routes to take. The most important part is the leadership of a team, without it there would be no organisation or planning, no push to get each component done and no way to improve as a team. There are a multitude of leadership styles which are valid required in different situations, so having a mixture of leaders is crucial. However, it is also important to step back as a leader if everyone is trying to control the direction of the project as it may actually hinder progress as everyone would want to do it their own way. Communication and acceptance of ideas is also important which comes with leadership and experience in engineering. I’ve learnt that any engineering project can be a long and tedious process, with many things going wrong and disagreements made. However, with a dedicated team and the right motivations, it is a rewarding and fulfilling task to be involved in.

situation: * Recently, I went Scuba Diving as a type 1 diabetic. This was not my first time diving with diabetes, and at the beginning of the dive I gave a small presentation about this. I talked about what it meant to dive as a diabetic, including the potential risks and what I would need from people in case a situation arises. However, during the dive a complication arose due to my diabetes. The group I was diving with felt confused and unprepared, they were unsure of what they should do. This made me realise something, that I didn’t do an adequate job informing people of their role to play in case of an emergency. I needed to prepare and script a better presentation, to explain my diabetes to my dive partners.
task_action: * A close friend of mine is one of the best cave divers in the world. He put me in touch with one of his students, another type 1 diabetic. We sat on a phone call for about 4 hours, brainstorming all of the potential problems I could have underwater due to my diabetes and what those problems would mean for me, for the people I’m diving with, and how those problems would be managed or mitigated. Once we came up with that list, we worked out which of those problems I could manage on my own, and which of those problems required help from other people. From there, we created clear and concise explanations, including props and images, to explain only the problems that would require help from other people.
result: * We came up with a new presentation, one which did a much better job of preparing people. We did this by explaining the condition, what it means for me as a diver, the important hand symbol for diving with diabetes and what it means for a dive, the potential things I need from people, and stressing that certain problems just need time for me to work through them on my own, and that if I require assistance I will signal people for it. Using this method, I was able to create a much more effective presentation. I tried this out recently and did a mock simulation of a diabetes problem underwater, and no one from the diving group was confused or felt unequipped to handle this situation. This presentation was a success.
pfr: * Initially, the whole ordeal of creating a new presentation was daunting. Not just because I had to communicate important information, but also because I had to answer some very uncomfortable questions about myself. I realised to avoid answering these questions I had been incredibly conservative with my first message, alluding too but not explicitly stating the problems that could be caused and the consequences of those problems. To fix this, I had to be very honest with myself about what would occur if these problems did occur and weren’t treated promptly and efficiently, and that is that I would die. I had to answer these questions, not just for my sake but for my diving group’s sake as well. By working out what each problem was, how it could be managed or mitigated, and whether I would need help (and if so what kind of help) to solve each problem, was instrumental in creating a new presentation. The phone call I had with a good friend who is also a diabetic diver proved instrumental in solving this issue.
learning: * What I learnt throughout this whole ordeal is something about myself, that I have a tendency to sugar coat things and make them easier to understand or hear. I saw first-hand the problems that can arise from this, and how being honest and forward with most definitely the optimal approach. It saves time, effort and causes less problems overall. I also learnt how valuable discussion and a brainstorming session can be, especially with someone who knows a topic as well as you. I don’t often look for help with my diabetes, but discussing problem areas with another diabetic scuba diver proved instrumental in identifying problems I hadn’t even considered. In the end, I realized how important testing and practice are after simulating a presentation and encountering a scenario with a different group of divers, which helped me see areas that needed clearer explanation. Through this encounter, I realised the crucial significance of honesty and openness in a professional setting, while also understanding the importance of relying on others.

topic: Perseverance, urgency and will to deliver, resourcefulness and flexibility
situation: In the third week of this semester, I was given a substantial assignment that was due in week 7. Initially, I did not prioritise it because the due date was so far away. By week 5 I had only completed about 15% of the work. I became overwhelmed with other pressing assignments and placed this one on the backburner, even as the due date rapidly approached.
task_action: As week 6 arrived and the assignment was due the next week, I realised I needed to make this my top priority. I began chipping away at the work, determined not to submit it late and incur a 5% penalty. The assignment was much larger than I had anticipated, requiring extensive research and writing for each of the 10 questions, ultimately taking around 2hr per question. To manage the workload, I made significant sacrifices, staying up late and working through the Easter long weekend to make progress. I had to cancel some of my mid-week plans in week 7 to focus solely on completing this large assignment. On the day before the due date, I was on campus and found myself preemptively completing class work to allow me to go home early work on the remaining sections at home.
result: Through sheer perseverance, urgency, and a strong will to deliver, I was able to complete the entire 6000-word assignment by 12:55am, submitting it with just 4 minutes to spare. This required a high degree of resourcefulness and flexibility, as I had to adapt my schedule and priorities to ensure I could devote the necessary time and effort to this assignment. Whilst the experience was extremely stressful, the outcome was successful. I was able to submit the assignment on time without incurring any late penalties. This experience has taught me valuable lessons about planning, organisation, and the importance of not becoming complacent when faced with a daunting task. In the future, I will aim to better assess the scope of an assignment and allocate my time accordingly, rather than leaving it until the last minute.
pfr: Looking back on this experience, I feel a range of emotions. I'm proud that I was able to persevere and ultimately complete the assignment on time, despite the significant challenges and obstacles I faced. The sheer determination and willpower required to push through and successfully complete the assignment is something I can take pride in. However, I also feel a sense of frustration with myself for not managing my time and priorities better from the get go. The fact that I allowed myself to become so overwhelmed and behind on such a substantial assignment is a bit embarrassing considering I normally am so on top of things like this. I shouldn't have let it get to the point where I was sacrificing other commitments and staying up late every night just to get it done. At the time, I was under immense stress and anxiety. The pressure of that looming deadline and the fear of failing to submit on time weighed heavily on me as I have never submitted late before. There were moments where I considered just leaving it until tomorrow and accepting the 5% penalty. That level of stress and uncertainty is not something I enjoy going through. The feeling of relief after submitting the assignment and knowing that it was over was something that I did thoroughly enjoy, but it did not outweigh the stress experienced to get there. Overall, this experience has been a valuable learning opportunity, though a difficult one. I've gained some important insights about myself and how I approach challenging academic tasks. While I’ve shown myself that I display the ability to persevere and that I have an underlying sense of urgency to get tasks done, it's clear to me that I need to work on my time management and prioritisation skills.
learning: The most important lesson I learned from this experience is that proactive preparation and organisation are more important than my ability to manage and react to a crisis. Going forward, I will ensure to thoroughly examine any new tasks or assignments as soon as they are assigned, and devise a practical schedule and strategy. I will be sure to not underestimate or ignore the amount of work that is required for a task. Furthermore, I've come to understand the importance of discipline and perseverance in the face of major challenges. Even though I want to steer clear of these last-minute stressful situations in the future, I am confident that I possess the strength and resolve to persevere when necessary. The satisfaction of submitting that assignment on time, despite the difficulty, is proof of that. Also, I now recognise the importance of flexibility and adaptability. I had to quickly adapt and come up with new strategies to make up the time and mental space I needed to concentrate on the assignment when my initial activities and obligations had to be postponed or cancelled. Being able to easily adjust my schedule and priorities is a skill I hope to keep. All in all, this difficult experience has given me insightful knowledge that I will use moving ahead. I'm sure I can use these lessons to improve my organisation, initiative, and resilience as a student, making me more capable of managing the challenges I may face whilst studying.

situation: At home, my space is in the garage. I have my computer, my tools/materials, musical instruments and have carved out my own little space because our house is quite small and everyone is living on top of eachother. Because our house is quite small, the garage is also the primary storage location for my mum, her partner and my sister, and as people accumulate random items my space in the house is filled with other peoples mess, this is a source of conflict in our household.
task_action: A potential solution didn’t jump out at me naturally to resolve this storage issue/conflict, I was working on welding together a flatbar in the garage (an obstacle for skateboarding) and my back was hurting because I didn’t have a workbench for these types of activities and I had to bend over to work on the ground. When I stood up, back aching, it occurred to me that if I used the materials in the garage to build a workbench there would be more room to store peoples clutter on the shelves, I would be utilising the offcuts taking up room in the garage and I wouldn’t be hurting my back every time I wanted to undertake a personal project. So I put my half finished flatbar aside and spoke to my family to see what they would think of my idea, and they liked it! I finished the workbench in the following days and then went on to build a few shelves in the garage with leftover materials.
result: Upon completion I was so excited. My space, the garage, was clean and I had much more room to move around, I also have a sense of pride everytime I use the workbench to build something, knowing that my work has helped me with undertaking future projects is very satisfying. Unfortunately, others in the house have seen all the new space I’ve carved out and it seems the garage is slowly starting to fill up with junk again (although its still currently far better than it was).
pfr: The garage space being tidier than before – as silly as it may sound - has bought me a lot of joy and pride because this is a space that I use almost everyday. I don’t always go out of my way to correct minor issues in life, being aware of these pain points isn’t something that comes naturally to me. Since I’ve put in so much time to creating this space and making it tidy, I get quite defensive of others trying to dump their unused items in the garage and feel it is a slap in the face if my family do this. I know they aren’t doing it to intentionally annoy me, so I should try not to take these actions personally.
learning: When it comes to addressing pain points, one take away from this scenario is that it shouldn’t take multiple issues stacking up and being seemingly unbearable to take action. The fact that I felt such a sense of pride to have improved the situation in my space is a testimony, looking out for these issues so that they can be addressed can really improve your daily living. I see some friends and family who seem to really have their life quite organised, I think of my grandad who has small things like hooks to hold wires out of the way and their lives do seem to run a whole lot more smoothly when addressing minor pain points like this regularly. This only occurs through constantly looking out for pain points, and brainstorming/acting on solutions. It may seem like an uninspired lesson to take from the conflict regarding others dumping rubbish in my space, but I’m aware that in coming years when I move out of home, having ample space to store equipment/items is something I’m now looking out for! I’ve realised it can be a source of conflict which doesn’t always have a simple solution. Life is too short to be upset by others actions, especially when they aren’t even intended to upset you in the first place!

situation: Leading up to the end of the ENGG3050 unit, it has come to my attention that ethics, integrity, and social responsibility are incredibly important in the engineering field. Both from my own personal experiences, as well as research done for my presentations done in class, it is clear that ethics and integrity have grown in the field and is changing vastly. This comes along with new technologies such as Artificial Intelligence models like ChatGPT as well as looking at renewable energies and technologies related to the company I presented in week 10, Wallbox. Ensuring as an engineer we understand our social responsibilities and how we take technology to the next level will ensure a positive impact is made on the society around us and improve the lives of future generations.
task_action: In terms of artificial intelligence, it can be applied to so many tasks which have occurred throughout my engineering degree. Especially in tasks which require writing like many lab reports or even these reflections, I have seen people using ChatGPT to copy and paste answers. I dislike this, and it does not reflect my true intentions as an engineer. Of course it is easy to do and would reduce the time it would take to do assessments, but it does not deliver the same gratitude and understanding that actually being involved in those assignments brings. This issue has been raised by many of the higher ups and academics at Macquarie University where they have addressed the issue of plagiarised and artificially created content, which I agree with. It should be used as a learning tool and to provide background information as needed, like google that gives summarised information. In extreme cases, it is important to hold moral ethics and integrity as an engineer as anything we create and present to the public will be used by people maybe across the world, so ensuring we take some level of social responsibility during our careers is important, and artificial intelligence does not have the capacity to think and consider the consequences and the many challenges that come with engineering. Action: I have used ChatGPT, I am not afraid to admit it, but I don’t believe that discredits my integrity or ethics as an engineer. topic: Trade-offs, judgment, and balance in resolution
situation: This semester, I overloaded myself by taking five units instead of the usual four. This resulted in periods where I was overwhelmed by an immense amount of work and assignments. For one of my units, we were assigned a significant Continuous Professional Development (CPD) project worth 60% of the final grade. Around weeks 5 or 6, I finalised my CPD project idea, choosing to work on a facial expression recognition program. Initially, I underestimated the project's complexity, thinking it wouldn't be too challenging since I had some prior exposure to machine learning. However, I made the mistake of prioritising other assignments and exam preparation over the holidays, completely neglecting my CPD project until week 9.
task_action: When I realised I needed to start working on the CPD immediately, panic set in. As I began, I quickly understood that learning everything and coding a complete model or program alone within the limited time frame was unrealistic. I used my better judgement and made the strategic decision to prioritise learning and comprehending the topics over focusing solely on delivering a final product. I slowed my pace, created a plan, and concentrated on grasping the concepts and expanding my knowledge rather than stressing over producing a fully functional program. I also made sacrifices in my personal life, cancelling social plans and non-essential activities like going to the gym to dedicate time to this task.
result: These trade-offs and my re-prioritisation proved to be a wise decision. By week 11, I had gained significantly more knowledge and understanding than I would have if I had solely focused on creating a working program. I became well-versed in machine learning topics and developed an understanding of how to approach problems, even if I didn't have a final product to showcase. This approach reduced my stress and equipped me with the theoretical knowledge needed to eventually start coding a functional product to present to the class. This experience taught me valuable lessons about acknowledging the importance of tasks, prioritising them accordingly, and managing my time more effectively. I realised that I should have recognised the significance of the CPD project earlier and prioritised it over other assignments. Furthermore, I became aware of my tendency to work on one assignment at a time, hoping to complete it quickly, which often led to a backlog of assignments due simultaneously. I recognised the need to change this approach to avoid overwhelming stress when facing multiple deadlines.
pfr: Looking back and reflecting on this experience evokes a range of emotions. On one hand, I feel a sense of pride and accomplishment for persevering through the challenges, gaining a deeper understanding of machine learning and working on a functional program. The determination and resilience required to navigate this situation successfully is something I can take pride in. However, I also feel frustrated with myself for not managing my time and priorities more effectively from the get go. The fact that I allowed the situation to escalate to a point where I was overwhelmed and behind on such a significant assignment is a source of embarrassment, as I typically pride myself on being organised and proactive. I’m quite disappointed that I ended up in a situation that required trade-offs in the first place. Deciding to prioritise learning and understanding the concepts over delivering a final product was a difficult but necessary decision. It required me to sacrifice personal time and activities, such as socialising and going to the gym, to dedicate myself fully to the task at hand. Although challenging, this approach allowed me to reduce stress and gain a deeper understanding of the subject matter. Throughout the process, I had to exercise my judgement and find a balance between my academic responsibilities and personal life. It was a constant struggle to manage my time effectively and avoid the tendency to work on assignments sequentially, which often led to overwhelming backlogs. Looking back, I can appreciate the valuable learning opportunity this experience provided, albeit a challenging one. It has allowed me to gain important insights about myself and how I approach demanding academic tasks.
learning: This experience taught me invaluable lessons about time management, prioritisation, and making well-informed trade-offs to achieve a balanced outcome. I realised the importance of acknowledging the significance of tasks early on and allocating my time and efforts accordingly. Moving forward, I will strive to change my approach to completing assignments. Instead of focusing on one task at a time, I will work on multiple assignments simultaneously to ensure steady progress across the board. This proactive approach will help me avoid overwhelming situations and manage my workload more effectively. Furthermore, I have learned the value of exercising my judgement and making strategic trade-offs when faced with competing priorities. While it may be challenging to sacrifice personal time or activities, it is sometimes necessary to ensure academic success and maintain a healthy balance. This experience has also highlighted the importance of self-reflection and continuous learning. By reflecting on my actions and their consequences, I have gained insights that will undoubtedly shape my future decision-making processes and help me navigate similar situations more effectively.

_My team and I came up with the final design mechanism/creative process: dropping a Berocca tablet into water. How this would work is, a marble would roll down a slope and hit a pendulum which would then hit the Berocca tablet tube, causing the Berocca to fall out of the tube onto a track, the Berocca then rolls down an inclined plane with the help of a folder and will roll off a benchtop onto a popped open umbrella, flying onto another benchtop. The marble at this time will roll down a tube, hit a stack of dominoes, and fall into a water bottle. Then, a soccer ball will hit a toilet paper roll which will in turn hit the water bottle, releasing the marble out of the water bottle. The marble will then roll off a benchtop, and down a shovel. As the next action, the Berocca would roll down a tube, whilst the marble will roll down a spiral. The Berocca then falls onto a tube __rolls down the__ tube and hits a windmill, the __windmill then sends it down. The marble at this point rolls down a track, balanced on a bearing well. The tablet falls onto a pulley system and triggers the dominoes on the other end, when the other end of the pulley is lifted, due to the weight of the marble on the opposite end.  __The water at the end of the domino effect now pivots onto a stick on the bottom of the bottle and falls after a prop gets removed from underneath consequently tipping the water into the glass. __The counterweight that pulls the prop out from under the bottle is a roll of tape that is balanced on the edge. Lastly, t__he marble rolls down the track well and knocks a block out, releasing the Berocca into the water. _
situation: We needed to brainstorm a design mechanism/creative process through weeks 1-11 for developing a Rube Goldberg machine. Our idea for this design was to develop a machine for dropping a Berocca tablet into the water via various complex processes, by using pendulums, the domino effect, shovels, pulleys, and legos, to name a few.
task_action: We went through various brainstorming sessions throughout the weeks and came up with our design for the RGM project. We would dispose of a Berocca tablet into the water through a series of complex processes. Our idea behind this experiment/ problem statement was to try to think outside the box and also showcase that engineering can be a hard course that might give us a headache, therefore popping a Berocca every once in a while isn't a bad idea. We had several offline/online meeting sessions to brainstorm and put together our ideas. We used various methods of brainstorming like starbursting, reverse brainstorming, rapid ideation, etc to come up with the best, feasible working project. Upon discussion, and trying our individual, and group parts, multiple times, we decided that the 'weight' of the marble should be in accordance with all 12 of our actions taking place, that is, it should not be too heavy or too light. We didn't want to make the project too 'complex' but also wanted it to be complex enough to showcase what we learned through the weeks. We also chose components that were easier to make/'manufacture' like household items that weren't impossible to achieve, which would help our project execute well. We also spoke about other parameters such as the distance between objects, the difference in height, the duration of the video, and the percentage credibility of the overall machine.
result: The result was brainstorming and being able to come up with the perfect solution which included 12 actions, 2 actions each, executed by the 6 of us in a particular sequence.
pfr: When we first found out about the RGM project, as a team, we were scared and overwhelmed as we had no idea where to begin or where to end, but once we understood the gist of the project, we as a team were excited to develop the machine and challenge ourselves in new, innovative ways. The project as a whole, though it is meant to be complicated, is actually easy and fun, and also challenges our art and craft skills. We in a very systematic and organized manner used miro to help keep track of our work, completed our work in our workshops every week, and worked outside our practical class hours to come up with a good RGM project. Upon brainstorming many ideas, we came up with the 'Berocca falling into water' idea, to be our best idea, according to everyone. Based on the problem statement, which was that 'Engineering is a hard unit', we thought our idea would be ideal, as Berocca helps calm our nerves when dealing with hard units and studies.
learning: Decision-making using a merit-based approach was a very sought-after approach that my team and I implemented. Decision-making helps us lay out various ideas and choose the best ones, suitable for the situation at hand. Decision-making doesn't help us come up with the 'best design', as there is no such thing as 'best design', but it helps us weigh out the pros and cons and helps us narrow down all possibilities to the most appropriate ones. Identifying and trying to overcome constraints is also a vital role in developing a project since no matter how good of a project we choose, we will have constraints, so the main idea is to overcome them. Through these 11 weeks, I have learned how to make well-informed decisions to overcome various constraints and obstacles thrown at us. I have learned to appreciate the diversity, intensity, and beauty of this project and that we need to work with what we have, to the best of our ability as there is no such thing as 'best design', and everyone's ideas are in themselves, the best designs.

situation: In my first year at Macquarie University, I took Engineering Design (ENGG1050). The objective of this course was to teach the necessary team-working, and organisation skills needed in a modern online engineering environment. This was facilitated by forming a team and working to create a Rube Goldberg Machine building and utilising a multitude of relevant skills along the way. During Week 5, my team needed to complete our conceptual design for our RGM with a theme of sustainability and an end goal of watering a plant.
task_action: I discussed the presentation of our conceptual design at week 5’s meeting and deconstructed the parts of the conceptual design into manageable parts. Each section of the 7 sections of the RGM required at least 2 action events. By this point, our group had already brainstormed a variety of ideas for each of our sections but no choice was committed to. I decided to set a goal for the team, to have decided on the two action items for their section before our week 6 meeting.
result: As a result of this goal we were able to start work on creating a visual representation of our conceptual design on Miro aiding in our ability to present to the tutor group. This also increased team engagement as we were able to monitor each other's work and review everyone's section.
pfr: When assessing what our team needed to complete in Week 5, I was nervous to assert a goal for our team to achieve. However, when I was in our pre-workshop meeting and I was able to perceive my team member’s reception to my proposed goal, I understood that I was able to suggest an idea and others would be able to constructively provide feedback or agreement.
learning: From this experience, I will no longer hesitate to share my ideas for team goals or practices because I am able to see that everyone will appreciate the effort. situation: We needed to create as new solution concept after deciding that our previous solution or cracking on egg and cooking it was too unrealistic.
task_action: Organised a team meeting to specifically address and create a new solution concept. After each member suggested a new solution concept, we collectively identified the strengths and weaknesses of each solution.
result: As a result of this meeting, it was decided that the new solution concept would involving boiling an egg rather than frying it. This changed reduced the number of complex and unreliable processes in the solution.
pfr: The decision to change the solution concept was quite frustrating. The team and I had already put in a lot of work into creating events and ideas for the solution concept. While not all of our work was wasted, as the new solution concept still involved cooking an egg, majority of the events thought up could not carry over to the new solution concept. However, despite this change being quite frustrating, it was ultimately the right decision. Our previous solution concept was too complex and would have been unreliable.
learning: Having a more careful and thorough look at the solution concept at an early stage is an absolute must in any project. It helps reduce unknown risks and issues appearing when planning the preliminary design, or prototyping. This situation has helped me to understand the importance of proper and thorough planning during the conceptual/solution design phase. Additionally, it has also helped my team and I to more easily identify potential issues and risks associated with the conceptual/solution design.

situation: Decide on the function our Rube Goldberg Machine (RGM) was to perform.
task_action: After several team meetings over the Week 4, we decided that frying an egg would be the ultimate goal of our RGM as we had a kitchen themed name so it would only be appropriate if we had a kitchen themed function. So in our final team meeting before the Week 5 finalisation of our RGM the idea was presented that this function was too hard and that we should consider another function. result: This resulted in a revamp of our MIRO board in order to incorporate this new final function and making our overall project simpler by unique events being easier to decide and splitting each event to different team members efficiently and effectively.
pfr: The brainstorming was a rough process as our group was not use to coming up with ideas for such a project. However, over the weeks our team began to bond over our weekly meetings and team synergy was prominent. Due to this, brainstorming started coming naturally to us. I was the one who brought up that our initial concept and design were to complicated, and that we should consider the thread burning option instead. I am happy that everyone on the team immediately agreed with this statement and thanked me. We immediately made substantial progress on our new idea as well.
learning: I understand that having synergy and getting along with your team is an important part of team-based project management. As when we first were assigned our groups we were all a bit hesitant to reach out. When creating something you have never done before it is best to start with really understanding your final goal and not making it too complex from the beginning. Through this experience, I now understand the perks of understanding and being friends with your team.

topic: TRANSFERABLE SKILL: Working as a team but, specifically, being able to identify and utilise team members' talents and weaknesses as a group leader.
situation: While the aforementioned skill can be applied everywhere it was best exemplified when planning, allocating and completing numerous tasks in our shortened week 6 workshop.
task_action: The organised agenda for the week required that we plan our graded presentation, complete our Work, Health, & Safety documents, write our group reflection, and finalise the detailed design aspects of our Rube Goldberg Machine. While normally we would have three hours to complete the workshop, our allocated time was reduced to two due to longer weekly presentations as well as the morning address from the tutors. Furthermore, we were also a group member down due to illness. As organised at the beginning of this semester, our group participated in a rotating roster for the overarching roles needed to cohesively function on a week-week basis. This resulted in me taking the lead as Chairperson this week (Team Leader). Thus to complete the required workload I allocated tasks based upon members' strengths as identified by myself and then agreed upon by the group. For example, one member was better at ideation for presentation while another was better at thinking critically in regards to risks and their mitigation.
result: By effectively evaluating group members' strengths and weaknesses individually, and as a group, we were able to meet the deadline for the workload, and thus, stay on target for our project timeline. When all tasks were completed we also shared our ideas and findings with each other in an informal presentation format so that everyone was on the same page moving forward.
pfr: When faced with the workload that was required to be completed in the roughly two-hour timeframe, it was met with many negative responses from team members due to the intimidating nature of the number of tasks at hand. I personally shared this group sentiment which was not constructive at the time, however, when mentally breaking down what needed to be done into manageable portions it was clear that the tasks could be done. By delegating the tasks in a fair manner all group members' attitudes shifted towards being focused and motivated. Furthermore, I believe that allocating tasks based on strengths helped to promote participation and respect for each other's abilities.
learning: This experience provided a workplace-like scenario for us to practice effectively managing a deadline by evaluating and utilising each member's strengths. Moving forward in the coming weeks, this can be applied when we rotate the leader role around to meet complete large workloads in an efficient manner regardless of the constraints we are faced with. Thus, this skill will be transferable in the workplace and will be something I can further build upon throughout my university degree and future career.

situation: During the mid-semester break our group, individually, gathered all the necessary household materials and equipment to construct their respective modularized events of the Rube Goldberg Machine (RGM). Adjustments and testing were also conducted to assess the level of reliability of the individual sections and hence, the overall system reliability. A video of the successful operation of the RGM was recorded.
task_action: Using the preliminary design concepts formulated in the previous group meetings, we each identified the relevant materials required for each of our two events. Next, we gathered all the necessary materials and tools to build RGM sections. Also, as one of the constraints is sustainability aspect, this meant that if we did not have the materials or equipment at home, we would look for alternatives by substituting it with a household item. Evidently, parts of the preliminary design were slightly changed to adequately meet the sustainability constraint. Once each section was constructed, each member would perform 20 test runs and record the success rate. Next, the source of errors was identified for each segment, and suggested improvements were amended into the system. Then, another 20 test runs were performed, and the improved success rate was documented. Additionally, each member recorded the successful operation of their sections of the RGM.
result: By the end of the mid-semester break we had 5 videos from each member consisting of two events from the RGM. Also, we presented the initial success rate and section reliability, which was used to determine the overall system reliability. We each presented the sources of error, the suggested improvement strategies and the resulting success rate and section reliability of each person to the rest of the group. As a resulted, the improved reliability of the entire machine was determined. Further, the 5 separate videos were merged into one to present a seamless operating RGM.
pfr: Initially, I felt the mid-semester break might not be enough time for us to perform all the necessary tasks of gathering material, constructing sections, testing, and improving the reliability of the RGM. I felt that we would get stuck somewhere along the construction process that we would have to come up with an entirely new design for certain sections. Additionally, a major aspect of our RGM is that we are taking a sustainable approach (not buying materials we do not have), which I thought might present another challenge. For example, if we did not have the necessary material and we could not replace it with an adequate alternative we would be forced to scrap the design and come up with another design. This could have easily halted the progress of our project. Fortunately, we made only minor changes to the sections of RGM, which did not take long to do.
learning: Through this, it was evident that taking a systematic approach and planning for contingencies is vital in the successful completion of any project within a designated timeframe. Collectively planning the tasks that need to be performed and setting the time frame and deadlines during the group meetings allowed for effective communication. By having each member outline what they will do by the next meeting helps each member understand the progress the team is making. Additionally, as each member will do their sections, it will in turn make a very effective team as no two members will be doing the same thing. Hence, by systematic planning my appreciation for time and resource management has enhanced.

situation: We needed to complete our final RGM video by the end of Week 12.

The second goal due date was for the video editor to finish combining and editing all of our videos to produce the final RGM video by the end of week 10.
result: By choosing appropriate goal due dates, we were able to successfully finish our final RGM video by the end of Week 10. Which gave us more time to work on other units' assignments. This also gave us an extended period of time to work on our week 13 presentation.
pfr: Initially, the task of finishing the final RGM video by the end of Week 12 seemed significantly overwhelming for the majority of us. The newly decided goal due date created a sense of urgency in all of us which proportionally increased our motivation to get it done by the goal due date. Unsurprisingly, by the end of our goal due date, we were able to finish the final RGM video due to our increased motivation that is derived from our sense of urgency. After the final video was finished, we felt even more relief that a major part of our RGM project was finished.
learning: The main thing I learned from this was that urgency is often the greatest source of motivation, and the main thing that creates urgency in a project is a due date. Thus, I learned the great importance of setting goals and due dates in order to complete tasks. Furthermore, through this experience, I came to realisation the importance of the mental aspect in a completing a task, as we were able to finish a task two weeks earlier than its official due date just by creating a sense of urgency in all of us.

I was able to quickly and easily iterate on the designs addressing the issues of the components as they became apparent saving time in theorising and ensuring a more reliable mechanism.

situation: In my previous course, ENGG2000/3000, students were allocated to a specific group within a team depending on their specialization (three groups: Structures, Motions, and Communications). As a mechanical student, I was placed in the ‘Structures’ group with four other civil/mechanical students. In my structures group, there were two students in their third year, and I was in my second year. The roles and responsibilities of each group were unique and specific to their discipline. The ‘Structures’ group was responsible for cube structure design, selection of material, and finally, manufacturing and assembly processes. The ‘Communications’ group was responsible for the software elements such as programming and debugging. The ‘Motions’ group was responsible for the motor plus sensor selection and electrical connections (wiring). Progress videos and pictures of the marble cube were compiled in a final video presentation.
task_action: As the structures group we brainstormed, and the finalized design concepts formulated for the structural element of the marble cube. Further, our group identified the relevant materials required for each relevant subsystem. Next, we gathered all the necessary materials and tools to build each section. Also, as one of the requirements is materials from certain suppliers only, this meant that if we did not have the materials or equipment available at these suppliers, we would look for alternatives by substituting them with something similar. Parts of the finalized design were slightly changed to adequately meet the supplier's requirements. Once each section was constructed, the group would perform 20 test runs and record the success rate. Next, the source of errors was identified for each subsystem and suggested improvements were amended to the system. Improvements or adjustments were made with the assistance of the other two groups in the team. Then, another 20 test runs were performed, and the improved success rate was documented. Additionally, a collection of videos and pictures were taken to document progress. Simultaneously, both other groups (communications and motions) were in frequent communication with our group, using our feedback, to make their selection of motors or sensors and their relevant programming. Whenever any changes big or small need to be made to the speed of the motors or the rate of the sensors, one member from the other group would make the necessary adjustments. Also, any other issue such as an increase or decrease in power output or dimension of the motor or sensor would be amended with the help of the other groups in the team. This streamlined the process as roadblocks or delays were attended to promptly.
result: By the end of the semester, we had developed a fully functioning marvellous marble machine that performed all the requirements outlined by our client. Also, the initial success rate and section reliability were improved and adjusted as necessary with the assistance of the other two groups. Immediate communication with the other groups when any issue presented itself allowed for efficient reliability improvements of the marble cube. Further, the progress videos and pictures were edited into the video presentation.
pfr: Initially, I felt that we were not competent to take on this project as it was a relatively substantial task given the client's requirements. I thought that it required a greater level of technical skills which we did not have to complete this project given the time constraints. During the mid-term break, our structures group (most of whom were available to make it in person to the workshop) began the optimization process by testing each subsystem and improving the reliability of the marble machine with the assistance of members from other groups. I felt that we would face too many overwhelming issues regarding the hardware and software limitations which would impede the progress of the marble cube. Luckily, we managed to address the issues in the marble cube promptly due to the competent members of our communications and motions group. The other members were very responsive and experienced in their areas which allowed our collective team to progress as rapidly as it did. Without their relevant knowledge and skills, I don’t believe we would have met the deadlines.
learning: Through this, it was evident that many members with different roles and responsibilities were necessary to complete a substantial project such as the marble cube. By having the relevant technical groups such as structures, communications, and motions with their assigned task, it meant that there was no confusion in how the cube workload was distributed. Further, it allowed for the rapid rate of design, development, and testing as multiple members were working on various parts of the marble cube at any given moment. Any mistakes or oversights were rectified or added promptly. Also, massive projects require knowledge and expertise that is wide-ranging and expansive, so having members from different technical backgrounds who have been assigned certain roles and responsibilities allows for immediate workload allocation. As a result, each member became more collaborative and communicative in the process which would help them in their career development as an engineer. Hence, having a clear understanding of the roles and responsibilities of each member of a team allows for an efficient and effective strategy to complete a massive project.
