Relief flowed through my body when I placed myself back on mute. I began rethinking the situation while other teams presented. Why do I get so nervous? Why do I have no control over it? How can I gain this control? I listened to my peers present so effortlessly and then I realised there is only twenty people in this class. I have no reason to shake this uncontrollably for only twenty people. Later, we split into our teams. Rockson joined soon after and notified us that we would present to the whole of Posse C. My anxiety began to rise again. I asked my team if anybody else would like to present. My team was understanding of my fears and offered if I couldn't do it. It was at this moment that I was tired of having a fear of public speaking. I wasn't going to let it hold me back any longer. I apologised to my team and let them know I had to learn at some point. I re-wrote my notes for the presentation based on what we were doing at that meeting. My hands shook the entire time but I didn't care. I was going to be presenting to ninety people but I wasn't letting it bother me.
learning: I began to view the situation in a better light. I'm behind a screen, despite my camera being on, everyone is concentrating on what I am showing them. I assured myself that the calmer I was presenting, the less chance I will mess up. I was dedicated to sounding clear and confident. When the time came, my team and I returned to Posse C and I presented my team's board. I spoke clearly and confidently. I forgot about the ninety people sitting on the other side of the screen. I pushed myself far beyond my comfort zone and delivered the presentation. I thanked everyone for listening and muted myself once again. I received messages from my team applauding my work. They were well aware of my fears and supported me after. I believe I have strongly developed my public speaking skills through this unit and will confidently and clearly present again in week 7 with my peers. I am significantly less nervous about this upcoming presentation as I have used my logic and knowledge to outline the reality of presenting, especially online.

topic: The most prominent transferable skill that has stood out within my group is reflecting over is ACCOUNTABILITY IN A TEAM'S OPERATION.
situation: As a team, we needed to ensure that each individual commits and follows through with weekly activities and finishes delegated tasks on time.
task_action: In our very first meeting as a team, we designed a team charter that describes and outlines the responsibilities and goals that we agree upon in undertaking the projects and assessments in this unit. We ensured and evaluated the alignment of expectations such as satisfactory levels of work, meeting times and communication channels, were established and to remain consistent in meeting those requirements in our group. Our team applied the S.M.A.R.T.E.R (Specific, Meaningful, Achievable, Relevant, Time-Bound, Evaluate and Re-adjust) framework to clearly define our project goals, roles and other commitments and have a verbal and written agreement to abide by these rules we have set for ourselves.
result: After the first team activities, there were some team members that did not abide by the charter and as a team made a few re-adjustments. After those re-adjustments were made, team members complied with their required tasks and were held accountable in team activities and assessable tasks.
pfr: As we set the first amendment of our team charter, I was hesitant about the motivation and commitments my other peers may contribute to the group project. By assessing their communication and general behaviour, I had some doubts. Thankfully, after the first team activities, re-adjustments could be made as early as possible to avoid situations where individual team members were unable to commit and were not held accountable when committing to a task. The framework we used as a group enabled us to adapt to these issues in a swift manner and make the necessary changes to how we go about confronting the accountability of each team member. I am grateful that the majority of my team is flexible in addressing the individual shortcomings of others and can commit to the end goal that we all agreed upon during our first meeting.
learning: Working with strict set rules may not always work in an ever-changing environment and may dissuade members to have less initiative, motivation, and general enjoyment of a team’s operation. Our team approach our measures of accountability by being flexible with the commitments of each individual member whilst maintaining certain thresholds of criteria that need to be met during assessable tasks. As the majority of our team has worked well thus far with a strong team dynamic, there is always room to improve in ensuring that our team is held accountable to the goals and roles we have set ourselves from day one. This is something I have seen that always recurs in both academic and commercial settings in the workplace. The ability to adapt is key to our team's accountability in team operations.

topic:
Team member management. 

Managing members of a team who are not meeting expectations and how to work with them to achieve that outcome that best serves everyone.
situation: We had a team member who has been continuously lacking in their contribution and effort throughout the semester.
task_action: Our task for this particular issue was to identify why this team member wasn't contributing to the level that was expected, as there are many reasons as to why this could be happening. Such as them not feeling that their contribution was appreciated, they didn't 'fit in' with the group, or other personal reasons that could be happening in their life. After some discussion within the rest of the team, we decided a good course of action was to message the team member and let them know that the rest of the group was unhappy with their performance. This felt like the right thing to do as the underperformer may not have even know that they weren't contributing enough. The message was important also in that it created evidence for us as a team that we had reached out and started to try and manage the situation. This could be important in future to show our teachers, in case our submitted work was lacking due to the performance of the problem member.
result: We received responses from the member, in which they apologised, and we hoped this would improve the situation going forward. At first we thought their contribution was starting to improve, however, within two week of sending the message it has become clear that their contribution is highly unlikely to improve. The team and I are now in discussions on how to manage this, with the lacking team member's RGM components likely to be excluded(if they ever get made) and their place in the final presentation to be taken by another member.
pfr: My feelings towards this situation were that of disappointment, as to have one member failing to contribute amongst what is otherwise a well functioning team, really hindered our team cohesion and constantly inhibited any planning or structure we made as a team. This disappointment led to me feeling frustrated, as over the semester there just seemed to be no effort made by the underperforming member to take part in even the bare minimum - yet they were quick to apologise and act remorseful when it was brought up. It felt very 'all talk no action', as they would agree to complete parts of group work, yet never came through and whenever placed in a position where their knowledge was tested, they failed miserably. Finally, I have to say that I felt sorry for this person, as I don't know what's happening in their life and the reasons for their performance. It bodes ill for the rest of their engineering education if they fail to perform in a 1000 level course.
learning: By talking as a team and hearing different perspectives on the position we had been placed in, we were able to put together a level headed approach that took all people into consideration. I admit to being lacking in compassion at times, and the input of my other team members helped me see the issue from sides I wouldn't have considered if left to making the decision on my own. Through this, I was able to not only learn effective team management skills, but also the importance of emotional consideration when dealing with other people.

topic: Initiative and the willingness to make decisions in the face of uncertainty.
situation: You and your team of engineers will undergo the planning, designing, construction and presentation of a Rube Goldberg Machine (AKA: RGM), over a 13-week period. One of the challenges given to our new team, was taking the initiative, and outlining clear goals/objectives for each meeting.
task_action: During week 8, we reacquainted and chatted about what we did over the break, this established a more friendly atmosphere in the meeting. Following this I took initiative and addressed the shortcoming of our leisure, we were behind and thus we brainstormed ways to remedy this issue, by constructing and improving our components during the meeting, during construction we had meaningful conversations and multitasked our way back on track. During week 9, the team faced the dilemma of presenting our improvements to the ‘Group C Possie’, a majority of the team hadn’t yet implemented their improvements, thus I took the initiative to present my improvements, this way I could ensure that the presenter knew the intricacies of the implemented improvements and thus is able to answer any questions the audience may have. This willingness to volunteer myself, enabled me to remove the weight over the team, as my team placed their trust in my ability to present, and this motivation cleared the uncertainties I had. In my opinion this led to the best presentation our group has delivered.
result: The outcome of the initiative I took, led to the smooth operation of the following weeks goals and objectives, and with the teams help I am able to confidently make decisions, knowing my team will back me up the entire way. This strengthened the unity of our group and grew each members confidence in taking the initiative to solve group dilemmas.
pfr: From my perspective, when our group reunited after the break, I felt that a vast majority of the momentum/enthusiasm was lost, and this created a similar experience to the first week our group met, it was uncomfortable, thus I broke the ice, I queried how everyone’s break was, this willingness to persevere my feelings worked, and I felt like we were part of a team again. I addressed how we hadn’t constructed any of our components yet and what we needed to do going forward. Thus we collaborated and constructed for the remainder of that period. The subsequent period revealed how despite my willingness to catch up, the team just wasn’t able to deliver, so I offered hesitantly the best solution I could come up with, the group agreed that this was the best course of action, and the outcome of this presentation had the boys cheering for me in the ‘WhatsApp’ group chat. This was a huge moral boost and inspired the boys for the upcoming weeks.
learning: This team-based project has truly taught me the importance of initiating conversations, as you cannot expect every meeting to go smoothly, and without an initiator this project would have far more challenges further down the line, as communication is the key to group projects. This experience has shifted my understanding of team equality. Team Equality is every member having an even contribution to the project, however now I believe it is everyone’s responsibility to further the teams progress, and sometimes be willing to assume a leader position to get the team underway.

topic:
A skill that I have developed throughout this course has been the skill and technique of looking at solutions and determining if it is a realistic solution. I believe this skill is important for engineers to help save on time and resources.

Throughout the development of the RGM project there have been many solutions developed, each with different and unique concepts. While many of these solutions were interesting, I was quick to point out that many of them were not possible due to a variety of factors such as time, complexity, and cost. After some team discussion it was decided that we would use more simple solutions to ensure that the project was completed on time.

Critical thinking is vitally important to engineers throughout all stages of the project. Looking at solutions objectively and with an open mind helps ensure that solutions can be created within the give time frame and budget. While it is important to understand when a solution is achievable, it is just as important to know when a solution is not.
situation: We needed to review our solutions to our RGM, which involves boiling an egg.
task_action: Look at the solutions objectively in our weekly meetings; listing the pros and cons for each solution; understanding the complexity and time it would take to complete the solution.
result: Many solutions to our RGM were created that the team and I believe are achievable within the given time frame and budget
pfr: It was fun to brainstorm different ideas for each event of the RGM. However, it was quite disheartening telling some of my team members that their solutions and ideas would be hard to achieve and complete due to time and complexity. While they didn't hold any grudges against me and were happy that I pointed out some issues with their ideas, it still bears some weight on my shoulders as I feel like I might have limited their creativity. However, after speaking with some other teams about their progress throughout this project and how they have faced challenges and issues with the complexity and budget of their events, I am confident that I made the right decision to point out some of the issues involved with our original solutions
learning: Coming up with effective solutions is essential for an engineer. However, it is arguably more important to be able to identify issues and challenges when coming up with new solutions. This can help save time, money, and ensure that the product that you are developing is completed in an above satisfactory way.

situation: We needed to develop creative ways to develop our rube Goldberg machine so it maintains a practical function of switching off an alarm clock, but also make it creative enough so it is interesting to watch from the viewers perspective.
task_action: After discussion with the team members, using the zoom breakout rooms, phone conversations and text conversations, it was understood that rube Goldberg machines function on the 6 simple machines; pulleys, levers, inclined planes, wheel and axle, wedges and screws. This information was then included onto a Miro board so we could brainstorm creative solutions involving these machines. For example, wheel and axles can be accomplished via use of a toy car, which uses the wheel and axles to roll down another simple machine, an inclined plane. Once we had brainstormed possible solutions, we then determined which ones would be possible to create with the equipment limitations of each member. In this way we would be able to dedicate time and resources to the creative solutions we can produce, instead of having to apply effort or purchasing resources to solutions we can't accomplish.
result: The result is the ability for each team member to successfully be able to accomplish a certain solution towards the project using the materials they have, without the need to purchase any items. These solutions will involve the application of the 6 simple machines and therefore be both entertaining to view, while also being true to the essence of what a rube Goldberg machine is.
pfr: When conducting projects such as this, occasionally ambition can get the better of one or all members of the team, myself included. This is where one or all of the team members produce ideas that are unreasonable or impossible to achieve in the given time frame. This prompts project creep as the more time dedicated to these overly complicated creative designs, the less time spent on the completion of the whole project. In our rube Goldberg machine we have avoided this effect and instead chosen less complex, but still creative, solutions to the project.
learning: From knowing the temptation to create overly ambitious solutions to projects, which ultimately result in the incompletion of tasks and the project whole, I have attempted a new strategy by prioritising the whole project over just a few specific parts. This is a learning experience due to projects I have done in the past where I choose tasks that would be above and beyond, however due to time and materials constraints, they aren't realistically achievable. Through the experience of this unit and prior events, I have also realised the importance of working and presenting ideas as a team. My colleagues produce ideas of themselves, and provide constructive criticism on ideas to ensure we all agree on creative, but attainable solutions that are ideal to complete our project.

situation: Good teamwork and communication skills are required in this unit due to working in groups to make a RGM.
task_action: In week 1, we had to get to know our team members and establish a good way of communicating offline. We each were actively listening to the others, told stuff about ourselves, became more friendly with each other and set up google spaces as our way of communicating offline.
result: This resulted in all the members feeling more comfortable with each other and meant we could communicate more effectively online as well as offline through google space.
pfr: Online class and teamwork was intimidating, as I hadn't done these at Uni yet. However, my teammates and I were able to get past the nervous stage and so we felt comfortable working together.
learning: By coming into class with a positive attitude and being open-minded can make working and communicating with new teammates much easier and in the future will cause less stress when I am working with new teammates at Uni or at work.

situation: As a part of 5 members team, I along with my other team members were tasked with building a Rube Goldberg Machine which equally serves the purpose of sustainability, user friendliness, and economical. We had a very limited time to design, build and solve any constraints of this unique project. On top of that, I had to enhance my team working, formal procedures and online based working skills by regularly submitting minutes, agenda and updating our clients. We had limited time of 12 weeks to come up with a functional Rube Goldberg Machine
task_action: Our main task was to build a Rube Goldberg Machine by the end of the semester while ensuring various project requirements. These are but not limited to sustainable. economical, environment friendly and unique user experience. In addition to that, I had to submit minutes, agenda, progress update presentations to our clients every week. To achieve our goal, we had to take several actions. On the very first week, we had a team meeting to get to know each other and discuss our availability. Each member was equally rostered for the weekly minute and agenda submission and to do the client presentations. By the next couple of weeks, we brainstormed and set our project goals and objectives. We had our detailed deadline and time frame as the following: * Design Phase: Week 6 * Initial Testing : Week 7-9 * Reliability Constraints and Problem Solving : Week 9-10 * Video of RGM : Week 11-12 * Final Presentation: Week 13 These time frame was designed in a way that we have at least one week of buffer time in case if anything doesn't go according to our plan. We had necessary backup members on standby if one of the team member failed to deliver their assigned part of the project. We regularly had team meetings outside of designated workshop to keep up with the project deadline and requirements. The next big challenge I faced was resource management. I had to come up with resources that is regularly used in our day to day activities and serves the purpose of sustainability. For my initial components, I had my reliability figures ready by the end of week 7 and shot my final video by week 9. This gave me enough time to make further improvements and help my team mates whenever it was necessary. When the question came to finding suitable resources, I took the inspiration from my passion of cooking. Most of the parts of my RGM components were sourced from food packaging boxes, containers which I planned to recycle later. To improve my team working, formal procedures, and online-based working skills, I attended regular meetings to discuss our progress and challenges. I also submitted minutes and agendas to keep track of project development and updated our clients regularly.
result: Despite the challenges we faced, we were hoping to complete our project on time and within the given constraints. We will present a functional Rube Goldberg Machine that meets the project requirements of sustainability, user-friendliness, and economic viability. By using recycled food packaging boxes and containers, I was able to contribute to the sustainability aspect of the project. Our team working skills also significantly improved throughout the project. We regularly communicated and coordinated with each other to make sure everyone was on track with their assigned tasks. The formal procedures we implemented, such as regular meetings, minute and agenda submissions, and progress update presentations to clients, helped us keep track of our project development and ensured that we were all working towards the same goal. In the end, our hard work and dedication are paying off as we received positive feedback from both our clients and our peers. Overall, this experience taught me the importance of time and resource management, effective communication, and teamwork in achieving a common go
pfr: Reflecting on the experience of building the Rube Goldberg Machine and managing time and resources effectively, I have mixed feelings of accomplishment, pride, and personal growth. At the beginning of the project, I felt a sense of excitement combined with a tinge of anxiety due to the limited time frame and the complexity of the task. However, as the project progressed, I became more confident in our team's abilities and our ability to meet the project goals. This project reminded me of my previous experiences working in team settings and managing time and resources effectively. I recalled instances where miscommunication, lack of planning, or poor resource management led to inefficiencies and suboptimal outcomes. Drawing from those experiences, I was determined to apply the lessons learned and avoid repeating similar mistakes in this project I also experienced a sense of fulfillment as I saw the machine taking shape and witnessed the successful integration of sustainable and user-friendly components. It was truly rewarding to witness the machine in action, knowing that we had overcome challenges and created something unique and impactful.
learning: This experience has taught me several valuable lessons. Firstly, effective time management is crucial in achieving project goals. By establishing clear deadlines, prioritizing tasks, and regularly monitoring progress, we were able to stay on track and complete the project within the given timeframe. I have gained insight into the importance of setting realistic schedules and allowing buffer time for unexpected delays or challenges. Secondly, I have learned the significance of resource management, especially in relation to sustainability. The creative approach of sourcing components from recycled food packaging not only contributed to the environmental aspect but also inspired me to think outside the box and explore unconventional solutions in future projects. Furthermore, this experience highlighted the significance of effective communication and collaboration within a team. Regular team meetings, minute and agenda submissions, and client updates ensured that everyone was aligned, leading to improved coordination and successful project outcomes. I have realized the power of open and transparent communication in fostering a positive team dynamic. In the future, I will be more proactive in planning and managing resources, considering sustainability as a priority. I will also continue to enhance my communication and team working skills, ensuring that all team members are involved and informed throughout the project. Additionally, I will carry forward the mindset of exploring creative and unconventional solutions, seeking inspiration from different domains, and embracing innovation. Overall, this experience has not only enhanced my technical skills but also deepened my understanding of the importance of time and resource management, effective communication, and the value of collaboration in achieving project success. I am excited to apply these insights in future endeavors, embracing challenges with confidence and striving for continuous improvement.

topic: Trade-offs, judgment, and balance in resolution
situation: The group task in ENGG1050; group members are choosing not to contribute, so the rest of the team have to organise how we are going to maximise our marks for the time we have left. We had set a time limit for our group members to send in their events before it was too late as we would need time to prepare a presentation as well as edit the final video.
task_action: We have 2 weeks left and 3/5 group members are not contributing so my remaining member and I discuss how we are going to maximise our marks. We decide that we will have to make a backup video for the occasion our group members don't produce something we are able to use, for which we brainstorm a way to shorten our video to not only give us enough time to prepare a presentation but to also still follow the initial video theme. We delegated each other 2 more events each to make in addition to the 2 each we already made, but I was to make the start of the video and he was to make the ending scene. These 4 events would then be put into a separate video to be used if we did not receive any further events from our group. Although, we did find it unfair to carry the weight of the other group members, it would be a trade off we are willing to take to pass the unit.
result: This resulted in us having a backup plan in the event of our group members not contributing in time or at all. This would allow us to maximise our marks we could receive with the time we had left.
pfr: Initially, I was not keen on contributing any more than I was as my other group members stopped, but in doing so would solidify failing the unit. As my topic states, trade offs, in order to pass this course I would need to contribute more which would be a trade off well worth. My personal judgement on the situation was that in order to succeed and maximise my success, I would personally need to step up and contribute more. Although, for me to step up, this would take more time and effort, but as I already enjoyed the task in creating an RGM, creating more would not only be fun to do, but will help my team in passing the unit. This connects to the last part in my topic being balance in resolution.
learning: With the help of Simon, I was able to learn that even though people may not contribute, it is ultimately up to them and although they may not develop from it, I still can. In addition, having a back up plan in the works to make sure I maximise my own marks, even though this creates more work for myself, I will be able to develop much greater, while also succeeding.

situation: In our team Head on hat, all the team members are working full time along with full time university, which makes it quite difficult for us to manage time for the weekly meeting. Similarly, our RGM revolves around being efficient and recycling the items that are available to us at home, which means we need to build a lot of the complex machine using the everyday items that are in our home.
task_action: the major issue for us was making time for the meeting as we are required to have meeting weekly for the project with all the team members having different time schedules availabilities. result: Making the google calendar helped us tremendously as we were able to find a common ay where al of us would be in university and would be able to have a meeting, as all the team members preferred the in-person meetings. Along with that the google docs allowed to put our work in the in the document which allowed us to track the progress of each member. Similarly, the idea of sharing the materials allowed us to make our RGM more interesting. Along with that the budgeting our expenses helped us to stay with in the theme of our RGM.
pfr: This method has helped me quite a lot as it allowed me to manage my time better and help me use the resources, I had available to me for my project. Along with that it helped me strengthen my team work skills by allowing to learn various news skills with my team members.
learning: this method to deal with the time and the limitation of the resources and management of time also help us as a team to better understand the importance of the common sharing apps such as the google docs, google slides, as they helped us out throughout the project as everyone could monitor the work of the others and give feedback on their work.

situation: Interpersonal skills have been necessary throughout the course of this semester’s group work and tasks. It has appeared in every aspect of the tasks and teachings of ENG1050, most importantly, communication, innovation process, responsibility, and roles.

learning: Overall, the development and implementation of ‘Interpersonal Skills: Teamwork and Communication’ has been essential to our success and educational development as Engineering students at Macquarie and for our future indevours and careers beyond university. situation: Our team had to decide a specific theme for our Rube Goldberg Machine. But we had conflicting opinions about certain ideas and designs.
task_action: During our group meeting sessions, we dedicated a section in Miro where each team member put in their ideas in different sticky notes. There were a few unique ideas and themes for the chain reaction portions and end result, but most of the themes listed were simple and straightforward; for instance: popping a balloon, dropping ice cubes into glass. We had to eliminate most of the visions and decide ONE theme for our project based on various limitations: time, material access, budget.
result: Upon taking all the constraints into consideration, all of us agreed to go for the most uncomplicated and manageable one: Popping a balloon. This design included of accessible resources for the chain reaction. For instance: A race car moving down a track, a lever ringing a bell etc.
pfr: Initially I was quite disheartened since I was really excited to make our Machine stand out by attaching in unique aspects to it. However, my idea was the first one to get eliminated by everyone. learning: My team members were really supportive of my idea and mentioned that it was brilliant. Even though we did not go for my exact vision, my teammates were generous enough to point out my hard work and appreciate it. Our understanding and friendly communication really shifted my mood in a positive manner.

situation: We had to use our critical thinking to be able to decide on which ideas to use in our Rube Goldberg machine as well as how to execute them.
task_action: I started with several different ideas of which to use for our Rube Goldberg machine, and then I had to think about how feasible each option was. I would weigh each idea's positives and negatives and weigh out how long it would take to complete each. the reliability of each task was brought into effect as I had to choose something which would work over and over again without failure.
result: I ended up with 2 different tasks which had a high level of reliability that wont take too long to set up and complete to create an effective and reliable Rube Goldberg machine.
pfr: The initial task seemed to be tough as I had so many different ideas to choose from which all seemed to look about the same level of ease. But as I started my initial testing I learnt that there were clear winners of what was better and worse. this allowed me to choose those ideas of which to pursue. the final design was chosen based on its feasibility to complete as well as reliability.
learning: Through this approach, I learned to first start to experiment with the different ideas before making assumptions about the task ahead as a lack of experience can lead to incorrect assumptions that won't give positive feelings. i also learnt that through critical thinking i am able to effectively narrow down the options which i am faced with.

topic: The skill that I will mainly be reflecting over is, Time and resource management.

learning: We learnt about the brainstorming method of generating ideas earlier in the session which really helped us a lot in putting my ideas forward. Deciding how to filter through all the themes everyone had put forth made sure there was an agreed upon system and easier to discard the themes that didn’t meet our needs.

topic: Oral Presentation of group C13's work to Posse C
situation: In week 6, we were tasked with presenting the preliminary design of our Rube Goldberg Machine idea to our larger group, Posse C. This included the work completed the previous week and all work completed during the meeting.
task_action: Planning the presentation; to prepare for this presentation, we all discussed the order in which to present the work. I was tasked with the presentation, with a decision to quickly go over the previous week's work and primarily focus on the preliminary design sketches. This allowed me to go into depth of the work that was being questioned while keeping the attention of the Posse through an engaging presentation. result: In presenting, I was able to get all of our ideas across to the posse in a quick and engaging way. All topics were covered, with each sketch in the preliminary design covered in great detail. The risk assessment was only looked at briefly, with not much time used to discuss this section due to time constraints.
pfr: Initially, I was quite daunted with presenting the work to our Posse due to a sense of pressure to get all our ideas across in an engaging way. This pressure was further increased as I compared our work to other presentations that had been completed in previous weeks. As I got further into the presentation, I was able to stay calm and clearly articulate our ideas. At times, it did seem to become repetitive as each sketch contained relatively similar components, like dominoes or small cars. By the end, I was able to talk through our risk assessment and answer some questions from the tutors without feeling like I was missing any information or leaving out important aspects of the design. Compared to the earlier presentation in our tutor group, I feel like I was far more concise with our work and ideas. Compared to presentations I have made in high school, it was less coherent as in those speeches, every idea was clear and each element of the speech contributed to the class' understanding and engagement with the topic.
learning: By taking thirty minutes before the presentation to prepare, taking some more creative ideas from the group, I could make the presentation more engaging for the whole posse. This could include setting up a small PowerPoint presentation, including more images, or by getting a better understanding of what the whole group has achieved by reading through each section thoroughly. Practicing a small speech with some key notes would also be key to improving a more streamlined presentation, ensuring that nothing important could be forgotten. Experiencing this situation has allowed me to truly appreciate the importance of preparation and professionalism in oral presentations, all whilst persevering through any uncomfortable feelings I may come across.

topic: Critical thinking and analysis of possible faults in our RGM designs.
situation: We needed to determine a method of selecting ideas and filtering out those ideas that aren’t feasible in our design though the use of critical analysis of our thought processes.
task_action: In creating the idea filter system we had a brainstorming session to determine the method in which ideas were challenged and decided upon. We determined the best method was to allow the person suggesting the idea to present the design idea then field questions posed by the group on the idea followed by a vote. This discussion on the method of filtering ideas was then used to remove or modify unfeasible ideas from our final design as the questioning process allowed for the group to think critically on what was suggested and caused the idea to form that all action must be repeatable, feasible and on a track of some description.
result: The result of creating this filtering method has allowed for the group to quickly and fairly remove or modify unfeasible events and ideas from our Rube Goldberg Machine. Which has resulted in the design process to be smooth and allowed for all members to understand what each member is doing and have a saying everyone’s component is to create a more uniform machine.
pfr: The progress to undertake critical analysis of ideas was complex at the start as we weren’t sure on what the criteria for good ideas were. As we discussed ideas and what makes them feasible options, we uncovered that we often overshoot what we could actually achieve. This discussion allowed us to feel like more of a group as we shared our options and ideas as a group.
learning: Through the experience of using critical analysis and thinking on our individual designs as a group. We could determine problems more expediently and start to rectify them as a group before they became a larger problem. Through this process of doing critical analysis and think as a group I have learnt that it is often better to discuss ideas as a group as many issues that you might overlook are often questioned and challenged by other allowing you to rectify and understand those issues as well as presenting and questioning ideas in a way that others can understand.

topic: THE DESIGN PROCESS PHASING AND APPROACHES
situation: During our design process, we had to create new designs for each of our stages for out RGM machine and plan an approach as to how we would take this design from paper to reality, which would allow us to step foot into the world of teamwork & project design, ultimately preparing us for the upcoming weeks ahead and ensuring we are able to build a RGM machine effectively.
task_action: Planning our initial design included assigning a stage to each team member, and discussing our responsibilities, common goals, team goals, strengths, and weaknesses. Whilst in the process of creating our design, we had communication issues leading us to devise a poorly constructed plan which would’ve remained unless we all decided to act collectively and start communicating effectively.
result: By collaborating and checking in with each other weekly through team meetings, we were able to finish our initial design and moved onto our testing process. By building each stage and testing each stage’s reliability, we were able to calculate the overall reliability for our RGM machine which gave us an understanding of the progress we’ve made so far. And by sharing our common goals and values we were able to understand each other better and work together as a team to improving the reliability and finish our planning process.
pfr: The initial task of working in a team seemed daunting at first as it was well outside my comfort zone. But by thoroughly working through team building exercises, I was able to step out of this zone and exceed my expectations of working a team. This allowed me to improve my teamwork skillset and also allowed me to gain an understanding of collaborative processes such as discussion of new ideas and common needs and goals, for that project design.
learning: I learned about the approach engineers take to ensure their design process aligns with their own and team objectives. And how they implement innovation to continuously improve the project’s reliability.

topic: Designing, prototyping and testing of components.
situation: We needed to create eye catching and invigorating mechanisms to use in a Rube Goldberg Machine. These mechanisms need to have a high consistency to work repeatedly over multiple camera shots.
task_action: Once we had a broad conceptual design of our RGM we needed to manufacture our components to work in the real world. Each section of the RGM machine was first configured separately to ensure that they would function efficiently and consistently on their own before combining together for the final produced RGM. I started each prototype by running the section of my personal RGM multiple times so I could establish a reliability. When changing my prototype vastly I could retest the reliability to Mathematically prove which of the Iterations of prototype are an improvement.
result: The result of improving the reliability of each design as much as possible before incorporating was that the overall reliability was massively improved by the power of the amount of components. Once a component was completed I could start the next component with the previous component already optimized and the new component was never needed to be reconfigured to take an alternate input from the previous component.
pfr: Beginning the development was difficult for me as the structure allocated in class to design and create an RGM didn't fit the method I would have wanted to take. By breaking the process of building into separate components I was able to regain control of the workflow of manufacturing my section of our groups Rube Goldberg Machine. This broken down workflow gave me security and eased my stress of staying on track with the checkpoints that were presented to us.
learning: This task has re-enforced a practice I have been working for the past few months. This practice is; separating tasks to their smallest components and completing the small goals one at a time, so that I can stay on task and also feel accomplished at each small step completed. This task was a big helping hand and really improved my trust in this method of completing an endeavour.

topic: I will be reflecting on the topic of the design process phasing and approaches of a mechanism design
situation: In order to finish our RGM machine before the deadline and make the RGM machine done as perfect as we can, we had to phase the design process for each week and precisely followed the each step of Engineering design.
task_action: First and foremost, as a team, we set out to finish the RGM machine and successfully achieve our objectives by strictly following to the engineering design process. The weekly team task description on ENGG1050 Ilearn weekly task (what's on this week) is what we would first read through in order to accomplish the goals. We divided the weekly tasks for each week into daily tasks that were assigned to each team member so that we could know what to do for the week and what we needed to prepare for the following week. We also made sure that we had two pre-meetings per week (on Tuesday and Thursday nights) to check in with each other and see if anyone was having any issues.or difficulties on the individual tasks and discussed the issues that we were facing on as well as making sure that we could finish up all the works before the deadlines.In order to maximise our progress towards our goals, we then referred to the engineering design documents to follow the design process (such as Conceptual design, Preliminary Design) step by step. We would also evaluate success or failure by achieving reliability and repeatability during the design process.
result: The results were being able to phase the RGM's design process step by step and as a team we could finish the final RGM on time and also ensured the reliability and repeatability of our RGM, so eventually we could accomplish our goals.
pfr: We were quite overwhelmed at first with the RGM design process, unsure of our ability to complete the final RGM by the deadline, and unsure of how we would manage to finish the weekly tasks. However, as we established the deadlines for each weekly work and explicitly allocated each team member to the task, as well as phasing the RGM design process, we began to move towards our objectives. Finally, we were able to work effectively as we made progress towards completing our final RGM.
learning: I have a deep appreciation for the importance of team organisation, setting clear objectives, and phasing those goals into each period after learning and working online with a team throughout the semester. Additionally, by learning the RGM design process, I have gained a deeper understanding of how the engineering design process works and how precise it is. This has improved my ability to think critically and solve problems, as well as increased my understanding of how to phase large problems or tasks into smaller ones and approach goals.

topic: ENGG1050 has allowed my team to improve our oral presentation skills through the weekly presentations in preparation for both the final Rube Goldberg Machine presentation and when we need to demonstrate our employability for a future job. Through modifying ideas seen from other groups and adapting to the feedback received, we have been able to create the best presentations possible. We saw how important communicating through oral presentations is as it is the way people share ideas with others and influence their decisions. Our goal was to achieve 100% in our weekly presentation marks and, later on, score highly in our final presentation.
situation: Every week, starting in Week 2, our teams have had to give a weekly presentation to the other teams in our Tutor group. If chosen, we would then present to our Posse. This presentation is based on the work completed throughout the week prior and the previous workshop to demonstrate how our Rube Goldberg Machine is progressing and what we are learning from it.
task_action: We needed to come up with a presentation based on each week’s topic, centering around what stage in our Rube Goldberg Machine we were up to by rotating through our team, ensuring that everyone had a turn. It is a collaborative task for everyone to work on before the chosen person presents during the Friday workshop, using the feedback we are given from our tutor on the previous presentation/s. Some of this feedback was a major aspect of the presentation that many teams were struggling with. When presenting the information, it had to be useful and relevant without cramming too much in one screen so that the audience wouldn’t know where to look. In order to create the best presentation possible, we used our time to provide the presenter with various graphs, tables or other visual aids to make the presentation look aesthetically pleasing and informative. We also worked together on providing a basic outline of what needed to be conveyed in the presentation to make the job of creating it easier for the presenter. To ensure the time stayed below five minutes, the presenter practiced beforehand, cutting or modifying sections as best they could while also seeking advice from other team members. Although these tasks were actioned correctly in most weeks, one week there was miscommunication within the group and each team member thought another person was presenting.
result: In the latter situation, everyone thought they were not the presenter which resulted in an awkward silence as we each waited for someone to present. However, since we hadn’t planned for this, nothing happened and we soon realised the mistake after texting in our group chat to find out what had happened. Despite this hiccup, after executing our ideas to improve our presentations and using careful planning, we finally reached our goal and received 100% for our last presentation.
pfr: At first, we were all still getting to know each other and didn’t know how to proactively collaborate on a presentation. Our very first presentation, in Week 2, was presented by me and I had felt very lost due to not having anything to base my presentation off of and little to no help from my equally confused team members. Fortunately, through doing this every week, we were able to gather the necessary ideas and structure to implement in creating a better presentation. We found that using a PowerPoint slideshow was a better method of maintaining control over the presentation and keeping the audience in one place at a time than scrolling rather aimlessly through our Miro boards. This positively aided our teamwork as we began to work together on the plan for each week at our weekly meetings which boosted our team morale and brought us closer together. For me personally, I gained more confidence in my presenting and oral skills, and was able to produce a great presentation with my team’s help to get us the marks we wanted.
learning: I learnt a good many new skills in oral presentation which I can use, both in university and in any future career as it is an incredibly easily transferable skill. My team learnt how to communicate by sending multiple reminders and making sure everyone is on the same page so that we don’t have a repeat of our presentation disaster and ensure that someone will be presenting that week. We also learnt collaboration is crucial so that each team member understands everything, such as the equations used or an explanation of an event, which means that we can all answer relevant questions and know how to best explain it to other people without leaving a team member behind. While those skills in the backend of oral presentations are important, we also gained skills that are more visible to the audience. These include the best methods of getting the necessary information across (such as using graphs and only certain sections of tables instead of the whole thing), keeping under a time limit (by practicing and anticipating any mishaps while still leaving time for questions) and staying engaging throughout the presentation (by keeping it professional in a formal way while also including an occasional joke to draw the audience in). These aspects came together to make the package of what I have learnt, both individually and with my team, when it comes to the skill of oral presentation.

topic: thinking calmly under pressure and failure assessment
situation: With the planning of the RGM concluding in the first half of the semester, it was time to build the machine which had an obvious problem, that was finding a way to keep my scene interesting enough to the audience while reducing the difficulty of filming the scene.
task_action: My initial scene was quite complicated and difficult to set up which resulted in a lot of failures while filming it, subsequently, I hit a creative block when I tried to come up with ideas to reduce the complexity, so I decided to refer to the slides on failure analysis and was able to come with several options on rebuilding my scene
result: I was able to narrow down the solutions and then I ended up increasing the length of my track so the balls would have enough force to knock over the dominoes while adding 2 extra balls to act as stoppers which allowed me to make the filming of my scene a bit easier
pfr: When I ran out of ideas to implement on my project I started to panic and was not able to think calmly. I kept repeating the same mistakes when trying to film my scene and it left me thinking if I was doing something wrong however I allowed myself to take a short break and refer to the slides which allowed me to think calmly and find a solution.
learning: I’ve learned that allowing myself to think calmly and do a proper failure analysis expedited the time I needed to film the scene when compared to the state of panic I was initially in. I’ve also learned from this experience that taking a deep breath and a step away from a task or a project that is clearly not progressing does a lot of help for my mental state and allows me to think with a fresh perspective which allows the creative processes in my brain to function again.

situation: A device is needed to unload boxes from a conveyer.
task_action: Smaller groups were formed and each individual member was asked to come up with an idea and give an oral presentation to the the rest of the group and then the groups would decide which idea was the best and then give an oral presentation to all the groups and then the final idea would be voted in by each group based on the idea and presentation.

situation: In my Rube Goldberg machines team, I was tasked with designing an element that not only performed its function reliably but also ensured consistent results when replicated by others. Firstly, the marble would roll down a sloped zigzag path, ensuring a controlled and predictable motion. Next, it would collide with a second marble attached to a string. This collision would set off a pendulum-like motion, swinging the second marble into contact with a platform, also attached to a string. The impact would release a third marble positioned on top of the platform, initiating the next stage of the sequence.
task_action: Having completed the 3D design of my build, the next crucial step was ensuring its reproducibility. While initially tempted to rely on trial and error, I recognized the importance of a more systematic approach. To achieve this, I sat down with a paper, pen, and ruler and made a series of calculated actions. I meticulously calculated the mass and diameter of the marbles, the angles of the slopes, and the lengths of the strings. This comprehensive approach allowed me to anticipate and account for potential variables, ensuring consistency in the machine's performance. Following these calculations, I conducted multiple test runs to validate their efficacy in real-world conditions. Through rigorous experimentation, I confirmed that my calculations translated seamlessly into practical applications. This iterative process not only affirmed the reliability of my design but also enhanced my confidence in its reproducibility.
result: The result of my approach was a machine built on factual numbers, ensuring its reproducibility by others wishing to replicate the design. By basing the design on precise calculations rather than trial and error, I provided a clear blueprint for anyone seeking to construct a similar machine.
pfr: At first, I felt uncertain and overwhelmed by the enormity of designing and constructing the machine. I considered taking shortcuts to ease the pressure, but I knew deep down that I wanted to approach it like a true engineer—with careful calculations and precision. As the machine began to take shape and eventually worked as intended, I felt a swell of pride. The journey was challenging but ultimately rewarding. I have no regrets about the hardships faced seeing the reproducible machine in action fills me with satisfaction and a sense of accomplishment.
learning: Through this experience, I learned the importance of reproducibility as a guiding principle in my engineering endeavors. Prioritizing reproducibility not only enhances the reliability of my machines but also ensures that they perform in line with my expectations. By adhering to reproducibility standards, my builds become more accurate and trustworthy, laying a solid foundation for future projects. Furthermore, we recognised the importance of modular construction in facilitating our design process. We divided the machine into modular sections, with each section assigned to individual team members. This modular approach allowed us to isolate track issues, troubleshoot problems, and fix individual components without disrupting the entire setup. By compartmentalising our design in this way, we maximised efficiency and minimised the impact of potential failures, thereby enhancing the overall robustness of our machine. Additionally, our modular construction approach allowed efficient troubleshooting, further enhancing the overall reliability of our machine. situation: During ENGG1050 Workshop we were assigned to work on a project on a Rube Goldberg Machine as a team of 6 people. result: The result was the accountability for the team was upheld. The presenter held himself accountable, learnt from his mistakes and rectified it.

learning: As we were a group of young strangers it was easy to deflect blame and accountability whenever it was on us. I have learnt to hold myself accountable throughout this unit. For example in the lead up to the week 9 presentation I was held responsible to prepare a slideshow for the presenter. I have learnt that it is better to be held accountable and learn from a mistake rather than to shift blame and have no rectification of the problem.

topic: IDENTIFYING THE ISSUE, PROBLEM, OR PARADOX
situation: We needed to increase our Rube Goldberg Machine reliability as a whole. In doing so we need to identify the issues and problems we were having with each individual component to devise a way to resolve it.
task_action: To determine the issues we used brainstorming sessions and root cause analysis as a group to determine the possible issues that we were having. In doing so we looked at each person's chain of events and their individual components as well as the task they were attempting to complete . This allowed us to understand what issues and problems were arising as we all discussed what they might be and also possible solutions to resolve them. To do this we asked these questions; what happened, why did it happen, what can we do to fix it. Which formed the bases of our root cause analysis.
result: The results of this root cause analysis allowed us to increase the reliability of our Rube Goldberg Machine greatly. This can be seen with our reliability increasing from 4% to 52% reliable. This process also allowed us to as a group understand each component in greater detail and share ideas on how to resolve the issue of each machine as often the issue we determined to be most affecting the components was a simple one that was overlooked.
pfr: The process of identifying the issues and problems with our Rube Goldberg Machine was a difficult task as we as a group designed and planned each component and when it didn't work as expected it took us a substantial amount of time to determine what the issues with our designs could be. Although as we watched the videos of each other's designs and discussed what was happening we soon realized what the issues were. Often finding why it was happening was again fairly difficult. Not to mention working out how to fix the issues. Although at the end of this process when we worked out the issues and then actually fixed them it was a quite joyful moment as we were able to see that our ideas were actually effective.
learning: Through this experience of determining the issues and problems in our Rube Goldberg Machine. We learnt how to as a group undertake root cause analysis and how humbling it can be after planning and building something that there are so many issues that need addressing. We also learnt that working as a group and having fresh eyes on the problems allowed us to determine what was actually causing it and often it was a small thing that we overlooked causing the issue. Which real taught is that we often need to step back and look at the wider picture to understand a problem more as when you design and build it you are often too close to see what is wrong until you step back.

topic: Transferable skills are vital as they overlap into different industries and occupations and provide beneficial outcomes for individuals. Creating good habits is a transferable skill which can be vital to an individual's development personally and professionally. Throughout ENGG1050 I have grown as an individual based on the habit creating methods discussed by tutors. The adoption of James Clear's - Cue --> Response --> Reward methodology has allowed me to create good habits that have assisted me in becoming more organised, feeling more motivated -- while creating discipline in all realms of life. The philosophy of instant gratification vs delayed gratification has made an impact on the way I now view tasks. Understanding that small changes everyday, even 1%, make a huge difference in the long run has allowed me to trust the process, even when results are instant I can be confident that these small 1% changes will pay off in the long run. This mentality that I am striving to continually improve on is a transferable skill that I can carry through personal and professional envious in the future
situation: As a group for ENGG1050 we have been tasked to design and construct a functional Rube Goldberg Machine(RGM) with a number of actions taking place. While doing this by following the engineering process we are building on our transferable skills which in turn are developing ourselves to be more valuable individuals in the workplace. Along the journey we have been introduced to the power of habits and creating good ones to allow for a more fulfilling life.
task_action: Although creating good habits and following them do not directly affect our task of constructing the RGM it does however indirectly affect it in ways. By creating good habits as an individual that energy that you possess can be felt in your team and in turn influence your team positively. Arriving on time to meetings is a simple habit that can be developed and hence also influence other members to show up on time and allow for a much more streamline process when undergoing the designing and construction process of our RGM.
result: The result of creating good habits has allowed myself as an individual to create a positive working environment which as a result made our task easier without much more effort. As these habits develop it becomes autonomous and not much thinking occurs, it just happens, for example when my team has weekly check in calls we know how to get straight into what needs to get done. We have developed this habit and it has saved us a lot of time. Creating small changes everyday to improve, even by as little as 1% can make an astronomical difference, as felt by myself and the team. Just 5min a day for a year, adds up to 30 hours of time. So although my team may be saving only 5 minutes sometimes it adds up in the long run
pfr: The initial task had me puzzled at the start as I have never constructed anything near the scale and complexity as the RGM we have been tasked to complete. While this was a hurdle in itself while being online for the unit my overall feeling was puzzled. As time progressed , I met my team, began to understand the task at hand and the confusion I once felt turned to excitement. While a positive working environment was developing I found myself more motivated to work and perform to the best of my ability. As the weeks progressed, as an individual I found creating good habits helped me stay on track and keep me on my path. Although good habits yield good results, especially in the long run, bad habits can very easily start to slip back into routine. In the recent weeks i have found myself picking up bad habits I used to do eg. not going to the gym. Going to the gym doesn't directly affect the task but physical exercise is shown to have a positive impact on mental stimulation which would be beneficial to any workplace.
learning: while these hurdles started by making me feel overwhelmed, getting into a routine and creating good habits such as staying on top of lecture work and not letting it pile on has allowed me to have some sort of success with the task. I have found that fighting off bad habits can be hard and especially easy to fall back into. The instant gratification bad habits bring is what makes them so dangerous and while going through ENGG1050 I am becoming better at staying with good habits over bad habits. To further grow my learning I have purchased James Clear's - Atomic Habits and plan to continue my growth as an individual.

situation: We had to begin constructing the action events of our RGM’s.
task_action: In preparation for week 8’s workshop we were asked to create a presentation on our RGM components individual reliabilities. Consequently, we were required to begin construction of the RGM events. We aimed to distribute the events equally amongst group members in our pre-workshop meeting. In this meeting, we created a Miro board with each unique action event and the materials required in each component. Action events were subsequently split between members based on who possessed necessary materials for a particular component. For example, I had string required for the zipline event and I had the cloth for our tablecloth event, and therefore I was assigned these two events. Following this meeting, each member was given the responsibility to construct and test their event, approximately 10-20 times, to determine reliability and then fill in their events subsection in our presentation for week 8. By the time of this workshop, we had tested a total of 6 events. I had tested the zipline event, however not extensively due to time restraints, and I could not acquire the slinky required in the tablecloth event, hence failing to test it. We presented these 6 events and their individual reliabilities in the week 8 workshop. The following week 9’s presentation required us to improve upon the individual reliability of our events, subsequently requiring us to construct what we failed to construct in the previous week. A pre-meeting was conducted where we discussed our failed attempt to get all action events in the previous week’s presentation, with a prevailing issue being time management, and thus decided on how to move forward. Specifically, we agreed each team member should allocate time to construct and test the remaining action events at least 2 days prior to our week 9 workshop. This deadline was put in place so that if someone had still not completed their event, they could ask for assistance in completing their event. Furthermore, we discussed each component we had already completed and how to improve reliability, with members suggesting changes in materials and alternative approaches to increase successful attempts. In order to improve time management each member decided and set aside 2 hours on a certain day to complete their assignments.
result: By the week 9 workshop, we were able to present 10 out of the 12 action events and their reliabilities, with us improving the 6 previously constructed events and their reliabilities considerably. We organised a time on the weekend to meet up and work on the final two events together.
pfr: Leading up to week 8, I was very confident in our groups progress as I believed we had completed our objectives up to this point consistently and successfully. This confidence somewhat diminished during week 8 when we had to construct the action events as I struggled to find time to do this. Up to this point in time I had considered my time management between work, my university load, gym, and social life to be good. I had created a framework which was solid for week-to-week content, however it lacked adaptability. I had noticed this weakness when I failed to fit in adequate time to complete my action events by the week 8 presentation. This lack of flexibility in my schedule led to me failing to construct the tablecloth action event. Whilst I had constructed the zipline component, its quality was somewhat poor due to the lack of time and effort I had put in it. Due to this failure in completing my events. I felt a sense of embarrassment and fear at what the other team members would think of me for failing. The way I had managed my time and resources in week 8 was not adequately done. Knowing this was an issue, I had addressed it in our meeting to see if others felt the same. Group members experienced the same issue and therefore we discussed how to implement a greater amount of project time into our lives. This somewhat relieved my embarrassment and fear from before as I realised the issue was more common than I thought. Implementing a deadline gave me more confidence also, as at least if I failed to complete an event, I could get help from a team member to assist me in completing the event by our week 9 presentation. The zipline event was improved drastically, which I was pleased about. The tablecloth event wasn’t complete as I could not find the materials needed (i.e. a metal slinky), however the team decided to meet up on the following Saturday where we proceeded to complete this event successfully. Going into the week 9 presentation, I felt my confidence in myself, and my team, come back as I was very pleased with the result of that presentation.
learning: I learned from this experience that good time management doesn’t certainly require a consistent framework, but also an adaptable one. My schedule was very good in completing week to week lectures and tutorials however it somewhat crumbles when a project or assessment is introduced. This was evident in week 8, as once an extra responsibility of the project was assigned to me, I struggled to fit in within my schedule. In week 9 I prepared for this, managing my time differently by shifting around when I watched my lectures and allocated certain times to complete my obligations for the RGM project. A good framework to apply to our lives is one that is flexible and doesn’t collapse when more pressure is placed on it. Therefore, this experience has caused me to learn that adaptability is a key component of an improved management of time and resources.

situation: As an electrical engineering student, I was assigned to lead a team of ~20 engineers for a marble machine project. This project involved integrating various subsystems, including mechanical, electrical, and software components, to create a complex, automated marble run. Midway through the project, we encountered a significant conflict between the mechanical and electrical teams. The mechanical team proposed a design that required specific motor specifications, while the electrical team argued that these specifications would exceed our power budget and lead to potential failures in the control system.
task_action: My task was to mediate between the two teams, negotiate a feasible solution, and ensure that the project stayed on track without compromising the integrity of either subsystem. The goal was to reach a consensus that would allow the project to proceed smoothly and meet our performance and safety standards. ACTION: I initiated a series of meetings with representatives from both teams to understand their concerns and requirements thoroughly. During these meetings, I emphasized the importance of open communication and active listening. I encouraged both sides to present their technical justifications and explore alternative solutions collaboratively. To facilitate the negotiation process, I: GATHERED DATA: Collected detailed specifications, performance data, and potential failure points from both teams. PROPOSED COMPROMISES: Suggested possible adjustments to both the mechanical design and the electrical specifications, aiming for a balance that would satisfy both teams. SET PRIORITIES: Helped the teams prioritize critical project requirements, such as power efficiency, performance, and safety, to guide the decision-making process. MEDIATED DISCUSSIONS: Acted as a neutral mediator to ensure that discussions remained focused and productive, steering the conversation towards finding a mutually acceptable solution.
result: Through persistent negotiation and willingness to compromise, we arrived at a solution that involved modifying the motor specifications slightly and optimizing the control algorithms to stay within our power budget. Both teams felt their concerns were addressed, and the final design met all project requirements. This resolution not only maintained the project's timeline but also fostered a collaborative spirit among the team members. The successful integration of the subsystems led to the completion of a fully functional and impressive marble machine, which was well-received during our engineering expo. This experience taught me valuable lessons in conflict resolution, the importance of compromise, and the effectiveness of clear communication in a technical team setting.
pfr: When I was first assigned to lead the marble machine project, I felt a mixture of excitement and apprehension. The excitement stemmed from the opportunity to lead such a significant project, while the apprehension came from the responsibility of managing a team of 20 engineers with diverse expertise and perspectives. The conflict between the mechanical and electrical teams regarding motor specifications was particularly challenging. Initially, it seemed like an insurmountable issue, and I was worried about the potential impact on the project's timeline and overall success. As we delved deeper into the problem, I felt the pressure of balancing technical requirements and maintaining team cohesion. The tension during the initial meetings was palpable, and I sometimes doubted my ability to mediate effectively. However, by encouraging open communication and fostering a collaborative environment, I gradually saw a shift in the team's dynamics. The willingness of both teams to engage in constructive discussions and explore compromises reassured me that we could find a solution. By the end of the negotiation process, I felt a sense of accomplishment and relief. The successful resolution of the conflict not only kept the project on track but also strengthened the team's collaborative spirit. This experience made me realize the importance of empathy, patience, and active listening in conflict resolution.
learning: This experience taught me several valuable lessons. Firstly, I learned the significance of approaching conflicts with an open mind and a willingness to understand different perspectives. By actively listening to both teams and validating their concerns, I was able to facilitate a more productive dialogue. Secondly, I realized the importance of data-driven decision-making. Collecting detailed specifications and performance data from both teams allowed us to make informed compromises that satisfied technical requirements without compromising the project's integrity. Furthermore, I learned that prioritizing critical project requirements, such as power efficiency and safety, can guide the decision-making process and help resolve conflicts. Setting clear priorities ensured that both teams remained focused on the project's overall goals. In the future, I will apply these insights by encouraging open communication, creating an environment where team members feel comfortable expressing their concerns and ideas. Additionally, I will emphasize the importance of using data to inform decisions and explore alternative solutions. Ensuring that the team remains focused on the critical requirements and overall objectives of the project will also be a priority. Through this experience, I have gained a deeper appreciation for the role of effective conflict resolution in team dynamics and project success. I am confident that these skills will be invaluable in my future endeavors as an engineer and team leader.

topic: Visual communications strategy and Communications structure

topic: The transferable skills / employability skill topic I will be reflecting over is the utilisation of brainstorming in order to obtain multiple event ideas for a Rube Goldberg Machine (RGM) and the evaluation of the brainstorming session.
