topic: Perseverance, urgency and will to deliver, resourcefulness and flexibility
situation: The goal of building a Rube Goldberg machine to fill a cup with water was the focus of our ENGG1050 course project. It needed careful preparation and execution. About halfway through the project's duration, a big obstacle presented itself to our crew. Our first design's intricacy was proving to be a barrier, endangering not only the machine's dependability but also our chance to meet the deadline. This insight made it imperative to reevaluate and modify the plan.
task_action: In light of the circumstances, our team decided to convene a number of brainstorming meetings with the goal of streamlining our design without sacrificing the innovative spirit of the project. We understood that each member brought distinct perspectives and abilities to the table, and that it was critical to capitalize on this diversity in order to execute a successful pivot. As part of the action plan, each team member had to critically assess the parts of the machine that they had been allocated, with the aim of determining where possible simplifications may be made. The creation of a buddy system, which pairs team members to offer criticism and ideas for improvement on each other's work, was implemented to support this effort. We also decided on an updated project schedule with checkpoints for finishing the testing and redesign stages, which would allow for plenty of iteration time.
result: We've had success thus far with streamlining our design and introducing a more team-oriented approach to problem-solving. In addition to being more useful, our updated Rube Goldberg machine blueprint maintains the intricacy and ingenuity required to achieve the project's learning goals. Individual component functioning and dependability have increased, according to preliminary testing, which has raised team morale and confidence in our capacity to finish the project on schedule. Even though the project is still in its early stages, our team has made great strides toward overcoming the initial obstacles. The importance of cooperation, flexibility, and effective communication in engineering projects has been reaffirmed by this experience. As we proceed with our efforts towards the final demonstration, we are devoted to preserving a strong and encouraging team.
pfr: We experienced a range of emotions when we realized how complicated our Rube Goldberg machine project was midway through the deadline. When we realized that our ambitious design might have been more of a burden than a demonstration of our ingenuity and technical prowess, there was initially a tangible sense of dissatisfaction and worry among us. This situation reminded me of other group initiatives where practical considerations had been subordinated to enthusiasm at the beginning, resulting in similar issues. But when we all agreed to streamline our strategy, a fresh spirit of purpose and cooperation surfaced. It was fascinating to see how our varied viewpoints—which had previously caused conflict—became our most valuable tool for overcoming this obstacle. The transition from a sense of personal accountability to a collective goal promoted a more supportive team environment.
learning: This has been a really instructive experience that has provided some important insights. First of all, it is impossible to exaggerate the value of flexibility in project management and design. The key to overcoming unforeseen obstacles is not to doggedly stick to an initial vision, but to be willing to simplify and adapt. Secondly, the project emphasized the significance of proficient communication and teamwork among members. More creative and useful ideas were reached when team members were encouraged to speak honestly and to play to one another's individual talents. Thirdly, it emphasized how important it is to establish reasonable benchmarks and goals in order to prevent ambition from getting in the way of reality. I promise to use these lessons going forward in my next endeavors. I'll push for frequent, introspective evaluations of our work, give priority to open and honest communication from the beginning, and balance the creative and practical aspects of such tasks.

situation: In a company I manage, we plan to enter a new global market. We needed to conduct an in-depth analysis of global market trends and economic forces to ensure that our entry strategy would be successful.
task_action: As the project leader, I began by assembling a cross-functional team that included market analysts, economists, and sales specialists. We identified key market trends that needed to be analysed, such as changes in consumer behaviour, competitive dynamics, economic growth forecasts and regulatory policies. Subsequently, we conducted market research and collected a large amount of quantitative and qualitative data. I organised regular team meetings to ensure that everyone was clear on their tasks and able to share the latest research findings. To gain a more comprehensive understanding of the market, we also engaged local consultants and partners to help us understand the economic forces and cultural differences in a given region. I led the team in a SWOT analysis (i.e. Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities and Threats analysis) and developed a series of scenario plans for entry strategies.
result: As a result of these efforts, we were successful in developing detailed market trend maps and economic force maps. These charts helped us identify potential opportunities and risks, and developed a detailed market entry plan for us. Ultimately, we selected an optimal market entry strategy and successfully entered the new market within six months. We achieved 120 per cent of our projected sales target and established solid brand recognition in the new market.
pfr: At the beginning of the assignment to analyse global market trends and economic forces, I felt daunted by the complexity and uncertainty of the task. The volatility of market trends and economic forces made me feel somewhat stressed, especially because these factors are critical to the success of a company entering a new market. However, as the project progressed, I found that dealing with these complexities through a systematic and structured approach was able to significantly reduce my stress and give me more confidence in the viability of the assignment. In working with the team, I learnt the importance of cross-functional teamwork. Each team member brought different expertise and perspectives to the table, which made our analyses more thorough and accurate. Although we were sometimes troubled by differences of opinion during the initial meetings, through continued communication and collaboration we were able to reach a consensus and form a coherent team during the analysis process.
learning: I learnt several important lessons through this experience. Firstly, a systematic and structured approach to analysis is key to tackling complex tasks. By clarifying the problem statement, breaking down tasks, and reporting and reviewing progress on a regular basis, I was able to manage the project more effectively and ensure that we didn't miss any important details. Secondly, I recognise the power of cross-functional teamwork. Team members with different backgrounds and expertise can bring diverse perspectives and innovative solutions. This not only improved the quality of our analyses, but also enhanced team cohesion and collaboration. Finally, I learned the importance of local consultants and partners in global market entry. The ability of external experts to provide localised insights and cultural context is crucial in developing an effective market entry strategy.

situation: During my third year in the mechanical engineering program, our team was tasked with designing a new gearbox using CREO. The project required us to design the gearbox and all the components using CREO, present all the relevant calculations to all the class in regards to the components, manufacture the gearbox and test its functionality. This project was part of our course in the unit mechanical design, and it involved applying both theoretical knowledge and practical skills. Our team consisted of three members, each with different strengths.
task_action: As the project leader, my primary responsibility was to ensure that our team collaborated effectively and met all project deadlines. This involved coordinating the efforts of each team member, managing resources, and addressing any conflicts or challenges that arose during the project. Additionally, I needed to ensure that our design met the specified technical requirements and adhered to safety standards. ACTION: To start things off we organized a meeting where we discussed the project requirements and divided the tasks based on each member's strengths. This task consisted in relation to the shafts, gears and casing. Having said that, I created a detailed project timeline with key milestones and deadlines. Each member was assigned specific responsibilities, such as CAD modeling, stress analysis, material selection, and manufacturing planning according to the selected component. I scheduled regular meetings to review progress, discuss any issues, and reassign tasks if necessary since one of our team member had been operated recently. These meetings helped keep everyone accountable and allowed us to address problems. I also propose the idea to upload all the files in a google drive such as excel files, CREO design, manufacturing drawings and reports so that all the team members could edit and have access to all the material and be aware of the process. When disagreements arose, I heled meetings of all team member's and listen to their perspective and find a compromise. For instance, there was a debate about the gear ratio to use for optimal performance. I encouraged the team to conduct a comparative analysis of different gear ratios and make a data-driven decision. Apart from that there was a disagreement in regards to a team member that could not do his part in the time frame proposed. To solve this issue me and the other student his part and another part was assigned to the person that was absent. For last, I made sure to recognize and celebrate small victories to keep the team motivated. I also provided support when team members faced difficulties, whether technical or personal. For example, the team member that had been operated recently could not model his part in CREO since his hand was immobilized consequently I reach out to him and helped him with his part.
result: As a result of these actions, our team successfully completed the gearbox design project. Our design calculations and CREO models were thorough and accurate, and we successfully manufacture the gearbox . The gearbox was tested and performed efficiently, meeting all the technical specifications and safety standards. Our team received positive feedback from our professors and classmates. But the most important thing was that we were able to identify were and at what weight the gearbox would fail which was at the second shaft in the grove and if the gear box lifted more than 17kg.
pfr: In the beginning, the gearbox design project felt like a distant objective that would be almost impossible to accomplish. The sheer complexity of designing a functional gearbox using CREO, presenting precise calculations, and then manufacturing and testing the prototype was overwhelming. Leading a team with diverse skills and ensuring that we stayed on track added to the pressure. I often felt the weight of responsibility, especially when conflicts arose or when we hit technical roadblocks. However, as we progressed through the project, I began to appreciate the value of systematic planning and collaborative effort. Organizing our tasks, having regular check-ins, and creating a supportive team environment gradually eased my initial anxiety. I found that by breaking down the project into manageable parts and addressing each issue methodically, we were able to make steady progress. Facilitating discussions and resolving conflicts helped me develop my leadership skills and taught me the importance of active listening and empathy. When we successfully tested the gearbox, I felt a deep sense of accomplishment. The positive feedback from our professors and the recognition at the engineering showcase validated our hard work and reinforced my belief in the power of teamwork and structured problem-solving.
learning: From this experience, I have gained several key insights that will shape my future approach to similar projects. Firstly, I learned the importance of breaking down complex tasks into smaller, more manageable components. This not only makes the project seem less overwhelming but also allows for more focused and efficient problem-solving. Secondly, I realized the value of clear communication and regular check-ins. Keeping everyone on the same page and addressing issues promptly can prevent misunderstandings and keep the project moving smoothly. I also learned that conflict, while challenging, can lead to better solutions when approached constructively. Facilitating open discussions and making data-driven decisions helped us navigate disagreements effectively. Thirdly, I gained a deeper appreciation for the iterative nature of design and engineering. Our initial ideas evolved significantly as we tested and refined our prototype like, placing the gears closer to the input and output shafts instead of further. This taught me to be open to feedback and flexible in my approach. In the future, I will place a stronger emphasis on planning and organization from the very beginning of a project. I will ensure that clear goals and timelines are established and that each team member understands their role and responsibilities. I will also foster a team culture where open communication and collaboration are prioritized, and conflicts are seen as opportunities for improvement rather than obstacles. Overall, this experience has reinforced my belief in the importance of structured, merit-based decision-making and the power of effective teamwork. By applying these lessons, I am confident that I will be better equipped to lead successful projects in the future.

situation: In my previous unit, ENGG2000/3000, students were assigned to a particular group within a team depending on their specialization (three groups: Structures, Motions, and Communications). As a mechanical student, I was placed in the ‘Structures’ group with four other civil/mechanical students. In my structures group, there were two students in their third year, and three second-year students (including me). For each of the three groups in a team, the third-year students were assigned as leaders of their group. As a result, we had two leaders for our group who were responsible for allocating roles and responsibilities out to the team. They were also responsible for preparing an agenda for each week’s SGTA and any meetings outside of class times. They also kept in regular contact with the tutors and unit convenors and importantly had constant contact with the other group leaders to ensure all groups were staying on track and sticking to deadlines. However, about week 5 our third-year students had to leave temporarily from university. One leader needed an important surgery and had to stay at the hospital for several weeks. The other leader had to go emergency trip overseas to see his family. As a result, we had no group leader so I filled the role of group leader and its associated responsibilities.
task_action: As a temporary group leader, I had to initially approach the other two group leaders (Communications and Motions) and explain the situation to them about the two third years who had to leave temporarily. I explained that they should direct all their messages to me and add me to the leaders’ group chat on both WhatsApp and Discord. In the weeks that followed I would send regular weekly update requests to ensure our team was meeting deadlines and staying on track with the schedule. I would at least once a week contact our group members individually and ask how they were doing their sections and if they needed any help or support. Also, as our group was down by two, me and the rest of the group had to handle more tasks to compensate for the reduced manpower. I had to prepare the team's agenda an extra week or two ahead to ensure we had sufficient time to complete the tasks. Further, I requested our group to conduct meetings (10-15 minutes briefly on Zoom 2 days after the SGTA) to discuss problems we might be having and get on top of it as soon as possible. Otherwise, members with issues would have to wait until the next SGTA to get proper assistance. Another aspect of being a team leader meant that I had to learn about everyone’s strengths and weaknesses. This was done by constantly asking questions to members about how they would do a certain task (their suggested approach would highlight their level of understanding and demonstrate if they would struggle with that task and might need assistance) or had a preference (this would signal strength). Being an effective communicator was very important in being able to organize tasks and assign them to members with minimal hiccups, streamlining the process of the project. Additionally, I would send weekly summarized text to the on-leave third-year members of the tasks done that week and the agenda for next week. This would not only keep them posted but also allow them to remind me of tasks that I may have neglected.
result: By the time the third-year students returned to class, we had almost completed the marble machine. They were updated about the progress the team had made and what was remaining on the to-do list. The marble cube was built but the testing needed to be conducted and documented as well as some aesthetic additions to the cube. My time as group leader was very important in our progress. My leadership kept us on track, and we were able to successfully finish the entire cube promptly. If I had not filled in for the group leader, there was a considerable chance of our team not completing the cube in time. My effective communication with the other group leaders allowed for a smooth transition without many disruptions.
pfr: Initially, I felt that I was not competent or ready to become a group leader so abruptly as it was such a substantial task given that I was never a group leader for a project of this magnitude. I thought that it required a personality who is naturally sociable, communicative, and approachable. I consider myself to be the opposite of these things. I am normally a quiet, shy, and conservative person who does not overly interact with the other students around me. As a result, being just a group member and being assigned tasks by the group leader was ideal and comfortable for me. Becoming a group leader abruptly caused considerable discomfort and anxiety. Simultaneously, as our original leaders had to leave, the necessity to fill and get the job done pushed me into this uncomfortable position. I had to get used to feeling uncomfortable and putting myself out there constantly communicating with tutors, unit convenors, workshop technicians, and all the members of the team. By the end, feelings of discomfort had subsided, and I had become accustomed to the roles and responsibilities of being a leader.
learning: Through this, it was clear that being an effective team leader is an immense responsibility that requires a lot of time and effort compared to a regular group member. By being put in a position of leadership abruptly, it highlighted that anyone could become a successful leader. Extroverted and open personalities do have a natural inclination towards being a leader as it requires constant and frequent communication with other people (requires a lot of soft social skills). Introverted people like me can also become effective leaders with consistent effort. Even though it is an uncomfortable position in the beginning, you will get more accustomed to interacting with people. With enough practice and time, team leadership is a skill that can be acquired by anyone with the right attitude and effort.

topic: Equity and diversity in leadership and managment
situation: During this semester, I was involved in a project where our team was tasked with designing a parking structure for a new mixed-use development in an urban area. The project required us to consider not only the technical aspects of the design but also to ensure that it addressed equity and diversity in its leadership and management approach. Our team consisted of members from diverse backgrounds, which added a layer of complexity in terms of communication and decision-making.
task_action: Our main task was to ensure that the parking structure would be accessible and accommodating to all users, including those from marginalised groups. This required us to incorporate features such as wheelchair-accessible parking spots, clear signage in multiple languages, and amenities that catered to various needs and preferences. Additionally, we aimed to create a leadership structure within our team that promoted equal participation and leveraged the diverse perspectives of all team members. ACTION: To address these challenges, I initiated several actions: * FORMING INCLUSIVE COMMITTEES: I suggested forming subcommittees within our team focused on specific aspects of the project (e.g., accessibility, safety, sustainability). Each subcommittee was led by a member with relevant expertise or interest, ensuring diverse leadership. * CONDUCTING USER SURVEYS: We designed and distributed surveys to gather input from potential users of the parking structure, including people with disabilities, non-native speakers, and various age groups. This helped us understand their needs and preferences, which informed our design decisions. * FACILITATING OPEN DISCUSSIONS: I organized regular meetings where all team members could voice their opinions and contribute ideas. These meetings were structured to ensure that quieter team members had an equal opportunity to participate. * IMPLEMENTING FEEDBACK MECHANISMS: We established a system for collecting and integrating feedback from both our team and community stakeholders. This iterative process ensured that our design remained responsive to the needs of all potential users.
result: The result of these actions was a well-rounded and inclusive parking structure design that received positive feedback from both the community and our faculty advisors. Specifically: * ENHANCED ACCESSIBILITY: The design included ample wheelchair-accessible parking spots, ramps, and braille signage, making it easy for differently-abled individuals to navigate. * MULTILINGUAL SIGNAGE: Clear signage in multiple languages was incorporated to accommodate non-native speakers. * POSITIVE TEAM DYNAMICS: The inclusive leadership approach led to high team morale and effective collaboration, with each member feeling valued and heard. * RECOGNITION AND LEARNING: Our project was highlighted as a model for incorporating equity and diversity in engineering projects, and I personally gained valuable skills in inclusive leadership and project management. This experience underscored the importance of equity and diversity in engineering leadership and management. It demonstrated that when diverse perspectives are actively included, the outcomes are not only more innovative but also more relevant and beneficial to the community.
pfr: When we first received the task of designing a parking structure as a group we tried to focus on equity and diversity as well, I felt a mix of excitement and anxiety as I am an international student myself. The challenge seemed a little bit overwhelming as we had to deal with the technical complexities combined with the need to consider diverse user needs. Initially, I was concerned about how we could effectively integrate the principles of equity and diversity into a project that was traditionally seen through a purely functional and technical views As we progressed, however, relieved as our systematic approaches and inclusive practices were paying off. Collaborating with team members from diverse backgrounds was enlightening, as it brought forward perspectives and solutions I hadn’t considered before. Organizing inclusive discussions and facilitating feedback mechanisms not only improved our design but also fostered a sense of unity and mutual respect within the team. *
learning: This experience has been profoundly educational in several ways. Firstly, I learned that incorporating equity and diversity into engineering projects is not only possible but also enhances the overall outcome. By actively seeking input from diverse users and team members, we were able to create a more comprehensive and user-friendly design. This process taught me the importance of empathy and active listening in engineering – understanding the real needs of users leads to better solutions. Secondly, I realized the value of structured and inclusive decision-making. Forming subcommittees and organizing regular open discussions ensured that all voices were heard, and this inclusivity resulted in a more robust and well-rounded project. Moving forward, I will continue to advocate for and implement these practices in future projects. I now understand that leadership is not just about directing but also about creating an environment where everyone feels valued and empowered to contribute. Finally, this project highlighted the importance of adaptability and continuous learning. The feedback loops we established allowed us to refine our design continuously, ensuring it remained aligned with user needs and expectations. This approach of continuous improvement is something I will carry forward, always remaining open to feedback and willing to make necessary adjustments to achieve the best possible outcomes. In future projects, I will prioritize establishing clear, inclusive processes from the start, ensuring that all team members and stakeholders have a voice. I will also continue to seek out and incorporate diverse perspectives, recognizing that these are crucial to developing solutions that are equitable, innovative, and effective. This experience has fundamentally shifted my approach to engineering design and leadership, making me a more empathetic, inclusive, and more effective.

situation: As part of ENGG1050, the students have been tasked with building a functioning Rube-Goldberg Machine (RGM) to perform a simple task. The machine is broken up into a number of sections, depending on the number of people in the group, so that each member is tasked with designing and constructing part of the contraption. There are a number of aims associated with this project, one of which is that the RGM must be reliable.
task_action: To ensure the RGM that I am a part of is reliable, my group has set a minimum standard that each component of each section must perform as required 9/10 times. If a component can not be modified to meet this degree of reliability, it must be removed from the machine and replaced with another, more reliable, action event. This guarantees that the machine as a whole is at least 90% reliable. ACTION: To meet this standard of reliability, each member of the group conducted testing of every component of their section 3 times. Each test consisted of 10 runs of the relevant event. The first test was conducted before any optimisation changes had been made. The second was conducted after making one adjustment to the component, and the third was conducted after all possible optimisation improvements were implemented. The number of times the action event was successful in each test was recorded and tabulated to make a graph of the change in reliability.
result: As a result of this rigorous testing approach, data was produced that greatly influenced the decision to keep or replace components in each section of the RGM. In each successive test for every group member, the reliability increased. In all but two components, the optimisation changes made allowed the event to function as intended at least 9/10 times. The data for the two components that did not reach 90% reliability drove us to replace these events. Further testing was conducted on the new actions to determine they performed at least 9/10 times. Overall, the RGM is now proven to be 90% reliable.
pfr: When we made the decision to only keep components that were 90% reliable after completing the optimisation process, I felt relieved. I was worried that tough conversations would have to be had with group members who wanted to keep events in their section that were not reliable. I was stressed that I would have to confront team members, who I had now become friends with, so the decision to follow what the tests communicated was very welcome by me. By letting the data drive our decision making, everyone knew that the choices made were practical rather than personal.
learning: From this situation I have learned that implementing data driven decision making is a great way to remove personal feelings from a situation and prevent individuals from feeling targeted. When everyone is aware that it is only numbers and statistics that influence the choices made, no one is made to feel hard done by when it comes time to make tough decisions. Furthermore, this way of reaching conclusions makes it easier to determine the best next step. As we all know, numbers do not lie. In future scenarios, I will remember what I have learned from this project, and be sure to implement numerical standards wherever possible to ease and destress the decision making process.

Analysed the Impact: Assessed how the misalignment affected the staircase's strength and the overall structure. 3. Redesigned the Rebar Layout: Adjusted the rebar placement and reinforced critical areas. 4. Implemented Checks: Established a step-by-step verification system for rebar alignment during installation.
result: The staircase rebar was realigned correctly, ensuring its strength and safety. The project stayed on schedule and the new check system improved our workflow, reducing the risk of similar problems in the future. This holistic approach ensured the staircase was built to last and highlighted the importance of considering all aspects of a project when solving problems.
pfr: When we found out the rebar for the staircase was off, I felt pretty stressed. Knowing it was a safety risk and needed a quick fix was overwhelming. But working with my team and the engineers made me feel more confident. It reminded me how important it is to look at the whole picture in construction.
learning: I learned that thinking about everything together is really important. By working as a team, checking how everything fits together, and double-checking our work, we fixed the problem and made our process better. This experience showed me the value of planning ahead and working together, which I'll use in all my future projects.

situation: In week 2, the group had to create several conceptual designs to create a basic understanding of what we would like to include for our "Tea of Things" machine.
task_action: Brainstorming initial ideas and conducting background research. Starting with familiarising ourselves with everyone's engineering major and what ideas they included for their tea machine, a list of important functions was created based on the client's needs. This was analysed from last week's work where we filtered through different questions and how the client responded to each of them. We then took a short time apart to generate several simple concepts, including at least one important function and listing their key components. It is important that no idea was scrapped or deemed as "bad".* This is where the brainstorming session had gone awry. Instead of presenting ideas we just kept them to ourselves and had others say what was interesting about each of them, giving shallow feedback.* For the rest of the session, we conducted background research for our separate ideas or fleshed out the conceptual design that was most liked. I decided to do research on the different processes of making tea and the anatomy of a coffee machine to see if there was a way that I could bridge these two designs together.
result: In the end, I was able to get a rough idea of what my peers valued as important for their tea machines. I was able to get some feedback on three of my initial concept designs a "hopper system", a "spin/stirring mechanism", and a "teabag dunking arm". I found that the hopper system was my most popular design as it was a good delivery system that bridges gaps between other designs. From this as a launching point, I researched different tea-making processes and how a simple coffee machine works. I landed on tea infusion which ditches the need for single-use tea bags and allows the use of loose tea leaves. Different designs use mesh to contain or plunge the leaves so they may release their flavours more efficiently as they are allowed to expand. This, and other useful information, is found on Reddit under r/tea. I also did some research on how coffee machines and coffee pods worked and found out that for the best blends, water is distributed evenly through the cross-sectional area of coffee pods. This is irrelevant to tea all that is needed is hot water to release flavour from tea leaves. Using information from this subreddit, I was able to learn that loose tea leaves provide the most variety of tea flavours and help reduce waste by avoiding the use of single-use paper tea bags.
pfr: The first stages of this task were difficult to start because people in my table group consisted of smaller friend groups that wanted to keep to themselves, thus reducing the flow of ideas between the table as a whole. I believe that this is due to feeling insecure about the thoughts of others. As we got more comfortable with each other, we were able to start on more meaningful work by sharing what we thought were important design parameters and providing feedback on our several conceptual designs. However, after giving feedback, everyone was left to their own devices as the discussion died down, resulting the the rest of the SGTA session being individual work. Nevertheless, the table group got a lot more done than I initially thought and was proud of my effort in leading meaningful group discussion. Because I was able to find a whole community about making tea on Reddit, I was able to think more creatively as I had more sources of information and opinions from other people to draw from. I was able to connect the dots from one design and apply it to the "Tea of Things" system. Additionally, I found it rewarding that I shared my findings about tea-making methods on the internet because, within the next week, someone from that old table group had begun asking me about the link so they could read further.
learning: By stating before brainstorming that "no ideas are bad or dumb.", I found that even the most shy in our group were willing to share their concept designs and get feedback for that session. I found that by being an active member of the group, I was able to steer discussions and communicate important ideas, concepts and sources for research for everyone's benefit. Because of this, I have found value in setting the group environment to communicate possibilities more fluidly and without the restraint of turning down so-called "bad" ideas. Even if ideas are shortsighted, important lessons can be drawn from that. Additionally, when discussion died down and I started doing individual work, researching the basic ideas of tea and coffee allowed me to think more creatively as I drew ideas from more sources. In future, I should spend some time to pause and research the key ideas and methods on how to make something and present my findings to others so they may draw more ideas from me or the information that I processed.

situation: In my ENGG2050 Engineering Design unit I explored various critical topics, one of which was "Ethics, Integrity, and Social Responsibility". A significant part of this exploration involved assessing real world scenarios where these principles were either upheld or violated. For the Case Study 1 assessment I was tasked to examine the Firestone 500 tires controversy. This case involved the manufacturing and sale of the Firestone 500 tire, which were found to be defective. Despite being aware of the defects, Firestone continued to sell these tires to the public and maximise profits. This led to numerous accidents, causing injuries and fatalities.
task_action: The primary task was to analyse the ethical breaches in the Firestone 500 case, understand the implications of these breaches on public safety and corporate responsibility, and propose solutions or actions that could have mitigated or prevented the negative outcomes. I was required to demonstrate my understanding of the ethical principles involved and apply ethical frameworks to evaluate Firestone's decisions and actions. ACTIONS: To tackle this task I followed a structured approach to breakdown, understand and analyse the situation entirely. 1. Research and information gathering: I started by researching the Firestone 500 case extensively. This involved reviewing supplied and external sources for reports, articles, and legal documents to gather a comprehensive understanding and adequate knowledge about the defects, the companys knowledge of these issues, and the subsequent impact on consumers. 2. Ethical analysis: I applied ethical frameworks to analyse Firestone's decisions. I evaluated the actions from the perspectives of the company and its shareholders, and the public/consumer perspective, while considering the consequences, duties and moral principles involves. 3. Identification of ethical breaches: I identified specific points where Firestone's actions violated ethical principles. key Breaches includes prioritising profits over safety, failing to disclose known defects and ignoring customer reports of tire failures. 4. Proposing solutions: I proposed several actions that could have been taken to address the situation ethically. These included issuing a recall as soon as the defects were identifies, transparently communicating with consumers about the risks, and implementing more rigorous quality control testing.
result: The outcomes of this reflective and analytical process was complex and had multiple aspects to consider. The key outcomes I received was: 1. Deeper understanding: I developed a deeper understanding of the critical role that ethics, integrity, and social responsibility play in engineering practices. This understanding was not just theoretical but grounded by real world implications and consequences. 2. Enhanced analytical skills: Through the detailed analysis of the Firestone case, my ability to critically evaluate corporate actions from an ethical standpoint improved significantly. I learned to apply ethical frameworks effectively to real world scenarios. 3. Awareness of impact: The task highlighted the importance of considering the broader impact of engineering decisions on society. It shows how lapses in ethical judgement can lead to severe consequences, both for public safety and corporate reputation. 4. Commitment to ethical practices: This case study reinforced my commitment to upholding ethical standards in my future engineering career. It served as a reminder that the welfare of the public should always take precedence over financial incentives. The case study 1 assessment on the Firestone 500 tire controversy was a profound learning experience that emphasised the significance of ethics. integrity, and social responsibility in engineering. By reflecting on this case, I gained valuable insights into the ethical dilemmas that engineers may face and the importance of making principled decisions to ensure the safety and well-being of society.
pfr: Reflecting on this case evoked a mix of emotions. Initially, I felt a sense of disbelief and frustation. It was difficult to comprehend that a company could knowingly endanger lives for financial gain. As i delve deeper, these feelings shifted towards a somber understanding of the gravity of ethical lapses, not just in engineering but the world as a whole, as financial stimulation is always the goal for companies and they will try to achieve it by any means often. There was also a strong sense of responsibility and determination to not only learn from this case study but to ensure such mistakes are not repeated in my future career.
learning: Looking back I realise how significant this case study was in shaping my understanding of professional ethics. This process of researching, analysing and discussing the Firestone 500 case highlighted the severe consequences of neglecting ethical considerations. It was an eye-opener to the real world impact of engineering decisions and showed the importance of maintaining integrity and social responsibility. After studying the methods of testing and seeing how thorough it can be, it was clear that Firestone cut some corners when it came to their testing. I was able to recognise that they could have explored more preventative strategies to foster an ethical corporate culture. This experience taught me several important lessons. It reaffirmed the necessity of always putting public safety above all else in engineering decisions. it also highlighted the importance of transparency and accountability in corporate practices. The Firestone case made it clear that ethical lapses not only harm individuals but also tarnish the reputation and sustainability of the company. I learned the value of ethical frameworks in guiding decision making processes by applying ethical frameworks to provide a structured way to evaluate the actions of Firestone and derive ethical solutions. If I were to encounter a similar situation in the future, I would advocate for immediate action upon discovering any defects or potential hazards, prioritising transparency with stakeholders. I would also push for the implementation of comprehensive quality control measures and ethical training programs within the organisation to prevent such issues from arising. This experience has instilled in me the importance of continuous self reflection and ethical vigilance. I now understand that maintaining integrity and social responsibility in an ongoing process that requires constant attention and commitment. Moving forward I will ensure the following: 1. Prioritise ethical decision making:in any professional role i will ensure that all decisions are made with a primary focus on safety, transparency and integrity. 2. Advocate for ethical practices: I will actively promote and support ethical practices within any organisation I am part of, including advocating for robust ethical training programs and stringent quality control procedures. 3. Engage in continuous learning: I will stay informed about ethical standards and the best practices in engineering, regularly revisiting and reflecting on real world cases to enhance my understanding. 4. Develop ethical leadership skills: I will work on developing my leadership skills that emphasise decision making and social responsibility, aiming to inspire and influence others to uphold these values.

situation: During this semester, I was given the task of creating an IOT tea maker for a client, who had only a vague idea of what they wanted. This task was an individual task, but we were informed that working collaboratively would increase our chances at being successful in this task.
task_action: The task was to define the client's needs and transform their vague requirements into a new, innovative design. The goal was to design an IOT tea maker using core engineering principles that met the client's expectations. The client's requirements included internet-based access, the ability to share tea designs and recipes with friends, and scheduling tea preparation to their preferences, and more. Effective communication was crucial between my group of fellow engineering students, as we all belonged to different disciplines of engineering, We could all bounce ideas off of each other that aligned with our discipline, and that would allow everyone else to gain a new perspective on how to tackle this task. This ensured a cohesive and comprehensive design of the IOT Tea Maker. To Address this challenge, I suggested we all join a google Doc where we would be able to write down our ideas without being spoken over or ignored, and at the end we could all talk through our ideas and explain our thought process. By doing this, we had thought of numerous ideas, which we would then evaluate based on a criteria of complexity, how well it would service the customer and how feasible it would be. I actively communicated with the group to refine these ideas, ensuring that each concept was thoroughly discussed and analysed. I also made sure that everyone felt included and that no one's ideas were being put on the back burner.
result: Through successful communication with engineering students from different disciplines, we significantly enhanced our individual designs of the IOT tea maker. My final design incorporated a user-friendly interface, automated brewing schedules, and connectivity features that allowed users to control the tea maker via a smartphone app. This collaborative approach not only improved the design quality but also ensured that the final product met the client's needs comprehensively.
pfr: Initially, the task of creating an IOT tea maker for a client who had such vague requirements felt overwhelming. The uncertainty around the client's needs and the complexity of integrating various unknown engineering principles added to this fear that I will not be able to successfully complete this task to the best of my capabilities. For future projects, I will aim to openly communicate with others and promote inclusivity, encouraging broad and unique ideas to be discussed. Additionally, I can work on improving my conflict resolution skills, handling differing opinions in a respectful manner, and maintaining a positive work environment where everyone feels safe. Overall, the ability to effectively communicate within a group has allowed me to appreciate the power of teamwork and build my communication skills, focusing on maintaining mutual respect within the group. These skills can be carried into my future prospects, in terms of group projects and working in a professional environment.

situation: During a group work last month in the ENGG2050 course, we were tasked with creating a comprehensive design document and presenting our final design, including testing plans, to the class. This required clear, precise, and professional written communication to ensure all aspects of our project were effectively conveyed. Our goal was to compile the contributions of multiple team members into a single, cohesive document and prepare a presentation that accurately represented our work.

Additionally, I had to prepare a section on testing and alternatives, detailing the selection methodology for COTS components and developing a comprehensive testing plan for our system. By the end of the project, I was proud of our collective achievement and grateful for the opportunity to enhance my leadership and communication skills.
learning: Through this experience, I learned the critical importance of structured and clear written communication in engineering projects. situation: In my last project, our customer service department faced a major pain point in the form of long customer complaint handling times, which led to lower customer satisfaction and customer churn. The root cause of the problem was the complexity of the complaint handling process and the lack of interdepartmental collaboration.
task_action: As a project manager, I was tasked with leading a cross-departmental team to re-engineer the complaint handling process in order to reduce handling time and increase customer satisfaction. This included identifying bottlenecks in the process, designing the new process, implementing improvements and monitoring the results. ACTION: Firstly, I organised a series of workshops bringing together key people from different departments to identify bottlenecks in the current process through process mapping techniques. We leveraged the expertise of cross-functional teams to streamline processes using the LEAN methodology and introduced automation tools to speed up certain aspects of the process. In addition, I ensured improved communication through regular cross-departmental meetings and created a shared complaint handling dashboard to track complaint status and KPIs in real time.
result: These improvements significantly increased processing efficiency, reducing the average complaint processing time from 5 days to 2 days. In addition, a customer satisfaction survey showed an increase in satisfaction score from 6.5 before the improvements to 8.2. Through this project, we not only solved a specific business pain point, but also enhanced interdepartmental collaboration and laid the foundation for future projects.
pfr: I initially felt both nervous and excited when faced with a customer service pain point. Nervous because I knew that the success or failure of the project would have a direct impact on the company's reputation and customer satisfaction, and excited because I had the opportunity to lead a challenging cross-functional project. Throughout the process, I felt a great sense of responsibility, as any wrong decision could lead to the failure of the project. By working closely with different departments, I learnt the importance of communication and collaboration, and how to solve complex problems by working together. This experience taught me that it is vital to stay calm and focused even under pressure.
learning: I learnt several key lessons through this experience. First, identifying and solving pain points requires a systematic approach and the collective wisdom of the team. Streamlining processes is not just about removing redundant steps, but requires a deep understanding of each part of the process and its impact on the end result. Second, the introduction of technology and tools to improve efficiency needs to be carefully considered to ensure that they are actually solving problems rather than adding new levels of complexity. Finally, cross-departmental collaboration is key to solving pain points within a company, and effective communication is its foundation. Moving forward, I will place greater emphasis on establishing and maintaining cross-departmental communication channels to ensure that all relevant parties contribute to problem resolution. In addition, I have recognised the importance of maintaining a positive team atmosphere and encouraging innovative thinking as a leader in a project. Through this reflection, I realise that my leadership style and decision-making process have been enhanced and I see these experiences as valuable assets for future challenges.

situation: During my tenure as an electrical engineer, the company undertook a critical project involving the design and implementation of an automated control system for improving the efficiency and output of a manufacturing line. The project faced tight deadlines and high performance requirements. Early in the project, we encountered a major challenge: the existing control system was unable to meet the new performance targets and was costly to upgrade.
task_action: As the lead electrical engineer on the project, I was tasked with leading a team to design a solution that would meet the performance requirements while staying within budget. After several iterations and tests, we devised a set of improvements, including the use of new sensor technology and updated control algorithms to improve the system's responsiveness and accuracy.
result: With these improvements, our control system successfully met performance requirements while staying within budget. The project was completed ahead of schedule, resulting in a 25% increase in line efficiency and a reduction in downtime due to equipment failure. In addition, the design of our solution enhanced the scalability of the system, facilitating future upgrades. pfr: I felt both nervous and excited when faced with this project. Nervous because the challenges we faced were real, with very specific performance goals and strict budget constraints. I was aware that any wrong decision could lead to project failure, with potential negative consequences for the company and my career. learning: The most important lesson I learned was that the power of cross-departmental collaboration is key to solving complex engineering problems. I plan to be more proactive in communicating with team members and stakeholders on future projects to ensure that everyone has a clear understanding of the project's goals, schedule, and potential issues. Lastly, I learnt from this experience that it is important to remain calm and focused even in the face of pressure and challenges. This not only helps me to make more informed decisions, but also helps to maintain the morale and motivation of the team. Through this reflection, I have gained a deeper understanding that as electrical engineers, we need to possess not only deep technical knowledge and skills, but also excellent leadership and cross-disciplinary collaboration skills. This experience not only deepened my professional knowledge, but also gave me a deeper understanding and respect for my role as an engineer and a leader.

pfr: I felt both excited and nervous while working on this community volunteer project.
