This process made me realise that as a team leader, it is important to focus not only on the end goal of the project, but also on every detail of the process. In particular, I realised that integrity is not only a reflection of personal qualities, but also a key factor for team success. During the project, whenever we faced difficulties and challenges, I would recall our original intention and social responsibility, which became my motivation to move forward.
learning: I learnt several key insights from this experience. First, transparency and integrity are the cornerstones of earning the trust and support of our community. By making public the progress of our fundraising activities and financial reports, we not only enhanced the transparency of our project, but also built trust with community members. Second, teamwork and communication are crucial when facing complex tasks. Ensuring that each team member understands their roles and responsibilities can effectively improve team efficiency and project outcomes. Lastly, I realise that taking up social responsibility is not an easy task; it requires patience, perseverance and a sense of responsibility. HOW I WILL ACT DIFFERENTLY IN THE FUTURE: In future projects, I will further strengthen the principles of transparency and integrity. This includes setting clear communication plans and transparency standards from the start of a project, as well as establishing stricter financial monitoring and reporting mechanisms. At the same time, I will also pay more attention to team building and training to ensure that each member understands and assumes his or her social responsibility, so as to enhance the effectiveness of the team as a whole and the impact of the project. Through this reflection, I have become more convinced that adhering to the principles of ethics, integrity and social responsibility in any endeavour is the key to achieving long-term success.

topic: Perseverance, urgency and will to deliver, resourcefulness and flexibility
situation: I'm taking part in a group project in my third year of mechanical engineering degree that involves designing and constructing a gearbox for a competition at the university. We are a three-person team, and this assignment is a vital part of our coursework. Given the short turnaround time and the fact that none of us had any prior expertise designing gearboxes, the problem is substantial.
task_action: Designing and building a working gearbox that could show durability and efficiency under a range of loads was our job. For the competition, we had to follow certain design guidelines and incorporate our gearbox into a bigger mechanical system. Due to time and budget restrictions, the task's intricacy required a thorough grasp of gear ratios, material selection, and assembly processes. Our group used a calculated strategy to address this problem. We started by breaking the project up into smaller, more doable jobs according to our unique skills and interests. In order to maximize our gearbox layout, I took the initiative to investigate gear design concepts and simulation tools. My partners concentrated on locating supplies, fabricating parts, and carrying out practical testing in the meantime. We met on a regular basis to discuss issues, exchange updates, and modify our plans in light of new information and disappointments. We were transparent in our communication and flexible in our design modifications in response to feedback and testing conducted in the real world.
result: Our group's perseverance and efforts are paying off. Even with unanticipated obstacles like wrong calculations, we are manage to design a gearbox that promises to outperform our first performance estimates. In addition, the project is teaching us important lessons about problem-solving, collaboration, and project management. This experience showcases clear how crucial it is to be persistent, quick thinking, and flexible in order to accomplish challenging engineering goals in cooperative settings and under pressure.
pfr: Starting the task of building a gearbox with my group felt a bit like taking a leap into something unknown at first. Given that none of us had any experience with designing gearboxes, the task appeared quite difficult. The impending deadline added to the pressure we were under. But as we began to approach the issue carefully and break it down into manageable pieces, my feelings of uneasiness started to give way to a feeling of purpose and determination. We were able to work together to overcome the complexity, and as a result, every phase of the decision-making process became more organized and clear. Seeing our group come together and agree on design decisions based on project objectives and established merits was comforting.
learning: I now have a clearer understanding of the value of well-organized decision-making and productive teamwork as a result of this experience. Our strategy, in which choices were taken on the basis of objective merits and careful evaluation of limitations, worked well to ensure group consensus and hastened our development. I discovered that there is rarely a "best design" that works for all difficult engineering projects; instead, a design's efficacy is greatly influenced by the particular problem statement and the restrictions that go along with it. My viewpoint on project management and problem-solving has expanded as a result of this insight. I plan to put what I've learned into practice by giving structured decision-making procedures top priority in any future group projects. I think it's important to have specific goals, define evaluation standards, and encourage candid communication among team members. Adopting this strategy, in my opinion, will enable us to make decisions more quickly and effectively—even when faced with difficult projects. This experience has shown how crucial it is to have persistence, flexibility, and teamwork in order to overcome challenges and accomplish challenging engineering goals.

situation: During one of our weekly workshops, we chose from a database of collected pain points people had around the university. I chose a pain point that many shared, university parking. This pain point had been coming from varying participants at the uni such as students AND tutors. Complaints were made about the oversized expensive staff parking and overcrowded student parking.
task_action: My task was to first create some base software solution, administrative solution and hardware solutions to address this pain point. To accomplish this, I also discussed with other's on my table for ideas on how they would solve the solution considering some of them related to this pain point. Additionally, I created two customer personas that would both suffer from different aspects of the pain point, i.e. one staff one student persona. These persona's would be viable customers for a product solution to this pain point. Moreover, to further detail and develop a solution, we identified key stakeholders in this solution and their concerns. This included those who would have an affect from all aspects of the solution, such as students, tutors, administrators, IT staff, and the marketing team. Finally, using my preferred solution, being a parking allocation app that would track occupancy in real-time and provide reserved parking incentive schemes. I tasked myself with creating a KVP in which I would aim to describe how my chosen solution appeals to key stakeholders and the two personas made earlier.
result: The outcome of this workshop was the development of a hypothetical solution to the parking situation pain point experienced by those at uni. This solution aimed to minimise parking imbalances and improve campus mobility by providing a parking management solution. I was able to successfully communicate with those at my table to further detail specifics about the pain in order to give a more detailed persona. This allowed me to more accurately cater my app using feedback. As a result, my parking management solution was refined further to specified feedback and allowed me to gauge my target customers and stakeholder within the solution, giving guidance for future development.
pfr: As all weekly workshops, the initial task to get through is always a bit daunting and overwhelming. This workshop especially was largely overwhelming due to the complexity and broad impact of the pain point I chose. It was clear that any solution would have to address the concerns of stakeholders within this pain point, making sure I would design a solution that would cover all bases. The task of creating personas and developing a solution put me a bit out of comfort zone. This was mainly due to the fact that I had to actively engage with stakeholders, like people on my table, and gather enough useful information to help base my response around. The communicative nature of the task, as well as the complex decision-making in designing such a solution proved both a challenge and an activity to grow my skills. It pushed me to gather solution outside my comfort zone, effectively gathering wider and more in-depth feedback to base my solution around.
learning: This process of gathering information through varying aspects taught me some valuable lessons. The importance of communication in research and task development. Even if its stepping outside your comfort zone, communication is an effective way of gather more information than just research a topic online. By engaging in a conversation with someone, you get a more real understanding on a pain point and how people personally feel about a subject rather than reading documented research on a website. Moreover, I was able to understand the significance of each stakeholder and how they play a part in the solution, even ones that don't seem obvious. This experience has shaped my understanding and approach to attacking a problem provided. Even though it was a weekly workshop, it allowed me to understand the effectiveness of communication in solving pain points, and understanding all stakeholders at play.

situation: In our engineering CAD design class, we were tasked with creating a CAD model for a new type of drone capable of extended flight times and then presenting our design process and final model to the class. My team, consisting of five members, had diverse ideas about the drone's design, leading to initial disagreements on the direction we should take.
task_action: My role involved coordinating our team's efforts to merge our individual design ideas into a cohesive CAD model and then preparing a compelling oral presentation that showcased our design process, challenges, and the innovative features of our drone. The ultimate goal was to communicate our project's value effectively and demonstrate our collaborative and technical skills. ACTION: To streamline our efforts, I organized several brainstorming sessions where each member could pitch their design ideas. We discussed potential features, materials, and technologies that could enhance our drone's flight time. After consolidating our ideas, we divided the work based on individual strengths—two members focused on the aerodynamics in the CAD software, two worked on the presentation visuals and script, and I oversaw the entire project to ensure cohesion and adherence to our timeline. Together, we iterated on our CAD model, integrating feedback from practice presentations in front of peers.
result: Our collaborative approach resulted in a highly innovative drone design, featuring lightweight materials and an aerodynamic shape that significantly extended flight times. The oral presentation was well-received by our classmates and instructors, highlighting not only the technical aspects of our design but also our team's ability to work together, solve problems, and communicate effectively. Our project was praised for its clear presentation, innovative design, and the comprehensive understanding of CAD tools we demonstrated. This experience not only solidified my skills in CAD design and teamwork but also underscored the importance of communication in engineering projects.
pfr: When we first embarked on the CAD design project for the new drone, I felt a mixture of excitement and apprehension. The excitement stemmed from the opportunity to apply my skills and creativity to something tangible and potentially groundbreaking. However, apprehension crept in due to the diverse opinions within the team on the direction of the project. Initially, the differing viewpoints led to some frustration, as it seemed challenging to find a common ground. The task ahead appeared formidable, not because of the complexity of the design itself but due to the need to unify our team's vision. Throughout the brainstorming sessions and collaboration, however, I discovered the value in each team member's perspective, realizing that our diversity was not a barrier but a strength that enriched our final design.
learning: The experience taught me several key lessons about teamwork, communication, and problem-solving in design projects. Firstly, I learned the importance of open communication and active listening. By truly listening to and considering each idea, we were able to integrate the best aspects of each proposal, leading to a more innovative and comprehensive design. This process underscored the notion that great ideas can come from anywhere, and a collaborative approach can harness these ideas into a coherent and effective solution. Moreover, I gained insight into the significance of flexibility and adaptability in teamwork. Rather than clinging to my initial ideas, I learned to be flexible, adapting my contributions to better fit the evolving design and team needs. This adaptability was crucial in overcoming obstacles and pushing the project forward. In future projects, I will act differently by proactively fostering an environment of open communication and respect for diverse ideas from the outset. I will also prioritize building a structured yet flexible project framework that allows for the seamless integration of different perspectives. This experience has taught me that the synergy of a well-coordinated team can transform individual ideas into innovations greater than the sum of their parts. Lastly, I've come to appreciate the process of reflection itself as a powerful tool for personal and professional growth, enabling me to approach future challenges with confidence and a more collaborative mindset.

situation: I was a part of a team tasked with planning and constructing a Rube Goldberg machine in my first year of engineering. However, the unit was being held online at the time due to the COVID-19 pandemic. This caused many difficulties as the collaborative nature of constructing such a complicated contraption required hands-on interaction and real-time problem-solving, which was not possible through the online environment. Even though we were able to make a strong start with each team member responsible for a certain section of the machine, it became apparent that certain design flaws were causing disruptions. As each member was working and individually constructing their own part, it was difficult to create synchronisation between components.
task_action: To overcome these obstacles, the team collectively organised virtual brainstorming sessions and established clear communication channels to ensure updates on progress. At times, the work had to be broken down into more manageable tasks. One of the biggest pain points was the fact that we were doing the project online, and it was hard to join individual parts together to create a functioning machine. To address this, the team decided to come on campus with individual components and equipment and construct the machine there. By doing this, we were able to clearly pinpoint the areas that were causing problems and work together to solve them. We maintained these regular in-person check-ins to ensure everyone stayed on track and that any issues were instantly addressed. Furthermore, we utilised digital modelling software and shared online platforms to visualise and troubleshoot the integration of individual components, ensuring compatibility and smooth operation when assembled.
result: Despite the challenges posed by the online work environment, my team and I successfully constructed a functioning Rube Goldberg machine. By utilising technology and maintaining open communication, we were able to collaborate effectively and overcome the limitations. The final result was not only evidence of our creativity but also demonstrated our ability to adapt and thrive in challenging circumstances.
pfr: Initially, navigating and trying to approach the project in a way that would be successful proved to be a difficult task. The online environment felt extremely overwhelming, and there was no sense of direction. We were faced with a lot of issues that made the entire team frustrated as well as tense, as everyone questioned whether we would even be able to complete the project successfully or not. However, as we began to tackle the problem systematically and communicate effectively as a team, I found a sense of reassurance and determination. Despite the obstacles, there was a shared commitment among team members to overcome the challenges and succeed in our goal.
learning: This experience taught me the importance of adaptability and resilience in the face of adversity. It also taught me how crucial it is to identify pain points before taking the correct steps to solve them. The online environment posed limitations, but it also made us think outside the box and find alternate solutions. The decision to come together in person to construct the machine was pivotal in our progress, and we were able to solve several issues. This experience also demonstrated the power of technology to facilitate collaboration. Moving forward, I have gained a deeper appreciation for the value of face-to-face interaction and hands-on problem-solving. In future projects, I will prioritise early and frequent communication, leveraging both digital tools and in-person meetings to ensure effective collaboration. Furthermore, I understand the importance of flexibility and adaptability in responding to unexpected challenges, recognising that innovation often arises from constraints. Overall, this experience has reinforced the importance of perseverance and teamwork in achieving success, even in the most challenging circumstances.

topic: Perseverance, urgency and will to deliver, resourcefulness and flexibility
situation: My journey as a full-time engineering student concurrently working part-time as a teaching academic at the university exemplified a demanding challenge. The dual commitment required me to juggle rigorous engineering coursework with the responsibility of assisting other students academically. This dual role was both an honour and a colossal task. The primary challenge arose from the conflicting schedules between my classes, study time, and teaching hours. Often, these commitments overlapped, leading to stress and the potential compromise of my academic performance and my ability to effectively support my students.
task_action: The critical task ahead of me was to devise a strategy that ensured my success as a student and as a teaching academic. The goal was to achieve a balance that would not only allow me to excel academically but also to fulfil my teaching responsibilities with the dedication and effectiveness they deserved. This required creating a flexible schedule that accommodated the intensive periods of my coursework, such as exams and project deadlines, without neglecting the needs of the students I was teaching. ACTION: To tackle this challenge, I embarked on a multifaceted approach. First, I initiated transparent discussions with my academic advisors and the department head, laying out the specifics of my situation. I proposed a flexible teaching schedule that could be adjusted during critical academic periods. Recognizing the need for efficiency, I also adopted digital tools such as Trello and iCal, even Notion and platforms to create online tutorials and forums for my students, ensuring they had continuous access to learning resources. This digital shift not only allowed me to manage my time more effectively but also catered to the diverse needs of my students. Moreover, I dedicated time each week to meticulously plan out my activities, prioritizing tasks based on urgency and importance. This disciplined approach to time management was pivotal in navigating through the busiest periods of the semester.
result: The outcome of these concerted efforts was highly positive in my first year of teaching in higher education. Proactive steps are taken to manage the dual roles effectively. The flexibility in my teaching schedule during peak academic times was instrumental in maintaining my academic performance. Furthermore, the digital resources were met with positive feedback from students, who found them to be valuable supplements to traditional learning methods. This experience not only underscored the importance of adaptability and proactive problem-solving but also highlighted the value of effective communication and digital innovation in educational settings. The skills and insights gained from this experience are invaluable, reinforcing my ability to manage complex situations and drive positive outcomes in both academic and professional environments.
pfr: Throughout this challenging period, my initial feelings were a mix of pride and trepidation. Pride, because being chosen to assist other students as a teaching academic was an honour that recognized my academic abilities and potential to contribute positively to their educational journey. Trepidation, because I was acutely aware of the substantial time and energy demands both roles would require, especially in a rigorous field like engineering. As the semester progressed, the reality of my situation set in. The overlapping schedules and mounting responsibilities led to moments of significant stress and anxiety. There were times when I questioned my capacity to manage both roles without compromising my academic goals or the quality of support I provided my students. However, through these challenges, I also felt a growing sense of resilience and determination. The process of negotiating a more flexible schedule, adapting my teaching methods to be more efficient, and learning to prioritize my commitments forced me to develop new skills and push beyond my perceived limits
learning: This experience was profoundly instructive, teaching me several key lessons: * THE IMPORTANCE OF COMMUNICATION: Engaging in open discussions with professors and the department head was crucial. It taught me that expressing needs and proposing solutions is often met with support and understanding, highlighting the value of transparent communication in resolving conflicts and achieving goals. * FLEXIBILITY AND ADAPTABILITY: Learning to adapt to changing circumstances and to find creative solutions to problems was a significant takeaway. The ability to adjust my teaching schedule and to leverage digital tools for teaching was instrumental in managing my dual responsibilities effectively. This adaptability is a skill I recognize as essential in any professional setting. * TIME MANAGEMENT AND PRIORITIZATION: The experience honed my ability to manage my time efficiently. Planning my week meticulously, prioritizing tasks, and being disciplined about my schedule were practices that not only helped me navigate my academic and teaching responsibilities but also prepared me for managing future professional commitments. * RESILIENCE UNDER PRESSURE: Perhaps the most critical learning was discovering my capacity for resilience. Facing the pressures of academic deadlines and teaching responsibilities, I learned the importance of maintaining a positive outlook, seeking solutions, and persevering in the face of challenges.

situation: For our ENG3000 group project we had to design a Massive Marvelous Marble Machine (MMMM). We were tasked with designing and developing a subsystem to launch marbles up throughout the system. We employed key stages of the innovation process in order to come up with a solution to the problem
task_action: Initially, we brainstormed some potential ideas. We collaborated with other groups to see what ideas they came up with. The majority of group were going with a simple screw design that was spun by a servo motor. We saw an opportunity to do something different. We chose to risk our time, energy and grades to pursue a design no other group committed to. A fly wheel. A subsystem that was significantly more aesthetically pleasing then the competition. Once again we hit the drawing board, brainstorming potential solutions/designs. We then ranked the designs that we came up with and decided to build a simple prototype for the top three to see which one would work best. After we were done with the prototyping process we were left with two acceptable design. From these two designs we moved to testing and validation. Making sure the each fly wheel design was consistent, efficient and accurate. After evaluating the performance of both designs we had to remove one due to a lack of consistency and added the positives from the removed design to the remaining one in order to complete our fly wheel subsystem. From there we implemented it into the system and ran it through even more tests and made iterative improvements to it.
result: We successfully designed the fly wheel subsystem by going through an innovation process. The key principals we followed were: * Identification of Opportunity * Idea Generation * Idea Selection * Concept Development * Testing and Validation * Implementation * Monitoring and Evaluation * Iterative Improvement * Knowledge Management * Collaboration and Cross-functional Teams
pfr: Engaging in the innovation process is a thrilling journey for me, one filled with both excitement and challenges. Working alongside a team of motivated individuals who share a common goal ignites my passion for innovation. The collaborative synergy we create fuels creativity and drives progress. However, it's not without its hurdles. There are moments of frustration when we encounter seemingly insurmountable obstacles, or when internal conflicts arise within the team due to differing perspectives on approaches to various issues. Navigating these challenges has been an opportunity for personal growth. It's through these experiences that I've discovered my unique role within the team and learned to leverage my strengths to contribute meaningfully. Providing support and value to my team members gives me a profound sense of fulfillment. Together, we confront challenges head-on, brainstorming innovative solutions, making crucial decisions, and adapting to dynamic environments. Embracing both success and failure as integral parts of the innovation process has been enlightening. Each setback serves as a valuable learning opportunity, propelling us towards greater insights and breakthroughs. Ultimately, it's the journey of learning and growth amidst the complexities of innovation that fuels my enthusiasm and drives my commitment to the process.
learning: Through my experiences in the innovation process, I've gleaned several key insights that continue to shape my approach: * Collaboration: I've learned the immense power of collaboration and the importance of fostering a supportive team dynamic. By leveraging diverse perspectives and skill sets, we can tackle challenges more effectively and drive innovation forward. * Conflict Resolution: Navigating conflicts within the team has taught me valuable lessons in communication and conflict resolution. By fostering open dialogue and practicing empathy, we can address differences constructively and strengthen team cohesion. * Adaptability: Innovation often entails navigating uncharted territory and confronting unforeseen obstacles. Cultivating adaptability has been crucial in responding effectively to evolving circumstances and seizing opportunities for innovation. * Resilience: Embracing failure as a stepping stone to success has fostered resilience within myself and my team. By reframing setbacks as opportunities for growth, we can persevere in the face of adversity and continue to progress towards our goals. * Continuous Learning: The innovation process is inherently iterative, requiring a commitment to lifelong learning and improvement. Embracing curiosity and remaining open to new ideas and perspectives fosters innovation and drives ongoing progress. Incorporating these insights into my approach to innovation has not only enhanced my effectiveness as a team member but has also fueled my passion for pushing the boundaries of what's possible. As I continue to embark on this journey of innovation, I am committed to embracing challenges, cultivating collaboration, and driving meaningful change through continuous learning and growth.

situation: As a web and mobile applications developer, I recently encountered a pivotal project that involved the conception and development of a new GPS tracking system designed for use across various mobile devices. The project was a direct assignment from my supervising senior software engineer, who envisioned a robust, universally compatible system that would enhance our company’s tracking capabilities. Given the complexity of ensuring compatibility across different hardware and the need for precise, reliable GPS functionalities, I initially felt overwhelmed. The task required a deep dive into the technicalities of GPS technology and an understanding of diverse mobile hardware specifications and operating systems.
task_action: My primary tasks were multifaceted. Initially, I needed to conceptualize the entire system’s architecture by understanding the core needs of our target users and setting specific, measurable goals. This involved defining the system’s functionalities, designing a user-friendly interface, and ensuring the solution’s scalability and adaptability to different mobile devices. One significant challenge was the seamless hardware and software integration across various mobile platforms, necessitating a thorough analysis and a strategic approach to the system’s engineering and modelling phases. ACTION: To navigate the complexities, I adopted a systematic approach grounded in systems engineering and management principles. I commenced by collecting and analyzing user requirements to define the project scope and goals accurately. Subsequently, I engaged in an iterative design process, sketching out the system’s architecture and establishing clear interfaces between its components. Collaborative discussions with multidisciplinary teams, including hardware engineers and software developers, were vital in bridging gaps and ensuring cohesive integration. I utilized project management tools to keep the project on track, setting milestones and adjusting timelines as necessary. The implementation phase involved rigorous testing across different mobile devices, making adjustments to improve compatibility and performance. Throughout, I remained focused on the end goal of deploying a functional, reliable, and user-friendly GPS tracking system.
result: The culmination of these concerted efforts was the successful design, implementation, and deployment of the GPS tracking system, which now operates seamlessly across a wide range of mobile devices. The system met all the predetermined functionality, user experience, and compatibility goals. It was well-received internally by the project team and externally by initial users, who reported satisfaction with the accuracy and reliability of the tracking service. The project not only bolstered my confidence in leading complex development tasks but also significantly enhanced my skills in systems engineering, interdisciplinary collaboration, and effective project management. This experience has prepared me to undertake future projects with a structured, goal-oriented approach to problem-solving and innovation.
pfr: Engaging with the significant challenge of designing a new mobile GPS tracking system initially stirred a mix of emotions, predominantly an overwhelming sense of apprehension. The complexity of ensuring a universally adaptable system appeared insurmountable at first glance. This feeling was magnified by the responsibility to not only conceptualise the solution but also ensure its functionality across diverse mobile hardware - a testament to the multidimensional nature of modern application development. Despite the initial doubts, the process of breaking down the task into manageable phases and the collaborative effort involved in achieving each milestone transformed my apprehension into a deep sense of accomplishment and confidence. The experience underscored the importance of resilience, structured problem-solving, and the value of a multidisciplinary team. Specifically, moments of successful integration of complex system components and positive feedback from initial users brought a profound sense of professional satisfaction and growth. These moments starkly contrasted the initial phase of feeling overwhelmed, mapping a journey of emotions from uncertainty to triumph.
learning: The project has been a significant learning curve, offering me invaluable insights into systems engineering, project management, and interdisciplinary collaboration. One of the key lessons learned is the power of a structured, systematic approach in dissecting and addressing a problem, echoing the importance of the systems engineering principles. Delving into user requirements, setting clear goals, designing processes, and meticulous testing have highlighted the significance of precision and attention to detail in software development. Furthermore, the experience accentuated the value of communication and collaboration in a multidisciplinary context. The integration challenges posed by diverse mobile hardware underscored the necessity of harmonious teamwork and shared understanding among differently skilled professionals.

situation: I was part of a diverse project team in a large, multicultural organization. We were working on a complex project requiring all team members' input. However, we noticed that during our team meetings, some members were not participating as much as others. This was concerning because we valued the diverse perspectives of all team members and believed that everyone had valuable contributions to make.
task_action: Recognizing this issue, we decided as a team to address it head-on. We wanted to foster an environment where everyone felt comfortable sharing their ideas and felt that their input was valued. I took the initiative to research best practices for promoting equity and diversity in team meetings and proposed a plan to the team. ACTION: I suggested several strategies to improve inclusivity in our meetings. First, I proposed implementing a round-robin format for discussions. This would ensure that everyone had an opportunity to speak and share their ideas. Second, I recommended unconscious bias training for the team. This would help us become more aware of unconscious biases affecting our interactions and decision-making. I also suggested that we should have regular check-ins with each team member. This would allow us to understand their comfort level in the meetings, address any concerns they might have, and gather suggestions for improvement. In addition to these actions, I also emphasized the importance of respecting and valuing the diverse backgrounds and perspectives of all team members. I encouraged team members to listen actively to each other and to be open to different viewpoints. I also reminded everyone that promoting equity and diversity was a shared responsibility and that we all had a role to play in creating an inclusive environment.
result: Implementing these actions led to a significant improvement in our team dynamics. Meeting participation increased, and team members reported feeling more valued and included. The diversity of ideas also improved, leading to more innovative solutions in our projects. Furthermore, the team became more aware of the importance of equity and diversity, and we continued to prioritize these values in our ongoing work.
pfr: The situation initially felt challenging, as it was disheartening to see some team members not participating as much as others. I felt a strong sense of responsibility to address this issue, as I believed in the value of each team member’s unique perspectives and contributions. Implementing the strategies to promote equity and diversity was a learning process, but it was rewarding to see the positive changes in our team dynamics.
learning: This experience has taught me the importance of proactive action in promoting equity and diversity. I learned that creating an inclusive environment requires intentional strategies and ongoing effort. The unconscious bias training was particularly enlightening, as it made me more aware of my own biases and how they can impact interactions. The improvement in our team dynamics and the innovative solutions we were able to develop as a result of increased participation reaffirmed my belief in the value of diverse perspectives. In the future, I will continue to advocate for equity and diversity, and I will apply these strategies in any team setting to ensure that everyone feels valued and included. I now understand that fostering an inclusive environment is not a one-time task, but a continuous process that requires constant reflection and adjustment.

situation: Our task was to form a team and select a company from a pool of 143 potential candidates for our upcoming in-class oral presentation.
task_action: Initially, I reached out to individuals seated nearby, forming a cohesive team committed to brainstorming potential companies. Together, we engaged in the gallery method, encouraging each member to contribute ideas freely. We fostered an environment of equity and diversity, valuing all suggestions and selections equally. From the myriad of options, we narrowed down our choices to several promising candidates: Dropbox, Duolingo, Canva, and Bumble, spanning sectors such as file sharing, software, video streaming, software education, and social networking. With a methodical approach, we evaluated each company's potentiality and current standing in their respective industries. After meticulous consideration, we collectively decided to focus our efforts on Duolingo, recognizing its unparalleled popularity and mission to revolutionize education by making it universally accessible.
result: We wrapped up our brainstorming session with a solid win - we had four potential companies to consider. After careful evaluation, we all agreed: Duolingo was the perfect fit for our presentation. Its innovative language learning approach and massive global reach aligned perfectly with what we wanted to showcase. With Duolingo as our chosen company, we transitioned into the preparation phase with a clear direction. We assigned specific tasks to each team member, ensuring that everyone had a meaningful role to play. This structured approach not only facilitated efficient preparation but also upheld our commitment to equity and diversity. Each team member's unique perspective and expertise were valued, contributing to a comprehensive and inclusive presentation. Through our collaboration, we demonstrated the power of diversity in decision-making and the positive impact it can have on achieving our objectives.
pfr: At the outset, the enormity of the task ahead felt like a mountain looming over us. The prospect of sifting through 143 potential companies for our presentation left me feeling daunted and unsure where to even begin. However, as we delved into the process, I was pleasantly surprised by the sense of camaraderie and collaboration that emerged within our team. Despite the diversity of backgrounds and perspectives among us, there was a shared determination to tackle the challenge together. The thing that struck me most was the genuine respect and value placed on each team member's input. In our discussions, every voice was not only heard but actively encouraged and considered. This commitment to equity and diversity fostered an environment where everyone felt empowered to contribute their ideas freely, regardless of hierarchy or prior experience. It was heartening to witness how our collective intelligence and varied viewpoints led us towards a deeper understanding of the task at hand. As we worked through the list of potential companies, I found myself increasingly inspired by the richness of our discussions. Each member brought their own unique lens through which to evaluate the options, shedding light on aspects I might not have considered otherwise. Despite the initial apprehension, I soon realized that the true magic lay in our ability to harness the power of our collective strengths. Together, we transformed what initially seemed like an insurmountable challenge into an opportunity for growth and learning. Through our shared efforts, we not only selected a company for our presentation but also cultivated a deeper appreciation for the importance of equity, diversity, and collaboration in achieving our goals.

task_action: Develop and incorporate an innovative spiral pathway into our marble machine, focusing on testing various sizes, heights, widths, and lengths to optimize functionality and enhance visual appeal. We then prototyped the spiral using available materials, testing its effectiveness in guiding marbles smoothly and reliably.
result: The integration of the spiral innovation showed significant improvements in marble flow within our machine. Our innovation not only enhanced the functionality of the marble machine but also distinguished our team's project as a standout among others.

Moving forward, I will carry this lesson with me and continue to take opportunities to challenge myself and explore new possibilities. situation: In my software engineering course (COMP4060), my team and I were tasked with creating and analysing a real-life scenario that highlighted ethical challenges in software development, particularly those involving user privacy and data protection. Our hypothetical situation involves a corporation that created an application that unintentionally acquired more user data than disclosed, including sensitive personal information, without the users' explicit agreement. This circumstance reflected real-world difficulties, highlighting the intricacies of ethical decision-making in the technology business.
task_action: Our goal was to provide a solution that addressed the ethical, technical, and social responsibilities involved in the case. We wanted not only to address the existing situation but also to prevent future instances from happening. The solution needed adherence to ethical standards, regulatory compliance, and data protection best practices. ACTION: We began our strategy by performing an extensive study on data privacy legislation, ethical software development principles, and industry standards for user data security alongside case studies related to the topic of utilising/trading customers’ data in illegal ways. Some of those included the recent allegations of OpenAI using illegally collected data to train their AI and Facebook’s history of illegally collecting data without its user’s consent. Based on our results, we started a brainstorming session for 20 minutes aimed at building a multidimensional solution to the problem. Our proposed solution comprised technical measures to protect user data that range from better sourcing analytics and providing ethical training to the development team, to a transparent communication approach to regain consumer trust such as publicising how and what data is collected and used and making public statements regularly regarding the company’s customer security and data privacy, and an internal audit of data-gathering processes. In addition, we proposed that employees receive regular ethical training in order to establish a culture of responsibility and honesty.
result: The initiative resulted in an extensive strategy that not only addressed the issue of unethical data collection but also laid the groundwork for long-term ethical procedures within the organisation. While our method was praised for its thoroughness and practicality, the process caused me to think hard about my ideals and obligations as a prospective software developer. I understood the vital need to incorporate ethical considerations into all stages of software development, from design to deployment. It strengthened my opinion that transparency, user permission, and personal data protection are non-negotiable values in technology. Furthermore, the experiment demonstrated the importance of ongoing ethical education and a strong ethical culture in preventing wrongdoing. This realisation has reaffirmed my dedication to prioritising ethical standards in my professional trajectory over profits or other means, ensuring that my activities benefit the tech industry and society as a whole.
pfr: I was both excited and nervous about participating in this discussion. The difficulty of addressing such a complicated ethical issue in the technology business was out of my comfort zone, but it also provided an opportunity to delve deeply into the complexities of software creation beyond mere writing code. Initially, I was overwhelmed by the enormity of the problem and the duty to suggest a workable answer. However, as we advanced, I became increasingly interested in exploring and comprehending the ethical components that underlay our digital world. The process of brainstorming solutions with my team was especially informative, providing varied viewpoints that improved our final approach. I felt accomplished as we devised a strategy that addressed not only the technical and ethical components of the issue but also showed our shared commitment to social responsibility.
learning: This experience has helped shape my perception of the importance of ethics in software development. It emphasised the importance of the need to evaluate the broader impact of technological solutions on consumers and society. The realisation that technology is not value-neutral but is inextricably linked to ethical considerations has altered my outlook on my future position as a software engineer. I've learned the importance of incorporating ethical decision-making throughout the development process, from basic design to final deployment. This thought has taught me the value of openness, user permission, and data protection as core concepts in technology. Moving forward, I intend to apply these values to my professional work, advocate for ethical practices, and continue to educate myself about the increasing difficulties at the confluence of technology and ethics. The knowledge obtained from this project will influence my actions, ensuring that I help design technology that respects user rights and supports a fair and just digital society.

task_action: As the group leader, my primary task was to guide the design and construction process while ensuring collaboration among my team members. pfr: Leading the marble machine cube project in ENG2050 was an exhilarating experience. Initially, I felt a surge of excitement at the prospect of guiding the team towards a creative solution. MOVING FORWARD: Going forward, I recognize the importance of fostering a collaborative environment where everyone feels valued and empowered to contribute. I will strive to improve my communication skills to ensure clear and timely information flow within the team. Additionally, I will actively seek diverse perspectives during brainstorming sessions to generate the most creative and well-rounded solutions. topic: Trade-offs, judgment, and balance in resolution
situation: During a recent transportation engineering design project, our team encountered a pivotal decision point regarding the pathing of a new road. We opted for a hybrid approach that incorporated elements from both design proposals. By embracing a collaborative and open-minded approach, we arrived at a solution that garnered broad support from all team members. pfr: I felt a sense of unease and tension as the disagreement over the two proposed road paths intensified within the team. situation: In a recent group project for my Distributed Systems class, we were tasked with designing and implementing a client-side simulator for job scheduling. task_action: The objective was to reach a consensus on the scheduling algorithm to implement, ensuring that our solution would not only meet the project requirements but also be feasible within our tight deadline. It was crucial to resolve this conflict quickly to start the implementation phase without delays. Action: I initiated a negotiation and compromise session with my team. Presentation of Ideas: Each member presented their preferred algorithm, detailing the pros and cons based on parameters like efficiency, implementation complexity, and expected performance. 2. Evaluation Criteria: We collectively established evaluation criteria, focusing on feasibility, potential for performance improvement, and alignment with project requirements. 3. Compromise Proposal: To find common ground, I suggested a hybrid approach. We would implement the FC scheduler first to ensure we had a working solution. Simultaneously, we would design and test the custom scheduler, comparing its performance against FC.
result: This approach led to a collaborative and productive workplace. By agreeing to first install the FC scheduler, we assured that we satisfied the project's baseline criteria. Parallel work on the custom scheduler enabled us to innovate and maybe outperform expectations. The end result was a dual implementation in which we effectively proved the efficacy of both schedulers. After extensive testing, the custom scheduler demonstrated increased performance, as mentioned in our final report, giving us top ratings for functionality and creativity. situation: As part of a recent group project as part of my engineering course, we were given the responsibility of creating a long-lasting water filtration system for a rural hamlet that was experiencing serious water contamination problems. The lack of access to potable water in the neighbourhood caused health issues for the locals. To guarantee the project's solution was practical, economical, and ecologically friendly, a great deal of study, creative thinking, and testing of several filtration techniques were needed. The pressure to provide a workable solution quickly increased due to the urgency of the issue.
task_action: As a member of the group, it was my responsibility to evaluate the various filtering techniques and determine which one would work best for the environment, the cost, the ease of implementation, and the effectiveness of removing impurities. It was my duty to make sure the selected approach would be doable for the community to maintain and run with little outside assistance. It was difficult to strike a compromise that would appease the community, project funders, and our academic supervisors while weighing these considerations. ACTION: I utilised a lot of critical thinking techniques to complete the work. I began by compiling information on different filtration techniques, including membrane filtration, sand filtration, and activated carbon filtration. I studied case studies of related initiatives, spoke with experts, and thoroughly reviewed the literature. I weighed the benefits and drawbacks of each approach and compared the results with the requirements of our project. I built a comparison matrix that emphasised important elements like cost, effectiveness, maintenance needs, and environmental impact in order to guarantee a thorough examination. After sharing my findings with my team, I led a series of discussions and encouraged them to challenge preconceived notions and pose questions. We were able to pinpoint possible blind spots and improve our understanding of the viability of each strategy thanks to this cooperative approach. To examine any potential obstacles and techniques for mitigating them, we also carried out a risk assessment for each alternative. Through this procedure, we were able to agree on the best filtration technique.
result: The result of my critical analysis and the team's collaborative effort was the selection of a dual-stage filtration system combining sand and activated carbon filters. This solution was not only effective in removing a wide range of contaminants but also affordable and easy to maintain. Our project was well-received by our professor and peers, and the rural community implemented our design successfully, significantly improving their access to clean water. The positive feedback from the community and the tangible improvement in their health outcomes validated our decision. Additionally, the project earned us recognition at a university-level competition, highlighting the practical impact of our work.
pfr: At first, I was intimidated by the difficulty of comparing different filtration techniques and felt overburdened by the weight of making a crucial choice that would affect the health and welfare of an entire community. The weight of this duty was really stressful since I wanted to make sure that our approach would work in the long run. Every team member contributed a different viewpoint, which enhanced our study and enabled us to reach a well-rounded conclusion. Since I now realise how important critical thinking skills are to the completion of great projects, this experience has motivated me to keep honing them. It became evident to me that solving problems methodically and incorporating other people in the process can result in more creative and practical solutions. This insight has deepened my respect for the benefits of varied perspectives and teamwork when addressing difficult problems.
learning: This project has taught me the value of teamwork in strengthening critical thinking and the significance of approaching problems methodically. I learned from the experience that critical thinking involves not just data analysis but also clear communication of findings and receptivity to criticism. I now recognise how important it is to build these vital talents through continual learning and constant development. I also discovered that more enduring and well-liked solutions might result from incorporating stakeholders early in the process and taking their input into account. My resolve to use critical thinking in all facets of my engineering career has been strengthened by this experience, as it will enable me to make wise decisions that will benefit my projects as well as the communities I serve. situation: I NEEDED TO COOPERATE WITH MY COWORKERS AND COMMUNICATE WITH CUSTOMERS TO SAFELY RUN A WORKSITE WHICH HAS CONSTANT TRAFFIC FLOW. AT KIMBRIKI ENVIRONMENTAL ENTERPRISES, I ALONG WITH MY COWORKERS CONTROL THE WASTE DISPOSAL OF ALL VEHICLES. WITH 1200 VEHICLES ON OUR SITE OVER THE COURSE OF THE 10 HOUR SHIFT THERE IS A CRUCIAL ROLE IN THE COMMUNICATION WITHIN THE TRAFFIC CONTROL ASPECT TO KEEP BOTH WORKERS AND CUSTOMERS SAFE. COMMUNICATION IS VITAL IN HAVING A SAFE WORKPLACE. COMMUNICATION IS CONSISTENT IN ALL WORKPLACES, WHETHER IN AN OFFICE OR ON A WORKSITE. CLEAR, SHORT AND UNIVERSAL COMMUNICATION ALLOWS FOR MESSAGES TO BE PHYSICALLY OR VERBALLY CONVEYED WITH EASE WHETHER THEY ARE INSTRUCTIONS OR WARNINGS.
task_action: Implementing meetings and training allow employees to be on the same page and create a minimum skill level. Having employees on the same page is one of the most important aspects in regards to communication because these workers will have similar unified verbal communications or sign language. Dealing with vehicle traffic flow requires my coworkers and I to have simple sign languages like a straight arm with palm up facing traffic for a ‘STOP’ or an extended arm with a pushing motion to the ground to communicate ‘SLOW DOWN’ to customers to maximise understanding and decrease the risk of injury or damage. Furthermore, messages between coworkers with short concise phrases over a two way radio system allow for there to be little confusion and increased radio silence. This is particularly important incase of an emergency. For example, a coworker can quickly inform the site coordinator that there has been a dumping of hazardous waste like unwrapped asbestos or chemicals because there is not unnecessary noise on the radios. In doing so customers can be properly protected, and the waste can be cleaned up efficiently.
result: The result was being able run a worksite which has clear communications between coworkers and customers, which leads to a heavily reduced risk level for a high-risk workplace. Workplaces with high levels of effective communications create a nearly risk free environment.
pfr: In a customer-facing role with my main responsibility being the safety of others' lives as well as my own, I felt very overwhelmed with the pressure of keeping people safe. Working at Kimbriki Environmental Enterprises, I am constantly surrounded by different vehicles ranging from sedans and suvs to forklifts and loaders. Although the various sizes of the vehicles, the operations of safety are the same. Traffic control is the most important factor and this requires the soft skill of communication. This skill is crucial because one incorrect hand gesture or a lack of specificity with instructions could lead to serious harm. As a result this potential harm created an anxiety which only settled with the aid of my coworkers and the high levels of communication we installed. With Kimbriki being open to the public, I am working with all ages, diverse nationalities and of people of all abilities. This poses a challenge with assuming a gesture or direction is straightforward and that every person would understand the instruction. However this is not the case and this can create dangerous habits if assuming that all people have the same understanding as myself. Sometimes it is people's first time at this specific site or first time disposing of waste or English is not their first language. I sometimes struggled with this concept as I would give people instructions and as they drove off they seemed still unsure or would get lost. I felt embarrassed and I questioned why this was happening. After seeking feedback from fellow coworkers on my communication skills, I realised I needed to simplify my communication skills using more universal ways of communicating including smaller words and more hand gestures.
learning: I was intrigued with how this soft skill of communication could be so effective by simplifying and reducing unnecessary communication. This realisation has dramatically improved my work, as I use less words, people are happier because they are given correct, concise directions and there is a very low risk level. I feel confident in running the work site with my coworkers as I know I can trust myself and coworkers to provide high levels of safety which massively reduce the risk of medium to catastrophic risk at Kimbriki Environment Enterprises. I can continue to bring this soft skill to all aspects of life because our world has diverse cultures and different abilities and for all parts of life to coincide we need good communication. I am optimistic that effective communication will be at the forefront of my work life and am proud to have the ability to manage multiple people and have the confidence in myself to look after their lives.

situation: During the ETHGlobal Hackathon in Sydney, April 2024, I led a team of five participants in developing a decentralised finance (DeFi) application. Our project aimed to create a platform for automated cryptocurrency trading strategies using smart contracts on the Ethereum blockchain. result: As a result of these actions, the team became more cohesive and productive. We successfully developed and deployed a functional prototype of our DeFi application by the end of the hackathon. This experience significantly enhanced my leadership skills and demonstrated the importance of effective communication, conflict resolution, and mentorship in a fast-paced, high-pressure environment.

learning: This experience taught me several critical lessons about leadership. First, clear and consistent communication is essential to align team members with the project's goals. topic: TOPIC/S: Throughout the first half of the semester, within my team, we have learnt how to effectively use data-driven decision making and create new solution concepts in order to obtain the best outcome possible that fits the requirements and then goes beyond. Splitting up isolated us and we often felt a bit helpless because we were only relying on ourselves. We learnt that we need a way to sort through the masses of ideas because we are good at coming up with them, but we need to work harder on actually picking out ones that will work. In the future, we can use our Idea Conveyor Belt and various ways of filtering like working out the advantages and disadvantages of a particular event and using online tools to share with our group exactly how they will work, using drawings for example. For example, having Milk next to the hot water system. * _Innovation: _As the task required innovation within the tea making industry, I began to research into differing ways for tea to be made while avoiding contamination of other tea ingredients into different tea types. I opted for a system flush function which would drain the previously used tea out of the extraction pipes and would remove the used leaves or bags. However, coming up with a functioning system which would avoiding: 1. injuring the consumer, 2. detecting when there is no tea cup under the dispenser, and 3. find a way for there to be tea automatically made after the system flush without human input. I struggled to find a system which would work. I then moved from that segment, due to lack of idea generation for the solution, of the project to the modularity which I wanted the machine to have for easy of used and cleaning purposes. This segment was not difficult and was intentionally designed so that certain segments could be bought after the machine if parts failed. In completing that segment, I moved back to the system flush and auto tea function. In stepping away from the problem for a while I gave my self a refresh to the idea and opted for a system which would make a tea push the cup to the left using a grated track system and flush the system then insert the next cup on the track system. The grated track system allows for the flushed water/tea to fall into a catching pan which needs to be changed every week. * _Testing and Iterations/Monitoring and Evaluation: _As the project did not require for the product to be produced this segment of the innovation process could not be fulfilled.
result: As previously stated in task/action I struggled to come up with a suitable solution to a problem which I faced. By taking step back from the solution process and moving my mind to another problem I allowed myself to effectively design the product. As such I considered most of the needs and wants of the consumer. HOWEVER, I neglected the friends aspect of the system and only focused on the different teas being made.
pfr: The initial task seemed simple at first. As I progressed into the project however, it began to become more complex as certain aspects needed to be considered and focused on. I struggled at points to innovate new ideas to allow for the needs and wants to be met and this did make it more difficult to complete the task to the standard i was hoping for. The final result did meet the requirements of the task, but I did not feel happy with the resulting design. In hindsight I would break down the needs more deeply and offer solutions for the more broken down aspects instead of trying to approach it from such a large scale.
learning: Within this project I learnt the process of innovation and the step required to successfully output a product to a high quality. I was also forced to learn how to more deeply consider the conceptual aspect of design. In doing so I will, in the future, consider the process more deeply and focus on aspects more carefully in order to achieve a better result than I did in this project.

situation: During my current Systems Engineering and Design Thinking course, one of the assignments was the A4 infographic. This assignment consisted in the creation of an infographic to explain a key concept from the textbook that I have learnt during this session. I chose Human Factors in Usability Design.
task_action: . My goal was to create an engaging and informative infographic that clearly conveyed the importance of human factors in usability design. I needed to ensure that the infographic structure had three sections: · An abstraction level · An implementation level · Interesting examples The methods I used to create the infographic were the following: RESEARCH: I conducted a thorough research to understand the definition of Human Factors in Usability Design and the main methodologies used to achieve it. I listed the definition and the main methodologies used as my _abstraction layer_. Similarly, I conducted my research for the implementation level. There is a significant number of ways to implement the Human Factors in Usability Design. I have chosen six methodologies which, in my opinion, are the ones most used by commercial entities that provide Usability Design services. These six methodologies formed my _implementation layer_. SELECTION CRITERIA CREATED AND USED I found many interesting examples and it was difficult to make choices. I used three selection criteria to ensure my examples were relevant and impactful: · Innovative approach · Impact on Users on global scale · Aesthetic Appeal Using the above criteria my selection consisted of 13 examples. These examples formed my _interesting examples layer._ BRAINSTORMING: I started by brainstorming different ways to present the information, focusing on clarity and engagement. I explored various themes, color schemes, and layouts. DESIGN ITERATION: I created multiple drafts, experimenting with different visual elements like location on the page, graphics, and fonts.
result: As a result of these efforts, I submitted the A4 infographic. In my opinion, the infographic effectively communicated complex concepts in an accessible and visually appealing way. Working on the A4 infographic not only enhanced my conceptual understanding of Human Factors in Usability Design but also strengthened my skills in creative problem-solving, visual communication, and user-centered design. It was a valuable exercise in integrating technical knowledge with conceptual design thinking principles.
pfr: I am a neurodivergent student (ADHD). I often experience challenges specific to that condition, especially the ones related to the Executive Function. The challenge of planning and completing the A4 infographic was mainly linked to feelings of inadequacy due to my tendency to procrastinate. For this task, I also found the concepts quite new to me and it took me some time to understand their application and their interaction within systems design. The textbook information helped, however I needed to also do additional research which increased the time I spent on finalising the task.
learning: As a result of this experience, I learnt the importance of a structured approach to engineering design and the value of using theoretical information and effective research. I have also developed an increased appreciation of the need for accurate planning ahead of time and ensuring tasks are completed in line with the schedule. I have consolidated my use of the calendar as an essential time management tool with very good results. Another important lesson learnt through this experience was related to the value of communicating concepts using the abstraction level and the implementation level. I have also better understood the value of the infographic as an efficient communication tool. For the future, I will keep a positive frame of mind when studying something new and will definitely use my planning tools and resources to improve my results. I feel that through this experience I have consolidated my approach to studying, working with new concepts and communicating them using a concise format. I will also be better at managing my stress and staying focused on the end goal.

situation: During an ENGG2050 team project, I believe I have improved my soft skills with several situations and challenges I have faced during the time. Throughout the process of developing the project, I was responsible for recording and taking notes of our each week’s tutorial work and talk to the group members about their tasks. We were given tutorial tasks each week in order to assist the process of developing our product. I was chosen to record and wrap each week’s work done by everyone. As it was group work my communication skill was to be challenged in order to get everyone’s idea correctly and precisely so that our project runs smoothly.
task_action: At first, it was easy for every member to communicate with each other, but as the project went on, I have noticed some of our members being unhappy about their given tasks. When the time came to discuss and brief about the tasks we had a pretty heated debate on wether or not whose idea was better than the other. result: As a result, I have realized how strong communication affects a group’s dynamics and productiveness. I noticed that I struggled with communicating my ideas correctly so that the other person understands it, as well as getting offended my constructive criticism. It was true that my design needed more work, and I couldn’t handle people saying it was not good to me. I have gotten somehow offended by it and flipped out. Listening to people and communicating while encouraging everyone else to speak their ideas are the soft skills that I have mostly improved during the project. I have encouraged everyone to speak one at a time and calmed everyone by letting them know that their ideas were all valid and not to be overlooked. I have simply reminded everyone that we should choose the best points from everyone's ideas and make the whole design on those little good points from everyone. Our design turned out really good, thanks to everyone's contribution.
learning: By leading the discussion and communicating effectively after that argument, I have learned how communication affects the group atmosphere and every member's feelings. Strong communication skills are key to achieving any goal as a team on any project. I will try and improve my communication skills in the future, by participating in more group projects and team settings. I will be a more effective speaker and listener from now on and will use that skill to be someone who is fun, enjoyable, encouraging, empowering to be in one group with.

result: This empathetic approach to leadership helped the team to merge the best aspects of each proposed design, leading to the development of a more efficient and robust gearbox design. pfr: Initially, leading the gearbox design project felt overwhelming due to the high stakes and technical complexities involved.
