topic: The design process phasing and approaches
situation: Our group needed to design a tea maker that was based on an IoT system and I was given the task of designing a subsystem of a loose-leaf tea dispenser. It was stated that the customer needs storage for four different types of tea in the machine and tea should be dispensed automatically.
task_action: When the tasks were equally divided within the team, I started to plan for my part. We needed to communicate our progress and design with our team so that it wouldn't mismatch the whole machine at the end. I used the design process phase (NEEDS--->CONCEPTUAL DESIGN--->PRELIMINARY DESIGN--->DETAIL DESIGN) graph as my reference to track my progress. Initially, I reviewed the customer's requirements to inform my design approach. I organized my workload over six weeks: dedicating the first three weeks to the conceptual design, the next two weeks to the preliminary design phase, and the final week to the detailed design. Our team analyzed the NEEDS of the customers and made a list of features(sub-systems) that can be included in the machine. We distributed the sub-systems to each person on the team to ease the process of building the machine. In the CONCEPTUAL DESIGN phase, I generated multiple conceptual designs based on the requirements. I conducted extensive research on various dispensing systems analogous to our project, which involved dispensing tea leaves. Through a week of brainstorming and reviewing different mechanisms, I expedited this phase to two weeks by maintaining regular communication with my team. I illustrated six conceptual ideas on paper and presented them for team discussion. After a detailed review, we refined and eliminated infeasible ideas, ultimately narrowing down to three preliminary designs. During the PRELIMINARY DESIGN phase, which spanned two weeks, we focused on material selection and refining our chosen design. We established key parameters such as cost, reliability, and sustainability. The designs were ranked based on these criteria, and the top-ranked design was selected for further development. Additionally, I developed the Technical Performance Measures (TPMs) and the House of Quality for this sub-system. In the DETAILED DESIGN phase, I translated the selected preliminary ideas into a CAD model and constructed a small prototype to verify that the actual test parameters aligned with our assumptions. Finally, I completed the final design, which the team agreed would seamlessly integrate into our tea dispensing machine.
result: As a result, I completed my task beforehand with much more efficiency and meeting the requirements of the client. The efficiency was primarily achieved by dividing the machine into sub-systems and allowing me to work on one sub-system while maintaining ongoing communication about their progress within the team. My design was reliable within the parameters and was meeting the client's requirements. This caused the seamless integration of my sub-system to integrate perfectly into our final machine design. Finally, the use of the design process phase graph allowed me to effectively track my progress. This facilitated the timely completion of each phase, ensuring that the project stayed on schedule.
pfr: Initially, when we were given a task to design a tea maker, our team was not organized properly and had no organized flow in making the system. pfr: The initial task of designing an Internet-based tea maker was both exciting and daunting. The customer's vague requirements created a sense of uncertainty, making the project seem overwhelming at first. However, as I began to break down the problem systematically and assign clear roles and responsibilities, my anxiety turned into determination. Developing a clear vision and approach made the project more manageable. Witnessing the project progress from concept to a functional prototype and receiving positive feedback was immensely rewarding. This process underscored the importance of structured problem-solving and thorough planning.
learning: This experience has taught me several valuable lessons. Firstly, I learned the importance of breaking down complex tasks into smaller, manageable parts. This approach not only made the project less intimidating but also helped in identifying and addressing specific challenges more effectively. Secondly, I realized the significance of clear communication and defined roles within a team. Ensuring that each aspect of the project was clearly outlined and that everyone involved understood their responsibilities was crucial for efficient collaboration and successful project completion. In the future, I will apply this structured approach to tackle complex projects more confidently. I will ensure to start with a detailed plan, clearly outline roles and responsibilities, and maintain open communication channels within the team. Additionally, this experience highlighted the value of iterative testing and user feedback. Engaging with users early and frequently provided me with valuable insights that significantly improved the final product. I will continue to prioritize user feedback in future projects to ensure that the end product meets their needs and expectations. Overall, this project has reinforced my belief in the power of structured problem-solving and continuous improvement through feedback. It has also enhanced my confidence in managing and executing complex engineering tasks.

situation: Through the development of my Internet of Teas maker I have had the opportunity to actively develop and strengthen my critical thinking skills. Utilising this skill has proven incredibly useful in the progression of my project, from simply deriving ideas to developing TPMs and further developing concepts and testing for my project. To be able to develop my project, I was required to be able to apply creative thinking with means of real-world application to produce viable and effective ideas.
task_action: Developing my understanding of TPMs was fundamental to my ability to progress in my project development. Investing time into reading the prescribed chapters of the ‘Systems Engineering and Analysis’ textbook aided my understanding of what a TPM is and how they shape the basic testing/requirements for a new project and/or existing project. Investing in the textbook also provided the comprehensive and detailed steps of system design. I completed a critical thinking course on LinkedIn learning which detailed the importance of critical thinking, developing the way of thinking and the application of such a mindset. I then committed to honing in on the customers functional requirements and how these could be incorporated into an inclusive and effective product, by being specific but not overly ‘over-the-top’; e.g. real-world applications we can already see in automatic coffee makers and how this could be adapted to make tea instead. Furthermore, applying the steps of preliminary design, conceptual design, testing etc. to my own project allowed me to actively practice critical thinking in development as well as troubleshooting.
result: Conclusively, I have been able to design and conceptually develop a concept which addresses consumer requirements. Through my use of critical thinking, I have been able to adapt to inconsistencies that were presented through each step within the design process. Working around potential flaws and devising alternative approaches are all a product of my further developed critical thinking skills. Had I not engaged in such growth, design and development of my independent project may have been stunted by inability to devise/innovate ideas and/or address flaws whilst also working to mitigate inconsistencies within the system.
pfr: As a registered nurse I’ve grown comfortable with the concept that I’ve _‘already’_ developed the ability to think critically; my experience through this degree and course have very quickly taught me that self-growth is lifelong and continuous. Whilst I may have the ability to think critically within a medical setting, I still have a long way to truly _‘thinking like an engineer’_. In contrast to my initial preconceived assumptions, I feel that I have significantly developed and strengthened my critical thinking skills throughout this course by working on my project, collaborating with other students, and investing time into the textbook. Whilst this may be true, I also feel that I still have a lot of growth to undertake as I continue to work through future units and even further into my career as a future engineer. Continuing to work on my thinking skills will undoubtedly enhance my ability to address questions, problems and even conversations throughout my lifetime as a student, individual and engineer.
learning: This experience has allowed me to realise the importance of critical thinking as a crucial form of thinking when faced with a problem. In the future, I will be able to utilise critical thinking to facilitate decision-making, logical reasoning, problem-solving, communication and most importantly self-reflection. By diving deeper than just the surface level, I can enhance my understanding and learnings. To further continue my learning, I will strive to engage in ongoing self-reflection to understand what was done right, what was wrong and why. In doing so, I encourage self-growth and personal understanding into my own strengths and weaknesses. Applying critical thinking here is vital to growing as an individual. As an aspiring engineer, I will strive to apply and continually develop my critical thinking skills across all future endeavours.

situation: During my internship at an engineering firm, we were tasked with developing a new industrial process that aimed to increase production efficiency. However, the proposed process involved the use of chemicals that could potentially harm the environment if not managed properly. This situation raised significant ethical, integrity, and social responsibility concerns, as we had to balance the efficiency gains with the potential environmental impact.
task_action: My responsibility was to lead a team in assessing the environmental risks associated with the new process and to develop a plan that would mitigate these risks while still achieving the efficiency goals. This involved conducting a thorough environmental impact assessment and exploring alternative methods or technologies that could reduce potential harm. ACTION: I initiated a comprehensive review of the proposed process, collaborating with environmental experts to analyze the potential risks and impacts. We conducted simulations and modelled various scenarios to understand the extent of environmental damage that could occur. Based on this analysis, we developed a set of recommendations that included changes to the process, investment in cleaner technologies, and the implementation of strict waste management and pollution control measures. I presented these findings and recommendations to the senior management and stakeholders, advocating for the necessary changes to uphold our ethical and social responsibilities.
result: The outcome of this initiative was the adoption of an environmentally responsible process that minimized the negative impacts while still improving efficiency. The firm implemented the recommended cleaner technologies and waste management practices, which resulted in a significant reduction in potential environmental damage. Additionally, this approach strengthened the company's commitment to corporate social responsibility and ethical practices, enhancing its reputation in the industry. My role in this process not only contributed to a sustainable engineering solution but also underscored the importance of integrating ethics and social responsibility into the core of engineering decision-making.
pfr: At the onset of the project, I was deeply concerned about the potential environmental impact of the new industrial process. The weight of making decisions that could affect not just the company’s efficiency but also the environment and society was daunting. I felt a strong sense of responsibility to advocate for sustainable practices, even though it might conflict with the company's immediate economic interests. Throughout the process, I experienced a mix of apprehension and determination, knowing that the decisions we made would have far-reaching consequences.
learning: From this experience, I learned the critical importance of balancing efficiency and environmental sustainability in engineering projects. It highlighted the complex interplay between business objectives and ethical responsibilities. I gained insight into how thorough analysis and collaboration with experts can lead to innovative solutions that align with both ethical standards and business goals. Moving forward, I will prioritize environmental and social considerations in my engineering decisions, advocating for sustainable practices. This experience has taught me that ethical dilemmas in engineering are not just obstacles but opportunities to drive positive change and innovation. I’ve learned that being an engineer is not just about solving technical problems but also about being a responsible steward of the planet and its resources.

situation: In a project I was involved in, our team was tasked with optimizing the cooling system of an industrial machine. We observed that the machine was overheating frequently, leading to shutdowns and decreased productivity. The existing cooling system was not effectively dissipating heat, primarily due to inadequate fluid dynamics within the coolant circuit.
task_action: My responsibility was to lead the analysis and redesign of the cooling system to improve its efficiency and prevent the machine from overheating. This required a thorough understanding of fluid dynamics principles to ensure optimal flow and heat transfer within the system. ACTION: I started by conducting a detailed analysis of the existing system, including flow rate measurements and temperature profiling to identify the bottlenecks in the coolant circuit. Using computational fluid dynamics (CFD) software, I simulated various modifications to the system's design, such as altering pipe diameters, adjusting flow rates, and incorporating more efficient heat exchangers. Based on these simulations, I proposed a redesigned cooling system with optimized fluid paths and improved heat exchanger performance. My team and I then implemented the new design, carefully monitoring the installation and initial operation to ensure that it performed as expected.
result: The redesigned cooling system significantly enhanced the machine's performance. The overheating issue was resolved, leading to a 30% reduction in downtime. Additionally, the improved efficiency of the cooling process resulted in a 15% decrease in energy consumption, saving costs for the company. The success of this project not only demonstrated the importance of applying fluid dynamics knowledge in practical engineering solutions but also contributed to increased productivity and operational savings for the client.
pfr: Addressing the fluid dynamics problem in the industrial machine's cooling system initially felt overwhelming. The technical complexity of optimizing fluid paths and heat transfer mechanisms in an operational industrial context presented a significant challenge. My apprehension was compounded by the pressure to not only improve the system's efficiency but also to ensure its reliability and cost-effectiveness. However, as I engaged more deeply with the problem, using analytical tools and simulations, I found myself becoming increasingly absorbed in the intricacies of fluid dynamics and its practical applications. The process of transforming theoretical knowledge into a tangible solution that had a direct impact on the machine's performance was immensely satisfying.
learning: This experience reinforced the importance of a methodical and analytical approach to engineering problems. I learned that complex problems like these require not just technical knowledge, but also a strategic mindset that considers the broader implications of design changes. The successful outcome of the project highlighted the value of computational simulations in preempting potential issues and refining designs before implementation. In the future, I plan to leverage advanced simulation tools more extensively in the initial stages of problem-solving to explore a wider range of solutions and optimize designs more effectively. This experience has also underscored the importance of patience and persistence in tackling challenging engineering problems, affirming that meticulous planning and execution can lead to significant operational improvements and cost savings.

situation: For our ENGG3050 class, we had to come up with pain points that we received from other students. This meant we needed to find out what was troubling our peers, how bad it is and how frequently they encounter it, and probe them to discover the root cause. We were interviewing multiple people so that we would have many opinions on what is hurting university students at the moment.
task_action: The way we obtained all of these pain points was by surveying random students and asking them questions. We would keep delving deeper and deeper into why they were feeling certain ways and why things were happening so that we could get them to realise the true reason for this problem. We put them all on iLearn so that we could compare everyone's pain points and what the causes were, meaning we had the chance to see how similarly everyone felt and what parts of university life needed to be restructured to accommodate for these issues. Later on, we had a new task to dig even deeper into a specific category of pain point by coming up with numerous strategies (in different categories such as administrative or software solutions) that students could employ to make their situation better. We drew on our own experiences, comparing ideas and feelings about the pain points we found so that we could come up with the best strategies, while also using them for ourselves.
result: As a result of this exercise and our approach to it, we ended up with an incredibly extensive list on iLearn of what other people in the same situations as us have been feeling bad about. We also were given an Excel sheet of many strategies from our peers of how to deal with the groupings of pain points. This not only connected the student body among engineering students because we have all of this information on how everyone is feeling, but we are also more connected with people outside of our discipline as we got to talk to them and have nice conversations that we relate to.
pfr: Honestly, the task we had to do seemed quite boring because I did not want to spend a long time asking people what's wrong with their university life and why it's happening. However, as I was talking to others and getting more into the conversation, I found it really helpful and comforting to see that other people have similar feelings about things like the amount of work we have to do or to class timetable struggles. Before that, I felt more isolated with my own pain points because I didn't have a database where I could see multiple people thinking the same way I do. I was stuck with my own ideas of how to solve my pain points and couldn't find the actual cause. The exercise really helped connect us with other university students.
learning: I can see how repeating this task in modified ways can help university life in general. If I'm struggling with something, I am able to ask around to see if others are feeling the same way and I know they will have different ideas from mine. The staff's involvement also assured me that I can communicate with them if all else fails. I can also come up with my own strategies to help others who are in the same position rather than this help and collaboration being a one-way street.

situation: As part of a group assessment, I was assigned with answering whether certification was necessary for cyber experts or job training would suffice.
task_action: As I collected information regarding the topic, I thought back to one of the Udemy courses I completed, which described presenting your data with a storyline. As such, I searched through the information to find a storyline. This led me to look deeper into the question, with an investigation into both the content of certifications that can currently be achieved, the total number of internet users, and the total cybercrime incidents that have occurred over time. This created additional data that I looked into, leading me to the discovery that both certification and job training is necessary to stay focused and up-to-date with future cybercrime. I then correlated this information to better create a storyline for my information.
result: I was able to present my findings in a way that began with a look into what certifications provide, then what job training achieves. I then asked the question of which was more necessary, using my data and graphs on cybercrime and total users as the climax before finishing the presentation with my findings. This resulted in a satisfying presentation for myself, while seeing the engagement from my peers as I presented.
pfr: Collecting and researching all the data took far longer than just answering the question. Normally, I would have simply looked into both sides, such as the positives and negatives for both certification and on the job training, before creating my conclusion. By forcing myself into looking and spending extra time researching what certifications give and the backgrounds of cyber crime, I took over three times the amount of time on the data collection that I normally would have taken. However, when presenting this information, I felt calmer and more confident in my presentation as I actually understood both my answer and the background. Additionally, the flow of information felt smooth and clear, making it harder to lose my spot in the moment as each sentence connected to the next in a satisfying and understandable way. The same goes for the actual graphs. By having looked into the background of the data, I could understand what the graphs meant for the question and explain their usage, rather than just show the data and move on.
learning: By approaching oral presentations with a storyline focus instead of simply answering the question, I can discover additional data to better present the topic. Additionally, others can understand where the presentation is headed, instead of jumping from point to point. Whilst I do need to take additional time out of my day to complete research, it is always going to be beneficial to follow this style of presentation. Also, I was praised for the style of presentation from the tutor due to the level of engagement I achieved from the class. Overall, I better appreciate the usage of a storyline presentation style as it engages both myself and the listeners better than simple statements.

situation: The members of our team at ENG3000 came from a variety of backgrounds, including different genders, ethnicities, and professional experiences.
task_action: It was important to me that all members of my team would have an equal voice on the important decisions we needed to take. So, the first thing I did was to facilitate an open discussion with all team members present. In the discussion, each person would share her or his thoughts about the campaign and their suggestions/ideas on the content and channel strategy. I made sure that everyone would have an equal opportunity to speak by paying close attention to what was being shared while refraining from adding on more thoughts/ideas. The other part of my tactic was to introduce a rotation structure whereby various team members took turns to facilitate a brainstorming session in each weekly team gathering, as well as greater decision-making. This would help us to tap on the diversity of expertise in the team and create a sense of inclusion and ownership for all. Another tactic I used was to delegate tasks based on the specific skills/interests of each person, rather than their background or status in the organisation (such as university rank/hierarchy).
result: Our team created a completely functional cube as a consequence of our inclusive strategy. We were able to combine many ideas and points of view to create innovative approaches. Our combined efforts also increased team cohesion and morale, which increased productivity and increased team members' job satisfaction. When everything was said and done, the environment in which we worked and the quality of our work were enhanced by our commitment to diversity and justice.
pfr: At first, my initial excitement about a group of young people with such a diverse range of backgrounds as part of the leadership gave way to ambivalence. I worried about our ability to harness the benefits of this diversity, but also anxious about how to handle potential conflict, and how to ensure everyone felt as involved as possible. However, I noticed over the duration of the project that the varied thoughts and perspectives that each team member brought to the table energised me more and more. Encouraging open discussion around elements of the design process from the outset, and rotating leadership throughout our team helped to build comradery and mutual respect among us that in turn inspired creativity and cooperation.
learning: This experience affirm my belief in the power of diversity and equity in finding innovative solutions to problems that requires insight from diverse experiences. Being consciously deliberate and appreciative of our differences helped us to see new ways to find the answers we search. Moving forward, equality and inclusiveness in team interactions would be top priority for me because I understand diversity is not just a catch-phrase but a necessity for success. Another learning is how much structured ways of making decisions can help make diverse groups maximise the collective wisdom. To ensure that all view points are heard and considered when making decisions, it would be my aim going forward to include more deliberate organised ways like the rotation system used in the process. In the end, this experience expanded my knowledge of how diversity and equity can drive creativity in finding solutions and also how it promotes great workplace culture.

situation: I ONCE WORKED AS A PART-TIME RETAIL CONSULTANT, ONE WEEKEND SHIFT I HAD I SPENT A SIGNIFICANT PORTION OF THE DAY ALONE AT THE REGISTERS. ONE CUSTOMER ATTEMPTED TO RETURN OR EXCHANGE THINGS THAT DIDN'T BELONG IN OUR STORE AT THE BUSIEST TIME OF DAY IN THE HOPES OF USING THE MONEY TO PAY FOR OTHER ITEMS THEY WANTED TO BUY. THOUGH THESE THINGS WERE PURPORTEDLY PURCHASED THREE WEEKS AGO, THE CLIENT HAS OBVIOUSLY DONE THIS KIND OF THING BEFORE, AS SEEN BY THE TAGS AND RECEIPTS REMAINING ATTACHED.
task_action: Fortunately, I had expertise with this kind of thing, so I was able to recognize that something did not match up, even if the items appeared to most associates to be properly tagged and genuine objects that belonged to us. Since I had no evidence to support my claim that this was fraud of any type, I initially handled this as though it were a legitimate refund. I looked up the items using the receipt to confirm that they were, in fact, the ones we sold and that their descriptions matched what I was looking at. From that point on, it was clear that the products were fake since they were marked as being much too cheap for what they were, the descriptions in our system did not correspond at all with what I had in front of me, and I had taken the actual items off the floor and put them in front of the customer to demonstrate this. I told the customer that I could not complete the transaction on their behalf because it would be unethical and I would lose my job, and that these products were not ours to return. They attempted to explain to me, in a very hostile and combative way, that they had experienced a similar event in another store, but that time they had received a refund, so if they could make it happen there, they should be able to accomplish it here as well. I made sure to conduct myself in a kind and professional manner during the entire exchange because I didn't want to upset a customer in any way, especially during such a busy time of the week. Because I was merely informing them in the most courteous manner possible that I was unable to reimburse those products, it became more and more difficult for them to work with me. This only served to enrage them. It had escalated much too much by then, so it was obvious that I should have approached my management for assistance much earlier. When I phoned my store manager, they effectively told me that the customer was acting unethically and that they should leave, threatening to call centre security due to their actions against me.
result: When my manager arrived, I had to leave the situation rather than allow it to emotionally impact me since, even though I had followed all the procedures up until then, they would not listen to me. I just continued working from that point on, going down to the next register and tending to the next person in line.
pfr: WHEN I THINK BACK ON THE EPISODE, I WAS REALLY NERVOUS, ESPECIALLY BECAUSE I HADN'T DEALT WITH SUCH UNUSUAL CLIENTS BEFORE. HAVING SAID THAT, I AM RATHER PROUD OF MYSELF FOR REMAINING COMPOSED UNDER PRESSURE FROM A VERY ASSERTIVE CUSTOMER AND FOR UPHOLDING A RESPECTABLE STANDARD OF HONESTY THROUGHOUT THE ORDEAL.
learning: The most significant lesson I learned from this incident, in my opinion, is that I should always uphold my moral principles and integrity by refusing to support people who behave in this way, regardless of the situation. Furthermore, regardless of who they are or what they have done, it is my duty as a member of society to hold them accountable if the situation involves unethical behaviour. By doing this, I hope to teach those around me the importance of ethics and integrity in both the workplace and in our personal lives through leading by example.

topic: Perseverance, urgency and will to deliver, resourcefulness and flexibility
situation: I was working on my race motorbike, in my garage. I was completing a routine, but last minute service, before a big event when I noticed something concerning. The fuel line leading to the injector seemed a little loose, and upon closer inspection, a small crack in the fuel line was visible. Eventually this could potentially cause engine problems or even a fire hazard, but regardless, was certainly not ready to be riding in race conditions the next day.
task_action: Replacing the fuel line seemed straightforward enough. However, a quick online search revealed that the part will be expensive, and not something I could source in time for the event. ACTION: I rummaged through my dad's old toolbox, hoping to find a spare fuel line or something close. I found a length of fuel hose that looked similar but slightly larger in diameter. Adapting to the Challenge: Knowing a larger hose wouldn't fit the injector nozzle directly, I looked at the internet again. My research led me to discover a solution a special kind of fuel line clamps. These clamps could potentially secure the larger hose to the existing injector nozzle. I ventured to a supercheap auto, with the measurements of the hose and nozzle. After some trial and error I found a perfect match.
result: The process took longer than a simple fuel line swap, but the outcome was a success. Using the larger hose and the appropriate clamps, I managed to create a secure and leak-proof connection between the fuel line and the injector nozzle. The fix worked. After a thorough inspection for any leaks, I was stoked to finally hear the engine come back to life, and the joy of a successful repair, fueled by perseverance, was unmatched.
pfr: Initially I was very stressed out and overwhelmed, I'd left this to the last minute and was concerned that my chances of making the event would be low. So I was not only under pressure to get it fixed, but also under pressure to do it quickly, otherwise I would miss the event. As it began to look at the task I became more confident that I'd be able to work but still a level of doubt played on my mind. But as I acquired the parts I knew that everything should be fine, and my mind was at ease. Upon completion of the task I was very happy that I managed to but my head down and remain calm, and persevere through the struggle.
learning: I learnt not only technical skills but the importance of being able to focus and complete the task even when there is alot of pressure to complete it. Though sometimes it will feel like the task is impossible or that there are no viable options, often times there is a solution which you just haven't yet considered. If you do the research and put the effort in it will usually work out for you.

situation: One of our customers called up informing us a delivery he ordered had been incorrectly packed. As I was the one who answered the phone i had to rectify this problem and send out the correct products which the customer required.
task_action: The end goal of an employee at my company is to ensure everything we do creates a positive experience for our customers. By quickly solving the problem at hand we can maximise our chances that the customer will remain happy and continue shopping with us. This is especially important with many competing suppliers creating a situation in which the customer does not come back. Before i delt with this pain point i immediately placed myself in a position of empathy to the customer while on the phone with him. This gave the appearance that i cared about the customer's problem and i understand the dilemma he is facing. As soon as i got off the phone with the customer i opened our sales screen and organised a delivery to the address provided. I found the product which was missing from the order and keyed it into the system. I then went straight to our delivery coordinator and asked him if we could get a delivery sent straight out. He obliged. Our delivery coordinator then spoke with our driver who retrieved the item and expedited the delivery to the customer's location.
result: The customer called up a few hours after the delivery saying thank you for the speedy process in getting the situation rectified. He is still a regular customer of ours and we've actually seen an increase in sales from him in recent times. I believe this may be due to us appearing more trustworthy. By dealing with the pain point quickly and efficiently it gave the customer confidence in our company and showed that we will do what we can to solve any potential problems our customers may face.
pfr: As soon as the customer explained the situation he was in I began thinking about the importance in directly dealing with the problem first. As troubling as this can be, especially when there may be no solution at all, by having experience and a team of fellow employees to help you, the problem can become more achievable. While i was getting the delivery organised i took a mental note of any deliveries we might have to prioritise before sending out this product to the customer. I checked our delivery screen and luckily nothing was showing. I knew from the past that this could be an issue so it was a relief to see otherwise. When i was packing the order i also made sure to double check the product as if I made an error while fixing the customer's pain point it would make the situation even worse. When i received the customer's call to say thank you i was filled with relief that the problem had been sorted out. I was also happy that in the face of a mistake the company which i worked for had a complete system in place to make the rectification a simple and painless process.
learning: By solving the customer's pain point with efficiency and speed it made the problem at hand easier to solve. Futhermore by sticking to my experience with the job and asking for help from my fellow coworkers it allowed me to more clearly see the problem and solve it. By being put in this scenario it allowed me to refresh on the process we have in place to solve these mishaps and it gave me the opportunity to refine my communication and problem solving skills.

topic: Initiative and the willingness to make decisions in the face of uncertainty
situation: In a project competition for autonomous droid racing in one of my societies, I encountered a critical decision point where we needed to choose between 3 design/manufacturing options pertaining to the chassis as it would affect the placement of batteries and other hardware.
task_action: The task at hand was to analyze the available options thoroughly, considering the potential impact on project timelines, paint points, and success. Given the uncertainty in the narrowed down pool of choices, it was essential to take the initiative and make a well-informed choice that would lead us to achieve the project. Action: To address the situation, I took the initiative to lead a short analysis of all options, gathering input from team members while keeping the requirements of the competition in mind. I facilitated discussions to explore the pros and cons of each design choice and in the end chose the option which would be the most doable in shortest amount of time and without bias for our collective "favorite idea" or any one person's idea so that we can consider improvements or other options if the solution doesn't work. The best course of action was to go with the option that we could quickly prototype during that same day as opposed to fleshing out design options over the week, requiring more resources and delaying the project further.
result: The decision-making process enabled us to move forward on a design option with clarity and purpose, mitigating indecision and potential delays. By taking decisive action in the face of uncertainty helped maintain momentum forward in our project timeline. Furthermore, the chosen design option proved to be successful while still leaving room for improvement. Overall, the experience highlighted the value of initiative and the willingness to make decisions, even when faced with uncertainty, in driving project success.
pfr: Reflecting on this experience, I felt torn between my desire to ensure all team members' ideas were considered and the need to make a timely decision to keep the project on track. I didn't want to diminish the contributions of my teammates by prematurely dismissing their ideas, yet I recognized the importance of initiating a design sooner rather than later to maintain progress. This internal conflict challenged me to strike a balance between inclusivity and efficiency. Despite the initial uncertainty and hesitation, I ultimately felt a sense of satisfaction in stepping up to lead the decision-making process. Guiding the team towards a practical solution required me to set aside personal biases and focus on what was best for the project as a whole. Seeing our chosen design option come to fruition and contribute to our project's success brought a profound sense of fulfillment and validation.
learning: It taught me the importance of taking initiative and making timely decisions, especially in fast-paced and uncertain environments like project competitions. Additionally, I learned the value of prioritizing action over prolonged deliberation, as it enabled us to maintain momentum and achieve tangible progress. Moving forward, I will carry these lessons with me, ensuring that I continue to approach challenges with confidence and decisiveness, even when faced with uncertainty.

situation: I had a case study due for ENGG3050 which I was not able to complete on the day it was due, hence I received an extension until Tuesday 26th of March.
task_action: The goal of the case study was to answer questions for the which the information was provided in 3 articles. All three articles were about the General Electric company, each being focused on a different topic such the “evolution of strategic planning at GE”, “Jack Welch’s creative revolution of GE”, and the “successful implementation of Six Sigma at GE”. There were 3 main questions with multiple parts, and they specified which document to extract the required information from for each question. Looking back, I had greatly underestimated the amount of time and effort it would take to complete this task and I had proceeded to focus on complete other assessment tasks. I had initially presumed it would take me one day to complete the task, which lead me to waiting until Sunday (the due date) to start working on the assignment whilst I completed an assessment for my MTRN4066 unit. As I was getting closer to the due date, my fatigued and tired self was unable to properly start the case study and I was forced to ask for an extension.
result: The result of me asking for extension, which was until Tuesday night (2 days), changed my university and life schedule for following days. I skipped all my lecture classes because I was worried and anxious about completing the assessment on time and I ended up spending far more time in front of the computer than was healthy. I did manage to complete the assignment in time, however I missed a few questions where I did not understand (because of my compounded stress) or I did not care to complete because I had other questions to complete (there was one question with multiple parts, and the entire question was worth 1 mark).
pfr: I feel that recently my ability to complete tasks has been lower than before, I’m not entirely sure whether this is because I’m in my penultimate year (and eager to graduate) or that I’m simply bored of university work, but I am certain that this needs to be resolved as soon as possible. When I was completing the case study task, I found questions themselves to be quite daunting, which led me to frequently procrastinate on completing the assignment. I feel frustrated with myself for becoming lax with university work because I have felt the impact across all my other units, and it really gets to me because I make set plan for each day where I state what work I must finish and which ones to prioritise but at the end of the day I only get one piece of work finished. Sitting down to complete this reflection task, I always remember how important it is to practice completing tasks without interruptions, and how difficult it can be because of bad study habits. Although I’m not entirely confident if I can do it, I am determined to improve my study habits over the next few weeks and during the session break so that I’m on my best game for any future assessments.
learning: In a proper workplace I would not be provided with an opportunity for an extension to my deadline without a proper justification, therefore I have come to understand how important accountability is for my work because I will not be provided with a second chance in normal circumstance. I will keep this incident in mind for any future work that I do and thereby hold myself accountable for my work. I am determined to hold myself accountable for my poor study habits and practice sitting down to complete assessment tasks without interruptions (such as mobile devices or social media) and aim for high distinctions for any future university assessments.

situation: In my second year at university, one of our assessments for the engineering design course required us to create a Rube Goldberg machine (RGM). task_action: Our goal was to design and construct an RGM that could successfully turn off a light switch using at least ten different steps. My role was to lead the brainstorming sessions, coordinate the construction efforts, and ensure that each step of the machine was innovative and functional. ACTION: To start the project, I organised a brainstorming session with my team. We used the "mind mapping" technique to generate a wide range of ideas for each step of the machine. This allowed us to visualise the overall process and think creatively about how to link different mechanical actions. Each team member contributed unique ideas, and we encouraged free-flowing discussion to explore all possible options. We identified and selected the most promising ideas by considering their feasibility, complexity, and how effectively they could be integrated into the overall machine. After compiling our ideas, we created a detailed plan for the sequence of steps. Each team member was responsible for constructing specific components, such as a domino cascade, a marble run, and a pulley system. Throughout the construction phase, we conducted regular testing and refinement to ensure each step worked seamlessly. We made several adjustments to improve reliability and ensure the machine's smooth operation from start to finish.
result: The result was a successful Rube Goldberg machine that turned off the light switch through a series of ten intricate and interconnected steps. Our machine included a combination of mechanical actions, such as a marble triggering a series of dominoes, a toy car rolling down a ramp, and a pulley system that ultimately pulled the switch. The project not only improved our technical and problem-solving skills but also demonstrated the importance of teamwork and creative thinking in engineering. Reflecting on this experience, I learned the value of collaboration and open-mindedness in tackling complex challenges. It reinforced the importance of creative thinking in engineering projects and encouraged me to continue seeking innovative solutions in my future endeavours. This project also highlighted the joy and satisfaction of turning imaginative ideas into functional, tangible results.
pfr: At the start of our second-year project to create a Rube Goldberg machine, I felt a mix of excitement and apprehension. Documenting our decisions and systematically testing each component allowed us to stay organised and focused. By focusing on one step at a time and ensuring each component worked correctly before moving on to the next, we were able to tackle the project without feeling overwhelmed. This systematic approach is something I will definitely apply to future projects, as it makes large tasks seem more achievable. situation: As a Quality Assurance (QA) engineer at Zeiss, a company specializing in ophthalmology, we encountered a significant issue with one of our new ophthalmic devices. The device was failing certain critical quality tests, leading to delays in its approval and potential release. This issue risked not only the timeline of the product launch but also the company's reputation for high-quality medical devices.
task_action: My task was to identify the root cause of the quality failures, implement corrective actions, and ensure the device met all regulatory standards and quality benchmarks. This required a detailed analysis of the device's production and testing processes, followed by strategic adjustments to address the identified problems. ACTION: I began by organizing a cross-functional team meeting with engineers, production staff, and quality control personnel to discuss the failures and gather insights. We used the Fishbone Diagram (Ishikawa) method to systematically identify potential causes of the quality issues, such as materials, methods, machines, and human factors. Once potential causes were identified, I led the team in conducting a thorough root cause analysis using the 5 Whys technique. This helped us pinpoint the primary cause of the failures: a specific calibration issue with the testing equipment that was causing inaccurate readings. To address this, we took several actions: Calibration protocoL: We revised the calibration protocol for the testing equipment, ensuring it met stricter standards and was calibrated more frequently. Training: I organized additional meetings with FSE to ensure they were well-versed in the new calibration procedures and aware of the critical checkpoints. Process audit: We conducted a comprehensive audit of the production and testing processes to identify any other potential issues and ensure all procedures were followed correctly. Implementation of control procedure: To monitor the quality of the devices in real-time, we implemented SPC tools. This allowed for early detection of deviations and immediate corrective actions.
result: The changes led to a significant improvement in the quality of the ophthalmic devices. The failure rates in critical tests dropped by 85%, and we were able to meet all regulatory standards well ahead of the revised schedule. The improved calibration protocol and process controls also ensured consistent device quality in subsequent production batches. The successful resolution of this issue not only allowed us to proceed with the product launch as planned but also reinforced our commitment to quality, earning positive feedback from regulatory bodies and enhancing our reputation in the ophthalmology industry.
pfr: The initial task of addressing the quality failures in our new ophthalmic device was quite daunting. As a team, we felt a considerable amount of pressure, given the high stakes involved in maintaining Zeiss’s reputation for quality. At first, the problem seemed overwhelming due to the complexity of the device and the numerous potential failure points. However, by approaching the issue systematically using tools like the Fishbone Diagram and the 5 Whys technique, we were able to break down the problem into manageable parts. Collaborating with a cross-functional team was particularly rewarding; everyone brought their unique perspectives and expertise, which helped us pinpoint the root cause more effectively. Throughout this process, I experienced a mix of frustration and determination, but the team's cohesive effort turned the situation around. I felt a great sense of accomplishment when we successfully identified the issue and implemented the necessary changes, knowing that our collective efforts had made a significant impact.
learning: This experience taught me the importance of a structured approach to problem-solving. Using established methods like the 5 Whys technique not only provided clarity but also ensured that we considered all possible angles. I learned that systematic analysis is crucial in identifying root causes effectively. Additionally, the value of cross-functional teamwork became evident; diverse expertise and perspectives can greatly enhance the problem-solving process. Moving forward, I will always advocate for a structured, methodical approach when facing complex issues. I will also prioritize fostering collaboration across different functions within the company. This experience highlighted that problems, no matter how daunting, can be resolved more efficiently when tackled with a clear, organized strategy and a strong team effort. I now appreciate the power of systematic problem-solving and the invaluable contributions of a well-coordinated team. These insights will guide me in future challenges, ensuring I approach them with confidence and a clear plan.

task_action: As a team, we needed to identify the problematic steps and determine the exact changes required to enhance the machine's performance. ACTION: I initiated a comprehensive data collection process, meticulously recording the performance of each step over multiple trials. We measured variables such as timings, angles, and the required force for each step. Using this data, I created a detailed spreadsheet to identify the steps that were deviating from our plans. Next, I collaborated with my team to brainstorm potential modifications for the identified steps. We conducted controlled experiments, adjusting one variable at a time and recording the corresponding results. This approach enabled us to isolate the impact of each change and make data-driven decisions on the optimal modifications.
result: We were able to make exact adjustments that considerably improved the performance of our RGM by relying on valid data. The machine performed well at every stage, and the improvements resulted in a 75% decrease in failure rates. The successful execution of a data-driven approach not only contributed to the success of our project but also emphasized the significance of evidence-based decision-making in complex projects.

Leading the data collection process and working together to analyze and implement changes based on factual evidence was incredibly rewarding. Our data-driven improvements allowed our Rube Goldberg Machine to function smoothly, which was a credit to our methodical approach and consistent effort. This success strengthened my confidence in the significance of cooperation and effective communication, as each team member's contribution was vital to accomplishing the goal.
learning: I've learned the tremendous benefit of using data to make decisions due to this initiative. topic: Perseverance, urgency and will to deliver, resourcefulness and flexibility
situation: I mentor a high school FRC robotics team and we needed to prototype a wheeled intake mechanism to pick up rings off of the floor for a large-scale robotics project
task_action: Firstly we started brainstorming and developing ideas based on how to approach the design, looking at existing solutions that other teams had already developed as well as real work solutions to alike problems. From there we identified common occurrences between designs and focused our attention on those aspects. In our case, I highlighted that the distance between the wheels and the distance from the floor were key dimensions that we had to tune perfectly. By identifying this, I then got the students to design modular testing rigs to test different heights from the floor, and different distances between wheels (for different compression) to obtain the most efficient and effective intake behaviour. The modular test rigs also allowed the students to explore multiple options for different wheels to see which wheels had a better time griping the rings as well as any other positive or negative behaviour. By doing so, the students were able to notice and document that the rings failed to pick up with too small or too large distances between wheels and the floor, and it extremely succeeded when there was slight compression on the ring due to a slightly smaller distance between the wheels than the ring's outer thickness. Furthermore, the students noticed that with the same compression, rigid wheels worked relatively well, however, softer squishy compliant wheels worked exceptionally well as once the wheels touched the ring nothing was stopping it from being acquired by the intake mechanism. The students also noticed that the compliant wheels could vector the ring laterally toward the centre of the mechanism if the ring was caught on the outer edge of the intake mechanism. This would ultimately prove extremely powerful for the final design as it could reduce the time taken to pick up a ring due to misalignment of the mechanism.
result: The result was that we tested all of our wheels and identified the most optimal ones to design the mechanism around, as well as measured and documented the appropriate key dimensions that would assist in designing the final mechanism design.
pfr: The way that I approached the situation made me feel good that I had led the team in a good direction without being too overbearing and let the students explore all the options and investigate all on their own. It also felt rewarding testing all the wheels ensuring we were resourceful and designing the best mechanism we could around the materials and components we had access to felt extremely rewarding, as not only did it teach the students a valuable lesson for future reference, but it would also reduce the worry and stress of needing to buy new parts and avoid slowing down production times due to waiting on said new parts.
learning: This process has made me better appreciate the ideas of iterative and modular designing as it made the whole situation much smoother to identify key areas of improvement, as well as allowed a simple way for the students to understand the way we were approaching design and where it led to next. It also taught me that understanding your constraints and being flexible and resourceful in the face of constraints can lead to inventive and ingenious designs that likely wouldn't have been developed if not for thinking outside the box.

situation: We were asked to build a gearbox for Mechanical Design 2 which involved a simple casing, bearings, shafts, and gears. The idea is that the gearbox will be used as part of a crane to lift a maximum mass of 28kg at a certain rate.
task_action: We were a group of three with each team member being assigned a certain component of the gearbox. The customer had multiple factors that we had to consider. This included the cost, the mass, the volume, the efficiency, and lastly the aesthetics. With all these factors in mind, it is hard to understand where to start. Moreover, it becomes easy to fall into the trap of tinkering or trial and error without a systematic process to track improvement or compromises. Therefore, to initiate an engineering process, we initially started off with brainstorming all the ideas without any consideration of the constraints provided by the customer. Next, with the bank of ideas, we could eliminate the ones with the most apparent problems or the ones that clearly would not meet the customer considerations and this put our critical reasoning into play. Next, we worked on a top-down design starting with the result and working our way back to the smallest of components. Not only that, but we also used spreadsheets to go through multiple iterations of our design and analyse how the final product would be affected. Testing procedures were also crucial to understand if our product would get better through the iterations and this would involve setting performance indicators, be it qualitative or quantitative. These procedures also allowed us to understand the compromises that we need to make, and which components would be prioritized over the others. And throughout all this, it was important to make sure that team members were sticking to these procedures instead of deviating to the easier methods of just tinkering which would produce a subpar product.
result: We were able to successfully create an order list for the gearbox for assembly and start the more in-depth testing procedures.
pfr: Throughout the project, there were times of challenges which required to preserve and try multiple solutions, but it was also exciting at the same time because it allowed us to use the critical skills we have been learning about in the previous units. There were times of frustrations, especially during the analysis which induced stress but also created a sense of teamwork as we were all in it together which allowed us to stay determined towards finding a solution. Moreover, there was stress towards building innovative solutions as there was a higher risk but the analysis with data helped us towards mitigating those risk and in the end, everything coming together created a sense of achievement.
learning: There were multiple things that we were able to learn and put into practice through this project. Lastly it was important for every member to show those skills and point out if another team member was moving away from these structured processes without a sufficient reason. Beyond this whole project, we learned about always being open to different solutions and when to start being critical. Not only that, we learned to stay within the set procedures even when everything started feeling stressful which taught us how to integrate perseverance into the team members as a leader.

situation: I was involved in a small sub-group (Motions) of an university engineering project that only consists of 4 members, meaning communication and accountability a high level so that the project could be successfully completed. learning: A seemingly uncomfortable task for my personality became a big learning opportunity. situation: During my third year of university, our engineering design course required us to complete a semester-long team project. learning: This project taught me the value of structured decision-making and effective team coordination. This experience has deepened my appreciation for the balance between rigorous security measures and user-centric design, and I will apply these principles in future projects to achieve more effective and cohesive outcomes.

situation: We had to build and construct a high-precision DC motor drive system for lift control as part of our ELCT3024 team project. Acquiring accurate speed control was necessary to guarantee seamless functioning and adjust to different load scenarios, both of which are essential for the dependability and efficiency of lift systems. The project was difficult because it required very precise motor control to strike a balance between passenger comfort and operational efficiency.
task_action: Specifically, we had to design a DC motor control system with closed-loop control mechanisms to achieve accurate speed regulation. To make sure the system satisfied the needs for high accuracy, comfort, and dependability, we had to develop and test it. Elevator applications often include dynamic situations that the control system has to be able to handle. ACTION: * INITIAL RESEARCH AND DESIGN: We started by researching the necessary components and control strategies. The Pololu 4824 brushed DC motor with an integrated gearbox was selected for its balance of torque, speed, and efficiency. We designed a schematic diagram for the DC motor drive system, incorporating a motor driver controlled by an Arduino UNO, which received feedback from the motor’s speed and position sensors. * MATHEMATICAL MODELLING: We developed the mathematical models to describe the motor’s behaviour, including torque and back EMF equations. We derived the open-loop transfer function and used MATLAB to perform root locus and frequency domain analyses (Bode plots) to understand the system dynamics. * CONTROLLER DESIGN: The primary challenge was designing a PI controller to meet the specified performance parameters: a settling time of 0.3 seconds ± 20%, overshoot less than 10%, and steady-state error less than 1%. We used root locus techniques and Bode plots to iteratively adjust the controller parameters. We also utilized Simulink’s PI block auto-tuner to refine these parameters. * SIMULATION AND TESTING: We built both open-loop and closed-loop systems in Simulink to verify our design. The closed-loop system incorporated the PI controller with the calculated values (Ki = 0.03194 and Kp = 0.00192). We tested the system under various conditions, including changes in load, to ensure stability and performance. * EXPERIMENTAL SETUP: We assembled the hardware, connecting the DRV8871 driver chip and Pololu 4824 motor to the Arduino UNO. We conducted multiple experiments to validate the system’s performance, adjusting the control parameters as needed based on the experimental results.

pfr: Designing a high-precision DC motor drive system for lift control seemed like a daunting challenge at first. The requisite accuracy and intricacy felt daunting. But my uneasiness subsided as we methodically dissected the issue and recorded every choice we made. We were able to come up with a successful design through cooperative conversations. Seeing our theoretical models convert into real-world results was incredibly exciting, even though the modelling and simulation phases were difficult and sometimes frustrating. It was exciting and unsettling to set up the gear and do testing, but it was also very satisfying to get the required results.
learning: * SYSTEMATIC PROBLEM-SOLVING: Tackling complex problems by breaking them into manageable tasks and documenting each step enhances clarity and collaboration. * ITERATIVE DESIGN PROCESS: Iteration in design, simulation, and testing is crucial for refining and achieving desired performance specifications. * TEAM COLLABORATION: Effective teamwork and communication lead to robust and innovative solutions. Clear documentation and regular meetings keep the team aligned. * ADAPTABILITY AND RESILIENCE: Being adaptable and resilient helps overcome unexpected challenges and maintain progress. * APPLYING THEORY TO PRACTICE: Practical application of theoretical concepts reinforces understanding and highlights real-world complexities. In the future, I will approach complex projects with greater confidence, emphasize team communication and documentation, and embrace iterative design and testing. This experience has taught me the value of systematic, collaborative, and iterative approaches to problem-solving.

situation: Me and two other students were asked to produce a gearbox as part of a project. The three of us would each be responsible for an individual component, which together creates the entire assembly.
task_action: Initially we began to work on the entire gearbox as a team. The resposniblity of each member wasnt fixed and we tried to contribute as much as we could to the gearbox as a whole - choosing motor speed & gear ratios, shafts material & sizing, as well as which performance metrics we thought most important i.e. torque output, mass/volume & cost. We used qualitative evaluation to choose a conceptual design that we thought met these criteria.
result: From the initial analysis we arrived at a conceptual design that we could then split into the individual components for each member to analise further so that we could get a detailed design to perform testing with.
pfr: Before the project had been divided up into the respective components it was DIFFICULT TO MANAGE ALL THE CONSIDERATIONS THAT HAD TO BE MADE TO MEET THE REQUIREMENTS. Multiple attemps were made to achieve the first conceptual designs, however early on no one had a good grasp of project details or what their individual responsibility would be. We kept iterating designs based on our current understanding of the performance that each concept would provide. Ultimately we arrived at what we thought best achieved the criteria, building on each 'failed' concept.
learning: The design process would have greatly benefitted from longer term planning, tasks could be broken down further WITH DEADLINES and the members responsible for completing them should have been listed early into the project to avoid confusion or workload imbalance. Implementing this would have GREATLY IMPROVED THE DECISION MAKING PROCESS and ultimately we could of had a better perfoming gearbox.

learning: Through the negotiation of ideas and clear communication, the conflict on design choice was resolved, with the decision resting in halfway between both options, which actually ended up being the best outcome. situation: As an engineering student, I was part of a team tasked with designing and implementing a feeder mechanism for a marble machine project. The feeder mechanism's goal was to efficiently transport marbles collected at the bottom of the machine back to the top, where they would enter a series of pathways leading to a collection box.
task_action: In this project, my role as the team leader was to oversee the design, fabrication, and testing of the feeder mechanism. This involved coordinating the team's efforts, delegating tasks according to each member's skills, and ensuring the feeder mechanism integrated seamlessly with the rest of the marble machine. ACTION: To begin, I facilitated a brainstorming session with the team to generate ideas for the feeder mechanism design. We considered factors such as efficiency, reliability, and ease of integration with the existing marble machine components. After evaluating several concepts, we settled on a design that utilized a conveyor belt system to transport marbles from the collection area to the top of the machine. I assigned tasks to team members, such as designing the conveyor belt system, fabricating mechanical components, programming any automation features, and conducting testing and optimization. Throughout the design and fabrication process, I provided guidance and support, ensuring clear communication and collaboration among team members. I also coordinated with other teams working on different aspects of the marble machine to ensure compatibility and alignment of our respective components. During testing, I led the team in identifying and addressing any issues or performance bottlenecks, iterating on the design as needed to optimize efficiency and reliability.
result: Through effective teamwork and leadership, we successfully designed and implemented a feeder mechanism that efficiently transported marbles from the collection area to the top of the marble machine. The conveyor belt system operated smoothly, ensuring a continuous flow of marbles through the machine's pathways. During the project presentation, we demonstrated the feeder mechanism's functionality and explained its design principles to our peers and tutors. Our project received positive feedback for its innovation, technical complexity, and contribution to the overall functionality of the marble machine.
pfr: Leading the design and implementation of the feeder mechanism for the marble machine project was both challenging and rewarding. I felt a sense of satisfaction seeing our concept come to life and contribute to the overall functionality of the machine. Despite encountering technical challenges and setbacks along the way, the collaborative effort and determination of our team propelled us towards success.
learning: This project provided invaluable lessons in engineering design, problem-solving, and teamwork. I learned the importance of thorough planning and iteration in the design process, as well as the significance of effective communication and collaboration among team members. Additionally, I gained hands-on experience in mechanical design and fabrication techniques, as well as troubleshooting and optimization of complex systems. Moving forward, I will apply the lessons learned from this experience to future projects and endeavors. I will continue to refine my leadership and teamwork skills, seeking opportunities to lead and collaborate on innovative engineering projects. Additionally, I will strive to deepen my technical knowledge and expertise in mechanical design and automation, exploring new technologies and methodologies to push the boundaries of what is possible in engineering design.

I also recommend the usage of collaboration tools like project management software. These steps were made to ensure transparency and easy access to information within the team. Finally, I led courses on active listening and practical communication techniques. These sessions sought to provide team members with the skills required to better understand and collaborate.
result: These actions improved the team's communication and collaboration. Trust and understanding were enhanced. The cultural exchange activies helped us to know each other's working sytle and values. The collaborative tools increased transparency and efficiency. Also it reduces misunderstandings. The workshops helped team members handle disagreements and slove problems. These efforts enabled us to execute the project on schedule while exceeding the specified quality requirements.
pfr: Because of the differences in the backgrounds and working styles of the team members, I felt depressed at the beginning. Finding a solution to everything is challenging and complex. situation: our group of 6 needed to complete a lab experiment however felt unorganised with everyone working on one section of the exercise. This would lead to mainly 2 members working on the experiment with the remainder not contributing with little discussion or ideas thrown around.

result: once everyone was accountable for their work productivity went up as well as general communication within the group. This resulted in our experiment being completed faster then we first thought and engaged every member to contribute due to each person not wanting to let down the group.
pfr: Initially our lab experiment seemed easy due to our group having 6 members however as it was our first time, and no one had any experience no one took the lead and our group became stuck with conflicting ideas on what we should do. It became apparent that we had to switch our approach if we were to complete this lab. Reflecting on our decision to assign roles and hold each member accountable was a great idea as it sped up the process, drove ideas and solutions to be shared which ultimately led to the completion of our lab.
learning: With each member accountable for their role, we were all motivated to not let the team down. Looking back at this approach I found the importance of accountability as it was a good way of motivating a team of people due to everyone having a task and purpose. This system effectively used each team member to their best abilities and created great conversation which led to new ideas and solutions. I have learnt in the future when assigned a task working in a team that the first step is to outline what needs to be achieved and then assigning each member to a role and hold them accountable. topic: Initiative and the willingness to make decisions in the face of uncertainty
situation: During the second half of my ENGG2000 unit, our team had a change in leadership roles, where our 3rd year peers changed involvement. task_action: Faced with this opportunity I stepped up to become the main development lead and communication between the 3 sub-teams. Even before this, I was tasked with designing and implementing certain 'motions' related aspects of the machine, so I had a good knowledge about the system, on top of this I had already been conversing with the structures team from time to time, so with this change in the leadership dynamic, it just seemed like I would be the right person for the job. Following this, I took on more and more responsibilities, regularly checked in with individual people and their progress, and at times even helped them out (as I had a wide knowledge of CAD, programming, designing, electronics, manufacturing I was able see the entire project to completion). When faced with problems I discussed with team members, before coming to a solution based upon my own and others' suggestions.
result: By having a designated (not officially in this case) person who has an over arching knowledge about the system, and with good communication between sub-teams, the marble machine was successfully completed, and as it turned out, ours was reliable and robust and thus had earned its spot on the marble machine wall.
pfr: While I found this quite draining, I personally was able to find certain aspects rather enjoyable and rewarding about my experience. The thrill of taking on a challenge this scale and intricate, and seeing the marble machine come to life definitely gave me a sense of deep pride and accomplishment. However, the thing that made it really draining was the lack of communication between the sub-teams, and especially when there was a plan laid out but due to pride or carelessness some team members still decided to go against our agreements.
learning: From my experience with taking the initiative to take on the role of the main development lead was firstly, that a project needs to have a person who oversees the making and design of the project, especially if there is a lack of communication between the individual sub-teams tasked with the creation of it. Secondly, this provided me with a tremendous opportunity to gain more experience and knowledge about management, making important and informed decisions, and even problem solving between individual team members (not just technical problems with regards to the machine, but how often and easily conflict can arise between the people themselves). Ultimately, taking initiative and making decisions even in the face of uncertainty has allowed me to grow as a person, manager, and engineer.

situation: I had completed a 3D puzzle project that took me six hours to complete. I left it on the table and when I came back home after 7 hours it was damaged. The walls collapsed and pieces fell on the floor.
task_action: I took time and reevaluated my choices in materials and types of glue used in the project. I also researched the potential reasons why it may have collapsed so easily- due to lack of drying time, the wrong type of glue mixing with the materials, excessive wind, an external reason (a person or animal knocking it down), or bad placement in my home.
result: Gathering my research I concluded that I must use the E6000 glue in accordance with the material types, I should place it in an area with no windows near (preferably my cupboard or desk), and I should let it dry for a good 8 hours before attempting to relocate it.
pfr: The project took me around 6 hours to complete, so when I came home to see it on the floor and it was damaged, I felt disappointed in myself for allowing this to happen. As an engineer, even small projects like this reflect the planning and intentional design and if it falls apart it generally does not mean good. I slowly started to think about my role as an engineer, and how all factors matter in projects (big or small). I decided not to wallow and researched my mistakes so I could learn from them. I redid the puzzle and it is now sturdy and able to be transported throughout the house.
learning: Mistakes happen throughout the industry, and the way to avoid them is to complete excessive planning and consider all factors that may affect the overall project. This lesson taught me to be more careful in my future projects, and also not to wallow in my mistakes and learn from them. Through this experience I was taught how to handle extreme situations with damaged projects, and how to collectively rise and grow from them.
