topic: Perseverance, urgency and will to deliver, resourcefulness and flexibility
situation: During the ENGG3000 project, I along with another student, were group leaders and were responsible for dividing up workload and documentation writing.
task_action: During the first half of the semester we all began to work on the project. This included documentation like the scoping document as well as design documents. Overall the group was performing well, with the quality of work being fairly similar amongst the group, with everyone delivering what was expected of them. There was one student whose work output was significantly worse than anyone else. This often meant that another group member would have to proofread their work and improve both the length and quality of what was written. This was due to language barriers as English was not their first language. We (the other group lead and I) were unaware of the impact that this had on them. Moving forward we would meet with them privately after our group stand-ups to really dissect their workload and tasks into sections they understood.
result: The result was that the work output of this student improved significantly in the second half of the semester. We were able to rely on them to deliver quality work on time. That contributed to the overall flow of the document.
pfr: At the beginning of the semester, it was challenging as our group members felt like not everyone was pulling their own weight. It seemed as if they were just lazy and not doing the work by choice. When we found out that this student was really struggling with understanding what was being asked of them, all of us wanted to help. Reflecting on this and the solution we came up with, I am glad that we persevered and found a middle ground as this greatly improved the project experience for everyone.
learning: This experience helped me to realize just how important good communication channels are not just within a group project but in engineering and life as a whole. It made me realize that part of being a good leader is being able to recognise not just each team member's strengths but their weaknesses as well. Through identifying weakness and offering support, A good collaborative and cohesive environment can be created and a positive outcome achieved.

situation: During one of my engineering units, our group at the time was tasked with delivering an oral presentation to the whole cohort consisting of students and teachers from diverse educational backgrounds. The topic was our engineering specialization.
task_action: To achieve our task, we had to thoroughly research the topic. We not only had to understand the content, but also know it indepth in such a way that we can explain it to someone that had no experience or prior knowledge on the topic. After the research phase, we divided the workload onto ourselves to create slides for the presentation with the key points and had mock presentations, while also taking feedback from our peers into consideration, to make sure we were ready.
result: When the day of the presentation arrived, we had proceeded like we practiced and our efforts had paid off. We were able to provide the audience a concise but engaging presentation. Moreover, the feedback from the audience let us know that the content was easy to understand and their overall knowledge on the topic had improved.
pfr: The task of an oral presentation to a large audience felt overwhelming, especially the fact that most of them were strangers. However, as I started to work on it with my group members, the task became bearable and at the end I actually was more confident. Moreover, I also overcame my stage fright, which was the biggest hurdle, by doing practice sessions often and got to know that not everyone was out to judge me.
learning: From this experience, not only have I gained more understanding of my degree I am studying, I have also learnt to collaborate with my peers. The importance of constructive criticism was also something that I have learned to appreciate.

situation: Several months ago, my workplace underwent a hiring process to onboard six additional casual workers. However, the training approach for these new hires merely involved shadowing longer-tenured colleagues. Despite recognizing the limitations of this method, I remained silent and allowed the process to proceed unquestioned. As time passed, frustrations emerged among my coworkers, including myself, regarding one new hire's lack of initiative and performance. While gossip circulated about his shortcomings, I refrained from participating, understanding its futility in fostering improvement.
task_action: To address the issue constructively, I devised a communication strategy aimed at effectively conveying concerns without provoking defensiveness. I scheduled a meeting with the individual to discuss the matter candidly. My approach involved presenting factual evidence of his performance and articulating how it was perceived by others. I then offered constructive feedback and clarified expectations to facilitate a mutual understanding.
result: The outcome of this intervention was a notable improvement in the individual's performance once expectations were clearly understood. Additionally, delving deeper into the underlying reasons for his struggles provided valuable insights that were shared with the team. This enhanced understanding fostered a supportive environment and contributed to overall workplace satisfaction.
pfr: In retrospect, my decision to address the issue directly was pivotal in resolving the situation positively. It reinforced the importance of accountability and proactive communication in fostering a harmonious work environment. Furthermore, this experience highlighted the value of empathy and understanding in effectively managing interpersonal challenges.
learning: Importance of Proactive Intervention: Recognizing issues and taking proactive steps to address them can prevent escalating problems and promote positive outcomes. Empathetic Communication: Approaching difficult conversations with empathy and understanding can facilitate constructive dialogue and resolution.

topic: Perseverance, urgency and will to deliver, resourcefulness and flexibility

result: The end code was sufficiently better and took lesser time to run.

situation: Within the ENGG4001 unit we needed to demonstrate a hypothetical solution for a net zero carbon emission export to replace coal within Australia. To this end we had to visually relay and defend our solution to the review and criticism of our peers.
task_action: A series of diagrams, plans and models were devised to be included within the defense presentation; flow charts were created to relay the proposed timeline of production, diagrams to visualize the area in question and 3D models to show the relationship between building elements and integration into the area. Parameters such as time, dimension and cost were also relayed visually through graphs .
result: An engaging and clear presentation of our solution could be given. By not inundating the presentation with words our audience were able to quickly grasp the information given in the oral component of the presentation without being confused or bored.
pfr: As a higher level engineering in practice unit the project at hand was of a greater scale than one previously encountered. The breadth of information that had to be shown and communicated was immense and without the appropriate visual strategies the solution we worked hard to develop could be misinterpreted or fall short of the standards required of an engineer. The presentation required the succinct demonstration of 10 weeks of work, relaying this work with the appropriate diagram or visual strategy was as important as the information itself.
learning: It is the responsibility of an engineer to not only create solutions but convey them with accuracy and clarity. To this end it is essential for a professional engineer to have a solid grasp of visual communication strategies. Selecting the appropriate techniques and strategies would be dependent on the situation and use case at hand; information, no matter how well formulated is of little use if not conveyed with effective communicative technique, in this case, appropriate visuals to support the verbal presentation.

learning: I learnt that accountability is one of the most important aspects of any team work. result: The final design was completed using our collective creativity and ability to overcome obstacles overall resulting in a flowing RGB machine final design that each group member had an equal say on.

learning: During the design process, individually and as a group, we learned how to overcome problems that arose during the early stages of the project. situation: We needed to brainstorm 10 unique scenes for our RGM in our first face to face meeting with each other.

Through this and past experiences I was also able to find that I do not like voicing my own opinion but must be comfortable with it to be able to effectively communicate and work as a team.

topic: Perseverance, urgency and will to deliver, resourcefulness and flexibility
situation: The ENGG2050 test was around the corner, and our in class group all had little to no idea what is was about, or when it was.
task_action: Prior to the date changes for the test, we came together as a group and tried to gather as much information as we could through comparing the differing unit guides and getting a firsthand account from someone who'd sat the unit previously. Once we could find the topics the test would be based on we worked to compartmentalize the textbook content before producing summaries of each point of interest.
result: We were able to walk into the test with a confident understanding of the content at hand.

This paired with the confusion from changing dates, locations and requirements only continued to cloud peoples expectations. With my groups communication, resourcefulness and problem solving abilities; we were able to work through the fog and come out confident in our understandings.
learning: Perseverance is an essential tool in learning, especially when you're faced with complex topics and expanding responsibilities. This alongside being able to assess the importance and expectations of assignments and tasks means you can choose priorities and use your time more efficiently. Being resourceful is vital when it comes to learning, being able to take understanding from the most unlikely of places is an amazing tool as a student. Having like-minded people alongside you is also a wonderful tool, being able to compare and contrast your learnings and working off of each other to further everyone's interpretations.

situation: In ENGG2050 we were tasked with designing and planning an intricate Tea Machine that would successfully do all the tasks required by the client. This project required extensive planning and a high level of creative thinking.

To Instigate creative thinking, we conducted brainstorming sessions where all ideas, were encouraged, discussed and considered. Once, the clients needs were understood, and all the ideas were on the table, we started planning out potential design from material used to the heating methods and power efficiency.
result: The result was a solid plan for the Tea Machine that addressed all the client’s requirements in a unique and creative manner
pfr: Initially the task of designing a Tea Machine seems very daunting. The task seemed very complex and every idea we came up with where commonly present and already in use in many other Tea Machines. However, after systematically approaching the idea brainstorming sessions, we were able to come up with some very creative ideas that were quite unique. Although the task seemed overwhelming at first, as we progressed thourgh the unit and did things one step at a time, the design started forming and becoming clear.
learning: This experience taught me the value of systematic and merit-based decision-making, and the importance of creative thinking. Having to design a tea machine that would only make tea with a lot of other client requirements had us thinking outside to box and come up with ideas we usually never would have.

situation: We were asked to come up with ideas and design an internet connective Tea Maker for our theoretical customer(s).

result: We had a list of features and ideas to send to the customers and receive feedback on in order to improve and refine our designs.

After putting aside our disagreements with the choice of beverage, we asked questions to our "customer" in order to better refine the final outcome of the project and the requested features. The features and ideas were much easier to understand after getting into the mind of our customer more.
learning: By using a team decision method, we all learned to better communicate our ideas, and work together to come up with improvisations or improvements to designs and features.

result: The final result was a few slight various of the same design that we all worked on strengthen and combine to the best possible solution
pfr: The task/brief, at first, seemed simple and easy to execute which lead us to feeling confident in our ability to adequately address and answer the clients requests. However it didn't take us long to realise that whilst the task was relatively simple from a mechanical perspective we couldn't really understand what it was the client actually wanted, this caused frustration and confusion which slowed down the development process. After more extensive communication and time we managed to gain a greater understanding which helped us fulfil our roles as the engineer.
learning: We learnt the importance of clear, constant and honest communication with each other and the client when designing a product that not only works but actually works as intended by the client and fulfils their original need/desire.

This process involved brainstorming multiple concepts and weighing the benefits and drawbacks of both. This involved discussion of the various options and how we should tackle the project in its entirety, with discussion about its level of modularity being key.
result: This discussion and brainstorming allowed us to narrow down the solutions to a single option we decided was worth pursuing and this further allowed us to progress in the project.
pfr: The scope of the task was overwhelming as we had the freedom to approach it from any angle and thus we had to examine a wide range of ideas and strategies in order to find even a set of possible solutions to sort through and further improve.
learning: Through reducing the concepts to a handful of ideas we effectively reduced the daunting nature of the task. Using guidelines and needs outlined through prior class discussion allowed us to feel less daunted by the scale of the task and allowed us to focus in on the key features of the design. These guidelines showed us that it is very important to have a central focus on the goals of your designs to ensure you don't lose sight of your specific goal and ease the daunting nature of such open ended tasks.

situation: The project throughout the ENGG2050 unit was to make a tea maker. This was inspired by reviewing the ethics, integrity and social responsibility while creating the tea maker for the customer.
task_action: Every week, there are weekly SGTAs and lectures to tackle the decision of the requirements on the tea maker while adhering to the customer needs and making sure that the tea maker's manufacturing process follow the the ethical standards for the customer to avoid environmentally harmful materials and a socially responsible tea maker that is good for the environment. This was challenging because of the customer needs are required to meet while also practicing the ethics, integrity and social responsibility that is required in the engineering environment. Ethically sourced materials from the supplier for our tea leaves was one of the main priority where we source it from the Fairtrade tea company where their tea leaves are ethically sourced to fit the standards. Honesty in the project was also considered as one of the main requirements where we are transparent with the customer, letting them know where all the materials are sourced from to create a sustainable and about 10% of commission of the tea maker will go into charity for world vision. For social responsibility, the tea maker is equipped with 'power saving mode' to make it environmentally sustainable and to also make the tea maker portable and last longer.

situation: As an undergraduate engineer working for the Central Coast Council, my team and I were tasked with assisting with upgrading a water mains infrastructure, which is a common job required for most projects. Traditional methods required a complete water shutdown to install new water mains or relocate them, causing significant disruption to the community. For this particular job, traditional methods did not seem applicable due to the time required for traditional methods to be done, and we were on tight deadlines. A new technology known as a S-gate valve, was proposed for trial. This valve could be installed on live water mains, eliminating the need for a full water shutdown.
task_action: My task was to assess the feasibility and potential benefits of implementing the S-gate valve technology. This included planning the trial installation, coordinating with my supervisors, and evaluating the performance and impact of the new technology. I was tasked with writing an article on the technology to inform the managers about the potential use of this new technology. Action: * Research and Analysis: I began by researching the S-gate valve technology, understanding its design, functionality, and previous implementations in other regions. * Stakeholder Coordination: I organised meetings with my managers, including the council's senior engineers. These meetings aimed to discuss the potential benefits, address any concerns, and ensure all parties were informed about the trial process. * Planning the Trial: I developed a detailed plan for the trial installation. This included scheduling the installation to minimise disruption and organising all necessary equipment and personnel. * Monitoring and Evaluation: During the installation, I helped to monitor the process and evaluate the outcome of the trial by writing an article about the installation.
result: The trial of the S-gate valve technology was successful and had several positive outcomes: * Minimised Disruption: The installation of the S-gate valve was completed without requiring a full water shutdown, significantly reducing inconvenience for the local community. This demonstrated the technology’s potential to streamline future projects. * Cost and Time Savings: The trial showed that using the S-gate valve could save considerable time and costs associated with traditional shutdown methods. Reduced labour hours and minimised service interruptions both reduced the cost of the project. * Improved Efficiency: The new technology improved the efficiency to our water mains maintenance procedures and was a lot easier job compared to traditional methods. * Positive Feedback: Feedback from the community and internal managers was positive. The community valued the reduced disruption, and the engineering team appreciated the innovative approach to the problem.
pfr: Initially, the task of trialling the new S-gate valve technology was both exciting and intimidating. I felt anxious about the potential challenges and the responsibility of helping to coordinate a trial that could impact the community and other council members. However, as the project progressed, the strong leadership in our council helped to reduce the risk of issues and made me feel a lot more relieved as time went on. The successful installation and positive feedback validated the effort and care put into the trial, providing immense satisfaction.
learning: * Systematic Approach: Breaking down complex tasks into manageable steps ensures clarity and confidence in execution. * Engagement with Management: Early and consistent communication builds trust and collaboration. * Adaptability: Being prepared to address unexpected challenges and learning from them is crucial. * Embracing new innovative technologies: A balanced approach to adopting new technologies is essential for successful implementation.

situation: At work, one of our freezers stopped working so we had a 'mission' to quickly (so the product did not thaw out) but also space effectively move all product from the broken freezer and get it into the one that was working.
task_action: I formed a plan and communicated with the other forklift driver (me and him were the only two), on which pallets to move first (based on which were most stackable, as a space saving measure), and I also communicated with the operator of another freezer nearby to take and hold overnight the pallets which would not fit into the 2nd freezer.
result: We were able to move all of the pallets out in a time effective manner, and, in my opinion, a space effective manner. We did however need the help of the other freezer operator to store some of our pallets overnight for us, so maybe we could have spent a little more time on the layout so as to increase the efficient use of space.
pfr: My personal feeling about the aforementioned task is that it was difficult to find a balance between doing the job quickly, and also optimising the amount of available space. I believe that we struck a good balance of time effectiveness and using the space afforded to us in an efficient manner. My plan was mostly based on the time pressures though, as too much time out of the freezer would result in lost product/stock.
learning: What I learnt from this situation is that in scenarios like this, it is impossible/very unlikely to arrive on the 'most optimal' use of time and space in this situation, as there will always be an argument for the extra time spent planning, but also in the argument for doing the job even faster. I feel like I also learnt to quickly plan, communicate and execute said plan in a high stress/time pressured environment better than I would have beforehand.

situation: As a first-year engineering student at Macquarie University, I was assigned a challenging task to design and build a Rube Goldberg Machine as part of our engineering design course. This project was designed to put not only our technical skills to the test, but also our ability to work collaboratively and professionally with our peers. The assignment was to design a complex, chain-reaction contraption capable of performing a simple task, such as turning on a light switch, through a series of intricate mechanical steps.
task_action: The project necessitated the collaboration of a diverse group of students, each with their own set of ideas and backgrounds. The main task was to design and build a Rube Goldberg Machine that not only met the project criteria but also demonstrated professionalism in our teamwork and communication with each other and the audiences to whom we presented. ACTION: To face the task while remaining professional throughout the project thus far, I have taken the following steps: Team Communication: Recognising the importance of clear and open communication, I established regular team meetings. These meetings ensured that everyone was on the same page when it came to our objectives, timeline, and individual responsibilities. To avoid misunderstandings and conflicts, effective communication is required. Active Listening: I made a conscious effort to actively listen to my teammates' ideas and concerns during our team discussions. I fostered a collaborative environment in which everyone felt heard and valued by encouraging open dialogue and respecting diverse viewpoints. Time Management: I realised that time management was critical to our project's success. I made a detailed project schedule that included milestones and deadlines. This allowed us to allocate our time more efficiently, ensuring that we meet project deadlines without having to rush at the last minute. Task Delegation: Recognising our team's strengths and weaknesses, I collaborated with my teammates to assign tasks that capitalised on each member's expertise. This approach fostered a sense of team ownership and motivation. Conflict Resolution: Because of differing opinions and approaches, conflicts have inevitably risen during the project. However, I dealt with these conflicts quickly and professionally, encouraging compromise and assisting in the mediation of discussions to reach mutually acceptable solutions. This helped to keep our project on track.
result: Our efforts to maintain professional behaviour throughout the project so far have had several positive outcomes: High Team Morale: By encouraging effective communication and professionally resolving conflicts, our team morale remained consistently high throughout the project. This optimistic atmosphere contributed to a more enjoyable and productive working environment. Collaboration Skills: I improved my collaboration skills, which included active listening, conflict resolution, and task delegation. These are highly transferrable skills that will undoubtedly help me in future engineering projects and in my professional career. The experience of designing and building a Rube Goldberg Machine thus far has highlighted the critical importance of professional behaviour in engineering projects. Effective communication, collaboration, and conflict resolution skills are not only necessary for project success, but they are also beneficial for personal and professional development. This project served as a stark reminder of the vital importance of professionalism in the ever-changing field of engineering.
pfr: The experience of designing the Rube Goldberg Machine was both educational and rewarding. During this project, I have felt frustration, joy, and satisfaction. The task's complexity has seemed overwhelming, but as we worked together as a team, I felt a growing sense of cooperation and shared purpose. Not only is the project testing my technical abilities, but also my ability to navigate the complexities of teamwork and professionalism. One of the most important personal lessons I have learned up to now is the importance of effective communication and conflict resolution in any collaborative endeavour. While I had always recognised the theoretical significance, this project allowed me to fully appreciate the practical significance of strong communication and conflict dispersion. There were times when disagreements threatened to derail our progress, but we were able to find solutions that ultimately improved our project by actively listening, mediating, and encouraging compromise.
learning: The most important lesson I've taken away from this experience is the importance of professionalism in engineering projects. It's not just about the technical aspects of the job; it's also about how we interact with our coworkers and deal with obstacles along the way. I've gained insights that I'll apply to my future endeavours: Communication is key: The foundation of successful teamwork is effective communication. I've learned that proactive communication ensures that everyone is on the same page in terms of goals and expectations, reducing the likelihood of misunderstandings. Conflict Resolution is a Skill: It is critical to address conflicts in a timely and professional manner. I now recognise that conflicts are opportunities for growth and that, when handled correctly, they can lead to better solutions and stronger team bonds. Time Management Is Non-Negotiable: Time management is a critical factor in project success, not just a technicality. In all of my future projects, I will continue to prioritise meticulous planning and strict adherence to deadlines. I will approach engineering projects in the future with a renewed emphasis on these lessons. I'll actively seek opportunities to lead and facilitate effective team communication. I'll also be more vigilant in identifying and addressing conflicts as soon as they arise, with a focus on finding collaborative solutions. Furthermore, I will always remember that professionalism is more than just a buzzword; it is a core characteristic that can have a significant impact on the success of any engineering project. This experience fundamentally shaped my perspective and will continue to guide my actions as my engineering career progresses.

situation: During a major RGM (Risk and Growth Management) project, our team faced the challenge of identifying and mitigating various risks that could impact the project's success and growth.
task_action: I was in charge of making sure our RGM (Risk and Growth Management) machine project ran smoothly and safely. result: My efforts paid off, as the RGM machine project operated more smoothly, safely, and with fewer unforeseen issues. situation: We were tasked with creating a video centred around designing a Rube Goldberg machine and the time management to present the video over an allotted time frame.
task_action: To tackle this challenge we embarked on a meticulous planning process. Firstly, we convened as a group to conceptualise the overarching storyline of the video, ensuring it showcased the intricacies of a Rube Goldberg machine while meeting marking criteria. With the narrative framework established, we divided the storyline into distinct sections, assigning each member responsibility for crafting one segment with two action tasks within. Next, we delved into the technical aspects of the project. Collaboratively, we brainstormed the various components and mechanisms that would comprise our Rube Goldberg machine, ensuring each section seamlessly transitioned to the next. Through iterative discussions and prototyping, we refined our ideas, prioritizing coherence and visual appeal. With the project scope defined, we turned our attention to resource management. Conducting an inventory of available equipment, we identified the tools necessary for realizing our vision. Recognizing potential constraints, we devised contingency plans and sought alternative solutions to mitigate risks.
result: The meticulous planning and coordination resulted in a presentation meeting time frame expectations, while adhering to marking criteria. Each section seamlessly transitioned to the next, maintaining the narrative flow decided by the group within the planning stages. By optimizing resource allocation, we maximized productivity and minimized unnecessary expenditures. Moreover, our strategic approach to time management facilitated adherence to deadlines, preventing delays and ensuring timely completion. As a result, we delivered a compelling Rube Goldberg machine video that not only met the project requirements but also exceeded expectations. The project's success underscored the effectiveness of our time and resource management strategies, demonstrating our ability to execute complex multimedia projects with precision and creativity.
pfr: Initially, I felt optimistic about our group project, eager to contribute to the creation of our Rube Goldberg machine video. However, as we progressed, I noticed challenges emerging, particularly in managing our time effectively. While there was excitement in collaborating with my peers and seeing our ideas take shape, there was also an underlying sense of pressure to meet deadlines and ensure cohesion within our project.
learning: Reflecting on this experience, I've come to realise the importance of proactive communication and realistic goal setting in managing time effectively. By fostering clear communication channels within the team and establishing achievable deadlines, we can streamline our workflow and minimize last-minute rushes. Additionally, I've learned that while enthusiasm is essential, it's equally vital to maintain a practical perspective and allocate sufficient time for each stage of the project. Moving forward, I intend to prioritise regular check-ins with my team members and adopt a more structured approach to planning and time allocation, ultimately enhancing both the efficiency and quality of our collaborative endeavours.
